questions.answer: एकूण कंकणे = २४ जणांची संख्या = ४ प्रत्येकाला मिळालेल्या कंकणे = २४ ÷ ४ = ६ त्यामुळे प्रत्येकाला ६ कंकणे मिळाले.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्न सोडवा व पूर्ण कामकाज लिहा.
questions.text: १५ फळे ५ जणांत समान वाटले. प्रत्येकाला किती फळे मिळाले?
questions.answer: एकूण फळे = १५ जणांची संख्या = ५ प्रत्येकाला मिळालेल्या फळे = १५ ÷ ५ = ३ त्यामुळे प्रत्येकाला ३ फळे मिळाले.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्न सोडवा व पूर्ण कामकाज लिहा.
questions.text: १६ पेरू ४ जणांत समान वाटले. प्रत्येकाला किती पेरू मिळाले?
questions.answer: एकूण पेरू = १६ जणांची संख्या = ४ प्रत्येकाला मिळालेल्या पेरू = १६ ÷ ४ = ४ त्यामुळे प्रत्येकाला ४ पेरू मिळाले.

questions.text: गणितीय कोडी अध्यायात आकारांची ओळख कसे केली जाते?
questions.answer: आकारांची ओळख त्यांच्या भुजा, कोन व बिंदुन समदूरता प्रमाणे केली जाते.

questions.answer: सापशिडीवरील संख्या ९२वरून ९५पर्यंतच्या संख्या सापाच्या तोंडावर दहा पायांचा फास घेऊन जातात.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: त्रिकोणाची ओळख कसे केली जाते?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: गणितीय कोडी अध्यायात आकार मोजण्याचे दोन उपाय सांगा.
questions.answer: आकार मोजण्याचे उपाय आहेत: त्यांची भुजा मापणे व त्यांची संख्या गणणे. उदाहरणार्थ, वर्तुळांची संख्या सात, त्रिकोणांची पाच, आयतांची तीन.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सापशिडीवरील संख्या ४८ येईल अशी बेरीज तयार करण्याचे दोन उदाहरण सांगा.
questions.answer: ४८ येईल अशी बेरीज तयार करण्यासाठी २४ + २४ किंवा ३० + १८ वापरता येईल. उदाहरणार्थ, २४ व २४ बेरीज एकत्र करण्याने ४८ मिळते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: गणितीय कोडी अध्यायात आकारांची ओळख का महत्त्वाची आहे?
questions.answer: आकारांची ओळख महत्त्वाची आहे कारण ती बच्चण्यांना वातावरणातील वस्तूंची ओळख विकसित करते. ते विविध आकारांची ओळखून गणितीय संकल्पना विकसित करते. उदाहरणार्थ, वर्तुळाची ओळखून बॉल, चाकू इत्यादीची ओळख होईल. त्यामुळे त्यांचा विचारशील विकास होतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सापशिडीवरील संख्या ९२वरून ९५पर्यंतच्या संख्या सापाच्या तोंडावर जाणे का सोपं आहे?
questions.answer: सापशिडीवरील संख्या ९२वरून ९५पर्यंतच्या संख्या सापाच्या तोंडावर जाणे सोपं आहे कारण प्रत्येक पायाला दहा जोडणे सोपं असते. ते बच्चण्यांना दहा tabel च्या अभ्यासासाठी उपयुक्त आहे. उदाहरणार्थ, ९२ + १० = १०२, पण सापशिडीवरील फक्त ९२ ते ९५पर्यंत आहे, त्यामुळे प्रत्येक पायाला एक जोडून ९३, ९४, ९५ मिळते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: गणितीय कोडी अध्यायातील आकारांची ओळख व संख्या ओळख यांची महत्त्वता सांगा.
questions.answer: गणितीय कोडी अध्यायातील आकारांची ओळख व संख्या ओळख बच्चण्यांना गणितीय आधार विकसित करण्यासाठी आवश्यक आहे. आकारांची ओळखून ते वर्तुळ, त्रिकोण, आयत इत्यादींची ओळख करतात, ज्यामुळे त्यांचा आकृतिज्ञेय विकास होतो. संख्या ओळखून ते गणना, जोड, घट व तुलना करणे शिकतात. उदाहरणार्थ, वर्तुळांची संख्या सात गणणे, त्रिकोणांची पाच गणणे हे त्यांचे गणितीय कौशल्य विकसित करते. सापशिडीवरील संख्या ओळखून ते दहा tabel च्या अभ्यासासाठी तयार होतात. त्यामुळे त्यांचा दैनंदिन जीवनातील गणितीय वापर विकसित होतो.

questions.subject: Maths

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why is school important in our life? Explain with two points.
questions.answer: School is important because it teaches us to learn subjects and follow rules. It also helps us learn discipline, respect, and how to behave in society, making us good citizens.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: How do students show friendly relations with each other in school?
questions.answer: Students spend time together with their friends, help each other, and take care of one another. They also learn and play together, which builds friendly relations.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: What happens during the annual sports competition in school?
questions.answer: During the annual sports competition, the playground is decorated with colourful flags, children participate with excitement, and events like running and kabaddi are held. Students cheer for their teams and congratulate winners.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why does the school uniform create a sense of belonging among students?
questions.answer: The school uniform creates a sense of belonging because all students wear the same dress, which shows they are part of one school community. It promotes equality and unity, making students feel proud and connected to their school.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why do we learn to respect our teachers in school?
questions.answer: We learn to respect our teachers because they teach us different subjects and guide us in learning. They also help us grow into good citizens by teaching discipline and good behaviour.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Describe your school and explain why you like going to school.
questions.answer: My school has a big building, a playground, and many classrooms. We wear a blue and white uniform. I like going to school because I get to learn new things, play with my friends, and take part in sports and games. My teachers are kind and help me when I have doubts. We also celebrate festivals and events together. School teaches me to be disciplined, honest, and helpful. I feel happy and safe in my school.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Explain how school is like a second family.
questions.answer: School is like a second family because we spend a lot of time there with our teachers and friends. Just like in a family, we care for, help, and respect each other. Teachers guide us like parents, and we learn values like sharing, honesty, and kindness. We celebrate events together and feel happy and safe. In school, we learn to live in society, just as we learn to live in a family. It gives us love, learning, and support, making it a second home for us.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Define 'discipline' as mentioned in the chapter.
questions.answer: Discipline means following rules, coming to school on time, wearing the uniform, and behaving in a proper and orderly way.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Define 'student-teacher relation'.
questions.answer: Student-teacher relation is the friendly and respectful bond between students and teachers, where teachers guide and students learn with trust and obedience.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write 3-4 points of difference between the following.
questions.text: Difference between learning at home and learning in school.
questions.answer: In school, we learn from trained teachers in a fixed schedule, while at home, learning is informal and done by parents. School provides facilities like playground, library, and labs, which may not be available at home. In school, we interact with children from different families, building social skills, whereas at home, interaction is limited to family members. School teaches discipline through uniform and assembly, while at home, routines are more flexible.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write 3-4 points of difference between the following.
questions.text: Difference between values learned in family and values learned in school.
questions.answer: In family, we learn love, care, and personal values like helping parents and sharing with siblings. In school, we learn social values like discipline, equality, unity, and respect for all. Family teaches us customs and traditions, while school teaches us to be good citizens and follow societal rules. In family, learning is emotional and personal; in school, it is structured and aimed at preparing us for society.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain how school helps us become good citizens.
questions.answer: School helps us become good citizens by teaching us to follow rules and respect others. We learn discipline through uniform, punctuality, and assembly. We are taught to help and care for classmates, which builds kindness and teamwork. By learning about society and behaving well, we prepare to live responsibly in the community. All these lessons shape us into honest, respectful, and responsible citizens.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain the importance of the school uniform.
questions.answer: The school uniform creates a feeling of equality among students, as everyone wears the same dress. It promotes discipline by reminding students to follow school rules. It builds unity and a sense of belonging to the school community. The uniform also serves as the identity of the school, making students easily recognizable. Wearing it with pride helps students feel proud of their school.

questions.answer: The Right to Education Act, 2009 ensures free and compulsory education for every boy and girl in India.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why is school considered a useful institution for society?
questions.answer: School gives us knowledge, teaches us to solve problems, and helps us learn to work together. It also teaches democratic values like speaking, sharing thoughts, and listening to others. These make school very useful for society.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: What responsibilities does a Cultural Minister have in school?
questions.answer: The Cultural Minister is responsible for organising and managing cultural programmes in school. They help plan events like dances, songs, and dramas. They work with teachers and students to make cultural activities successful.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: How does school teach us democracy?
questions.answer: In school, we learn to speak, share our thoughts, and listen to others’ opinions. We take part in elections like the School Council, where we vote for our leaders. This helps us understand how democracy works.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why is a ramp built next to stairs in school?
questions.answer: A ramp is built to help children who use wheelchairs move in and out of school easily. Stairs are difficult for wheelchair users, so the slope provides smooth access. This ensures that all students, regardless of ability, can enter and exit the school safely.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why is it important for every child to get education under the RTE Act?
questions.answer: Education helps children gain knowledge and skills for a better future. It promotes equality by giving every boy and girl the same opportunity to learn. Educated children grow up to be responsible citizens who can contribute to society.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe how your school works like a small democracy.
questions.answer: Our school works like a small democracy in many ways. We elect class monitors and school council members through voting, just like in a real election. Every student gets a chance to share their ideas during meetings or class discussions. Teachers listen to our opinions and consider them when making decisions. We follow rules that are made for the good of everyone, not just a few. During events like Cleanliness Week, we divide into groups and share work fairly. We learn to respect others’ views and work together as a team. These experiences teach us the values of liberty, equality, and fraternity. Thus, school prepares us to be responsible citizens in a democratic country.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain the importance of the Right to Education Act, 2009 for children in India.
questions.answer: The Right to Education Act, 2009 is a very important law that ensures every child in India gets free and compulsory education. It applies to all boys and girls between the ages of 6 and 14. No child can be denied admission to school because of poverty, caste, or gender. The government must provide schools, teachers, and learning materials. This law helps reduce illiteracy and gives equal opportunities to all children. It also prevents child labour by making school attendance mandatory. Children with disabilities are also included and given special support. By educating every child, the Act helps build a stronger, fairer, and more developed nation. It is a big step toward social justice and national progress.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Define 'ramp' as used in the context of school.
questions.answer: A ramp is a sloping path built next to stairs to help people, especially those using wheelchairs, move easily in and out of a building.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: What is democracy?
questions.answer: Democracy is a system of government where people choose their leaders by voting and have equal rights to participate in decision-making.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Write the difference between stairs and a ramp in school.
questions.answer: Stairs are vertical steps used for walking up and down, while a ramp is a sloping surface. Stairs can be difficult for wheelchair users or those with mobility issues, but a ramp allows easy access for wheelchairs. Stairs take less space, but ramps require more horizontal space. Ramps promote inclusivity, whereas stairs may exclude some students.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Write the difference between the roles of Discipline Minister and Cultural Minister in school council.
questions.answer: The Discipline Minister ensures students follow school rules and maintain order, while the Cultural Minister organises cultural events like songs, dances, and dramas. The Discipline Minister focuses on behaviour and safety, whereas the Cultural Minister focuses on creativity and participation. The Discipline Minister may monitor corridors and assemblies, while the Cultural Minister plans annual day or festival activities. Both roles help in the smooth functioning of school but in different areas.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain how school helps us learn to work together.
questions.answer: In school, we do many activities in groups, such as projects, sports, and cleaning drives. We learn to share tasks, listen to others, and help our friends. During Cleanliness Week, we divide into groups and each group takes responsibility for a specific area. We also celebrate festivals and cultural events together, which requires cooperation. These experiences teach us the value of teamwork and prepare us to work well in society.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain why the School Council of Ministers is formed in schools.
questions.answer: The School Council of Ministers is formed to give students a chance to learn about leadership and responsibility. It helps students understand how elections work by letting them vote for their peers. Each minister takes charge of a specific area like culture, cleanliness, or sports, which teaches them to manage duties. This system encourages students to contribute to school improvement. It also builds confidence, decision-making skills, and a sense of belonging among students.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why do we have a complaint box in school?
questions.answer: We put our complaints or suggestions in the complaint box so that the school can improve.

questions.text: What do students do in the library?
questions.answer: Students read books, newspapers, or study quietly in the library.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Who teaches us drawing and craft in school?
questions.answer: The art teacher teaches us drawing and craft in school.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: What are the different things you learn at school?
questions.answer: At school, we learn to read, write, and count. We also learn good habits, how to behave with others, and about plants, animals, and our surroundings. We learn to work together and respect everyone.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: What work does the mid-day meal cook do in school?
questions.answer: The mid-day meal cook prepares food for all students every day. She makes sure the food is clean, hot, and tasty. She serves the food with care so that no student stays hungry.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: How do parents help in school activities?
questions.answer: Parents help by attending meetings, volunteering for events, and supporting school programs. They also guide their children at home and give feedback to teachers. Their involvement makes school better for everyone.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why is a laboratory important in a school?
questions.answer: A laboratory is important because it allows students to do science experiments and see how things work. It helps them understand concepts better by doing rather than just reading. It develops curiosity and interest in science. Students learn to observe, measure, and record results safely.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why should we keep the school clean?
questions.answer: We should keep the school clean to stay healthy and avoid diseases. A clean school looks nice and makes everyone feel happy and proud. It also helps us learn better in a fresh and tidy environment. Cleanliness teaches us good habits for life.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Describe your school playground and what you do there.
questions.answer: Our school playground is big and open with green grass and a boundary wall. It has swings, slides, a see-saw, and a football ground. We play games like cricket, kho-kho, and kabaddi during recess. Sometimes we do yoga or march practice in the morning. The playground keeps us active, happy, and friendly with our classmates.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain how different people in school help us every day.
questions.answer: The teacher teaches us lessons and clears our doubts. The principal manages the school and ensures everything runs well. The peon rings the bell and helps in carrying things. The sweeper keeps the classrooms and toilets clean. The cook gives us tasty mid-day meal. The librarian helps us find books. The gardener takes care of plants. All of them work together so that we can learn safely and happily.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: What is a library?
questions.answer: A library is a room or place in school where books, newspapers, and magazines are kept for students to read and learn.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: What is a principal?
questions.answer: The principal is the head of the school who leads teachers, students, and staff to make the school run smoothly.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write the difference between the following.
questions.text: Teacher and Student
questions.answer: A teacher teaches and guides students in learning. A student learns and follows the teacher's instructions. The teacher is older and trained to educate. The student is younger and comes to gain knowledge. The teacher prepares lessons; the student does homework and classwork.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write the difference between the following.
questions.text: Classroom and Playground
questions.answer: A classroom is an indoor room where we study with books and notebooks. A playground is an outdoor open space where we play and do physical activities. In the classroom, we sit quietly and listen. In the playground, we run, jump, and play games. The classroom has desks and a blackboard; the playground has swings, slides, and open ground.

questions.text: Explain how the mid-day meal helps students in school.
questions.answer: The mid-day meal gives students nutritious food so they do not feel hungry during school hours. It helps poor children get at least one healthy meal a day. When students are not hungry, they can concentrate better on their studies. It also encourages regular school attendance. Eating together promotes friendship and equality among all students.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain why we have different rooms like library, laboratory, and computer room in school.
questions.answer: Different rooms are made for different activities to help us learn better. The library is for reading books and gaining knowledge. The laboratory is for doing science experiments and seeing how things work. The computer room helps us learn to use technology and digital tools. Each room has special things needed for that activity. This way, we can focus and learn each subject in the right environment.

questions.answer: The basic needs of a person are food, clothing, shelter, health, and education. These are essential for survival and well-being. Without them, it becomes difficult to live a healthy life.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: What types of goods are sold in a weekly market?
questions.answer: In a weekly market, we get fresh vegetables, fruits, grains, flowers, spices, clothes, pots, baskets, farming tools, and snacks. Sellers also sell sweets, handicrafts, and sometimes animals. The market is full of variety and activity.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why did Raghu’s father buy ladyfinger and spinach even though they were not on the list?
questions.answer: Raghu’s father bought ladyfinger and spinach because they are healthy vegetables with important nutrients. He believed that the body needs all kinds of tastes — sweet, bitter, spicy, and sour — to stay fit. Buying them was necessary for good health, not just based on liking.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why did Rama carry cloth bags to the market?
questions.answer: Rama carried cloth bags to avoid using plastic bags, which harm the environment. Cloth bags are reusable and eco-friendly. Her father had taught her to be a responsible customer. Carrying cloth bags is a small step toward protecting nature.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why do sellers in a weekly market call out loudly to advertise their goods?
questions.answer: Sellers call out loudly to attract customers and inform them about what they are selling. In a busy market with many stalls, loud calls help their goods stand out. It is a traditional way of advertising without using signs or technology. This helps increase sales and reach more buyers.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe your visit to a weekly market. What did you see, hear, and buy?
questions.answer: I visited the weekly market with my mother. The market was full of colors and sounds — vendors were calling out, baskets were filled with red tomatoes, green chillies, and yellow marigolds. The air smelled of fresh flowers and hot snacks. I saw farmers selling vegetables from their farms and women buying bangles and clay pots. My mother bought rice, lentils, and a bunch of coriander. I wanted to buy a spinning top, and she agreed. We carried our purchases in a cloth bag. The market was lively, and everyone seemed happy. It was a wonderful experience of seeing how people buy and sell things in our village.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain the difference between a weekly market and a supermarket.
questions.answer: A weekly market is held on a fixed day every week, usually in an open space, where sellers sit on the ground or in small stalls. It sells fresh, local goods like vegetables, fruits, and handmade items. Prices are often bargained. A supermarket, on the other hand, is a big shop in a building, open every day, selling packed and branded goods like biscuits, soaps, and stationery. It has fixed prices, barcode scanners, and gives receipts. Supermarkets are common in cities, while weekly markets are found in both villages and cities. Both serve the purpose of buying and selling, but in different ways.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Define 'market'.
questions.answer: A market is a place where people come together to buy and sell goods and services.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Define 'customer'.
questions.answer: A customer is a person who buys goods or services from a seller.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: State the difference between a weekly market and an animal market.
questions.answer: A weekly market sells daily use items like vegetables, fruits, clothes, and household goods for general public. An animal market is specifically for buying and selling animals like cows, buffaloes, goats, and bullocks. Weekly markets are held every week in villages or cities, while animal markets are often held on specific days like Sundays and are famous in places like Sangola. In weekly markets, people buy for home use; in animal markets, farmers buy animals for farming, milk, or bullock cart races. The atmosphere in animal markets includes checking the health and breed of animals, which is not done in weekly markets.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: State the difference between needs and wants.
questions.answer: Needs are things essential for survival, such as food, water, clothing, and shelter. Wants are things we desire but can live without, like toys, chocolates, or fancy clothes. Needs must be fulfilled to stay healthy and safe, while wants bring happiness but are not necessary. For example, eating vegetables is a need, but buying an ice cream is a want. We should prioritize needs over wants, especially when resources are limited.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain why it is important to carry a shopping list when going to the market.
questions.answer: A shopping list helps us remember what we need to buy and prevents us from forgetting important items. It stops us from buying unnecessary things on impulse, thus saving money. It makes shopping faster and more organized, especially in busy markets. Parents can involve children in making the list to teach them responsibility. It also helps in checking the budget and avoiding overspending.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain how a market helps people in a village or city.
questions.answer: A market provides a place where people can buy essential goods like food, clothes, and tools without traveling far. It allows farmers and artisans to sell their products and earn income. Markets create opportunities for people to meet, exchange ideas, and build community bonds. They support the local economy by keeping money within the village or city. Weekly markets also preserve traditional ways of buying and selling, strengthening social ties.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Write about the basic needs of human beings and why they are important.
questions.answer: Basic needs are essential for survival and a healthy life. They include food, water, clothing, shelter, and education. Food gives us energy, water keeps us hydrated, clothes protect us from weather, shelter gives safety, and education helps us grow. Fulfilling these needs allows us to live happily and contribute to society.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: How can we help people with disabilities in our society?
questions.answer: We can help people with disabilities by being kind and respectful. We should support facilities like ramps, Braille books, and sign language interpreters. Schools and public places should be accessible. We must not laugh or ignore them. Instead, we can offer help when needed and create a barrier-free environment so they can live with dignity.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Define 'needs'.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Define 'natural resources'.
questions.answer: Natural resources are things we get from nature that are useful to us, such as water, air, and sunlight.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write 3-4 points of difference between the following.
questions.text: Difference between needs and wants.
questions.answer: Needs are essential for survival, while wants are not necessary but make life enjoyable. We cannot live without needs, but we can live without wants. Needs must be fulfilled first, while wants can be controlled. Examples of needs: water, food. Examples of wants: toys, sweets.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write 3-4 points of difference between the following.
questions.text: Difference between natural resources and human-made resources.
questions.answer: Natural resources are obtained from nature, like water and air. Human-made resources are created by people, like machines and money. Natural resources exist without human effort, while human-made resources require human work. We must use natural resources carefully to avoid depletion.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain why clean air is necessary for good health.
questions.answer: Clean air is necessary because it keeps our lungs strong and helps us breathe easily. Polluted air can cause coughing, asthma, and other health problems. When we breathe clean air, we feel fresh and active. It gives us energy to play, study, and work. Therefore, clean air is essential for a healthy body and mind.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain how farmers help fulfill our needs.
questions.answer: Farmers grow food crops like grains, vegetables, and fruits, which fulfill our need for food. They also grow cotton and other materials used to make clothes. Their hard work ensures we have enough to eat and wear. Without farmers, we would face food and clothing shortages. Thus, farmers play a vital role in meeting our basic needs.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain how rainwater harvesting helps in increasing groundwater level.
questions.answer: Rainwater harvesting collects rain from roofs and grounds and directs it into tanks or soak pits. This water seeps into the soil and recharges the groundwater. As a result, wells get filled and water level rises.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why is it important to keep water sources clean?
questions.answer: Dirty water can cause diseases when used for drinking or farming. Polluted water harms health and damages crops. Clean water ensures safety and proper growth.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: What did Dr. Rajendra Singh do to solve water problems in Rajasthan?
questions.answer: Dr. Rajendra Singh built johads, which are small earthen dams, to store rainwater. These structures helped increase groundwater and made the land green. His work earned him the title 'Waterman of India'.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why are dams built on rivers?
questions.answer: Dams are built on rivers to store rainwater during the monsoon. This stored water is used throughout the year for drinking, farming, and electricity. It ensures water availability even in dry seasons.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why should we repair leaking taps immediately?
questions.answer: A leaking tap wastes a lot of water over time. This increases water scarcity and puts extra burden on water resources. Fixing it saves water and reduces utility bills.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Write about the importance of water conservation in your own words.
questions.answer: Water is essential for life, but its sources are limited. We must save water by closing taps, harvesting rainwater, and planting trees. Conserving water helps prevent droughts, keeps the environment clean, and ensures future generations have enough water. Small efforts by everyone can make a big difference.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Describe any two traditional water conservation methods used in India.
questions.answer: In ancient India, wells were dug in houses and communities to store groundwater, as seen in the Indus Valley Civilization. Another method was building johads—earthen dams that collect rainwater and recharge the soil, promoted by Dr. Rajendra Singh in Rajasthan. These methods are simple, low-cost, and effective in increasing water availability.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Water literacy
questions.answer: Water literacy means understanding the importance of water, saving water, and making efforts to increase the level of underground water.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Groundwater conservation
questions.answer: Groundwater conservation is the practice of directing rainwater into the soil through soak pits or tanks to increase the water level underground and keep wells filled.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write the difference between the following.
questions.text: Flood and drought
questions.answer: Flood occurs when there is excessive rainfall causing water to overflow, while drought happens due to very little or no rainfall leading to water shortage. Floods damage crops and homes; droughts affect drinking water and farming. Both are caused by uneven rainfall distribution.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write the difference between the following.
questions.text: Rainwater harvesting and water wastage
questions.answer: Rainwater harvesting means collecting and saving rainwater for future use, while water wastage is using water carelessly, like leaving taps open. Harvesting increases groundwater; wastage reduces available water. One conserves, the other depletes water resources.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain how tree plantation helps in water conservation and environmental balance.
questions.answer: Tree roots hold soil and help rainwater seep into the ground, increasing groundwater level. They reduce soil erosion by holding the soil firmly. Trees also release moisture into the air, helping maintain the water cycle. Their shade reduces evaporation from soil and water bodies. Overall, trees support water conservation and keep the environment healthy and balanced.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain why it is everyone’s responsibility to protect and conserve water.
questions.answer: Water is a limited resource essential for all living beings. If we waste water, there may not be enough for drinking, farming, or industry in the future. Pollution and overuse harm ecosystems and cause scarcity. By saving water, we ensure health, food security, and a clean environment. Every small action, like closing taps or harvesting rain, contributes to a sustainable future.

questions.text: How do festivals help in creating unity among people in India?
questions.answer: Festivals bring people together regardless of their religion or region. During festivals, people share good wishes, celebrate together, and participate in common activities like singing, dancing, and eating. This sense of togetherness strengthens unity in diversity.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Describe how bulls are decorated and honored during Bail Pola.
questions.answer: During Bail Pola, bulls are bathed, cleaned, and decorated with painted bodies, beautiful cloth on their backs, ornamented horns, headpieces, shell garlands, and bells. questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why do people in different parts of India eat different types of food?
questions.answer: People in different parts of India eat different types of food due to differences in climate and crops available in their region. For example, coastal areas have more fish, so they eat rice and fish, while Punjab grows wheat, so people eat dal and roti. This leads to regional specialties in food.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why is it said that 'the most beautiful thing about India is that no matter whose festival it is, everyone celebrates it together'?
questions.answer: This is said because India has unity in diversity. People of all religions and cultures respect each other’s festivals and join in the celebrations with joy. This mutual respect and participation strengthen national unity and harmony.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why are traditional sports like kabaddi and mallakhamb still popular in India today?
questions.answer: Traditional sports like kabaddi and mallakhamb are still popular because they are deeply rooted in Indian culture and promote physical fitness, mental strength, and values like teamwork and discipline. They are also now recognized internationally, which increases pride and interest in playing them.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Describe the diversity in India based on festivals, food, and clothing.
questions.answer: India shows great diversity in festivals, food, and clothing. Festivals like Diwali, Eid, Christmas, and Navroz are celebrated by different communities with joy. Food varies from dal and roti in Punjab to rice and fish in coastal areas, and idli-sambar in South India. Clothing also differs — women wear sarees, salwar-kameez, choli-ghagra, or Mekhela chador depending on the region. Despite these differences, all Indians celebrate together, showing unity in diversity.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain how folk arts help in preserving culture and spreading awareness.
questions.answer: Folk arts like Lavani, Bhangra, Garba, and Bamboo dance are cultural identities of different states. Saints like Sant Tukaram and Annabhau Sathe used kirtans and abhangs to teach values like equality, cleanliness, and kindness. These arts are performed during festivals and fairs, helping to pass on traditions to younger generations. They make learning enjoyable and keep India’s rich heritage alive.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Culture
questions.answer: Culture means the special way of living our life as a part of society. It includes language, clothing, food, festivals, religion, ways of worship, art, skills, literature, and celebrations.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Unity in Diversity
questions.answer: Unity in Diversity means that although people in India have different languages, cultures, foods, and traditions, they are all united as one nation and live together with peace and respect.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: North Indian food and South Indian food
questions.answer: North Indian food mainly includes wheat-based items like roti, paratha, and dishes like dal and paneer. South Indian food is rice-based and includes idli, dosa, sambar, and coconut-based curries. North Indian food uses more dairy like ghee and cream, while South Indian food uses coconut oil and curry leaves. Spices like garam masala are common in the North, while mustard seeds and curry leaves are used more in the South.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Traditional clothing of women in Rajasthan and women in Assam
questions.answer: Women in Rajasthan wear colorful choli-ghagra and chunri, which are bright and often mirror-worked. Women in Assam wear the Mekhela chador, a two-piece silk dress draped gracefully. Rajasthani attire reflects desert culture with bold colors and heavy embroidery, while Assamese clothing is light, made of silk like muga or pat, and suited to humid climate. The styles differ in draping, fabric, and motifs based on regional culture.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain how festivals help in preserving Indian culture.
questions.answer: Festivals help preserve Indian culture by passing down traditions from one generation to the next. During festivals, people wear traditional clothes, cook special foods, perform folk dances, and sing old songs. Rituals like worshipping bulls in Bail Pola or lighting lamps in Diwali keep ancient customs alive. These activities teach children about their heritage and values. Thus, festivals act as a living classroom for Indian culture.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain why India is called a land of unity in diversity.
questions.answer: India is called a land of unity in diversity because it has many languages, religions, foods, clothes, and festivals, yet all people identify as Indians. Despite differences, Indians respect each other’s cultures and celebrate festivals together. National events like Independence Day and Republic Day are celebrated by all with equal pride. This harmony in diversity makes India unique and strong.

questions.text: Why were pigeons used to send messages in olden times?
questions.answer: Pigeons were used because they can fly long distances and find their way home accurately. They were reliable when no other fast means of communication existed. Kings and people trusted them to carry important messages safely.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why is Speed Post used for important letters?
questions.answer: Speed Post is used because it delivers letters faster than regular post. It uses air and rail transport for quick delivery. It is reliable for sending urgent or important documents.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe how communication has changed from olden times to today.
questions.answer: In olden times, messages were sent through pigeons, messengers on horses or camels, which took days or weeks. Later, postal services were started using bicycles, trains, and ships. The invention of the telephone allowed instant voice communication. Today, we use mobile phones, email, and video calls to communicate instantly across the world. Communication has become faster, easier, and more accessible.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain the importance of communication in our daily life with examples.
questions.answer: Communication helps us share ideas, express feelings, and stay connected with family and friends. For example, we call our parents when we are late, send birthday wishes through messages, and teachers explain lessons in class. During emergencies, communication helps us call for help. It also helps in learning through television, radio, and books. Without communication, we would feel isolated and unable to work together.

questions.subject: EVS

questions.answer: Communication is the exchange of information, ideas, or messages between two or more people.

questions.text: Letter and Telephone
questions.answer: 1. A letter is written and takes days to reach, while a telephone call is instant. 2. A letter requires paper and post, while a telephone needs a network connection. 3. A letter can be kept as a record, but a telephone call is temporary unless recorded. 4. Writing a letter takes time, but speaking on the telephone is quick.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write 3-4 points of difference between the following.
questions.text: Olden times communication and Modern communication
questions.answer: 1. In olden times, messages were sent by pigeons or messengers, which were slow; today, we use phones and internet for instant communication. 2. Old methods depended on animals or people, while modern methods use technology like satellites and towers. 3. Earlier, only rich or kings could send messages easily; now, almost everyone can communicate affordably. 4. Old communication had no proof of delivery, but modern methods give delivery reports and timestamps.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: How do satellites help in communication?
questions.answer: Satellites orbit the Earth and receive signals from one place and send them to another. They help in making phone calls, watching TV, and using the internet across long distances. Satellites are especially useful in remote areas where cables cannot reach. They also help in weather forecasting and navigation. Without satellites, global communication would be much slower and limited.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why is the invention of the telephone considered a revolution in communication?
questions.answer: Before the telephone, sending a message took days or weeks through letters or messengers. The telephone allowed people to talk to each other instantly, no matter the distance. It brought families and friends closer and helped businesses work faster. It laid the foundation for modern communication like mobile phones and the internet. This invention changed how humans connect and share information forever.

questions.text: Why is Phule Wada considered a heritage site?
questions.answer: Phule Wada is considered a heritage site because it was the home of Mahatma Phule and Savitribai Phule, who worked for education and equality. The well in its courtyard was open to all, irrespective of caste or religion, reflecting their social reform work.

questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.

questions.answer: My ideal heritage tour would include visiting Shivneri Fort to see where Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was born, Sindhudurg Fort to experience a sea fort with fresh water inside, and Lonar Lake to see the crater formed by a meteor. I would also visit Phule Wada to learn about the Phule couple’s work for education and equality. I would take pictures, listen to guides, and make sure not to litter or damage any site. Such a tour would help me learn history, feel proud of our culture, and understand the importance of preserving our heritage.

questions.answer: I would like to visit Raigad Fort because it is where Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was crowned and where his samadhi is located. I hope to see the grand fort walls, the coronation platform, and the memorial. I would learn about the bravery and leadership of Shivaji Maharaj and how he established Swarajya. Visiting such a place would inspire me to be courageous and honest. I would also make sure to keep the place clean and respect its historical importance.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Define: Heritage
questions.answer: Heritage refers to the valuable things such as historical monuments, traditions, and culture that we inherit from our past and must protect for the future.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Define: Historical Monument
questions.answer: A historical monument is a structure or site like a fort, temple, or palace that has importance due to its connection with past events, people, or culture.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write 3-4 points of difference between the following.
questions.text: Difference between a hill fort and a sea fort.
questions.answer: A hill fort is built on a hill or mountain for natural protection, e.g., Shivneri Fort. A sea fort is surrounded by water and built in the sea, e.g., Sindhudurg Fort. Hill forts are accessed by land paths or ropes, while sea forts require boats. Sea forts often have fresh water wells inside despite being in saline surroundings.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write 3-4 points of difference between the following.
questions.text: Difference between a temple and a museum as historical places.
questions.answer: A temple is a place of worship dedicated to a deity, often with religious rituals, e.g., Lord Shri Ram temple at Ramtek. A museum preserves and displays objects of historical, cultural, or scientific value, e.g., Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Museum. Temples are primarily for prayer, while museums are for learning and education. Both can be heritage sites but serve different purposes.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain why we should not write our names or litter at historical places.
questions.answer: Writing names or littering at historical places damages their beauty and historical value. Such actions show disrespect to our cultural heritage. These places are preserved for everyone to learn from and enjoy. If we damage them, future generations will lose the chance to see and understand our past. Therefore, we must keep them clean and treat them with care.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain how visiting historical places helps us learn about our culture and history.
questions.answer: Visiting historical places allows us to see real evidence of the past, like forts, temples, and museums. We can learn about the lives, bravery, and ideas of people who lived before us. For example, visiting Shivneri Fort teaches us about Shivaji Maharaj’s birth and early life. Seeing Phule Wada helps us understand the struggle for education and equality. Such visits make history alive and inspire us to be better citizens.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Write about the 'Earn and Learn' scheme started by Karmaveer Bhaurao Patil.
questions.answer: Karmaveer Bhaurao Patil started the 'Earn and Learn' scheme so that poor students could work and study at the same time. He also started hostels for students. This helped students from all castes and religions to get education.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why did Shanti Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury decide to attack Stevens?
questions.answer: Stevens was a British officer who beat and hurt Indians who protested. The girls decided to teach him a lesson for his violent acts. They learned to use a pistol and fired at him when he came out of his house.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why did Shirishkumar organize a protest against the British rule?
questions.answer: Shirishkumar organized a protest because the British treated Indians unfairly and exploited them. He wanted to join the Quit India Movement and fight for India's freedom. He believed in standing up against injustice, even at a young age.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why is 26th November celebrated as Constitution Day?
questions.answer: 26th November is celebrated as Constitution Day because the final draft of the Constitution of India was presented on this day in 1949. It honors the work of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar and the Drafting Committee. The Constitution came into force two months later, on 26th January 1950.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Write a short paragraph on the life and contribution of Babu Genu Said.
questions.answer: Babu Genu Said was a young man from Mahalunge in Pune district who worked in a textile mill in Mumbai. In 1930, during the boycott of foreign goods, he actively participated in protests. He laid down in front of a truck carrying foreign goods, holding the Tiranga, to stop it. The driver ran the truck over him, and he sacrificed his life for the nation. His bravery inspired many to join the freedom struggle. He is remembered as a martyr who gave his life for India’s independence.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Describe the story of Shirishkumar and his friends in Nandurbar during the Quit India Movement.
questions.answer: In 1942, during the Quit India Movement, Shirishkumar, a 16-year-old student from Nandurbar, organized a protest with his friends Shashidhar, Laldas, Ghanshyam, and Dhansukhlal. They led a peaceful rally through Jhanda Chowk. When the police ordered them to stop, they refused. The police opened fire on 9th September 1942, and all five students were martyred. Their courage inspired many others to join the freedom struggle. They are remembered as young heroes who gave their lives for India’s independence.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: What is a revolution?
questions.answer: A revolution is a strong effort by people to bring about a big change, especially to remove unfair rule and gain freedom.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: What is patriotism?
questions.answer: Patriotism is love and devotion for one's country and a willingness to work for its good.

questions.instruction: Write 3-4 points of difference between the following.
questions.text: Difference between the contributions of Karmaveer Bhaurao Patil and Babu Genu Said.
questions.answer: Karmaveer Bhaurao Patil worked for education by starting schools, hostels, and the 'Earn and Learn' scheme to help poor students. Babu Genu Said fought against foreign goods by sacrificing his life in a protest. Patil’s work was long-term and social, while Genu’s was a direct act of protest. Both contributed to nation-building in different ways.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write 3-4 points of difference between the following.
questions.text: Difference between the Quit India Movement and the protest by Babu Genu Said.
questions.answer: The Quit India Movement was a nationwide protest started by Gandhi in 1942 asking the British to leave India. Babu Genu Said’s protest was a local act in 1930 against foreign goods in Mumbai. The Quit India Movement involved lakhs of people, while Genu’s act was individual. Both were part of the freedom struggle but differed in scale and time.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain how Shanti Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury showed courage in their fight against the British.
questions.answer: Shanti Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury were inspired by Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose’s speech and joined the revolutionary group Yugantar. They learned to use a pistol despite being young schoolgirls. They bravely went to the house of the cruel British officer Stevens in Comilla. When he came out, they confronted him and Suniti fired at him, collapsing him on the spot. Though they were caught and sentenced to life imprisonment, their act inspired many to resist injustice.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain the importance of the 'Earn and Learn' scheme started by Karmaveer Bhaurao Patil.
questions.answer: The 'Earn and Learn' scheme helped poor students earn money while studying, so they did not have to drop out due to financial problems. It promoted dignity of labor and self-reliance among students. The scheme was started in hostels run by Rayat Shikshan Sanstha. It allowed students from all castes and religions to study together. This scheme is still used in many educational institutions today and has helped thousands of students get education.

questions.text: What are two things we should do to keep our surroundings clean?
questions.answer: We should throw garbage in the proper place and manage drainage water properly. We should also keep our homes and public places clean.

questions.text: Why did people in the Chipko Movement hug trees?
questions.answer: People hugged trees to protect them from being cut down. They wanted to save the forests and the environment.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: What are two benefits of planting trees mentioned in the lesson?
questions.answer: Trees give us fruits, vegetables, medicines and wood. They also prevent soil erosion and help store rainwater in the soil.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why should we stop cutting trees?
questions.answer: We should stop cutting trees because they give us oxygen, fruits, medicines, and wood. They prevent soil erosion, reduce pollution, and provide shelter to birds and animals. Cutting trees harms the environment and disrupts nature’s balance.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why is personal cleanliness important for everyone?
questions.answer: Personal cleanliness keeps us healthy and prevents diseases from spreading. It makes us feel fresh and active. When everyone stays clean, our surroundings also remain clean and pleasant.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph (6-10 lines) on:
questions.text: How can students keep their school clean?
questions.answer: Students can keep their school clean by throwing waste in dustbins, not littering in classrooms or playgrounds, and keeping their desks tidy. They should wash hands before meals and after using the toilet. Students can help in cleaning the blackboard, arranging books, and watering plants. They should avoid scribbling on walls or desks. Taking part in cleanliness drives and encouraging friends to keep the school clean also helps. A clean school keeps everyone healthy and happy.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph (6-10 lines) on:
questions.text: Why is tree plantation important for our environment?
questions.answer: Tree plantation is important because trees give us oxygen to breathe and absorb harmful carbon dioxide. They prevent soil erosion by holding soil with their roots. Trees provide shade, fruits, medicines, and wood for our use. They give shelter to birds, insects, and animals. Trees also help in bringing rain and reducing heat in cities. Planting more trees makes our environment fresh, green, and healthy for all living beings.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Cleanliness
questions.answer: Cleanliness means keeping our body, clothes, home, and surroundings free from dirt, germs, and waste to stay healthy and prevent diseases.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Tree plantation
questions.answer: Tree plantation means planting new saplings and taking care of them so they grow into healthy trees.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Personal cleanliness and environmental cleanliness
questions.answer: Personal cleanliness means keeping our body, clothes, and hands clean to stay healthy. Environmental cleanliness means keeping our surroundings like homes, schools, streets, and parks free from garbage and pollution. Personal cleanliness prevents diseases in individuals, while environmental cleanliness keeps the whole community healthy. Both are important and should be practiced together.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Natural things and man-made things
questions.answer: Natural things are found in nature like trees, rivers, animals, and air. Man-made things are created by humans like plastic, buildings, cars, and toys. Natural things grow or exist without human help, while man-made things need human effort to make. Natural things are usually biodegradable, but many man-made things like plastic harm the environment.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: How do trees help in reducing pollution?
questions.answer: Trees absorb harmful gases like carbon dioxide and release oxygen, which makes the air fresher. They trap dust and smoke particles on their leaves, keeping the air clean. Trees also reduce noise pollution by acting as sound barriers. By providing shade, they lower the temperature in cities, reducing the need for coolers that cause pollution. In this way, trees help keep our environment clean and healthy.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why is it everyone’s responsibility to keep the environment clean?
questions.answer: Everyone produces waste, so everyone must help in keeping the environment clean. If only a few people clean, garbage will still pile up and cause diseases. A clean environment keeps all living beings healthy and happy. When each person does their part, like using dustbins and saving water, the surroundings stay clean for all. Thus, protecting the environment is a shared duty of every citizen.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Describe the Indian National Flag in short.
questions.answer: The Indian National Flag is a horizontal tricolour of saffron at the top, white in the middle, and green at the bottom. In the centre of the white band is a navy blue wheel with 24 spokes, called the Ashoka Chakra. It symbolizes courage, peace, prosperity, and the eternal law.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: How can students show respect for national symbols?
questions.answer: Students can show respect by standing still during the national anthem, not damaging the flag, hoisting it properly on national days, and singing patriotic songs with sincerity. They should also learn about the meaning behind each symbol.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why is diversity important in India?
questions.answer: Diversity makes India rich in languages, cultures, festivals, and traditions. It teaches us to live in harmony and learn from each other. Despite differences, unity in diversity makes our country strong and unique.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why do we celebrate Republic Day on 26 January?
questions.answer: We celebrate Republic Day on 26 January because on this day in 1950, the Constitution of India came into effect. It marked the day India became a sovereign democratic republic. The day is celebrated to honour the Constitution and the values of justice, liberty, and equality.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why is national unity important for a country like India?
questions.answer: National unity is important because India has many languages, religions, and cultures. Unity helps people live peacefully together despite differences. It strengthens the country and helps in progress and development.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Write about the importance of national festivals in promoting national unity.
questions.answer: National festivals like Independence Day and Republic Day remind us of our shared history and values. They bring people from all over the country together in celebration. Hoisting the flag, singing the national anthem, and participating in parades create a sense of pride and belonging. These festivals help us forget our differences and remember that we are all Indians. They teach children about patriotism and the sacrifices made for freedom. Celebrating them strengthens the bond of unity among all citizens.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: How can students contribute to national unity in their daily life?
questions.answer: Students can contribute to national unity by respecting classmates from different backgrounds and treating everyone equally. They can learn about various cultures, languages, and festivals celebrated in India. Sharing food, stories, and traditions during school activities promotes understanding. Standing up against bullying or discrimination also supports unity. By being kind, helpful, and inclusive, students build harmony in their class and school. Such small actions, when practiced by many, strengthen the spirit of 'unity in diversity' across the nation.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: National integration
questions.answer: National integration means the feeling of unity and togetherness among people of different religions, languages, and cultures living in the same country.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: National symbol
questions.answer: A national symbol is an object, animal, bird, flower, or emblem that represents the identity and values of a nation.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write 3-4 points of difference between the following.
questions.text: Independence Day and Republic Day
questions.answer: Independence Day is celebrated on 15 August to mark freedom from British rule in 1947. Republic Day is celebrated on 26 January to mark the coming into effect of the Indian Constitution in 1950. On Independence Day, the Prime Minister hoists the flag at Red Fort. On Republic Day, the President hoists the flag and a grand parade is held at Rajpath.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write 3-4 points of difference between the following.
questions.text: National flag and State flag
questions.answer: The national flag represents the entire country and is the same all over India. A state flag represents a particular state and may vary from state to state. The national flag has saffron, white, green with Ashoka Chakra. State flags may have different colours, symbols, or emblems based on state culture.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Explain how the story of the sparrows and the hunter teaches us about unity.
questions.answer: The story shows that when the sparrows were trapped in the net, they could not escape individually. But when they united and worked together by holding the net with their beaks, they flew away safely. This teaches us that unity gives strength which we do not have alone. Just like the sparrows, people in a nation can overcome difficulties when they stand together. The hunter could not catch them because of their collective effort. Hence, unity is power.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why are national symbols important for a country?
questions.answer: National symbols represent the identity, pride, and values of a country. They help people feel connected to their nation and foster a sense of belonging. Symbols like the flag, anthem, and emblem are used during important events to show respect and unity. They remind citizens of their shared history and responsibilities. Seeing or hearing these symbols evokes patriotism and encourages people to work for the country's welfare.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: What are two things you should do if you experience inappropriate touch, according to the text?

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why is unity important in achieving success, as shown in the chapter?
questions.answer: Unity is important because when people work together, they can accomplish difficult tasks more easily and quickly. The sparrows were freed only because the mouse and his friends helped together. Similarly, the Blind Women’s Cricket Team won through teamwork. This shows that collective effort leads to success and pride.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Why should you not keep quiet if someone touches you inappropriately?
questions.answer: You should not keep quiet because speaking up helps stop the wrongdoing and protects you and others. Telling a trusted adult or using the POCSO e-box ensures action is taken. Staying silent may allow the harm to continue.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Write a short story based on the picture of two swans and a tortoise holding a stick in their beaks, as seen at the Khidreshwar Temple.
questions.answer: Once, two swans and a tortoise wanted to cross a dry field to reach a pond. They found a stick and decided to carry it together. The swans held the stick in their beaks, and the tortoise held it in its mouth. As they walked, they talked and encouraged each other. Though the journey was long, their teamwork made it easy. When they reached the pond, they were happy and thanked each other for their help.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Describe how teamwork helps in school activities, giving examples from your experience.
questions.answer: Teamwork in school makes learning fun and effective. For example, during group projects, we divide tasks like research, drawing, and presentation, which helps us finish faster and learn from each other. In sports, passing the ball and supporting teammates leads to better performance. When we help a classmate who is struggling, we create a kind and strong class. Just like the sparrows and the mouse, working together helps us overcome challenges and achieve success.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: Unity
questions.answer: Unity means working together as a team with cooperation and mutual support to achieve a common goal.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: POCSO e-box
questions.answer: POCSO e-box is an online platform to report cases of inappropriate touch or child abuse, managed by the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write 3-4 points of difference between the following.
questions.text: Difference between working alone and working together.
questions.answer: Working alone means doing a task by oneself, which may take longer and be harder. Working together involves sharing ideas and efforts, making the task easier and faster. In a team, members support each other, while working alone lacks such support. Teamwork builds unity and pride, whereas working alone may lead to frustration.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: Write 3-4 points of difference between the following.
questions.text: Difference between appropriate and inappropriate touch.
questions.answer: Appropriate touch is safe, respectful, and makes you feel comfortable, like a hug from a parent. Inappropriate touch makes you feel uneasy, scared, or confused and is often done in private. Appropriate touch is given with consent, while inappropriate touch is forced or unwanted. One is healthy and caring, the other is harmful and wrong.

questions.answer: The sparrows were trapped in a net and could not free themselves alone. The mouse and his friends came together and used their teeth to chew the net. Hence, unity gives strength to overcome challenges.

questions.text: Explain why the achievements of the Indian Blind Women’s Cricket Team are a matter of national pride.
questions.answer: The Indian Blind Women’s Cricket Team won international championships in 2025, showing excellence in sports. Their success is special because they achieved it despite visual challenges, proving determination and skill. This victory brings honor to the country and inspires others, especially differently-abled individuals. It highlights the power of teamwork and practice. Such achievements make the nation proud and promote inclusivity in sports.

questions.answer: चूक

questions.instruction: खालील कथनांची सत्यता तपासा व बरोबर/चूक लिहा.
questions.text: शाळेत शिक्षक-विद्यार्थीचे नाते आदरावर आधारित असते.
questions.answer: बरोबर

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: खालील कथनांची सत्यता तपासा व बरोबर/चूक लिहा.
questions.text: शाळेचा वार्षिक क्रीडास्पर्धा फक्त धावण्याची स्पर्धा असते.
questions.answer: चूक

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: खालील बऱ्यांची जोडा लावा.
questions.answer: शाळेचा गणवेश – ओळख व एकता, शिक्षक – विद्यार्थ्यांना ज्ञान देणे, क्रीडा स्पर्धा – शरीरिक वायायाम, शाळेत मैत्री – एकमेकांची काळजी

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: शाळेत आपण काय शिकतो?
questions.answer: विषय ज्ञान आणि सामाजिक मूल्ये

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: शाळेत एकमेकांशी मदत करणे काय विकास करते?
questions.answer: मैत्री

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: शाळेचा गणवेश विद्यार्थ्यांमध्ये काय भावना निर्माण करते?
questions.answer: एकता

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: खालील पर्यायांमधील विसमष्टी शोधा व कारण सांगा.
questions.text: शाळेत पाठ्यपुस्तक, डस्टर, पायाभात, घंटा
questions.answer: पायाभात - हे शाळेत वापरले जाणारे साधन नाहीत, शेतीसाठी वापरले जाते.

questions.subject: EVS
questions.instruction: खालील पर्यायांमधील विसमष्टी शोधा व कारण सांगा.
questions.text: शिक्षक, विद्यार्थी, पालक, डॉक्टर
questions.answer: डॉक्टर - हे शाळेतचे नियमित सदस्य नाहीत, इतर त्रय शाळेतच संबंधित आहेत.

questions.subject: EVS

questions.answer: मित्र

questions.subject: EVS

questions.answer: शिस्त

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: शाळेत वेगवेगळ्या कुटुंबांमधील मुले-मुली एकत्र येतात ते दर्शवते?
questions.answer: एकता

questions.subject: EVS
questions.text: शाळेत शिक्षक आपल्याला काय शिकवतो?
questions.answer: विषय
