questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: पुस्तक वाचण्यामुळे शब्दसंपत्ती वाढणे कसे होतो?
questions.answer: पुस्तक नियमितपणे वाचल्यामुळे नवीन शब्द शिकवतात, ज्यामुळे शब्दसंपत्तीत वाढ होऊन भाषेवर प्रभुत्व मिळतो.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: कवितेत सांगितलेले दोन फायदे पुस्तक वाचण्याचे लिहा.
questions.answer: पुस्तक वाचण्यामुळे ज्ञान मिळतो आणि वाचन आनंद मिळतो. त्यामुळे मनामनात गोष्टी साठवली जाऊ शकते.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: घराघरांमध्ये ग्रंथ मंदिर उभारवणे कसे करावे?
questions.answer: घराघरांमध्ये पुस्तके जमा करून वाचण्याची शिकव देऊन, त्यातील प्रगतीचा दीप प्रज्वलित करून ग्रंथ मंदिर उभारवावे.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: पुस्तक वाचणे एक चांगली सवय का?
questions.answer: पुस्तक वाचणे एक चांगली सवय आहे कारण ते ज्ञान वाढवते, शब्दसंपत्ती समृद्ध करतो, आणि एकाग्रता व कल्पनाशक्ती विकसित करते. त्यामुळे बोलणे-लेखन प्रभावी होतात आणि जीवन आनंददायी होतो.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: ग्रंथ मंदिर उभारवणे आवश्यक का?
questions.answer: ग्रंथ मंदिर उभारवणे आवश्यक आहे कारण ते घरघरात वाचण्याची संस्कृति तयार करते, मुलांना ज्ञानमार्ग दर्शवितात, आणि त्यामुळे सामाजिक प्रगती होऊ शकते. दीप प्रज्वलित करणे म्हणजे ज्ञानाचा प्रकाश फैलवणे.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: पुस्तक वाचण्याचे महत्त्व सांगा व त्यामुळे होऊ शकलेले फायदे लिहा.
questions.answer: पुस्तक वाचणे ज्ञानाची मुख्य स्त्रोत आहे. ते शब्दसंपत्ती वाढवते, भाषेची दक्षता वाढवते, आणि एकाग्रता व कल्पनाशक्ती विकसित करते. वाचनामुळे विविध विषयांचे सखोल ज्ञान मिळतो, जे जीवनात उपयुक्त साबत होते. कथा, कादंबऱ्या व चरित्रे वाचून आदर्श व्यक्तींचे गुण शिकवले जातात. नियमित वाचनेने मानसिक शांती व आनंद मिळतो. त्यामुळे जीवन समृद्ध, सुजाण व आनंददायी होतो. वाचन हा जीवनसाठी अनमोल सवय आहे.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: कवितेच्या संदर्भात 'ग्रंथ मंदिर' अवधारणा स्पष्ट करा.
questions.answer: कवितेत 'ग्रंथ मंदिर' म्हणजे घरघरात पुस्तकांचे संग्रह करून वाचण्याचा वातावरण तयार करणे. यामुळे मुलांना पुस्तकांचे सुलभ उपलब्ध होतो आणि त्यातील ज्ञानाचा उपयोग करू शकते. मंदिरासारखे ही जगह शांत, पवित्र व ज्ञानमय असावी. त्यातील प्रगतीचा दीप प्रज्वलित करणे म्हणजे प्रत्येक बालकाच्या ज्ञानाचा ज्वाला जागृत करणे. यामुळे वाचनाची आदत पाळली जाते आणि सामाजिक विकास होतो.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: कवितेत 'पंख नवे देऊ' वाक्याने काय सांगितले आहे?
questions.answer: कवितेत 'पंख नवे देऊ' वाक्याने सांगितले आहे की पुस्तक वाचण्यामुळे मुलांना ज्ञानाचे पंख मिळतात, ज्यामुळे ते उंचींची ओर उडू शकतात. हे पंख वास्तविक नाहीत, परंतु ज्ञानाने प्रेरणा, आत्मविश्वास व क्षमता मिळवते. त्यामुळे बालक अपने लक्ष्यांना साधू शकते. हे रूपक द्वारा ज्ञानाची शक्ति दर्शविली आहे.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: कवितेत 'दीप प्रज्वलित करू' वाक्याचा अर्थ काय?
questions.answer: कवितेत 'दीप प्रज्वलित करू' म्हणजे प्रत्येक घरात ज्ञानाचा दीप, अर्थात वाचनाची ज्वाला जागृत करणे. दीप म्हणजे ज्ञानाचा प्रकाश, जो अंधेर दूर करतो. त्यामुळे प्रत्येक बालकाच्या मनात जिज्ञासा व ज्ञानाची इच्छा जागृत होऊ शकते. यामुळे पीढी दर पीढी वाचनाची परंपरा पाळली जाते. यामुळे सामाजिक विकास होतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe the difference between a cube and a cuboid based on their faces.
questions.answer: A cube has all six faces as equal squares, while a cuboid has six rectangular faces where opposite faces are equal. All edges of a cube are equal, but in a cuboid, length, breadth, and height can be different.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain why a ball rolls easily but a box does not.
questions.answer: A ball is spherical with a smooth curved surface, allowing it to roll smoothly in any direction. A box, usually cuboid-shaped, has flat faces and sharp edges, which prevent smooth rolling and cause it to slide or topple.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: What is a net? Give one example of a net of a 3D shape.
questions.answer: A net is a two-dimensional outline that can be folded to form a three-dimensional shape. For example, the net of a cube consists of six connected squares arranged in a cross shape.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why does a cone have only one vertex?
questions.answer: A cone has only one vertex because it tapers smoothly from a flat circular base to a single point at the top. This pointed top is where all the curved surface meets, forming one vertex.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is a sphere said to have no edges?
questions.answer: A sphere has no edges because it is a perfectly round shape with a continuous curved surface and no straight lines or boundaries where surfaces meet.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe the shapes you can see in your classroom. Name at least five objects and their corresponding 3D shapes.
questions.answer: In my classroom, I see many objects of different shapes. The blackboard is rectangular, so it is like a cuboid. The dustbin is round and tall, shaped like a cylinder. The football is spherical in shape. The dice used in games are cubes. The ice cream cone held by students is cone-shaped. The water bottles are cylindrical. The chalk box is also a cuboid. These shapes help us recognize geometry in everyday life.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain how nets help us understand 3D shapes. Use the example of a cuboid to explain your answer.
questions.answer: Nets are flat layouts of 3D shapes that show all faces connected in a way that they can be folded to form the solid. For a cuboid, the net consists of six rectangles arranged in a specific pattern — usually four in a row for the sides, with one attached to the top and one to the bottom. By folding along the edges and taping the sides, we can reconstruct the cuboid. This helps us visualize how 2D surfaces form 3D objects and understand properties like number of faces, edges, and vertices.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: A cuboid box has a length of 10 cm, breadth of 6 cm, and height of 4 cm. How many cubes of 2 cm side can fit inside it without leaving any space?
questions.answer: Volume of cuboid = 10 × 6 × 4 = 240 cm³ Volume of one small cube = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 cm³ Number of cubes = 240 ÷ 8 = 30 Therefore, 30 cubes of 2 cm side can fit inside the cuboid.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: A teacher has 5 cube-shaped blocks, 3 cuboid-shaped blocks, and 2 cylinder-shaped blocks. If each cube has 6 faces, each cuboid has 6 faces, and each cylinder has 3 faces (2 flat + 1 curved), what is the total number of faces of all blocks combined?
questions.answer: Faces from cubes = 5 × 6 = 30 Faces from cuboids = 3 × 6 = 18 Faces from cylinders = 2 × 3 = 6 Total faces = 30 + 18 + 6 = 54 Therefore, the total number of faces is 54.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: A net of a cube is made of 6 squares. If each square has a side of 3 cm, what is the total surface area of the cube formed?
questions.answer: Area of one square = 3 × 3 = 9 cm² Total surface area = 6 × 9 = 54 cm² Therefore, the surface area of the cube is 54 cm².

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: A cylinder has a height of 10 cm and a circular base of radius 7 cm. Use π = 22/7 to find the area of one circular base.
questions.answer: Area of one circular base = πr² = (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 22 × 7 = 154 cm² Therefore, the area of one base is 154 cm².

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: A cone and a cylinder have the same base radius of 5 cm and same height of 12 cm. Which shape has more volume? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.answer: Volume of cylinder = πr²h = (22/7) × 5 × 5 × 12 = (22/7) × 300 = 942.86 cm³ Volume of cone = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3) × 942.86 = 314.29 cm³ Since 942.86 > 314.29, the cylinder has more volume. Therefore, the cylinder has more volume than the cone.

questions.text: Explain the difference between face value and place value with an example.
questions.answer: Face value of a digit is the digit itself, while place value depends on its position in the number. For example, in the number 462, the face value of 6 is 6, but its place value is 60 because it is in the tens place.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: How do you find the place value of a digit in a number? Explain with an example.
questions.answer: To find the place value, multiply the digit by the value of its position (units, tens, hundreds). For example, in 583, the place value of 8 is 8 × 10 = 80 because it is in the tens place.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the place value of 0 always zero in any number?
questions.answer: Because zero means no value, and multiplying zero by any place value (like 10, 100) still gives zero. So, the place value of 0 is always 0.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the face value of 5 the same in the numbers 523, 253, and 325?
questions.answer: The face value of a digit is always the digit itself, regardless of its position in the number. Hence, in all three numbers, the face value of 5 remains 5.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the place value of 7 in 470 equal to 70?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain how to write a number in expanded form. Use the number 509 as an example.
questions.answer: To write a number in expanded form, break it down according to the place value of each digit. For 509: the digit 5 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 500; the digit 0 is in the tens place, so its value is 0; the digit 9 is in the units place, so its value is 9. Therefore, the expanded form of 509 is 500 + 0 + 9. This shows the value of each digit based on its position.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: How do you compare two three-digit numbers to find which is greater? Explain with an example.
questions.answer: To compare two three-digit numbers, first compare the hundreds place. If they are different, the number with the larger hundreds digit is greater. If the hundreds are equal, compare the tens place. If tens are also equal, compare the units place. For example, to compare 472 and 489: hundreds are both 4 (equal), so compare tens: 7 < 8, so 472 < 489. Hence, 489 is greater.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Give reason for your answer in 3-4 sentences.
questions.text: Why is it important to start addition from the units place?
questions.answer: We start from the units place because addition is done place by place, and any carry from the units affects the tens place. Starting from units ensures correct place value alignment. If we start from hundreds, we might miss the carry from lower places, leading to errors.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Give reason for your answer in 3-4 sentences.
questions.text: Explain why subtracting a number from itself always gives zero.
questions.answer: When a number is subtracted from itself, we are taking away the entire amount, leaving nothing. For example, 5 - 5 means we have 5 and remove all 5, so 0 remains. This is true for any number because the quantity taken away equals the quantity present.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe how number bonds help in understanding addition and subtraction. Give examples.
questions.answer: Number bonds show how a number can be split into two parts that add up to it. For example, 10 can be split as 7 and 3, or 6 and 4. This helps children see that addition and subtraction are related: if 7 + 3 = 10, then 10 - 3 = 7 and 10 - 7 = 3. Using number bonds builds mental math skills and makes it easier to solve problems like 8 + 5 by thinking of 8 + 2 + 3 = 10 + 3 = 13. They also help in understanding missing number problems.

questions.text: Explain the process of subtraction with borrowing using the example 507 - 268.
questions.answer: In 507 - 268, we start from units: 7 - 8 is not possible, so we borrow from tens. But tens is 0, so we borrow from hundreds: 5 hundreds become 4 hundreds and 10 tens. Now tens become 10, we borrow 1 ten for units: 10 tens become 9 tens and units become 17. Now 17 - 8 = 9 units. Tens: 9 - 6 = 3 tens. Hundreds: 4 - 2 = 2 hundreds. So the answer is 239. Borrowing ensures we can subtract when the top digit is smaller.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: There were 381 books in a library. Subash donated 51 books to the library. How many books are there in the library now?
questions.answer: Step 1: Write the numbers in column form: 381 + 51 ----- Step 2: Add units: 1 + 1 = 2 Step 3: Add tens: 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 and carry 1 to hundreds Step 4: Add hundreds: 3 + 0 + 1 (carry) = 4 Step 5: Result is 432 Therefore, the library now has 432 books.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: In a farm there are 478 mango trees and 256 chikoo trees. How many trees are there in total?
questions.answer: Step 1: Arrange in columns: 478 + 256 ----- Step 2: Units: 8 + 6 = 14, write 4, carry 1 Step 3: Tens: 7 + 5 + 1 (carry) = 13, write 3, carry 1 Step 4: Hundreds: 4 + 2 + 1 (carry) = 7 Step 5: Result is 734 Total trees = 734

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.answer: Step 1: Column addition: 628 + 357 ----- Step 2: Units: 8 + 7 = 15, write 5, carry 1 Step 3: Tens: 2 + 5 + 1 = 8, write 8 Step 4: Hundreds: 6 + 3 = 9, write 9 Step 5: Result is 985 Answer: 985

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.answer: Step 1: Column subtraction: 507 - 268 ----- Step 2: Units: 7 < 8, so borrow from tens. But tens is 0, so borrow from hundreds. Hundreds: 5 becomes 4, tens become 10. Now borrow from tens: tens 10 becomes 9, units become 17. Units: 17 - 8 = 9 Step 3: Tens: 9 - 6 = 3 Step 4: Hundreds: 4 - 2 = 2 Step 5: Result is 239 Answer: 239

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: Sayali has 500 rupees. She bought books worth 375 rupees. How much money is left with her?
questions.answer: Step 1: Subtraction: 500 - 375 ----- Step 2: Units: 0 < 5, borrow from tens. Tens is 0, so borrow from hundreds. Hundreds: 5 becomes 4, tens become 10. Borrow from tens: tens 10 becomes 9, units become 10. Units: 10 - 5 = 5 Step 3: Tens: 9 - 7 = 2 Step 4: Hundreds: 4 - 3 = 1 Step 5: Result is 125 Money left = 125 rupees

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Differentiate between proper and improper fractions with one example each.
questions.answer: A proper fraction has numerator less than denominator, e.g., 2/3. An improper fraction has numerator greater than or equal to denominator, e.g., 5/4 or 4/4.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain with examples how fractions are used in daily life. Give at least three examples.
questions.answer: Fractions are used in cooking (e.g., half a cup of sugar), telling time (quarter past 3), and sharing food (dividing pizza into four equal parts). They help us measure parts of a whole accurately. For instance, if a ribbon is cut into 3 equal parts and 2 parts are used, we say 2/3 of the ribbon is used. Fractions also help in understanding discounts, like half-price sale.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe how to teach the concept of equivalent fractions using paper folding. Mention the steps and what students learn.
questions.answer: Take a sheet of paper and fold it into two equal parts; shade one part to show 1/2. Fold the same paper again into two more parts (now four parts); the shaded area now shows 2/4. Students see that 1/2 and 2/4 cover the same area, so they are equivalent. Repeat with more folds to show 3/6, etc. This activity helps students understand that different fractions can represent the same quantity.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe how a weighing balance works to compare the weight of two objects.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why do we need standard units for measuring length and weight?
questions.answer: We need standard units so that everyone gets the same measurement for the same object, regardless of who measures it or where it is measured. This ensures consistency and fairness in trade, education, and daily life.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the weight of an object the same even if measured by different people using the same standard weights?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe the activity of measuring the length of a rope to make metre, half metre, and quarter metre ropes. Explain how you would use them to compare the length of objects.

Use these ropes as guides: place the object next to the metre rope to see if it is longer or shorter than one metre. Repeat with half and quarter metre ropes to estimate length in fractions. This helps in understanding length comparison without a scale.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain the activity of weighing a notebook using marbles. Discuss why different students might get different counts and what this teaches about measurement.
questions.answer: Place the notebook on one pan of the balance and add marbles to the other pan until both sides are level. Count the marbles used. Different students may get different counts if their marbles vary in size, weight, or material. This shows that non-standard units like marbles give inconsistent results. It teaches the need for standard units like grams and kilograms for accurate and reliable measurement.

questions.answer: First fold: 1 metre ÷ 2 = 0.5 metre = half metre Take one half metre rope and fold it into two equal parts: 0.5 metre ÷ 2 = 0.25 metre Convert to centimetres: 0.25 × 100 = 25 centimetres So, the smallest piece is a quarter metre rope, which is 25 centimetres long.

Actual verification: Place the pencil next to the quarter metre rope. If the pencil ends before the rope does, it is shorter. In most cases, the pencil will be shorter than 25 cm. questions.text: Describe how tally marks are drawn and why a gap is left after every five marks.
questions.answer: Tally marks are drawn as four vertical lines and a diagonal line across them to make a group of five. A gap is left after every five to make counting easier and to avoid confusion when reading large numbers.

questions.answer: By dividing the picture into columns and rows labelled with letters and numbers, we can name the exact box where the fruit is located. For example, if an apple is in the second column and third row, its position is B-3. This makes it easy to describe and find objects.

questions.answer: The top view shows the layout of the table as seen from above, which helps in placing it correctly on a map. questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why do we use different colours for different symbols on a map?
questions.answer: Using different colours makes the map easier to read and understand. It helps distinguish between features like water (blue), green areas (green), and buildings (grey or red). This visual difference allows quick identification of symbols.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain why the product of any number and zero is zero.
questions.answer: When we multiply a number by zero, it means we are adding zero to itself that many times. Since adding zero any number of times always gives zero, the product is zero. For example, 5 × 0 = 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 0.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: What is the product of 9 and 6? How can you verify it using addition?
questions.answer: The product of 9 and 6 is 54. We can verify it by adding 9 six times: 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 = 54, or by adding 6 nine times: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 54.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the product of 3 and 4 the same as the product of 4 and 3?
questions.answer: The product of 3 and 4 is the same as the product of 4 and 3 because multiplication is commutative. This means changing the order of the numbers does not change the product. Both 3 × 4 and 4 × 3 equal 12.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why does multiplying any number by 1 give the same number?
questions.answer: Multiplying any number by 1 means taking one group of that number. So, the product is the number itself. For example, 7 × 1 = 7 because one group of 7 is 7.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain the terms multiplicand, multiplier, and product with an example from daily life.
questions.answer: In multiplication, the multiplicand is the number that is multiplied, the multiplier is the number by which we multiply, and the product is the answer. For example, if there are 6 boxes and each box has 4 pencils, then 6 is the multiplicand (number of boxes), 4 is the multiplier (pencils per box), and the product is 6 × 4 = 24 pencils in total. This helps us find the total when we have equal groups.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe how multiplication is used in real-life situations with two examples.
questions.answer: Multiplication is used in daily life to find totals when things are in equal groups. For example, if a box contains 10 laddus and there are 5 such boxes, we multiply 10 × 5 = 50 to find the total laddus. Another example: if each student gets 3 notebooks and there are 20 students, we multiply 3 × 20 = 60 to find the total notebooks needed. Multiplication makes repeated addition easier and faster.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe the steps to divide 84 by 7 using the vertical method.
questions.answer: First, see how many times 7 goes into 8 (the first digit of 84), which is 1 time. Write 1 in the quotient. Multiply 7×1=7, subtract from 8 to get 1. Bring down the 4 to make 14. Then, 7 goes into 14 exactly 2 times. Write 2 in the quotient. Multiply 7×2=14, subtract to get 0. The quotient is 12 and remainder is 0.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the remainder always less than the divisor in a division problem?
questions.answer: The remainder is always less than the divisor because if it were equal to or greater than the divisor, we could form one more complete group. For example, if dividing by 5 and remainder is 5 or more, we could give one more item to each group, reducing the remainder. Hence, remainder must be less than divisor.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why do we write a zero in the quotient when the dividend digit is smaller than the divisor during long division?
questions.answer: We write a zero in the quotient when the current dividend digit is smaller than the divisor because it means we cannot form even one group from that digit. This zero holds the place value (like tens or hundreds) so that the next digit can be brought down correctly to continue the division process.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain how division is used in daily life with two different examples from the chapter or your experience.
questions.answer: Division helps us share things equally in daily life. For example, if a mother has 20 biscuits and 4 children, she divides 20 by 4 to give each child 5 biscuits. Another example is when a teacher distributes 30 worksheets among 5 groups, each group gets 30 ÷ 5 = 6 worksheets. Division also helps in grouping, like packing 50 books into boxes of 10, needing 5 boxes. It ensures fairness and avoids waste by distributing items evenly.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe the process of long division with an example, showing how to divide 75 by 5 step by step.
questions.answer: To divide 75 by 5 using long division, first consider how many times 5 goes into 7 (the tens digit). It goes 1 time, so write 1 in the tens place of the quotient. Multiply 5×1=5, subtract from 7 to get 2. Bring down the 5 (units digit) to make 25. Now, see how many times 5 goes into 25 — it goes 5 times. Write 5 in the units place of the quotient. Multiply 5×5=25, subtract to get 0. The quotient is 15 and remainder is 0. This shows each of 5 people gets 15 rupees if 75 is shared equally.

questions.answer: To check symmetry, fold the shape along a line. If both halves match exactly, the shape is symmetrical and that line is the axis of symmetry. If they do not match, the shape is not symmetrical along that line.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe two real-life examples where symmetry is used.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why does a square have more lines of symmetry than a rectangle?
questions.answer: A square has all sides equal and all angles equal, so it can be folded along its vertical, horizontal, and both diagonal lines to get matching halves. A rectangle only has equal opposite sides, so only vertical and horizontal folds produce matching halves, not the diagonals.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the letter 'Z' not symmetrical?
questions.answer: The letter 'Z' does not have any line — vertical, horizontal, or diagonal — that divides it into two identical halves. When folded along any line, the two parts do not match, so it is asymmetrical.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Explain the concept of symmetry with examples from daily life and nature. How is it useful in art and festivals?
questions.answer: Symmetry means that one half of a figure is the mirror image of the other half when divided by a line called the axis of symmetry. In nature, we see symmetry in butterflies, leaves, and flowers. In daily life, symmetry is used in rangoli making during Diwali, in the design of buildings like the Taj Mahal, and in drawing national flags. It makes objects look balanced, beautiful, and harmonious. Artists and architects use symmetry to create pleasing designs. In festivals, symmetrical patterns in kolam, rangoli, and alpana reflect cultural richness and mathematical beauty. Learning symmetry helps us observe patterns and appreciate the order in the world around us.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: How can you create a symmetrical figure using dot paper? Explain with an example.
questions.answer: To create a symmetrical figure on dot paper, first draw a line which will act as the axis of symmetry. Then, draw a shape on one side of the line. For each point you draw, count its distance from the axis and mark a corresponding point on the opposite side at the same distance. Join these points to complete the figure. For example, to make a symmetrical heart, draw half a heart on the left of the vertical line, then mirror each dot to the right side. The completed figure will be symmetrical. This method ensures accuracy and helps understand mirror reflection.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: A rectangular sheet of paper is folded exactly in half along its length. If the original length of the paper is 20 cm and the width is 10 cm, what is the area of one half after folding?
questions.answer: Original area = length × width = 20 cm × 10 cm = 200 cm². When folded in half along the length, the paper is divided into two equal parts. So, area of one half = Total area ÷ 2 = 200 ÷ 2 = 100 cm². Alternatively, after folding, the dimensions of one half are: length = 10 cm (half of 20), width = 10 cm. Area = 10 × 10 = 100 cm². Hence, the area of one half after folding is 100 cm².

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: A square-shaped rangoli has a side length of 8 cm. If it is folded along one of its diagonals, what is the area of one of the symmetrical halves?
questions.answer: Area of square = side² = 8 × 8 = 64 cm². When folded along a diagonal, the square is divided into two congruent right-angled triangles. Each triangle has area = half of square = 64 ÷ 2 = 32 cm². Alternatively, area of triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 8 × 8 = 32 cm². Hence, the area of one symmetrical half is 32 cm².

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: A rectangular photo frame has a length of 16 cm and a breadth of 12 cm. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
questions.answer: A rectangle has lines of symmetry only along the lines that join the midpoints of opposite sides. So, one line is vertical (joining midpoints of the longer sides), and one is horizontal (joining midpoints of the shorter sides). The diagonals of a rectangle do not produce matching halves unless it is a square. Hence, a non-square rectangle has exactly 2 lines of symmetry.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: An equilateral triangle has a side of 6 cm. If it is folded along one of its lines of symmetry, what is the length of the base of the resulting half-triangle?
questions.answer: In an equilateral triangle, a line of symmetry goes from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side. So, when folded along this line, the base of the original triangle (6 cm) is divided into two equal parts. Each half has a base = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm. Hence, the length of the base of the resulting half-triangle is 3 cm.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: A circle is folded along its diameter. If the radius of the circle is 7 cm, what is the area of one of the symmetrical halves?
questions.answer: Area of circle = πr² = (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 154 cm². When folded along a diameter, the circle is divided into two equal semicircles. So, area of one half = Area of circle ÷ 2 = 154 ÷ 2 = 77 cm². Alternatively, area of semicircle = ½ × πr² = ½ × (22/7) × 49 = 77 cm². Hence, the area of one symmetrical half is 77 cm².

questions.text: Differentiate between volume and capacity in your own words.
questions.answer: Volume is the space occupied by an object or substance, while capacity is the amount a container can hold. For example, the volume of water in a jug is how much water is there, but the capacity is how much more it can hold.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why do we say that two half-litres make one litre?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe the position of the hour and minute hands at half past any hour.
questions.answer: At half past any hour, the minute hand points at 6 (30 minutes). The hour hand is exactly halfway between the current hour and the next hour. For example, at half past 5, the hour hand is between 5 and 6.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why do we use terms like 'quarter past' and 'half past' instead of only saying numbers?
questions.answer: We use these terms to tell time more easily and quickly in daily life. They help us communicate time without always saying the exact number of minutes. These phrases are common in speech and clocks.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is 3:45 called 'quarter to 4' and not 'quarter past 3'?
questions.answer: 3:45 is called 'quarter to 4' because it is 15 minutes before 4 o'clock. It is not quarter past 3 because quarter past 3 would be 3:15. The term 'quarter to' is used when approaching the next hour.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain why the hour hand moves slowly compared to the minute hand.
questions.answer: The hour hand moves slowly because it completes one full round in 12 hours, while the minute hand completes one round in 1 hour. This makes the hour hand move 1/12th the speed of the minute hand. Hence, it advances gradually as minutes pass.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe how you would tell the time using an analog clock. Include the roles of the hour hand, minute hand, and common terms like quarter past, half past, and quarter to.
questions.answer: To tell time on an analog clock, first look at the minute hand to determine minutes past the hour. If it is at 3, it is quarter past; at 6, half past; at 9, quarter to. Then look at the hour hand to know which hour it is or approaching. If the hour hand is between two numbers, the hour is the lower number unless the minute hand is past 6. Practice helps in reading time quickly and accurately for daily activities.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the pattern 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 called an odd number pattern?
questions.answer: This pattern is called an odd number pattern because each number in the sequence is an odd number, and they increase by 2 each time, starting from 1.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the pattern △, ○, △, ○, △, ○ considered a repeating pattern?
questions.answer: It is considered a repeating pattern because the sequence of triangle followed by circle occurs again and again in the same order without change.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain the difference between repeating and growing patterns with two examples each.
questions.answer: Repeating patterns have a core that repeats over and over, like AB AB AB or ○ △ ○ △. Growing patterns increase or decrease by a constant amount, like 2, 4, 6, 8 or 10, 20, 30, 40. In repeating patterns, the same set of elements appears again, while in growing patterns, each term changes based on a rule. For example, in the pattern 3, 6, 9, 12, the number increases by 3 each time, showing growth. In contrast, the pattern Red, Blue, Red, Blue repeats the same colours. Both types help us understand sequences and predict what comes next.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe how you can create a pattern using paper folding and cutting, and what kind of pattern you might observe.
questions.answer: Take a rectangular strip of paper, fold it several times, then cut shapes out of the folded edges. When you unfold the paper, you will see a symmetrical pattern repeated across the strip. The pattern depends on the number of folds and the shape of the cut. For example, folding twice and cutting a triangle will produce a pattern of triangles in a line. This activity helps students see how symmetry and repetition create beautiful designs. It also develops spatial awareness and creativity. Such patterns can be used for decoration or to understand mathematical concepts like reflection and repetition.

questions.answer: The pattern increases by 2 each time. 2 + 2 = 4 4 + 2 = 6 6 + 2 = 8 8 + 2 = 10 10 + 2 = 12 12 + 2 = 14 So, the next three numbers are 10, 12, 14.

questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: Complete the pattern: A, AA, AAA, _______, _______, _______.
questions.answer: Each term adds one more 'A'. A has 1 A AA has 2 A AAA has 3 A So next: AAAA (4 A), AAAAA (5 A), AAAAAA (6 A) Thus, the next three terms are: AAAA, AAAAA, AAAAAA.

questions.answer: १०० पासून ११0 पर्यंतच्या संख्यांतील शतक स्थानातील अंक १ आहे, त्यामुळे त्याची स्थानिक किंमत १०० आणि दर्शनी किंमत १ आहे. दशक स्थानातील अंक ० पासून १ पर्यंत बदलतो, त्यामुळे त्यांची स्थानिक किंमत ० पासून १० पर्यंत आणि दर्शनी किंमत त्यांचे स्वयंच मूल्य (० पासून १) असते. एकक स्थानातील अंक ० पासून ० पर्यंत बदलतो (१०० पासून १०९ पर्यंत) किंवा ० पासून ९ पर्यंत (११०), त्यामुळे त्यांची स्थानिक किंमत त्यांचे स्वयंच मूल्य (० पासून ९) आणि दर्शनी किंमत देखील त्यांचे स्वयंच मूल्य (० पासून ९) असते.

questions.answer: क्रमवाचक संख्या क्रम वात दर्शवितात. 'सातवी' असे सांगण्याने समजते की वस्तू सातव्या क्रमाने आहे, जसे सातव्या डब्यात, सातव्या रांगेत.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: मूल्यबाचक संख्यांमध्ये शून्य कदाचित वापरला जात नाही का?
questions.answer: मूल्यबाचक संख्या वस्तूंची गणना करतात, जसे एका वस्तू, दोन वस्तू. शून्य म्हणजे वस्तू नाही, त्यामुळे मूल्यबाचक गणनेत शून्य वापरला जात नाही, परंतु स्ट्रक्चरमध्ये (जसे १०, १००) तो स्थानधारक म्हणून वापरला जातो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: मूल्यबाचक व क्रमवाचक संख्यांची फरक सांगा. प्रत्येकचा दोन उदाहरण दे.
questions.answer: मूल्यबाचक संख्या वस्तूंची गणना करते, जसे १, २, ३, १०. क्रमवाचक संख्या क्रम वात सांगतात, जसे पहिला, दुसरा, तिसरा, दसवा. मूल्यबाचक: ५ किताबे, २० रुपये. क्रमवाचक: पाचवी रांगेत, दसवा डब्बा.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: २९५ रुपये परत करण्यासाठी दुकानदार कसे नोटे परत देईल? तपशीलवार सांगा.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील उदाहरण सोडवा. पूर्ण कार्य दाखवा.
questions.text: गौरीने १ किलो सफरचंद व १ किलो चिकू खरेदी केली. सफरचंदाची किंमत १ किलो २३५ रुपये, चिकूची किंमत १ किलो ६० रुपये असल्यास, तिने एकूण किती रुपयांची खरेदी केली?
questions.answer: सफरचंदाची किंमत = २३५ रुपये चिकूची किंमत = ६० रुपये एकूण खरेदी = २३५ + ६० = २९५ रुपये ∴ तिने २९५ रुपयांची खरेदी केली.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील उदाहरण सोडवा. पूर्ण कार्य दाखवा.
questions.text: एक राजा के प्रत्येक बाजूकडून ९ घोडे दिसत असे ठेवले. त्यामुळे एकूण घोडे किती होते?
questions.answer: प्रत्येक बाजूकडून ९ घोडे दिसते. आता, दोन बाजू (उजवीकड व दावीकड) असल्यामुळे, एकूण घोडे = ९ + ९ = १८ ∴ राजा के पास १८ घोडे होते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील उदाहरण सोडवा. पूर्ण कार्य दाखवा.
questions.text: वाटसरूने ४ घोडे घेतले व राजा के ४ घोडे घेतले. त्यानंतर प्रत्येक बाजूकडून ९ घोडे दिसत असे ठेवले. एकूण घोडे किती?
questions.answer: वाटसरूने ४ घोडे घेतले. राजा के ४ घोडे घेतले. एकूण घोडे घेतले = ४ + ४ = ८ पण, प्रत्येक बाजूकडून ९ घोडे दिसत असे ठेवले. त्यामुळे, एकूण घोडे = ९ + ९ = १८ ∴ एकूण घोडे १८ होते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील उदाहरण सोडवा. पूर्ण कार्य दाखवा.
questions.text: यशने एक कॅरमबोर्ड व एक बुद्धिबळ संच विकत घेतला. कॅरमबोर्डची किंमत २४० रुपये, बुद्धिबळ संची किंमत ३५० रुपये असल्यास, यशने एकूण किती रुपयांची खरेदी केली?
questions.answer: कॅरमबोर्डची किंमत = २४० रुपये बुद्धिबळ संची किंमत = ३५० रुपये एकूण खरेदी = २४० + ३५० = ५९० रुपये ∴ यशने ५९० रुपयांची खरेदी केली.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील उदाहरण सोडवा. पूर्ण कार्य दाखवा.
questions.text: एक दुकानदाराने यशला ७०० रुपये दिले व खरेदी ५९० रुपये झाली. दुकानदार यशला किती रुपये परत देईल?
questions.answer: दिलेल्या रक्कम = ७०० रुपये खरेदी = ५९० रुपये परत करण्यायाची रक्कम = ७०० - ५९० = ११० रुपये ∴ दुकानदार यशला ११० रुपये परत देतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: ५०७ - २६८ सोडवताना ७ एककातून ८ एकक वजा होत नाही, म्हणून १ दशक मोकळा केला. याचा कारण काय?
questions.answer: ५०७ - २६८ सोडवताना एकक sthanात ७ - ८ केला जाऊ शकत नाही, म्हणून दशक sthanaatून १ दशक (१० एकक) मोकळा केला. त्यामुळे एकक sthan १७ होतो, त्यातून ८ एकक वजा केल्याने ९ एकक मिळाले.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: दूध संकलन केंद्रात शिल्लक दूध काढता येईल, हे सांगिते कारण द्या.
questions.answer: दूध संकलन केंद्रात प्रारंभिक ६२४ लीटर दूध होते. शेतकऱ्यांकडून ३४७ लीटर जास्त जमा केले, त्यामुथ एकूण ९७१ लीटर दूध झाले. त्यानंतर ५१२ लीटर दूध उपाहारगृह चालकांना व ३४६ लीटर इतर ग्राहकांना दिले, त्यामुथ उपयोजित दूध ८५८ लीटर झाला. शिल्लक दूध ९७१ - ८५८ = ११३ लीटर राहिला.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: वजाबाकीचे दोन शब्दांत उदाहरण द्या व त्यांचे अर्थ सांगा.
questions.answer: वजाबाकीचे दोन शब्द उदाहरण: १) घटाव - दोन संख्यांमध्यापासून लहान संख्येचा मोठ्या संख्येने घटणे. २) शिल्लक - खर्च केल्यानंतर शिल्लक राहिली रक्कम. उदाहरण: ५०० - ३७५ = १२५, येथे १२५ शिल्लक रक्कम आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: एकूण, घटाव, शिल्लक यांच्यामधील संबंध सांगा. एक उदाहरण दे.
questions.answer: एकूण म्हणजे सुरूवातीला असलेली एकूण रक्कम किंवा संख्या. घटाव म्हणजे एकूण पासून खर्च किंवा घटलेली रक्कम काढणे. शिल्लक म्हणजे घटाव केल्यानंतर राहिली शिल्लक रक्कम. उदाहरण: सायलीकडे एकूण ५०० रुपये होते. तिने ३७५ रुपयांची पुस्तके खरेदी केली. त्यामुळे घटाव ३७५ रुपये झाला. शिल्लक रक्कम ५०० - ३७५ = १२५ रुपये.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्न सोडवा. पूर्ण कार्य दाखवा.
questions.text: एक दूध संकलन केंद्रात आधी ६२४ लीटर दूध जमा होते. शेतकऱ्यांकडून आणखी ३४७ लीटर दूध जमा करण्यात आले. त्यामधील ५१२ लीटर दूध उपाहारगृह चालकांना व ३४६ लीटर दूध इतर ग्राहकांना दिले. तर दूध संकलन केंद्रात किती लीटर दूध शिल्लक राहिले?
questions.answer: प्रारंभिक दूध = ६२४ लीटर जमा केलेली दूध = ३४७ लीटर एकूण दूध = ६२४ + ३४७ = ९७१ लीटर उपahारgruha चालकांना दिलेली दूध = ५१२ लीटर इतर ग्राहकांना दिलेली दूध = ३४६ लीटर एकूण दिलेली दूध = ५१२ + ३४६ = ८५८ लीटर शिल्लक राहिली दूध = एकूण दूध - एकूण दिलेली दूध = ९७१ - ८५८ = ११३ लीटर अतः, दूध संकलन केंद्रात ११३ लीटर दूध शिल्लक राहिले.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्न सोडवा व पूर्ण कार्यप्रदर्शी लिहा.
questions.text: एक चॉकलेट आठ बराबर भागांमध्ये विभाजित केली. त्यामध्ये तीन भागे खालील आहेत. चॉकलेटचा किती भाग राहिलं?
questions.answer: एक चॉकलेट = 8 भाग. खालील भागे = 3. राहिलेले भाग = 8 - 3 = 5. राहिलं भाग = 5/8. उत्तर: ५/८.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्न सोडवा व पूर्ण कार्यप्रदर्शी लिहा.
questions.text: एक पिझा पाच बराबर भागांमध्ये विभाजित केला. त्यामध्ये एक भाग खालील आहे. पिझाचा किती भाग राहिलं?
questions.answer: एक पिझा = 5 भाग. खालील भाग = 1. राहिलेले भाग = 5 - 1 = 4. राहिलं भाग = 4/5. उत्तर: ४/५.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्न सोडवा व पूर्ण कार्यप्रदर्शी लिहा.
questions.text: एक टॉफी दोन बराबर भागांमध्ये विभाजित केली. त्यामध्ये एक भाग खालील आहे. टॉफीचा किती भाग राहिलं?
questions.answer: एक टॉफी = 2 भाग. खालील भाग = 1. राहिलेले भाग = 2 - 1 = 1. राहिलं भाग = 1/2. उत्तर: १/२.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: वस्तूची लांबी मोजण्यासाठी मीटर व सेंटिमीटर यांचा वापर कसे केला जातो? त्याचे उदाहरण द्या.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: वजन मोजण्यासाठी तराजू वापरून अनुभव कसे घ्यावे? खालील वस्तूंचे वजन 1 किलोग्रामपेक्षा कमी किंवा जास्त असेल याचा अंदाज कसे लावा?
questions.answer: तराजूच्या एका पारड्यात 1 किलोग्राम वजन ठेवा. दुसऱ्या पारड्यात वस्तू ठeva. जर वस्तूची पारडी उंच राहिली तर वस्तू 1 किलोग्रामपेक्षा जास्त आहे. जर वस्तूची पारडी तळ राहिली तर वस्तू 1 किलोग्रामपेक्षा कमी आहे. यामुळे वजनacha अंदाज सोपे होतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेटीच्या माहितीवर आधारित तक्ता tayar karanenche फायदे काय आहेत?
questions.answer: तक्त्याने माहिती सोप्या पद्धतीने दिसवते. सर्वांत जास्त व कमी काय आहे ते तुरुंत ओळखता येते. तुलना करणे सोपे होतो. तक्त्यापासून प्रश्नांचे उत्तर सोपे होतात. माहितीचे व्यवस्थापन होतो. विद्यार्थ्यांना डेटा समजणे सोपे होतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: ताळ्याच्या खुणा वापरून माहिती दाखवण्याचे फायदे काय आहेत?
questions.answer: ताळ्याच्या खुणा ने माहिती सोप्या प्रतीकाने दाखवली जाते. पाच रेघे एका गटाने दर्शवितात, ज्यामुळे गणना सोपे होते. तुलना करणे सोपे होतो. त्रुटी कमी होतात. माहिती स्पष्ट व आकर्षक होते. विद्यार्थ्यांना डेटा वाचणे आवडते.

questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नाचे उत्तर लिहा, काम दाखवा.
questions.text: एक वर्गात ३० विद्यार्थी आहेत. त्यामध्ये १/३ विद्यार्थी रिकामाने येतात, १/५ विद्यार्थी सायकलने येतात, शेष विद्यार्थी पायाने येतात. पायाने येणाऱ्या विद्यार्थ्यांची संख्या किती?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नाचे उत्तर लिहा, काम दाखवा.
questions.text: एक शाळेत ४० विद्यार्थी आहेत. त्यामध्ये १० विद्यार्थी बसने येतात, ८ विद्यार्थी रिक्षाने येतात, १२ विद्यार्थी सायकलने येतात, शेष विद्यार्थी पायाने येतात. पायाने येणाऱ्या विद्यार्थ्यांची संख्या किती?
questions.answer: एकूण विद्यार्थी = ४० बसने येणारे = १० रिक्षाने येणारे = ८ सायकलने येणारे = १२ पायाने येणारे = एकूण - (बस + रिक्सा + सायकल) = ४० - (१० + ८ + १२) = ४० - ३० = १० अतः पायाने येणाऱ्या विद्यार्थ्यांची संख्या १० आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नाचे उत्तर लिहा, काम दाखवा.

questions.answer: लांब उडी = १५ उंच उडी = २० दोरीवरची उडी = १० एकूण सहभाग = १५ + २० + १० = ४५ (शेता: एकूण मुलांना ५०, तर ५ मुलांनी कोणतीही स्पर्धेत सहभाग न घेतला.)

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नाचे उत्तर लिहा, काम दाखवा.
questions.text: एक दुकानात ५० वस्तू विकली गeli. त्यामध्ये १५ पेन, १० पेन्सील, १२ कंपासपेटी, शेष वस्तू इतर आहेत. इतर वस्तूंची संख्या किती?
questions.answer: एकूण वस्तू = ५० पेन = १५ पेन्सील = १० कंपासपेटी = १२ इतर वस्तू = एकूण - (पेन + पेन्सील + कंपासपेटी) = ५० - (१५ + १० + १२) = ५० - ३७ = १३ अतः इतर वस्तूंची संख्या १३ आहे.

questions.text: नजरी नकाशेतील चिन्हे कशा प्रकारे फायदेशीर ठरतात?
questions.answer: नजरी नकाशेतील चिन्हे वस्तूचे नाव व त्यांचे ठिकाण सोप्या प्रकारे ओळखवतात. ते नकाशा वाचणे सोपे करतात. त्यामुळे रस्ता शोधणे व जागा ओळखणे सोपे होतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: बागेच्या नकाशेत घसरगुंडी व पक्षी निवास यांचे स्थान तुलना करा.
questions.answer: घसरगुंडी बागेच्या प्रवेशद्वारापासून उजवीकडे असते, तर पक्षी निवास त्याच्या डाव्या बाजूला असतो. घसरगुंडी खाली व पक्षी निवास वरील बाजूला आहेत. त्यामुळे ते एकमेकांशी सटे नाहीत.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: जाळी पद्धतीने वस्तूचे स्थान कसे लिहायचे?
questions.answer: जाळी पद्धतीने वस्तूचे स्थान स्तंभाची अक्षर व ओळीचा क्रमांक जोडून लिहायचे. जसे, अ-२, ब-४ इत्यादी. स्तंभ उभ्या रांगा व ओळी आडव्या रांगा असतात.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: नजरी नकाशेतील चिन्हे शब्दे वापरण्याऐवजी वापरले जाते का?
questions.answer: नजरी नकाशेतील चिन्हे शब्दे वापरण्याऐवजी वापरले जाते जेते की ते सर्वात सोपे व स्पष्ट ठरतात. शब्दे वाचण्यासाठी शिकावे लागते, पण चिन्हे सर्वात ओळखणे सोपे आहेत. ते भाषा न जानणाऱ्यांसाठी देखील उपयुक्त आहेत. त्यामुळे सर्वांनाही नकाशा समजणे सोपे होतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: जाळी पद्धतीने वस्तूचे स्थान सांगणे सोपे का?
questions.answer: जाळी पद्धतीने वस्तूचे स्थान सांगणे सोपे आहे कारण ते स्तंभ व ओळीचा संयोजन वापरते. अक्षर व क्रमांक सोपे ओळखणे व लिहणे आहेत. ते त्रुटी कमी करतात व सर्वांनाही एकसारखे समजतात. त्यामुळे ठिकाण अचूकपणे दर्शविते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: नजरी नकाशा काय आहे? त्याचे फायदे व वापर काय-काय आहेत?
questions.answer: नजरी नकाशा हे वरुन बघण्याचे दृश्य दर्शवणारा सादर नकाशा आहे. त्यामध्ये वस्तूचे चिन्हे व त्यांचे ठिकाण दर्शविते. त्याचे फायदे: रस्ता शोधणे सोपे होतो, जागा ओळखणे सोपे होतो, नकाशा वाचणे सोपे होतो. त्याचा वापर: शाळेतील बागicha, गावातील जत्रा, घराची रचना दर्शविण्यासाठी केला जातो. ते दिशा ज्ञान व ठिकाण ओळखण्यास मदत करतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: बागेच्या नकाशेतील सर्व चिन्हे ओळखा व त्यांचे ठिकाण सांगा.
questions.answer: बागेच्या नकाशेतील चिन्हे: प्रवेशद्वार - बागेच्या उघडण्याचा स्थान, घसरगुंडी - वाहनतळ, पक्षी निवास - पक्षींचे घर, झोपाळा - विश्रांतीचा ठिकाण, स्वच्छतागृह - सफाईचे स्थान. प्रवेशद्वार मध्ये असतो, घसरगुंडी प्रवेशद्वारापासून उजवीकडे, पक्षी निवास घसरगुंडीच्या डाव्या बाजूला, झोपाळा पक्षी निवासाच्या बाजूला, स्वच्छतागृह झोपाळ्याच्या बाजूला असतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नाचे उचित प्रक्रिया दर्शवून उत्तर लिहा.
questions.text: जाळीतील ब-३ च्या स्थानावर केळी असते. अ-२ च्या स्थानावर दाख असते. ड-४ च्या स्थानावर संता असते. तर क-३ च्या स्थानावर कोणती वस्तू असते?
questions.answer: जाळीतील स्तंभ: अ, ब, क, ड. ओळी: १, २, ३, ४. ब-३ = केळी. अ-२ = दाख. ड-४ = संता. स्तंभ ब पासून क एक उजवीकडे विसरे. ओळी २ पासून ३ एक वरी विसरे. त्यामुळे ब-३ पासून एक उजवीकडे (क-३) व एक वरी (ब-४) जाणे आवश्यक आहे. पण आम्हच क-३ शोधतो. ब-३ च्या उजवीकडे क-३ असतो. त्यामुळे क-३ च्या स्थानावर केळी असतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नाचे उचित प्रक्रिया दर्शवून उत्तर लिहा.
questions.text: जत्रेच्या नकाशेत आकाश पाळणा ब-२ च्या स्थानावर असते. मदतकेंद्र ड-४ च्या स्थानावर असतो. तर आकाश पाळण्यापासून मदतकेंद्रापर्यंत जाण्यासाठी कोणती दिशा पाहिजे?
questions.answer: आकाश पाळणा = ब-२. मदतकेंद्र = ड-४. स्तंभ ब पासून ड तीन उजवीकडे विसरे (ब->क->ड). ओळी २ पासून ४ दोन वरी विसरे (२->३->४). त्यामुळे उजवीकडे व वरील दिशेने जाणे पाहिजे, अर्थात उत्तर-उजवीकडे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नाचे उचित प्रक्रिया दर्शवून उत्तर लिहा.
questions.text: बागेच्या नकाशेत प्रवेशद्वार क-१ च्या स्थानावर असतो. घसरगुंडी प्रवेशद्वारापासून दोन उजवीकडे असली तर तिचा स्थान काय आहे?
questions.answer: प्रवेशद्वार = क-१. दोन उजवीकडे = क पासून दोन स्तंभ उजवीकडे = म-१ (परंतु स्तंभ फक्त अ, ब, क, ड असतात). त्यामुळे क पासून एक उजवीकडे ल-१ (असले नाही), दोन उजवीकडे असेल तर ड-१ (क->ड). त्यामुळे घसरगुंडीचा स्थान ड-१ आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नाचे उचित प्रक्रिया दर्शवून उत्तर लिहा.
questions.text: जाळीतील अ-४ च्या स्थानावर केळी असते. ब-३ च्या स्थानावर दाख असते. तर क-२ च्या स्थानावर कोणती वस्तू असते?
questions.answer: अ-४ = केळी. ब-३ = दाख. अ पासून ब एक उजवीकडे. ४ पासून ३ एक खाली. त्यामुळे ब-३ पासून एक उजवीकडे व एक वरी = क-२. त्यामुळे क-२ च्या स्थानावर केळी असतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नाचे उचित प्रक्रिया दर्शवून उत्तर लिहा.
questions.text: जत्रेच्या नकाशेत फुगेबाला उपहारगृह ड-३ च्या स्थानावर असते. आकाश पाळणा ब-१ च्या स्थानावर असते. तर फुगेबाला उपहारगृह आकाश पाळण्यापासून कोणती दिशेने असतो?
questions.answer: फुगेबाला = ड-३. आकाश पाळणा = ब-१. ड पासून ब दोन उजवीकडे विसरे (ड->क->ब). ३ पासून १ दोन खाली विसरे (३->२->१). त्यामुळे दोन उजवीकडे व दोन खाली = दक्षिण-खाली दिशा.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सममिती शोधण्यासाठी कागद फोल्ड करणे व कापणे हे दोन पद्धती कसे वेगवेगळे?
questions.answer: फोल्ड करणे कागद bend करून अक्ष ओळखतो, कापणे दोन भाग कापून जुळत नाहीत पाहतो. दोन्ही पद्धतींमधील उद्देश सममिती शोधणे आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सममित अक्ष काढण्यासाठी ट्रेस पेपर वापरण्याचे फायदे काय आहेत?
questions.answer: ट्रेस पेपर वापरण्याने आकृतीचे अचूक प्रतिबिंब मिळतो, ज्यामुठे सममित अक्ष सोपेपणे काढता येतो. हे पद्धत शाळेत वापरली जाते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सममित आकृतीतील बिंदूंची दूरी सममित अक्षापासून समान क्योंती?
questions.answer: सममित आकृतीतील बिंदूंची दूरी सममित अक्षापासून समान असते, कारण सममित अक्ष फोल्ड लाईन आहे. फोल्ड केल्यावर बिंदूंची प्रतिमा एकमेकांवर पडते, त्यामुठे दूरी समान राहते. हे सममितीचा मूलभूत गुणधर्म आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सममित नाही असलेली आकृती फोल्ड केल्यावर जुळत नाहीत का?
questions.answer: सममित नाही असलेली आकृती फोल्ड केल्यावर जुळत नाहीत, कारण त्याचे दोन भाग आकारात वेगवेगळे असतात. फोल्ड केल्यावर भाग एकमेकांवर पडत नाहीत, त्यामुठे जुळत नाहीत. हे सममित नाही असलेली आकृतीची ओळख करण्याचा मार्ग आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सममितीचा दैनंदिन जीवनातील वापर सांगा. दोन उदाहरणे द्या.
questions.answer: सममिती दैनंदिन जीवनात विविध ठिकाणी पहातो. उदाहरणार्थ, फुलांचे पंखुड़ी, पात, झाडांचे शाखा, इमारतांचे डिझाइन, वाहनांचे डिझाइन, कपडे, शुभेच्छापत्रे, इत्यादी. सममिती सौंदर्य व संतुलन दर्शवते. त्यामुठे कला, वास्तुशास्त्र, व डिझाइनमध्ये सममिती वापरली जाते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सममिती शोधण्यासाठी कागद फोल्ड करणे व कापणे हे दोन पद्धती तुलना करा.
questions.answer: कागद फोल्ड करणे व कापणे हे सममिती शोधण्याची दोन सामान्य पद्धती आहेत. फोल्ड करणे कागद bend करून अक्ष ओळखतो, ज्यामुठे आकृतीचे भाग जुळतात. कापणे दोन भाग कापून त्यांचे जुळत नाहीत पाहतो, ज्यामुठे सममित नाही ओळखतो. फोल्ड पद्धतीत आकृती सुरक्षित राहते, कापणे त आकृती नष्ट होतो. दोन्ही पद्धतींमध्ये सममित अक्ष ओळखण्याचा उद्देश एकच आहे. फोल्ड पद्धती शाळेत वापरली जाते, कापणे प्राथमिक शाळेत वापरले जाते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: एक सममित आकृतीतील 8 बिंदू आहेत. सममित अक्षापासून प्रत्येक बिंदूची दूरी 2 सेमी आहे. अक्षापासून बिंदूंची एकत्र दूरी किती?
questions.answer: प्रत्येक बिंदूची दूरी 2 सेमी आहे. 8 बिंदू आहेत. एकत्र दूरी = 8 × 2 = 16 सेमी.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सममित आकृतीतील बिंदूंची संख्या 12 आहे. सममित अक्षापासून बिंदूंची दूरी 3 सेमी आहे. अक्षापासून बिंदूंची एकत्र दूरी किती?
questions.answer: प्रत्येक बिंदूची दूरी 3 सेमी आहे. 12 बिंदू आहेत. एकत्र दूरी = 12 × 3 = 36 सेमी.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सममित आकृतीतील बिंदूंची संख्या 6 आहे. सममित अक्षापासून बिंदूंची दूरी 4 सेमी आहे. अक्षापासून बिंदूंची एकत्र दूरी किती?
questions.answer: प्रत्येक बिंदूची दूरी 4 सेमी आहे. 6 बिंदू आहेत. एकत्र दूरी = 6 × 4 = 24 सेमी.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सममित आकृतीतील बिंदूंची संख्या 10 आहे. सममित अक्षापासून बिंदूंची दूरी 1.5 सेमी आहे. अक्षापासून बिंदूंची एकत्र दूरी किती?
questions.answer: प्रत्येक बिंदूची दूरी 1.5 सेमी आहे. 10 बिंदू आहेत. एकत्र दूरी = 10 × 1.5 = 15 सेमी.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सममित आकृतीतील बिंदूंची संख्या 5 आहे. सममित अक्षापासून बिंदूंची दूरी 5 सेमी आहे. अक्षापासून बिंदूंची एकत्र दूरी किती?

questions.answer: पातेल्याला पाण्याने पूर्ण भरा. त्यानंतर तो पाणी एक लीटरची मापण्याची बाटलीत ओता. बाटली किती वेळा भरली जाते ते numerate करा. त्यामुळे पातेल्याची धारकता मिळते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची दोन-तीन वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: पाव लीटर, अर्धा लीटर आणि पाऊण लीटर यांची संबंधे स्पष्ट करा.
questions.answer: दोन पाव लीटर एकत्रित करण्यासाठी अर्धा लीटर मिळतो. दोन अर्धा लीटर एकत्रित करण्यासाठी एक लीटर मिळतो. तीन पाव लीटर एकत्रित करण्यासाठी पाऊण लीटर मिळतो. त्यामुळे पाऊण लीटर = तीन पाव लीटर, अर्धा लीटर = दोन पाव लीटर, एक लीटर = चार पाव लीटर.

questions.subject: Maths

questions.answer: विद्यार्थ्यांना वेगवेगळे आकारे व आकारांची भांडे घेण्यांची गरज आहे. त्यानंतर एक लीटरची मापण्याची बाटली वापरून प्रत्येक भांड्यामध्ये किती वेळा पाणी ओता ते numerate करावी. त्यामुळे त्यांची धारकता मोजली जाऊ शकते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची तीन-चार वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: एक पातेल्याची धारकता पाऊण लीटर आहे. ते सांगितले की ती एक लीटरपेक्षा जास्त पाणी साठवू शकते. हे कसे सांगता येईल?
questions.answer: पाऊण लीटर म्हणजे तीन पाव लीटर. एक लीटर म्हणजे चार पाव लीटर. चूंकि तीन पाव लीटर चार पाव लीटरपेक्षा कमी आहे, म्हणजे पाऊण लीटर एक लीटरपेक्षा कमी आहे. परंतु प्रश्नामध्ये सांगितले की पाऊण लीटर एक लीटरपेक्षा जास्त आहे, जे चूक आहे. त्यामुळे कथन चूक आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची तीन-चार वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: घरातील नातळी व कप, कोणती भांडे जास्त पाणी साठवू शकते? कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: नातळी जास्त पाणी साठवू शकते. कारण नातळीचा आकार कपापेक्षा मोठा आहे आणि त्याची आधार विस्तार जास्त आहे. त्यामुळे त्यात जास्त आयतन पाणी जाऊ शकतो, ज्यामुळे त्याची धारकता जास्त आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची पाच-शा वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: आकारमान आणि धारकतेचा फरक स्पष्ट करा. दोन उदाहरणे द्या.
questions.answer: आकारमान म्हणजे काय वस्तूंचा आकार (लांबी, रुंद, उंची) मापणे. उदाहरणः मेजेची लांबी, किताबाची उंची. धारकता म्हणजे काय भांड्यात जाऊ शकते पाण्याचा प्रमाण मापणे. उदाहरणः बाटलीतील पाण्याची मात्रा, कडबातील दूध. आकारमान मीटर, सेन्टीमीटर इत्यादींमध्ये मापतो, धारकता लीटर, मिलीलिटर इत्यादींमध्ये मापतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची पाच-शा वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: शाळेतील पाणी टंकींची धारकता कसे मोजावी? पद्धत सांगा.
questions.answer: शाळेतील पाणी टंकींची धारकता मोजण्यासाठी, पहिल्यांदा एक लीटरची मापण्याची बाटली घ्यावी. त्यानंतर टंक्यामध्ये बाटलीने पाणी ओतावे. प्रत्येक वेळा बाटली पूर्ण झाल्यावर तो एक गणिती ओतं. टंकी पूर्ण झाल्यावर ओतलेली बाटलींची संख्या numerate करी. त्यामुळे टंक्यांची धारकता (लीटरमध्ये) मिळते. उदाहरणः जर २० बाटलीं ओतली तर धारकता २० लीटर आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची पूर्ण प्रक्रिया दाखवून उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: एक बाटलीमध्ये दोन पाव लीटर पाणी आहे. दुसरी बाटलीमध्ये अर्धा लीटर पाणी आहे. त्या दोन्ही बाटलींतील पाणी एकत्रित केल्यास एकूण किती पाव लीटर पाणी होईल?
questions.answer: पहिल्या बाटलीत पाणी = दोन पाव लीटर. दुसऱ्या बाटलीत पाणी = अर्धा लीटर = दोन पाव लीटर (कारण अर्धा लीटर = दोन पाव लीटर). एकत्रित पाणी = दोन + दोन = चार पाव लीटर. उत्तर: चार पाव लीटर.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची पूर्ण प्रक्रिया दाखवून उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: एक पातेल्यामध्ये पाऊण लीटर पाणी जाऊ शकतो. त्यात किती अर्धा लीटर पाणी जाऊ शकते?
questions.answer: पाऊण लीटर = तीन पाव लीटर. अर्धा लीटर = दोन पाव लीटर. त्यामुळे पाऊण लीटरमध्ये अर्धा लीटरची संख्या = तीन पाव लीटर / दोन पाव लीटर = १.५. त्यामुळे एक पातेल्यामध्ये एक अर्धा आणि आधी अर्धा लीटर पाणी जाऊ शकते, किंवा सांगता येईल की पाऊण लीटरमध्ये एक अर्धा लीटर आणि एक पाव लीटर पाणी जाऊ शकते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची पूर्ण प्रक्रिया दाखवून उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: शाळेतील एक बाटलीमध्ये पाच पाव लीटर पाणी आहे. त्यात किती लीटर पाणी आहे?
questions.answer: एक लीटर = चार पाव लीटर. त्यामुळे पाच पाव लीटर = (पाच / चार) लीटर = १.२५ लीटर. किंवा सांगता येईल की एक लीटर आणि एक पाव लीटर. उत्तर: १.२५ लीटर.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची पूर्ण प्रक्रिया दाखवून उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: एक बाटलीमध्ये एक लीटर पाणी आहे. त्यात किती पाव लीटर पाणी ओता येईल?
questions.answer: एक लीटर = चार पाव लीटर. त्यामुळे एक लीटरची बाटलीमध्ये चार पाव लीटर पाणी ओता येईल.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची पूर्ण प्रक्रिया दाखवून उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: विद्यार्थ्याने दोन पातेल्यांची धारकता मोजली. पहिल्याची धारकता पाऊण लीटर आहे, दुसऱ्याची धारकता दोन लीटर आहे. त्या दोन्हींची एकत्रित धारकता किती लीटर आहे?
questions.answer: पहिल्या पातेल्याची धारकता = पाऊण लीटर = ०.७५ लीटर (कारण पाऊण लीटर = तीन पाव लीटर = ३/४ लीटर = ०.७५ लीटर). दुसऱ्या पातेल्याची धारकता = दोन लीटर. एकत्रित धारकता = ०.७५ + २ = २.७५ लीटर. उत्तर: २.७५ लीटर.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील आकृती बनवा व लेबल लिहा.
questions.text: एक लीटरची बाटली बनवा व तिच्यावर पाव, अर्धा, पाऊण आणि एक लीटरचे खुणा दाखवा.
questions.answer: बाटलींचा आकार, पाव (१/४) लेबल, अर्धा (१/२) लेबल, पाऊण (३/४) लेबल, एक लीटर (१) लेबल.

questions.subject: Maths

questions.text: धारकता परिभाषित करा.
questions.answer: धारकता म्हणजे काय भांड्यात जाऊ शकते पाण्याचा प्रमाण.

questions.subject: Maths

questions.text: पाव लीटर परिभाषित करा.
questions.answer: पाव लीटर म्हणजे एक लीटरचा चौथाई भाग.

questions.text: पावणेचार वाजले म्हणजे किती वाजून किती मिनिटे?
questions.answer: तीन वाजून पैंतालीस मिनिटे

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: एक तासात किती मिनिटे?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सव्वा नऊ वाजले म्हणजे काय?
questions.answer: सव्वा नऊ वाजले म्हणजे नऊ वाजून पंद्रह मिनिटे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: साडे पाच वाजले म्हणजे काय?
questions.answer: साडे पाच वाजले म्हणजे पाच वाजून तीस मिनिटे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: पावणेचा वाजले म्हणजे काय?
questions.answer: पावणेचा वाजले म्हणजे एक वाजून पैंतालीस मिनिटे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: एक मिनिटात किती सेकंद?
questions.answer: एक मिनिटात शصت सेकंद असतात.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सव्वा, साडे व पावणे यांचे अर्थ सांगा.
questions.answer: सव्वा म्हणजे वाजून पंद्रह मिनिटे, साडे म्हणजे वाजून तीस मिनिटे, पावणे म्हणजे वाजून पैंतालीस मिनिटे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: एक तास व एक मिनिट यातील फरक सांगा.
questions.answer: एक तास शصت मिनिटे होते, तर एक मिनिट शصت सेकंद होते. तास वेळ मापण्याची मोठी एकक आहे, मिनिट तिची लहान एकक.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: घड्याळात मिनिट काटा ६ वर असल्यास किती मिनिटे?
questions.answer: मिनिट काटा ६ वर असल्यास तीस मिनिटे. कारण प्रत्येक काटा पाच मिनिटे दर्शवते, त्यामुळे ६ × ५ = ३०.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सव्वा तीन वाजले म्हणजे तीन वाजून पंद्रह मिनिटे असे का सांगितले?
questions.answer: सव्वा म्हणजे एक तासाचे चौथाई भाग, जी पंद्रह मिनिटे असते. त्यामुळे तीन वाजून सव्वा म्हणजे तीन वाजून पंद्रह मिनिटे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: एक दिवसात २४ तास असते का?
questions.answer: पृथ्वीला एक पूर्ण परिक्रमा करण्यामध्ये २४ तास लागतात, त्यामुळे दिन व रात यांचा चक्र एक दिवसात पूर्ण होऊन २४ तास होतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: घड्याळ वाचण्याचे पद्धत सांगा.
questions.answer: घड्याळात दोन काट्य असतात: लहान काटा मिनिट दर्शवतो, मोठा काटा तास दर्शवतो. मिनिट काटा १२ वर असल्यास शून्य मिनिटे, ३ वर असल्यास पंद्रह मिनिटे, ६ वर असल्यास तीस मिनिटे, ९ वर असल्यास पैंतालीस मिनिटे. तास काटा ज्याकडून ओळखला जातो, तेव्हा तास सांगितले जाते. उदाहरणार्थ, मिनिट काटा ३ वर व तास काटा २ वर असल्यास सव्वा दोन वाजले.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सव्वा, साडे व पावणे यांचे व्यावहारिक वापर सांगा.
questions.answer: सव्वा, साडे व पावणे यांचा वापर दैनंदिन जीवनात वेळ ओळखण्यास किया जातो, जसे की शाळेचा वेळ, बसचे वेळ, टीव्ही कार्यक्रमांचे वेळ. यामुळे वेळ जास्त अचूकपणे ओळखली जाऊ शकते. उदाहरणार्थ, 'सव्वा पाच' म्हणजे पाच वाजून पंद्रह मिनिटे, ज्यामुळे मुलांना वेळ समजणे सोपे होतो. यामुळे वेळ व्यवस्थापन सोपे होतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: एक चित्रकार एक चित्र पूर्ण करण्यास २ तास ४५ मिनिटे लागतो. तो एक दिवसात ३ चित्र पूर्ण करतो. त्याने एक दिवसात किती वेळ खर्च केली?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: एक विद्यार्थी शाळेत जाण्यास ३० मिनिटे लागतो व परत येण्यास ३० मिनिटे लागतात. तो एक आठवड्यात (५ दिवस) शाळेत जायचे-यायचे किती वेळ खर्च करतो?
questions.answer: एक दिवस जायचे-यायचे = ३० + ३० = ६० मिनिटे = १ तास पाच दिवस = ५ × १ तास = ५ तास उत्तर: ५ तास

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: एक चित्रakangण एक चित्र बनवण्यास १ तास २० मिनिटे लागतो. तो सात चित्र बनवण्यास किती वेळ लागेल?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: एक रेलगाडी एक ठिकाणी जाण्यास ३ तास ५० मिनिटे लागतो. परत येण्यास ४ तास १० मिनिटे लागतात. एक फेर वाटण्यास किती वेळ लागते?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: एक बँक १० वाजून उघडते व ३ वाजून पैंतालीस मिनिटे वाजते बंद होते. बँक एक दिवसात किती तास उघडली राहते?
questions.answer: उघडणे = १० वाजू बंदणे = ३ वाजून पैंतालीस मिनिटे = १५ वाजून पैंतालीस मिनिटे (दुपारी) कालावध = १५ वाजून पैंतालीस मिनिटे - १० वाजू = ५ तास पैंतालीस मिनिटे उत्तर: ५ तास ४५ मिनिटे

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: त्रिकोण, चौकोन व वर्तुळ यातील कोनांची संख्या तुलना करा व त्यांचे गुणधर्म सांगा.
questions.answer: त्रिकोणात तीन कोने असतात, त्यामुळे त्याची कोनांची संख्या तीन आहे. त्याचे कोनांची बेरीज 180 डिग्री असते. चौकोनात चार कोने असतात, त्यामुळे त्याची कोनांची संख्या चार आहे. त्याचे सर्व कोने सम असतात, प्रत्येक 90 डिग्री. वर्तुळात कोने नाहीत, त्यामुळे त्याची कोनांची संख्या शून्य आहे. वर्तुळ एक पातळी आकृती आहे जसात कोनांचे बिंदू नाहीत. त्यामुळे त्रिकोण व चौकोनात कोने असतात, परंतु वर्तुळात नाही.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: आकृतिबंध 5, 10, 15, 20 मध्ये पातळीवर क्या वाढतो व पाचवी पातळी कोणती? त्याचे नियम सांगा.
questions.answer: आकृतिबंध 5, 10, 15, 20 मध्ये प्रत्येक पातळीत 5 वाढतो. पहिली पातळी 5, दुसरी 10, तिसरी 15, चौथी 20 आहे. पाचवी पातळीत 20 + 5 = 25 असेल. त्यामुळे पाचवी पातळी 25 आहे. आकृतिबंधाचा नियम आहे: प्रत्येक पातळीमध्ये अंदाजे 5 जोडले जाते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: त्रिकोणACHE दोन कोने 40 डिग्री व 60 डिग्री असतील. तिसरा कोन काय असेल?
questions.answer: त्रिकोणACHE कोनांची बेरीज 180 डिग्री असते. दिलेले दोन कोने 40 डिग्री व 60 डिग्री आहेत. त्यांची बेरीज 40 + 60 = 100 डिग्री. तिसरा कोन = 180 - 100 = 80 डिग्री. त्यामुळे तिसरा कोन 80 डिग्री आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: चौकोनACHE एक कोन 90 डिग्री असतो. त्यामुळे चौकोनACHE सर्व कोनांची बेरीज कती?
questions.answer: चौकोनACHE सर्व कोने सम असतात, प्रत्येक 90 डिग्री. त्यामुळे सर्व कोनांची बेरीज = 90 + 90 + 90 + 90 = 360 डिग्री.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.answer: आकृतिबंध मध्ये प्रत्येक पातळीत 10 वाढतो. पहिली पातळी 10, दुसरी 20, तिसरी 30, चौथी 40, पाचवी 50. त्यामुळे पाचवी पातळी 50 आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: वर्तुळACHE कोने नाहीत. त्यामुळे वर्तुळACHE कोनांची बेरीज कती?
questions.answer: वर्तुळACHE कोने नाहीत, त्यामुळे त्यACHE कोनांची बेरीज शून्य आहे.

questions.answer: Water is considered precious because very little of it is available for drinking and no living being can survive without it.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: List any three activities at home that lead to water wastage.
questions.answer: Leaving the tap running while brushing teeth, taking long showers, and using a hose to wash a car instead of a bucket lead to water wastage at home.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How can we reuse water at home to prevent wastage?
questions.answer: We can reuse water used for washing vegetables or rinsing clothes to water plants. Leftover drinking water can be used for cleaning or gardening. This helps in recycling water and reducing wastage.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why were old tanks (haud) important in earlier times?
questions.answer: Old tanks (haud) were important because they stored water for drinking, farming, and construction. In some places, they are still used today for these purposes. They provided a reliable water source throughout the year.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What does the barrel analogy teach us about Earth's water?
questions.answer: The barrel analogy teaches us that if all Earth's water were in a barrel, fresh water would fill only a cup, and potable water would be just a single drop. This shows how scarce drinking water really is.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we not waste even a single drop of water?
questions.answer: We should not waste even a single drop of water because very little of Earth's water is available for drinking. Most water is in oceans, frozen, or underground, and only a tiny fraction is potable. Wasting water reduces this limited supply, affecting life and health.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are bunds built in fields and along streams?
questions.answer: Bunds are built to stop the flowing water of rivers and streams, which helps prevent soil erosion and stores water in fields for farming. This stored water can be used later for irrigation, especially during dry seasons.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is water called 'Life'?
questions.answer: Water is called 'Life' because no living being can survive without it. It is essential for drinking, farming, cleaning, and all bodily functions. Without water, plants, animals, and humans would not survive.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain how we can save water in our daily life at home and school.
questions.answer: We can save water at home by turning off taps while brushing teeth, using a bucket to wash cars, and reusing water from washing vegetables to water plants. At school, we can fix leaking taps, use water wisely in labs and toilets, and spread awareness through posters. Collecting rainwater and avoiding wastage during activities also help. Every small effort adds up to conserve this precious resource.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the importance of old tanks (haud) and their use in the past and present.
questions.answer: Old tanks (haud) were stone structures built in earlier times to store water for drinking, farming, and construction. They were especially common in forts and villages. Today, in some places, these tanks are still in use, showing their durability and usefulness. They helped communities survive dry seasons and are examples of traditional water wisdom.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define 'potable water'.
questions.answer: Potable water is safe and clean water that is suitable for drinking.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define 'bunds'.
questions.answer: Bunds are embankments made of stones or soil built to stop the flow of water in rivers or streams and to store water in fields.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain why fresh water is a scarce resource on Earth.
questions.answer: Although about 71% of Earth's surface is covered by water, most of it is in oceans and seas and is salty. A large portion is frozen in ice caps and glaciers. Only a small fraction is fresh water found in rivers, lakes, and groundwater. Of this fresh water, an even smaller amount is potable and easily accessible for human use. This makes fresh water a scarce and precious resource that must be used wisely.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how water wastage affects the environment and daily life.
questions.answer: Water wastage reduces the availability of fresh water for drinking, farming, and cleaning. It increases the burden on water supply systems and can lead to shortages, especially in dry areas. Wasted water often flows into drains without being reused, increasing energy use for treatment. It also harms ecosystems by reducing water levels in rivers and ponds. Conserving water helps protect nature and ensures supply for future generations.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: List the internal organs of the human body and state one function of each.
questions.answer: The internal organs include the brain (processes information), heart (pumps blood), lungs (supply oxygen), liver (helps in digestion), stomach (churns food), small intestine (absorbs nutrients), and large intestine (absorbs water and stores waste).

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Differentiate between external and internal organs with two examples each.
questions.answer: External organs are visible outside the body, such as eyes and ears. Internal organs are inside the body and cannot be seen, such as the heart and lungs. External organs help in sensing and movement, while internal organs carry out vital life processes.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how the heart and lungs work together to keep the body healthy.
questions.answer: The lungs take in oxygen from the air and pass it to the blood. The heart then pumps this oxygen-rich blood to all parts of the body. After delivering oxygen, the blood returns to the lungs to release carbon dioxide and pick up more oxygen. This continuous process keeps the body energized and healthy.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What happens to food after it enters the stomach?
questions.answer: Food enters the stomach through the oesophagus, where it is churned and mixed with digestive juices. The stomach breaks down the food into a semi-liquid form. This partially digested food then moves into the small intestine for further digestion and nutrient absorption.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is the brain considered the most important organ in the body?
questions.answer: The brain is considered the most important organ because it controls all body functions, processes information from the senses, stores memory, and enables thinking, emotions, and decision-making. Without the brain, we cannot perceive, respond, or carry out any activity. It coordinates the working of all other organs.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we not drink dirty water?
questions.answer: We should not drink dirty water because it may contain harmful germs, chemicals, or waste that can cause diseases like diarrhea, stomach ache, or cholera. Dirty water is not safe for drinking and can make us very ill. Drinking contaminated water affects our health and weakens the body.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important to protect our sense organs?
questions.answer: It is important to protect our sense organs because they help us see, hear, smell, taste, and feel the world around us. If they are damaged, we may lose the ability to perceive our surroundings properly, which can affect learning, safety, and daily life. Protecting them ensures we remain aware and responsive to our environment.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Describe the journey of food in the human body from the mouth to the anus.
questions.answer: Food enters the mouth where it is chewed and mixed with saliva. It then passes through the oesophagus to the stomach. In the stomach, food is churned and broken down by acids and enzymes. From the stomach, it moves into the small intestine, where digestion is completed and nutrients are absorbed into the blood. The remaining undigested material goes to the large intestine, where water is absorbed. The waste is stored in the rectum and finally expelled through the anus. This entire process helps the body get energy and remove waste.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the functions of the brain, heart, and lungs and how they work together to keep us alive.
questions.answer: The brain controls all body activities, processes sensory information, and enables thought and emotion. The heart acts as a pump, continuously circulating blood throughout the body. The lungs take in oxygen from the air and remove carbon dioxide from the blood. The lungs supply oxygen-rich blood to the heart, which then pumps it to all body parts. The brain regulates the heart and lung functions based on the body’s needs. Together, these three organs ensure that oxygen reaches every cell, waste is removed, and the body functions properly. Their coordination is essential for life.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define external organs.
questions.answer: External organs are body parts that can be seen from the outside of the body, such as eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin, hands, and legs.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define internal organs.
questions.answer: Internal organs are body parts that are located inside the body and cannot be seen from the outside, such as the brain, heart, lungs, liver, stomach, intestines, and kidneys.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how the stomach and small intestine work together in digestion.
questions.answer: The stomach receives food from the oesophagus and churns it into a semi-liquid form using muscular contractions and digestive juices. This process breaks down food into smaller particles. The partially digested food then moves into the small intestine, where enzymes from the liver and pancreas further break down nutrients. In the small intestine, nutrients and water are absorbed into the bloodstream. The inner walls of the small intestine have villi that increase surface area for absorption. Together, the stomach and small intestine ensure food is digested and nutrients are absorbed for energy and growth.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain why the heart is called a pump and how it helps in blood circulation.
questions.answer: The heart is called a pump because it continuously contracts and relaxes to push blood through the blood vessels, just like a mechanical pump moves liquid. It receives deoxygenated blood from the body and pumps it to the lungs for oxygenation. After receiving oxygen-rich blood from the lungs, it pumps it to all parts of the body. The heart’s rhythmic beating ensures that blood flows steadily to deliver oxygen and nutrients to cells and remove waste products. This continuous circulation is essential for maintaining life and body functions.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Write the difference between planets and stars.
questions.answer: Stars produce their own light and heat through nuclear fusion, while planets do not produce light and only reflect the light of stars. Stars are massive and hot, whereas planets are much smaller and cooler. Planets orbit stars, but stars may orbit each other or remain relatively fixed in space.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1

questions.answer: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and has a very short year. Earth is the third planet from the Sun and is the only known planet to support life.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain why the Moon appears to change shape every day.
questions.answer: The Moon does not produce its own light; it reflects sunlight. As the Moon orbits the Earth, the portion of its illuminated side visible from Earth changes, causing the different phases. This cycle repeats approximately every 29.5 days.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What is the solar system made of?
questions.answer: The solar system consists of the Sun, eight planets, their moons (satellites), dwarf planets, asteroids, comets, and other small celestial bodies. The Sun is at the center, and all objects orbit it due to its gravitational pull.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is the Sun considered the center of the solar system?
questions.answer: The Sun is considered the center of the solar system because it contains over 99% of the system's mass and its strong gravitational pull keeps all the planets, asteroids, comets, and other objects in orbit around it. All planets revolve around the Sun in elliptical orbits. The Sun's gravity dominates the motion of all other bodies in the solar system.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we not feel the Earth moving even though it rotates and revolves?
questions.answer: We do not feel the Earth's motion because everything on Earth, including the atmosphere and objects, moves with it at the same constant speed. The rotation and revolution are smooth and uniform, without sudden changes in speed or direction, so there is no sensation of motion. Additionally, gravity keeps us firmly on the surface.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is life possible only on Earth in our solar system?
questions.answer: Life is possible on Earth because it has the right temperature range, liquid water, a suitable atmosphere with oxygen, and protection from harmful solar radiation by the magnetic field and ozone layer. No other planet in the solar system has all these conditions together. Earth's distance from the Sun allows for moderate temperatures, unlike the extreme heat of Mercury or Venus or the extreme cold of outer planets.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Describe the solar system and mention the position of Earth in it.
questions.answer: The solar system is a family of celestial bodies centered around the Sun, which is a star. It includes eight planets that revolve around the Sun in elliptical orbits. The planets are divided into inner planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars) and outer planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune). Earth is the third planet from the Sun and is located in the inner region. It has one natural satellite, the Moon. Besides planets, the solar system contains dwarf planets like Pluto, asteroids mostly between Mars and Jupiter, and comets that come from the outer regions. The Sun provides light and heat, making life possible on Earth.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Explain the phases of the Moon with the help of a diagram description.
questions.answer: The phases of the Moon are the different shapes of the illuminated part of the Moon visible from Earth over a month. They occur because the Moon orbits the Earth while reflecting sunlight. At new moon, the Moon is between Earth and Sun, so its dark side faces us. As it moves, we see a growing illuminated part (waxing): crescent, first quarter, gibbous. At full moon, Earth is between Moon and Sun, so we see the fully lit side. After full moon, the illuminated part decreases (waning): gibbous, last quarter, crescent, back to new moon. This cycle takes about 29.5 days. The changing angles between Sun, Moon, and Earth cause the phases.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define rotation.
questions.answer: Rotation is the spinning of a celestial body on its own axis.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define revolution.
questions.answer: Revolution is the movement of a celestial body around another celestial body in an orbit.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how day and night occur on Earth.
questions.answer: Day and night occur due to the rotation of the Earth on its axis. As the Earth rotates, different parts face the Sun at different times. The part facing the Sun experiences daylight, while the part facing away experiences darkness. One full rotation takes approximately 24 hours, which we call a day. This cycle of daylight and darkness repeats continuously. The axis of rotation is tilted, which also causes seasons, but day and night are primarily due to rotation.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain why planets do not twinkle like stars.
questions.answer: Stars twinkle because they are point sources of light located very far away, and their light passes through Earth's turbulent atmosphere, which bends the light randomly. Planets, however, are much closer and appear as small disks in the sky, not points. The light from different parts of the planet's disk averages out the atmospheric distortions, making their light appear steady. This is why planets shine with a steady light, while stars seem to flicker. The closer distance of planets reduces the effect of atmospheric turbulence on their apparent brightness.
