questions.answer: A seed germinates in the soil when it gets water, air, and warmth. A sprout and a root emerge from it. The sprout grows into a seedling, which then develops into a mature plant.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How do trees help in reducing heat in our surroundings?
questions.answer: Trees provide shade, which gives relief from heat. They also release water vapour through transpiration, which cools the air. Planting trees on roadsides helps keep the environment cool.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we not over-polish rice?
questions.answer: Over-polishing rice removes the nutritious bran layer. This reduces the fibre, vitamins, and minerals in rice. Therefore, it is advised not to over-polish rice to retain its nutritional value.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What are insectivorous plants? Give one example.
questions.answer: Insectivorous plants are those that trap and digest insects to obtain nutrients. An example is the pitcher plant.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do some plants like Dodder grow on big trees?
questions.answer: Dodder is a heterotrophic plant that cannot prepare its own food. It grows on big trees to absorb food and water from them for its survival.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are medicinal plants being cultivated in backyards?
questions.answer: Medicinal plants are being cultivated in backyards because their numbers are decreasing in forests due to overuse. Growing them at home helps in their conservation and easy availability for use.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we plant trees on both sides of roads?
questions.answer: We plant trees on both sides of roads to provide shade to people and vehicles, reduce heat, and improve air quality. Trees also prevent soil erosion and enhance the beauty of the surroundings.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the importance of plants in our daily life.
questions.answer: Plants are essential for life on Earth. They provide us with food like fruits, vegetables, and grains. They give us clothing materials such as cotton and jute. Plants give us wood for shelter and furniture. They provide shade and cool the environment. Many medicines are made from plants. They also give us oxygen and absorb carbon dioxide. Plants support biodiversity by giving food and shelter to animals and birds. Thus, plants are our green companions and we must protect them.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: How can we help trees survive and grow?
questions.answer: We can help trees by planting more saplings and taking care of them. We should water young plants regularly, especially in summer. We must not harm trees by carving on their bark or breaking branches. Using seed balls is a good way to grow trees in open areas. We should avoid plastic and use eco-friendly products to reduce pollution. Schools and communities can organize tree plantation drives. By protecting trees, we protect our environment and future.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define autotrophic plants.
questions.answer: Autotrophic plants are those that prepare their own food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide through the process of photosynthesis.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What is photosynthesis?
questions.answer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to prepare their own food and release oxygen.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the journey of a seed to a fruit.
questions.answer: A seed germinates in the soil when it gets the right conditions of water, air, and warmth. From the seed, a root grows downward and a shoot grows upward. The shoot develops into a seedling with leaves. The seedling grows into a mature plant. The plant then produces flowers. After pollination, the flower transforms into a fruit, which contains seeds inside it.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how roots help a plant besides absorbing water and nutrients.
questions.answer: Roots absorb water and nutrients from the soil and transport them to the stem and leaves. They anchor the plant firmly in the ground, providing support and preventing it from falling over. Roots also store food in some plants, like carrots and radishes. They help prevent soil erosion by holding the soil together. In some cases, roots interact with helpful microorganisms in the soil that aid in nutrient uptake.

questions.text: Write down the effects of seasonal changes on human health.
questions.answer: Seasonal changes affect human health by causing fatigue, body aches, and changes in appetite. In summer, heat can lead to dehydration and fatigue, while in winter, cold weather may increase the risk of infections. Our diet and clothing also change with the seasons to maintain health and comfort.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short answer in 2-3 sentences.
questions.text: How are seasons formed? Write in two-three sentences.
questions.answer: Seasons are formed due to the Earth’s revolution around the Sun and the tilt of its axis by 23° 30'. As the Earth revolves, different parts receive varying amounts of sunlight at different times of the year. This causes changes in temperature and weather, leading to the formation of seasons like summer, monsoon, and winter.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1

questions.text: What changes do we make in our diet and clothing during summer?
questions.answer: In summer, we wear loose and cotton clothes to stay cool and comfortable. We drink plenty of water, cold drinks, juices, and buttermilk to avoid dehydration. We also eat fruits like mangoes, watermelons, and oranges that are abundant in this season.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short answer in 2-3 sentences.
questions.text: How do animals protect themselves during the rainy season?
questions.answer: During the rainy season, animals like snakes and frogs stay in cool, sheltered places such as burrows or under rocks to avoid getting wet. Some animals live in trees or move to higher ground to escape floodwaters. They also reduce their activity and may change their feeding habits to cope with the weather.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we need to drink more water and cold drinks in summer?
questions.answer: We need to drink more water and cold drinks in summer because the weather is very hot, which causes excessive sweating and loss of body fluids. Drinking more fluids helps prevent dehydration and keeps the body cool. It also maintains energy levels and supports normal body functions during high temperatures.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do farmers start sowing during the monsoon season?
questions.answer: Farmers start sowing during the monsoon season because the rains provide the necessary water for seeds to germinate and crops to grow. The soil becomes soft and moist, making it easier to prepare the land for planting. Adequate rainfall ensures better crop yield and reduces the need for irrigation.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it beneficial to eat dry fruits in winter?
questions.answer: It is beneficial to eat dry fruits in winter because they provide heat and energy to the body, which helps in keeping warm during cold weather. Dry fruits are rich in nutrients, vitamins, and healthy fats that support immunity and overall health. They are also easy to store and consume when fresh fruits are less available.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a descriptive answer in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Describe how seasonal changes affect our daily life in terms of food, clothing, and activities.
questions.answer: Seasonal changes greatly influence our daily life. In summer, we eat light, hydrating foods like fruits and drink lots of water and juices; we wear cotton clothes and avoid going out in the afternoon sun. During monsoon, we enjoy warm meals, use raincoats and umbrellas, and farmers begin sowing crops. In winter, we eat warm, energy-rich foods like dry fruits and guava, wear woolen clothes, and enjoy festivals like Diwali. Our activities, diet, and clothing all adapt to the weather to keep us healthy and comfortable throughout the year.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a descriptive answer in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Explain how the Earth’s movement and axial tilt lead to the formation of seasons and mention its effects on nature and human life.
questions.answer: The Earth’s revolution around the Sun and the tilt of its axis by 23° 30' cause the seasons. When the Northern Hemisphere tilts toward the Sun, it experiences summer due to more direct sunlight and longer days, while the Southern Hemisphere has winter. This tilt changes as the Earth orbits, reversing the seasons after six months. These changes in temperature and sunlight affect nature—plants grow, bloom, or shed leaves; animals migrate or hibernate. Human life also changes: we adjust our food, clothing, and daily routines according to the season to stay healthy and comfortable.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define 'season'.
questions.answer: A season is a period of the year characterized by specific weather conditions, temperature, and daylight hours, caused by the Earth's revolution around the Sun and the tilt of its axis.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define 'migration' in the context of animals.
questions.answer: Migration is the regular movement of animals from one place to another, usually with the seasons, in search of food, better climate, or breeding grounds.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how seasonal winds cause rain in our country.
questions.answer: Seasonal changes create differences in temperature between land and sea, leading to changes in air pressure. Winds blow from high-pressure areas to low-pressure areas. When these winds pass over oceans, they pick up moisture. As this moist air moves over land and cools, it condenses to form clouds, which results in rainfall. In India, the monsoon rains are caused by such seasonal winds blowing from the Indian Ocean.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain why we should not waste food, based on the chapter.
questions.answer: We should not waste food because it is the result of hard work by many people, including farmers who grow grains, traders who transport them, and others who process and sell food. Wasting food means disrespecting their effort and the resources like water, soil, and energy used in production. The chapter teaches that food is sacred—'Food is Purna Bramha'—and essential for our health and energy. By avoiding waste, we honor this value and promote responsible living.

questions.answer: Birds build nests to lay eggs and protect their chicks from predators and weather.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What are the factors necessary for good crop production?
questions.answer: Good crop production requires improved seeds, fertile land, sufficient sunlight, and sufficient water. These factors help seeds germinate well and plants grow healthy. Farmers also use proper farming methods to get a good yield.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: State any three methods of food preservation used at home.
questions.answer: Common methods include sun drying, storing in a well-ventilated place (like onions and potatoes), and preserving with salt, oil, or spices (as in pickles). These methods prevent spoilage by removing moisture or stopping microbial growth. They help food last longer without refrigeration.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What are the characteristics of eco-friendly houses?
questions.answer: Eco-friendly houses use natural materials like mud, bamboo, and recycled items. They use solar or wind energy, recycle water, and are designed for natural light and air flow. These homes do not harm the environment and promote sustainable living.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we avoid eating food kept in the open for a long time?
questions.answer: Food kept in the open gets contaminated by dust, flies, and microbes from the air. It may also lose moisture and become stale or develop fungus. Eating such food can cause stomach ache, diarrhea, or food poisoning.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are grains dried in the sun before storing?
questions.answer: Grains are dried in the sun to remove moisture, which prevents the growth of fungus and insects. Moisture leads to spoilage during storage. Sun drying makes grains last longer and remain safe to eat throughout the year.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we need shelters for animals and birds?
questions.answer: Animals and birds need shelters to protect themselves from extreme weather like heat, cold, and rain. Shelters also keep them safe from predators. For birds, nests are essential to lay eggs and raise chicks safely.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important to wash vegetables before cutting them?
questions.answer: Washing removes dirt, pesticides, and germs from the surface. If we cut first and then wash, nutrients may leak out into the water. Washing before cutting keeps the vegetables clean and nutritious.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the process of making a raw mango pickle at home, as mentioned in the chapter.
questions.answer: First, clean and dry a glass jar. Cut raw mango into thin slices and put them in the jar. Add pickle masala, chili powder, and salt. Stir well with a dry spoon. Heat oil, add mustard seeds, and pour the cooled oil into the jar. Tie a clean cloth over the mouth and cover the jar. This pickle stays good for months due to salt and oil acting as preservatives.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain how food gets contaminated and what effects it has on our body.
questions.answer: Food gets contaminated by microbes, chemicals, unclean water, or dirty utensils. It can also happen if food is kept open for long or mixed with substances like plastic or glass. Eating contaminated food may cause stomach ache, vomiting, diarrhea, or fever. It weakens the body and can lead to serious illness if not treated.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Contaminated food
questions.answer: Food that is spoiled, poisoned, or contains harmful substances that can cause illness is called contaminated food.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Organic farming
questions.answer: Organic farming is a method of growing crops using natural fertilizers like dung and compost, without using chemical fertilizers or pesticides.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the importance of farmers in our society.
questions.answer: Farmers grow food grains, vegetables, fruits, and pulses that we eat every day. They work hard in the fields preparing land, sowing, watering, and harvesting crops. Their work ensures food security for the entire population. Farmers also adopt new methods like using better seeds and machines to increase yield. Without farmers, we would not have enough food to survive.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the differences between rural and urban houses in Maharashtra.
questions.answer: Rural houses are made from locally available natural materials like mud, bamboo, grass, and wood. They have simple designs and sloping or thatched roofs suited to the local climate. Urban houses are built with durable materials like cement, bricks, steel, and concrete. They are often multi-storey and have amenities like electricity and water supply. Rural homes rely on nature, while urban homes use modern construction techniques.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What are the effects of excessive rain?
questions.answer: Excessive rain causes rivers and streams to overflow, leading to floods. It damages houses, crops, trees, and animals. Therefore, we should move to a safe or high place along with animals.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What precautions should be taken in the kitchen to avoid accidents?
questions.answer: Never play near the gas stove when it is in use. Always turn off the stove button and regulator when not in use. Keep inflammable items away from the flame.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How can we help visually impaired people in school?
questions.answer: We can act as a 'Vision-Friend' by guiding them verbally, holding their hand, and helping them avoid obstacles like tables and chairs. We should give clear instructions like 'turn right' or 'there is a chalk below'.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What safety measures should be taken while using electrical appliances?
questions.answer: Do not touch broken wires or damaged switches. Never use electrical appliances with wet hands. Adults should wear rubber gloves and slippers while repairing them.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important to listen to weather department warnings during a cyclone?
questions.answer: It is important because the weather department gives early alerts about cyclones, allowing people to move to safe places, avoid travel, and prepare emergency kits. This helps reduce loss of life and property.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we help elderly and differently abled persons during emergencies?
questions.answer: They may move slowly or need support to reach safety. Helping them ensures their protection and reflects our responsibility to care for vulnerable members of society.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it dangerous to play with medicines or chemicals at home?
questions.answer: Medicines and chemicals can be poisonous if ingested or touched incorrectly. Accidental exposure may cause illness, burns, or serious harm, especially to children.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph on the following.
questions.text: How can we keep our environment safe and clean?
questions.answer: We can keep our environment safe by planting trees, saving water, reducing waste, and avoiding plastic. We must not pollute rivers or litter public places. Protecting the environment is our duty because our health and well-being depend on it. Just like we care for our family, we must care for nature.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph on the following.
questions.text: What should be included in a life-saving bag and why?
questions.answer: A life-saving bag should contain a water bottle, dry snacks, a torch, regular medicines, and a copy of emergency contacts. These items help survive during disasters when basic services are unavailable. Water prevents dehydration, snacks provide energy, torch helps in darkness, and medicines treat illness. Being prepared saves lives.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define drought.
questions.answer: A drought is a water shortage caused by insufficient or untimely rainfall, affecting people, animals, and agriculture.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define natural disaster.
questions.answer: A natural disaster is a calamity that occurs naturally, such as flood, earthquake, landslide, or cyclone, causing widespread damage.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how landslides occur and their impact.
questions.answer: Landslides occur due to heavy rainfall on hills, which loosens soil and rocks, causing them to slide down suddenly. They can bury houses, fields, and trees under debris. The impact includes loss of life, destruction of property, and blocking of roads. Rescue becomes difficult in such situations. Therefore, avoiding construction on steep slopes and planting trees can help reduce landslide risks.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the safety measures to be followed at home to avoid accidents.
questions.answer: To stay safe at home, we must never play with fire, matchsticks, or lighters. Electrical appliances should not be touched with wet hands, and broken wires must be reported. Medicines and chemicals should be kept out of children's reach. While climbing stairs, walk slowly and hold the railing. These small precautions prevent major accidents and keep everyone safe.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how wet waste is converted into compost fertilizer.
questions.answer: Wet waste like vegetable peels and food scraps is put in a pit or container. A little soil is added and water is sprinkled regularly. After 4-6 weeks, it decomposes and turns into compost fertilizer.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What are the three principles of 3R? Give one example of each.
questions.answer: The three principles are Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. Example of reduce: using a steel cup instead of plastic. Example of reuse: using an old ice cream box to store pencils. Example of recycle: making new paper from old newspapers.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important to segregate waste into wet and dry?
questions.answer: Segregating waste helps in proper disposal. Wet waste can be turned into compost, and dry waste can be recycled. This keeps surroundings clean and reduces pollution.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How can students help keep their school clean?
questions.answer: Students can throw waste in the correct dustbins, not litter on floors, avoid scribbling on walls, and save water by closing taps. They can also reuse old materials for projects.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why does garbage left in the open cause diseases?
questions.answer: Garbage in the open attracts houseflies that sit on it and carry germs. These germs spread to food and water, causing illnesses. The foul smell also affects breathing and health.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it better to use a cloth bag instead of a plastic bag when shopping?
questions.answer: A cloth bag can be used many times, reducing plastic waste. Plastic bags are often thrown away and do not decompose, harming the environment. Using cloth bags supports the Reuse principle of 3R.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we not throw pencil shavings on the classroom floor?
questions.answer: Pencil shavings make the floor dirty and unclean. They can be swept away easily but if left, they accumulate and look untidy. Keeping the floor clean is part of maintaining good hygiene in school.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: How can you turn wet waste from your home into useful compost? Describe the steps.
questions.answer: Collect wet waste like vegetable peels, fruit skins, and leftover food in a container. Dig a pit in the school garden or use a big bin. Put the waste daily, add a little soil, and sprinkle water. Cover it to keep moisture. Stir it occasionally. After 4-6 weeks, the waste turns into dark, crumbly compost. This compost can be mixed with soil to grow healthy plants.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain how following the 3R principle helps keep our surroundings clean and beautiful.
questions.answer: By reducing waste, we use fewer things like plastic cups and paper. By reusing, we use old items like bottles and boxes again instead of throwing them. By recycling, we send dry waste like paper and plastic to factories to make new products. This reduces garbage in streets, prevents foul smell and disease, and keeps nature safe for plants and animals. Our surroundings stay clean, green, and beautiful when everyone follows 3R.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Dry waste
questions.answer: Dry waste is waste that does not rot or decompose and remains as it is for many years, such as plastic, metal, and glass.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Compost fertilizer
questions.answer: Compost fertilizer is the nutrient-rich soil formed when wet waste decomposes over 4-6 weeks, used to help plants grow.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How does improper disposal of dry waste harm the environment?
questions.answer: Improper disposal of dry waste like plastic and metal leads to accumulation in landfills and streets. These materials do not decompose and stay for hundreds of years. They can block drains, cause waterlogging, and harm animals if ingested. Plastic waste breaks into microplastics that enter soil and water. Recycling dry waste reduces this harm and saves resources.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important to teach children about waste management from a young age?
questions.answer: Children learn habits early, and teaching them about waste helps them grow into responsible citizens. They understand the impact of littering and the value of cleanliness. When they practice 3R at school and home, they influence their families too. Early awareness leads to lifelong eco-friendly behaviour. This helps build a cleaner, healthier society for the future.

questions.text: Explain the difference between oviparous and viviparous animals with examples.
questions.answer: Oviparous animals lay eggs, and their young ones hatch outside the mother's body, e.g., birds and insects. Viviparous animals give birth to live young ones, e.g., humans, cows, and dogs. In viviparous animals, the embryo develops inside the mother's body.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: In the Wonderful World of Animals
questions.text: Describe how insects help in plant reproduction.
questions.answer: Insects like bees and butterflies help in pollination by transferring pollen from one flower to another. This process is essential for the formation of fruits and seeds. Without insects, many plants would not be able to reproduce effectively.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1

questions.text: What precautions should be taken while making an insect collection?
questions.answer: We should never touch live insects, eggs, or nests. Only fallen specimens on the ground should be collected. Tools like scissors and needles must be used carefully and under elder supervision.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1

questions.text: Why are animals that live in groups better protected?
questions.answer: Animals living in groups can detect danger more easily, protect each other, and work together to find food. They can also take care of young ones collectively, which increases their chances of survival.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1

questions.text: Why do birds like the Coppersmith Barbet sing in the afternoon?
questions.answer: Birds like the Coppersmith Barbet sing in the afternoon to communicate, mark their territory, and attract mates. This behaviour is part of their daily activity pattern.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: In the Wonderful World of Animals
questions.text: Why are insects important for the environment?
questions.answer: Insects are important because they help in decomposing dead matter, pollinating plants, and serving as food for many birds and animals. They play a key role in maintaining ecological balance.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1

questions.text: Why should we not throw stones at honeycombs?
questions.answer: We should not throw stones at honeycombs because it can harm or kill honeybees, destroy their home, and stop the production of honey and wax. Honeybees are useful insects that help in pollination.

questions.text: Describe the observation of a bird based on the points: name, date, time, size, beak shape and colour, head, neck, back, feet colour and structure, and what the bird was doing.
questions.answer: On July 3, at 8:00 AM, I observed a Kingfisher (Khandya). It was larger than a sparrow but smaller than a crow. Its beak was long and thick (stout) and reddish-pink in colour. The head was brown, the neck was white, and the back was blue. The feet were reddish-pink and short-legged. At the time of observation, the bird was sitting on a branch and eating a fish. This careful observation helps us understand the bird’s features and behaviour.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: In the Wonderful World of Animals
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain how animals depend on each other for food with the help of a food chain.
questions.answer: All living things depend on each other for food, forming a food chain. Plants make their own food using sunlight, air, water, and soil. Herbivores like deer and rabbits eat plants. Carnivores like frogs eat insects, and snakes eat frogs. Eagles eat snakes, making them top consumers. When one link is affected, the whole chain gets disturbed. For example, if insects disappear, frogs will have no food, and then snakes and eagles will suffer. This shows how every living being is connected in nature.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: In the Wonderful World of Animals
questions.text: Explain the life cycle of a butterfly.
questions.answer: The life cycle of a butterfly has four stages: egg, larva (caterpillar), pupa (chrysalis), and adult. The female butterfly lays eggs on leaves. After hatching, the larva eats leaves and grows rapidly. Then it forms a pupa, inside which it transforms into an adult butterfly. Finally, the adult emerges, dries its wings, and flies off to feed on nectar and lay eggs. This cycle continues generation after generation.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: In the Wonderful World of Animals
questions.text: Explain how animals that live in groups benefit from this behaviour.
questions.answer: Animals living in groups can find food more easily by working together. They can protect each other from predators by staying alert and giving warning signals. Group living helps in taking care of young ones, as multiple adults can look after them. It also increases chances of survival during harsh weather or food scarcity. Examples include ants in colonies, deer in herds, and fish in schools.

questions.text: Describe the basic elements of a map and their importance.
questions.answer: The basic elements of a map are title, direction, index, and scale. The title tells us what the map is about. Direction helps us orient the map correctly, usually with north at the top. The index explains the meaning of symbols and signs used on the map. The scale shows the ratio between distance on the map and actual distance on the ground. These elements make a map easy to read, understand, and use for locating places and measuring distances.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Write about the geographical diversity of Maharashtra.
questions.answer: Maharashtra has diverse geographical features. The western part has the Sahyadri mountain ranges, also known as Western Ghats. The coastal strip is called Konkan, with beautiful beaches. The central part is the Maharashtra plateau, part of the Deccan Plateau. The eastern part consists of the plains of Vidarbha. The state also has rivers like Godavari, and hill ranges such as Ajintha and Satmala. This diversity supports varied agriculture, climate, and natural resources.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how to prepare a map of your school premises.
questions.answer: To prepare a map of your school premises, first observe the layout and list all important features like buildings, playground, flagpole, and gates. Use signs and symbols to represent them, following conventional signs. Decide on a scale, for example, 1 cm = 1 meter, and measure the actual lengths to draw them on paper. Show direction with an arrow pointing north. Include a title, index explaining the symbols, and the scale used. Colour different features appropriately, like green for playground and grey for buildings.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the importance of conventional signs and symbols in map reading.
questions.answer: Conventional signs and symbols make maps easy to read and understand universally. They represent complex features like rivers, roads, and buildings in a simple visual form. Using standard symbols ensures that anyone reading the map can interpret it correctly, regardless of language. They help avoid clutter and make the map neat and informative. Symbols are explained in the index so users can refer to them when needed.

questions.answer: The diversity in forests of Maharashtra is due to uneven distribution of rainfall across the state. Areas with high rainfall have evergreen forests, while low rainfall areas have thorny and shrub forests.

questions.text: Describe the different types of forests found in Maharashtra and where they are located.
questions.answer: Maharashtra has five main types of forests: evergreen, semi-evergreen, deciduous, thorny, and mangrove. Evergreen forests are found in the Western Ghats with high rainfall. Semi-evergreen forests are on the eastern and western slopes of the Sahyadri. Deciduous forests are in Konkan, eastern low rainfall regions, and Satpura plateau. Thorny and shrub forests are in rain shadow areas with less than 600 mm rainfall. Mangrove forests are found along the coastal intertidal zones. The type of forest depends on the amount of rainfall received in the region.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Write about the major crops grown in Maharashtra and the regions where they are grown.
questions.answer: In Maharashtra, rice is grown in high rainfall areas like Konkan and Western Ghats. Jowar, bajra, maize, and pulses are grown in low rainfall plateau regions. Sugarcane and cotton are major commercial crops grown in areas with irrigation, such as Marathwada and Western Maharashtra. Fruits like mango, banana, orange, and grape are grown in specific districts: mango in Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg, orange in Nagpur, banana in Jalgaon, and grapes in Nashik. The type of crop depends on climate, soil, and water availability.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the difference between solar energy and bioenergy.
questions.answer: Solar energy is obtained from the light and heat of the sun, using solar panels to generate electricity. Bioenergy is produced from organic waste like animal excreta, agricultural residue, or plant material through processes like fermentation or combustion. Solar energy is available during daytime and depends on sunlight, while bioenergy can be produced continuously as long as organic waste is available. Solar energy does not produce pollution, whereas bioenergy may produce some emissions during processing. Both are renewable sources of energy used in Maharashtra for sustainable development.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain why evergreen forests are found in the Western Ghats of Maharashtra.
questions.answer: Evergreen forests are found in the Western Ghats because this region receives high rainfall, often more than 3000 mm annually, due to its location on the windward side of the mountains. The heavy and consistent rainfall supports dense vegetation with trees that retain their leaves throughout the year. The warm and humid climate allows a wide variety of flora and fauna to thrive. Trees like jackfruit, jambul, bamboo, and nagchampa are commonly found here. These forests are rich in biodiversity and help in soil and water conservation.

questions.text: Name one facility that is better in urban areas compared to rural areas.
questions.answer: Medical facilities are easily available in urban areas.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What is a traffic garden?
questions.answer: A traffic garden is an open space with models of signals and roads to teach children traffic rules while they play.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Give one example of modern means of transport mentioned in the text.
questions.answer: Mumbai-Pune Expressway is an example of modern transport.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Write the difference between facilities in urban and rural areas.
questions.answer: In urban areas, facilities like roads, electricity, water supply, transportation, communication, medical and educational services are better and more advanced. In rural areas, such facilities are limited; primary health centers and schools up to secondary level are available, but for higher education, one must go to the city. Urban areas have markets and malls, while rural areas offer a natural and pollution-free life.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: List the modern and traditional means of communication.
questions.answer: Traditional means of communication include post, newspaper, telephone, television and radio. Modern means include mobile phones, Internet, e-mail, computers and artificial satellites.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What solutions would you suggest to reduce traffic congestion?
questions.answer: To reduce traffic congestion, people should use public transport, follow traffic rules, avoid using mobile phones while driving, and use helmets. Carpooling and using bicycles for short distances can also help. Governments should build more roads and expressways and promote awareness about traffic safety.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How does geographical location affect the means of transport?
questions.answer: In mountainous regions, only road transport is used due to steep slopes. In plateaus and plains, road and rail transport are common because of flat terrain. In coastal areas, water transport is used via seas and river beds. Air transport connects large cities and requires airports and runways.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why does transportation and travel take less time now than before?
questions.answer: Transportation takes less time now because of the development of modern means like expressways, highways, and air transport. Infrastructure such as the Mumbai-Pune Expressway and Atal Setu Sea Link allows faster movement. Improved vehicles and better roads also reduce travel time.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we follow traffic rules?
questions.answer: We should follow traffic rules to ensure our own safety and that of others. Following rules reduces the chances of accidents and increases overall safety on the roads. It also helps in smooth flow of traffic and prevents chaos.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are mobile phones being used for communication on a large scale today?
questions.answer: Mobile phones are used widely because they are portable, allow instant communication, and have access to internet and apps. They are affordable and available even in remote areas. Their network is spread across the world, making communication easy and fast.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Describe the changes in means of transport over time with examples from your surroundings.
questions.answer: Earlier, people used bullock carts, bicycles, and boats for transport. Now, we have buses, trains, cars, and metro systems. Highways like the Mumbai-Pune Expressway and sea links like Atal Setu have made travel faster. Air transport connects distant cities quickly. In rural areas, tractors and autorickshaws are common. These changes have reduced travel time and made transport more comfortable and accessible.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Explain how modern means of communication have changed the way we live and work.
questions.answer: Modern communication like mobile phones, internet, and e-mail has made it possible to send messages instantly across the world. People can now work from home, attend online classes, and conduct business meetings through video calls. Farmers use mobile apps to check crop prices, and traders use the internet for online sales. It has brought people closer, saved time, and made access to information easy. However, it should be used wisely to avoid misuse.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Transportation
questions.answer: Transportation is the movement of passengers and goods from one place to another using various means such as road, rail, air or water.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Communication
questions.answer: Communication is the process of obtaining information and conveying it to others through means such as letters, telephone, television, mobile phones or internet.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how geographical factors influence the choice of transport in different regions.
questions.answer: Geographical factors like terrain, slope, and water bodies affect the type of transport used. In mountainous areas with steep slopes, only road transport is feasible. In flat plateaus and plains, both road and rail transport are common due to ease of construction. Coastal areas use water transport via seas and river beds for moving goods and people. Air transport is used between large cities where speed is essential and requires airports. Thus, the landscape determines the most suitable mode of transport.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the importance of following traffic rules with reference to safety and accident prevention.
questions.answer: Following traffic rules is essential for maintaining safety on the roads for everyone—drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists. Rules like stopping at red lights, wearing helmets, and not using phones while driving help prevent accidents. When people follow rules, traffic flows smoothly, reducing jams and confusion. Traffic gardens teach children these rules early so they grow up to be responsible citizens. Thus, traffic rules protect lives and promote orderly movement.

questions.answer: We should save energy to conserve resources and reduce pollution.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: List three forms of energy and give one example of each.
questions.answer: Three forms of energy are solar energy (from the sun), wind energy (from moving air), and heat energy (from fire or the sun).

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What are magnetic and non-magnetic substances? Give one example of each.
questions.answer: Magnetic substances are attracted to a magnet, e.g., iron. Non-magnetic substances are not attracted to a magnet, e.g., wood or plastic.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How does a solar water heater work?
questions.answer: A solar water heater uses sunlight to heat water. The sun's energy is absorbed by black panels, which transfer heat to the water stored in a tank.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we feel hungry again after some time even after eating breakfast?
questions.answer: We feel hungry again because our body uses the energy from food to do work, and when that energy is used up, we need more food to regain energy.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it advised to switch off lights and fans when not in use?
questions.answer: It is advised to switch off lights and fans when not in use to save electrical energy. This helps in reducing energy wastage and lowers electricity bills. Conserving energy also protects the environment by reducing pollution from power plants.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why does a shadow disappear on Zero Shadow Day?
questions.answer: On Zero Shadow Day, the sun is exactly overhead at noon, so its rays fall vertically downward. Since there is no angle, opaque objects do not block light sideways, and thus no shadow is formed on the ground.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are solar cookers useful in villages?
questions.answer: Solar cookers are useful in villages because they use free sunlight to cook food, reducing the need for firewood or gas. They are eco-friendly and help prevent deforestation and smoke-related health issues.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain how energy from the sun is useful in our daily life. Give at least three examples.
questions.answer: The sun gives us solar energy, which is very useful in daily life. Sunlight helps plants grow through photosynthesis, which gives us food and oxygen. Solar energy is used in solar water heaters to get hot water without electricity. Solar lights charge during the day and glow at night, saving electricity. In villages, solar cookers are used to cook food using sunlight, saving fuel. Thus, solar energy helps in cooking, lighting, heating, and growing food, making our life easier and cleaner.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe an activity to show that light travels in a straight line. What do you observe?
questions.answer: Take three cardboard sheets with a small hole in the center of each. Place them in a straight line and put a candle on one side. Look from the other side—you will see the flame. Now, move the middle card slightly out of line. The flame disappears from view. This shows that light travels only in a straight line and cannot bend. If the path is not straight, light is blocked and we cannot see the object. This activity proves that light propagation is rectilinear.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how wind energy is used to generate electricity.
questions.answer: Wind energy is harnessed using windmills. When wind blows, it rotates the blades of the windmill. This rotation turns a shaft connected to a generator. The generator converts the mechanical energy into electrical energy. This electricity is then stored or supplied to homes and schools for use.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the formation of a shadow with the help of an example.
questions.answer: A shadow is formed when light cannot pass through an opaque object. For example, when you stand in sunlight, your body blocks the light rays. The area behind you where light does not reach appears dark—this is your shadow. The shape of the shadow depends on the angle of the light source. Shadows are longer in the morning and evening and shortest at noon.

questions.answer: बंधारा नदीचा प्रवाह अडवण्यासाठी व शेतात पाणी साठवण्यासाठी बांधले जाते. होद पाणी साठवण्यासाठी तळ म्हणून बनवले जाते, ज्यातील पाणी पिण्यासाठी, शेतीसाठी व बांधकामासाठी वापरला जातो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पिण्यासाठी उपलब्ध पाण्याची कमी का वाटते?
questions.answer: पृथ्वीवर उपलब्ध पाण्यामध्ये बहुतेक पाण्य महासागर व समुद्रात सामलेले आहेत, ज्यामध्ये लवण असल्याने पिण्यासाठी योग्य नाही. पिण्यायोग्य पाण्याचा फक्त १ टक्केपासून कमी भाग उपलब्ध आहे, त्यामुळे त्याची कमी वाटते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याचा अपव्यय टाळण्यासाठी घरात काय करावे?
questions.answer: घरात पिण्यासाठी वापरासाठी भरून ठेवलेले पाणी कधीही शिळे होऊ नये हे लक्षात ठेवावे. पाण्याचा वापर काटकसरीने करणे, जेथे शक्य आहे तेथे पाणी साठवणे व शक्य तेथे पुनर्वापर करणे हे उपाये अपव्यय टाळण्यासाठी केल्या जातात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: बारामोट्याची विहीर कशी विशेष आहे?
questions.answer: बारामोट्याची विहीर शिवकालीन स्थापत्यशास्त्राचा उत्कृष्ट नमुना आहे. यात दगडी बांधकाम, भरपूर पायऱ्या आणि प्रशस्त महालासारखी रचना दिसते, ज्यामुळे पर्यटक नेहमी गर्दी करतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाणी अमूल्य आहे का?
questions.answer: पाणी अमूल्य आहे कारण कोणताही सजीव पाण्याशिवाय जिवंत राहू शकत नाही. पाणी पिण्यासाठी, शेतीसाठी, बांधकामासाठी व दैनंदिन जीवनात सर्व कृतींमध्ये आवश्यक आहे. पिण्यासाठी उपलब्ध पाण्याची फक्त १ टक्केपासून कमी मात्रा आहे, त्यामुळे त्याचे योग्य वापर करणे आवश्यक आहे.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पिण्यासाठी उपलब्ध पाणी का खूप कमी आहे?
questions.answer: पिण्यासाठी उपलब्ध पाणी खूप कमी आहे कारण पृथ्वीवर उपलब्ध पाण्यामध्ये ९७ टक्के पाणी महासागर व समुद्रात आहे, ज्यामध्ये लवण असल्याने पिण्यासाठी योग्य नाही. शेष ३ टक्के पाण्यामधील फक्त १ टक्केपासून कमी पिण्यायोग्य पाणी उपलब्ध आहे, ज्यामुही त्याची कमी वाटते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याचा अपव्यय टाळणे का आवश्यक आहे?
questions.answer: पाण्याचा अपव्यय टाळणे आवश्यक आहे कारण पिण्यासाठी उपलब्ध पाणी खूप कमी आहे. पाण्याचा अनावश्यक वापर करण्याने भविष्यात पाणीची कमी होऊ शकते, ज्यामुळे जीवंत राहणे कठीण होऊ शकतो. त्यामुळे पाण्याचा योग्य व काटकसरीने वापर करणे हवे.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याचा महत्त्व सांगा व त्याचे अपव्यय टाळण्यासाठी उपाये लिहा.
questions.answer: पाणी जीवनाचा आधार आहे. कोणताही सजीव पाण्याशिवाय जिवंत राहू शकत नाही. पाणी पिण्यासाठी, शेतीसाठी, बांधकामासाठी व दैनंदिन जीवनात सर्व कृतींमध्ये वापरला जातो. पृथ्वीवर उपलब्ध पाण्यामध्ये बहुतेक पाणी महासागर व समुद्रात आहे, ज्यामध्ये लवण असल्याने पिण्यासाठी योग्य नाही. पिण्यायोग्य पाण्याचा फक्त १ टक्केपासून कमी भाग उपलब्ध आहे. त्यामुळे पाण्याचा अपव्यय टाळणे आवश्यक आहे. अपव्यय टाळण्यासाठी पाण्याचा वापर काटकसरीने करणे, जेथे शक्य आहे तेथे पाणी साठवणे, शक्य तेथे पाणी पुनर्वापर करणे व घरात पिण्यासाठी भरून ठेवलेले पाणी कधीही शिळे होऊ नये हे लक्षात ठेवणे हे उपाये आहेत.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: बांधणे, तलाव व होद यांचे स्वरूप व उद्देश सांगा.
questions.answer: बांधणे म्हणजे नदीचा वाहते पाणी अडवण्यासाठी दगडांचे किंवा मातीचे बंधारे बांधणे. यातील पाणी शेतात साठवला जातो व ओढ्याचा प्रवाह थांबवला जातो. तलाव व टाके पूर्वीच्या काळी किल्ल्यावर राहणाऱ्या लोकांसाठी खोदले जायचे थेट पाण्य साठवण्याचे साधन आहेत, ज्यातील पाणी वर्षभर वापरला जातो. होद म्हणजे पाणी साठवण्यासाठी तळ, ज्यातील पाणी पिण्यासाठी, शेतीसाठी व बांधकामासाठी वापरला जातो. यातील सर्व पाण्य साठवण्याचे साधन पाण्याचा अपव्यय टाळण्यासाठी व पाण्याचे योग्य वापर करण्यासाठी उपयुक्त आहेत.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: बंधारा
questions.answer: बंधारा म्हणजे नदीचा वाहते पाणी अडवण्यासाठी दगडांचे किंवा मातीचे बंधारे बांधणे, ज्यातील पाणी शेतात साठवण्यासाठी व ओढ्याचा प्रवाह थांबवण्यासाठी वापरला जातो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: होद
questions.answer: होद म्हणजे पाणी साठवण्यासाठी वापरले जाने वाला तळ, ज्यातील पाणी पिण्यासाठी, शेतीसाठी व बांधकामासाठी वापरला जातो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पिण्यासाठी उपलब्ध पाण्याची कमी दर्शविण्यासाठी पिंपात मावण्याची कल्पना कशीच मदत करते?
questions.answer: पिण्यासाठी उपलब्ध पाण्याची कमी दर्शविण्यासाठी पिंपात मावण्याची कल्पना केली जाते. यामुळे पृथ्वीवर उपलब्ध सर्व पाणी एका पिंपात मावत असेल मानले जाते. तेव्हा गोडे पाणी केवळ कपभर होईल व नद्या, नाले, विहिरी, धरणे, तलाव यांमधील पिण्यायोग्य पाणी केवळ थेंबभर असेल. यामुळे विद्यार्थ्यांना पिण्यासाठी उपलब्ध पाण्याची खूप कमी मात्रा स्पष्टपणे वाटते व त्याचे योग्य वापर करण्याचे महत्त्व समजते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याचा अपव्यय टाळण्यासाठी घरात काय करावे हे सांगा.
questions.answer: पाण्याचा अपव्यय टाळण्यासाठी घरात काही उपाये केल्या जातात. पहिल्यांदाच पिण्यासाठी वापरासाठी भरून ठेवलेले पाणी कधीही शिळे होऊ नये हे लक्षात ठेवावे. दुसऱ्या, पाण्याचा वापर काटकसरीने करणे, अर्थात फक्त आवश्यक प्रमाणातच वापर करणे. तिसऱ्या, जेथे शक्य आहे तेथे पाणी साठवणे, जसे की शेवटचा पाणी वापरासाठी वापरणे. चौथे, शक्य तेथे पाणी पुनर्वापर करणे, जसे की पळण्याने वापरलेले पाणी बागातील पाण्यासाठी वापरणे. यांचे पालन करण्याने पाण्याचा अपव्यय टाळला जाऊ शकतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याचे पुनर्वापर करणे म्हणजे वापरलेले पाणी _______ करणे.
questions.answer: पुन्हा वापरणे

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: निर्मळ पाण्याला _______ पाणी असे म्हणतात.
questions.answer: निर्धोक

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याचे संवर्धन म्हणजे पावसाचे पाणी _______ करणे.
questions.answer: साठवणे

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: मातीची सुपीकता वाढवण्यासाठी _______ खतांचा वापर केला पाहिजे.
questions.answer: सेंद्रिय

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: हृदय आपल्या छातीच्या _______ भागात असतो.
questions.answer: डाव्या

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याचे पुनर्वापर करणे आवश्यक नाही.
questions.answer: चूक

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: माती तयार होण्यासाठी खूप वर्षे लागतात.
questions.answer: बरोबर

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: जीभ बाह्येंद्रिय आहे.
questions.answer: चूक

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: फुप्फुस शरीरात ऑक्सिजन पुरवण्याचे काम करते.
questions.answer: बरोबर

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: खालील बायांमध्ये सही जोडा लावा.
questions.answer: गाळणे – मातीचे कण वेगळा होतो, निवळणे – कचरा तळाशी जातो, उकळणे – जंतू नष्ट होतात, निर्जंतुकीकरण – ब्लिचिंग पावडर टाकते

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याचा सर्वात महत्त्वाचा उपयोग कोणता?
questions.answer: पिण्यासाठी

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: खालीलपैकी कोणती माती पाणी धरून ठेवते?
questions.answer: चिकणमाती

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: हृदयाचा मुख्य कार्य कोणता?
questions.answer: शरीरभर रक्त खेळते ठेवणे

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: माती प्रदूषणाचा खालीलपैकी कोणती कारण नाही?
questions.answer: जमिनीवर वनस्पती वाढवणे

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याचे संवर्धन करण्याचा एक उपाय सांगा.
questions.answer: साठवणे

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: मातीची सुपीकता कमी होण्याचा एक कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: प्रदूषण

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: हृदय आपल्या कोणत्या भागात असतो?
questions.answer: छाती

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: फुप्फुसांची संख्या किती?
questions.answer: दोन

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: जठराचा कार्य कोणता?
questions.answer: अन्न घुसळणे

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: निर्मळ पाणी म्हणजे काय?
questions.answer: निर्मळ पाणी म्हणजे जो पिण्यासाठी स्वच्छ व सुरक्षित असतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याचे पुनर्वापर करणे आवश्यक का?
questions.answer: होय, कारण पाणी एक महत्त्वाचा नैसर्गिक संसाधन आहे.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: मातीचा संरक्षण करणे आवश्यक का?
questions.answer: होय, कारण माती तयार होण्यासाठी खूप वर्षे लागतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: हृदयाचा कार्य कोणता?
questions.answer: हृदय शरीरभर रक्त खेळते ठेवण्याचा काम करते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: फुप्फुसांचा कार्य कोणता?
questions.answer: फुप्फुस शरीरात ऑक्सिजन पुरवण्याचे काम करते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाणी निर्धोक करण्याच्या पद्धती सांगा.
questions.answer: पाणी निर्धोक करण्याच्या पद्धती गाळणे, निवळणे, उकळणे व निर्जंतुकीकरण आहेत. गाळणे मातीचे कण वेगळा करते, निवळणे कचरा तळाशी जातो, उकळणे जंतू नष्ट करते, निर्जंतुकीकरण ब्लिचिंग पावडर किंवा क्लोरीन टाकता यामुळे होतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: माती प्रदूषणाची कारणे सांगा.
questions.answer: माती प्रदूषण रासायनिक खतांचे अतिवापर, कारखान्यातील विषारी पदार्थ व कचरा मातीत मिसळणे, कीटकनाशके यांचे वापर यामुळे होतो. यामुळे मातीची सुपीकता कमी होते व ती दूषित होते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: आंतरेंद्रiye काय? उदाहरण सांगा.
questions.answer: आंतरेंद्रiye म्हणजे शरीरात असणारी आणि बाहेरून न दिसणारी इंद्रiye. उदा. मेंदू, हृदय, फुप्फुस, यकृत, जठर, अन्ननलिका, लहान आतडे, मोठे आतडे, मलाशय, गुदद्वार.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पावसाच्या पाण्याचे संवर्धन कसे केतात?
questions.answer: पावसाच्या पाण्याचे संवर्धन पावसाचे पाणी साठवून जमिनीतील पाण्याची पातळी वाढवण्यासाठी केला जातो. शेततळी खोदली जाऊन, डोंगर उतारावर चर खणले जातात. यामुळे पावसाचे पाणी मातीमध्ये घुसते व पातळी वाढते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: का? / Give reason शैलीत उत्तर लिहा.
questions.text: हृदय आपल्या छातीच्या डाव्या भागात असतो का?
questions.answer: हृदय आपल्या छातीच्या डाव्या भागात असतो कारण त्याचा आकार व आकार असे असते की तो डाव्या भागात सोयले जाते. हृदय पंपाप्रमाणे काम करते व रक्त पंप करण्यासाठी त्याला डाव्या भागात ठेवणे सोयते. हृदयाच्या डाव्या भागात असण्याने रक्त वाहिन्यांमध्ये सोयता हात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाणी निर्धोक करण्याच्या पद्धती व त्याचे महत्त्व सांगा.
questions.answer: पाणी निर्धोक करण्याच्या पद्धती गाळणे, निवळणे, उकळणे व निर्जंतुकीकरण आहेत. गाळणे पाण्यातील मातीचे कण व इतर कचरा वेगळा करते. निवळणे पाण्यातील सूक्ष्म कण तळाशी जाऊन पाणी स्पष्ट करतो. उकळणे १० ते १५ मिनिटे पाणी उकळण्याने पाण्यातील जंतू नष्ट होतात. निर्जंतुकीकरण पाण्यात ब्लिचिंग पावडर किंवा क्लोरीन टाकण्याने जंतू नष्ट करणे. यामुळे पाणी पिण्यास सुरक्षित होतो व पोटदुखी, जुलाब आजार टाळता येतात. पाणी निर्धोक करणे आवश्यक आहे कारण निर्मळ पाणी पिण्यासाठी स्वच्छ व सुरक्षित असतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: माती प्रदूषणाची कारणे व त्याचे उपाय सांगा.
questions.answer: माती प्रदूषण रासायनिक खतांचे अतिवापर, कारखान्यातील विषारी पदार्थ व कचरा मातीत मिसळणे, कीटकनाशके यांचे वापर यामुळे होतो. यामुळे मातीची सुपीकता कमी होते व ती दूषित होते. माती प्रदूषण रोकण्यासाठी सेंद्रिय खतांचा वापर केला पाहिजे, रासायनिक खतांचे वापर कम करणे, कचरा सोयट करणे व रिसायकल करणे, कारखान्यातील कचरा प्रक्रिया करणे, मातीचा संरक्षण करणे व जैविक खेती करणे ये उपाय केला पाहिजे. मातीचा संरक्षण करणे आवश्यक आहे कारण माती तयार होण्यासाठी खूप वर्षे लागतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: निर्मळ पाणी परिभाषित करा.
questions.answer: निर्मळ पाणी म्हणजे जो पिण्यासाठी स्वच्छ व सुरक्षित असतो, त्यामुळे पोटदुखी, जुलाब आजार टाळता येतात व शरीर निरोगी राहते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: आंतरेंद्रiye परिभाषित करा.
questions.answer: आंतरेंद्रiye म्हणजे शरीरात असणारी आणि बाहेरून न दिसणारी इंद्रiye.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: हृदयाचे कार्य स्पष्ट करा.
questions.answer: हृदय आपल्या छातीच्या डाव्या भागात असतो. ते आपल्या हाताच्या बंद मुठीएवढे असते. ते पंपाप्रमाणे काम करते. शरीरभर पसरलेल्या रक्तवाहिन्यांतून रक्त खेळते ठेवण्याचे काम हृदय करते. हृदय रक्त पंप करून शरीरातील सर्व अंगांपर्यंत पोहोचवतो. हृदय व फुप्फुस यांची कामे एकमेकांवर अवलंबून असतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याचे संवर्धन कसे केतात?
questions.answer: पावसाच्या पाण्याचे संवर्धन म्हणजे पावसाचे पाणी साठवून जमिनीतील पाण्याची पातळी वाढवणे. पावसाचे पाणी दगडधोंड्यांतून वाहून जाते परंतु मातीमध्ये ते मुरते. मातीमध्ये पाणी धरून ठेवण्याची क्षमता असते. शेततळी खोदली जाऊन पाणी मातीमध्ये घुसतो. डोंगर उतारावर चर खणले जातात. यामुळे पावसाचे पाणी मातीमध्ये संग्रहित होतो व पातळी वाढते.

questions.answer: पौर्णिमा

questions.answer: बर्फ, धूळ आणि खडक

questions.answer: पृथ्वी

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: चंद्राच्या प्रकाशित भागाची कमी होण्याचा प्रक्रिया काय म्हणतात?
questions.answer: कृष्ण पक्ष

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: तारे आणि ग्रह यातील मूलभूत फरक काय आहे?
questions.answer: तारे स्वतःच्या प्रकाशाने चमकतात, तर ग्रहांचे प्रकाश नसतो त्यांना सूर्यापासून मिळतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पृथ्वीला सूर्याभोवती एक फेरी पूर्ण करण्यास किती वेळ लागते?
questions.answer: पृथ्वीला सूर्याभोवती एक फेरी पूर्ण करण्यास सुमारे ३६५ दिवस लागतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: चंद्रकला म्हणजे काय?
questions.answer: चंद्रकला म्हणजे चंद्राच्या रोज बदलत्या आकारे.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: अमावस्या कधी होते?
questions.answer: अमावस्या चंद्राचा प्रकाशित भाग सर्वात कमी झाल्यामुळे चंद्र दिसत नाही तेव्हा होते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्योदय आणि सूर्यास्त यामधील काळा काय म्हणतात?
questions.answer: सूर्योदयापासून सूर्यास्तापर्यंत आपल्याला सूर्यप्रकाश मिळतो त्या काळास 'दिन' म्हणतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्यमालेतील अंतर्गृह ग्रहांची नावे लिहा.
questions.answer: सूर्यमालेतील अंतर्गृह ग्रह बुध, शुक्र, पृथ्वी आणि मंगळ आहेत.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: धूमकेतू काय आहे? त्याचे एक उदाहरण द्या.
questions.answer: धूमकेतू बर्फ, धूळ आणि खडक यांनी बनेले खगोलीय पिंड आहेत. उदाहरणार्थ हॅलेचा धूमकेतू.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: लघुग्रह काय आहे? ते कोणत्या भागात मिळतात?
questions.answer: लघुग्रह मंगळ व गुरू ग्रहांच्या दरम्यान असलेले लहान खगोलांचे पट्टा आहेत. ते सूर्याभोवती फिरतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पृथ्वीchwकी स्वत:भोवती फिरण्याच्या गतीला काय म्हणतात?
questions.answer: पृथ्वीchwकी स्वत:भोवती फिरण्याच्या गतीला 'दैनिक गती' किंवा 'परिवलन' म्हणतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पृथ्वीवर दिवस आणि रात्र कसे होतात?
questions.answer: पृथ्वी गोलाकार असल्यामुळे सूर्यप्रकाश पृथ्वीच्या अर्ध्या भागावरच पडतो. प्रकाशित भागात दिवस असे, अंधार भागात रात्र असे असते. पृथ्वींच्या स्वत:भोवती फिरण्यामुळे हा भाग बदलतो, त्यामुळे दिवस व रात्र होतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: ग्रह स्वतःच्या प्रकाशाने चमकत नाहीत का?
questions.answer: ग्रह स्वतःच्या प्रकाशाने चमकत नाहीत कारण त्यांचे आतंरिक तापने प्रकाश उत्पादन करण्याकाफी असत नाही. त्यांना प्रकाश सूर्यापासून मिळतो आणि त्याच प्रकाशाचे परावर्तन होतो. त्यामुळे ग्रह तार्यांपेक्षा कम चमकतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: चंद्राच्या आकारात रोज बदल येते का?
questions.answer: चंद्र पृथ्वीभोवती फिरतो त्यामुळे त्याचा प्रकाशित भाग पृथ्वीवरून वेगवेगळ्या दिशांपासून दिसतो. चंद्राचा सूर्याकडील भाग प्रकाशात असे, पृथ्वीकडील भाग अंधार असतो. त्यामुळे पृथ्वीवरून दिसणारा भाग रोज बदलतो, त्यामुळे चंद्रकला बदलते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्यमाला काय आहे? त्याचे मुख्य घटकं व त्यांची भूमिका सांगा.
questions.answer: सूर्यमाला सूर्य व त्याबोवती फिरणारे ग्रह, उपग्रह, लघुग्रह, बटुग्रह, धूमकेतू व इतर पिंडांचे संग्रह आहे. सूर्य तारा असून प्रकाश व उष्णता देता. ग्रह सूर्याभोवती फिरतात, उपग्रह ग्रहांभोवती फिरतात. लघुग्रह मंगळ-गुरू दरम्यान पट्टा निर्माण करतात, बटुग्रह स्वतंत्रपणे सूर्याभोवती फिरतात, धूमकेतू बर्फ-धूळ-खडक यांनी बनेले असतात. सूर्यमाला हा खगोलीय पिंडांचे समूह आहे ज्यामध्ये सूर्य केंद्रस्थान आहे.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: चंद्रकला काय आहे? त्यांचे प्रकार व कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: चंद्रकला म्हणजे चंद्राच्या रोज बदलत्या आकारे. चंद्र पृथ्वीभोवती फिरतो, त्यामुळे त्याचा प्रकाशित भाग पृथ्वीवरून वेगवेगळ्या प्रमाणात दिसतो. अमावस्येपासून पौर्णिमेपर्यंत प्रकाशित भाग वाढतो हे शुक्ल पक्ष, पौर्णिमेपासून अमावस्येपर्यंत कमी होतो हे कृष्ण पक्ष. चंद्रकला अमावस्या, प्रतिपदा, चतुर्थी, अष्टमी, दशमी, एकादशी, पौर्णिमा इतीखाली असते. हा बदल चंद्राच्या कक्षेच्या स्थितीचा परिणाम आहे.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: ग्रह
questions.answer: ग्रह हा आकाशी पिंड आहे जो स्वतःच्या प्रकाशाने चमकत नाही, तर सूर्याभोवती फिरतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: तारा
questions.answer: तारा हा आकाशी पिंड आहे जो स्वतःच्या प्रकाशाने चमकतो, उध्या ऊष्मा व प्रकाश उत्पादन करतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: परिभ्रमण व वार्षिक गती यांचे फरक स्पष्ट करा.
questions.answer: परिभ्रमण म्हणजे पृथ्वीchwकी स्वत:भोवती फिरण्याची गती, ज्यामुळे दिवस व रात्र होतो. वार्षिक गती म्हणजे पृथ्वीchwकी सूर्याभोवती फिरण्याची गती, ज्यामुळे एक वर्ष पूर्ण होतो. परिभ्रमण एक दिवसात होतो, वार्षिक गती ३६५ दिवसात होतो. परिभ्रमणचे अक्ष ध्रुवांमधील रेषा आहे, वार्षिक गतीचे पथ कक्षेवर असतो. हा फरक पृथ्वीchwकी दोन प्रकारची गती दर्शवतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्यमालेतील ग्रहांचे क्रम सूर्यापासूनच्या अंतरानुसार सांगा.
questions.answer: सूर्यापासूनच्या अंतरानुसार सूर्यमालेतील ग्रहांचे क्रम खालीलप्रमाणे आहे: बुध (०.३८७ AU), शुक्र (०.७२३ AU), पृथ्वी (१.००० AU), मंगळ (१.५२४ AU), गुरू (५.२०३ AU), शनि (९.५३९ AU), युरेनस (१९.१८२ AU), नेपच्यून (३०.०५८ AU). १ खगोलीय एकक (AU) म्हणजे पृथ्वीचे सूर्यापासूनचे सरासरी अंतर १४९ दशलक्ष किमी. हा क्रम सूर्यापासून जवळच्या ग्रहांपासून सुरू होत दूरच्या ग्रहांपर्यंत जाते.

questions.answer: प्रकाशसंश्लेषण

questions.answer: सोटमूळ

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: फुलातील रंग व वास _______ ला आकर्षित करतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: वनस्पतींचे भाग जुळून तयार केलेली वस्तू _______ यात येतात.
