questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: Maratha Sardars – The Famous House of the Bhosales
questions.text: Describe the role of Maratha Sardars during the period of unrest.
questions.answer: During the period of unrest, Maratha Sardars had their own private armies and were employed by the Sultans of Bijapur and Ahmadnagar in their wars. They were brave and loyal to their masters but often fought for others’ interests, keeping the warlike spirit alive among the youth.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: Maratha Sardars – The Famous House of the Bhosales
questions.text: Explain how the Bhonsales of Verul became rich and powerful.
questions.answer: The Bhonsales of Verul became rich and powerful when Maloji Raje was granted the Jagir of Pune and Supe Parganas by the Shah of Nizamshah. Later, Shahaji Raje gained honour and respect in the courts of Nizamshah and Adilshah, enhancing the family’s status.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: Maratha Sardars – The Famous House of the Bhosales
questions.text: Write about the temple of Ghrushneshwar and its restoration.
questions.answer: The temple of Ghrushneshwar was about four hundred years old and had fallen into neglect, with cracked walls and deserted priests. A great devotee of Shiva visited it regularly, offered flowers and bel on the lingam, carried out extensive repairs, and arranged for its proper maintenance, restoring its lost grandeur.

questions.chapter: Maratha Sardars – The Famous House of the Bhosales
questions.text: How did Shahaji Raje show his valour and gain reputation?
questions.answer: Shahaji Raje displayed great valour in battle, fighting bravely to save Nizamshahi from the Mughal and Adilshahi armies. His courage earned him praise everywhere and enhanced his reputation in the court, even making Malik Amber jealous.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: Maratha Sardars – The Famous House of the Bhosales
questions.text: Why did Shahaji Raje leave the court of Adilshah and return to Nizamshahi?
questions.answer: Shahaji Raje left the court of Adilshah and returned to Nizamshahi because Nizamshah appealed to him to save the kingdom from the growing threat of Mughal aggression. He felt his duty lay with Nizamshahi, despite his honours in Adilshahi court.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: Maratha Sardars – The Famous House of the Bhosales
questions.text: Why did the devotee express his innermost thoughts to God at the temple?
questions.answer: The devotee expressed his innermost thoughts to God because he was a great devotee of Shiva and believed that sincere devotion and prayer at the temple would please the deity and bring blessings.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: Maratha Sardars – The Famous House of the Bhosales
questions.text: Why did the Maratha Sardars’ valour serve the interests of others?
questions.answer: The Maratha Sardars’ valour served the interests of others because they were often employed by the Sultans of Bijapur and Ahmadnagar to fight in their wars, rather than uniting to work for their own people’s welfare.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: Maratha Sardars – The Famous House of the Bhosales
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the life and achievements of Shahaji Raje as a brave Sardar and his role in the history of the Bhonsale family.
questions.answer: Shahaji Raje was a brave and capable Sardar who earned great respect in the courts of Nizamshah and later Adilshah. He was honoured with the title 'Sar Lashkar' for his military leadership. He fought valiantly to protect Nizamshahi from Mughal aggression. His marriage to Jijabai, daughter of Lakhujirao Jadhav, strengthened alliances among Maratha families. He managed the Jagir and family affairs responsibly, laying the foundation for future greatness. His reputation as a general inspired loyalty and courage in his descendants, especially Shivaji Maharaj.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: Maratha Sardars – The Famous House of the Bhosales
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain the tradition of valour among the Maratha Sardars and how it was kept alive through generations.
questions.answer: The Maratha Sardars were known for their bravery, fearlessness, and loyalty to their masters. They maintained private armies and took pride in battlefield achievements. Though they often served others, their courage inspired the youth to uphold the tradition of valour. Families like the Bhonsales, Jadhavs, and Nimbalkars passed this spirit down through generations. The temple of Ghrushneshwar’s restoration by a devotee also reflected the cultural and spiritual strength of the community. This tradition eventually contributed to the rise of leaders like Shivaji Maharaj, who united the Marathas for self-rule.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: Maratha Sardars – The Famous House of the Bhosales
questions.text: Jagir
questions.answer: A Jagir was a grant of land or revenue given by a ruler to a Sardar in recognition of his service, which made him feel like a Raja.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: Maratha Sardars – The Famous House of the Bhosales
questions.text: Sar Lashkar
questions.answer: Sar Lashkar was a title meaning 'Chief of Army', conferred by the Adilshah of Bijapur upon Shahaji Raje in honour of his military leadership.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: Maratha Sardars – The Famous House of the Bhosales
questions.text: How did the period of unrest affect the Maratha Sardars and their role in society?
questions.answer: The period of unrest saw constant warfare between the Sultans of Bijapur and Ahmadnagar, who employed Maratha Sardars and their armies for their conflicts. The Sardars, though brave and loyal, often fought for others’ interests rather than uniting for their own people. This kept the warlike spirit alive, especially among the youth, who grew up valuing bravery and military service. Over time, this environment produced many famous soldiers and leaders. The Sardars’ experience in warfare and administration later helped in the establishment of Swarajya under Shivaji Maharaj.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: Maratha Sardars – The Famous House of the Bhosales
questions.text: Describe the condition of the temple of Ghrushneshwar before its restoration and the efforts made to restore it.
questions.answer: Before restoration, the temple of Ghrushneshwar was in a neglected state, with its walls cracked and the priests having deserted it. The devotee who visited regularly felt sorrow at its condition and decided to take action. He carried out extensive repairs to bring it back to its original state. He also arranged for proper maintenance, including lighting inside and outside the temple. As a result, the lost grandeur of Ghrushneshwar was restored, and devotees could once again worship in peace.

questions.text: How did Jijabai influence Shivaji’s character during his childhood?
questions.answer: Jijabai influenced Shivaji by telling him stories of saints, great men, and brave warriors like Rama and Krishna. This instilled in him respect, honour, and a desire to display valour.

questions.text: What happened to Shahaji Raje’s Jagir after the downfall of Nizamshahi?

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shivaji feel that he should display valour like brave men?
questions.answer: Shivaji felt that he should display valour like brave men because Jijabai regularly told him stories of saints, great men, and heroic figures such as Rama, Krishna, Bhim, and Abhimanyu. These stories inspired him to be brave and courageous.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shahaji Raje leave the Moghuls and join Adilshahi services?
questions.answer: Shahaji Raje left the Moghuls because Emperor Shahjahan marched South against him and threatened Adilshah, who then joined forces with Shahjahan against Shahaji Raje. To save himself, Shahaji Raje joined Adilshahi services.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did the children of the Mavlas enjoy playing with Shivaji?
questions.answer: The children of the Mavlas enjoyed playing with Shivaji because he joined them in their games like hide and seek, ball play, and building earth forts. His friendly nature made him popular among them.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Describe Shivaji’s childhood life at Shivneri fort.
questions.answer: Shivaji spent his early childhood at Shivneri fort in unsettled times. Despite the turmoil, Jijabai lovingly educated him every evening by telling stories of Rama, Krishna, Bhim, and Abhimanyu, and singing devotional songs of saints like Namdeo and Dnyaneshwar. She also told him tales of brave men, which inspired his courage. Shivaji played with children from poor families, shared simple meals of bhakri and onion, and participated in games like hide and seek, building earth forts, and imitating animal sounds. These experiences shaped his character, instilling humility, bravery, and love for his people.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Explain how Shahaji Raje’s struggles affected Shivaji’s early life.
questions.answer: Shahaji Raje faced constant political turmoil, being caught between the Moghuls, Nizamshah, and Adilshah. He lost his Jagir, was betrayed, and had to keep shifting forts for safety. As a result, young Shivaji had a restless childhood, moving from one fort to another with his mother Jijabai. Despite this, Jijabai ensured his moral and cultural upbringing through stories and songs. Shahaji’s struggles taught Shivaji resilience and the importance of Swaraj, which later inspired him to establish an independent Maratha kingdom.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Swaraj
questions.answer: Swaraj means self-rule or independence, especially the dream of a free Maratha kingdom ruled by its own people.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Jagir
questions.answer: A Jagir was a land grant given by a king to a noble or officer in exchange for military service and administrative duties.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Explain in four or five sentences.
questions.text: Explain how the environment of Shivneri fort contributed to Shivaji’s early development.
questions.answer: Shivneri fort, located on a hill with steep cliffs and strong fortifications, provided a safe and secure environment for Shivaji’s birth and early years. Despite the political unrest outside, the fort’s strength gave Jijabai a sense of security to raise her child. The natural surroundings of hills and forests allowed Shivaji to play freely with other children. He observed nature, imitated animal sounds, and built earth forts, which developed his creativity and observation skills. The fort’s atmosphere of bravery and protection, combined with Jijabai’s teachings, nurtured his future leadership qualities.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Explain in four or five sentences.
questions.text: Explain why Jijabai’s storytelling was important for Shivaji’s character building.
questions.answer: Jijabai’s storytelling played a vital role in shaping Shivaji’s values and ambitions. By narrating tales of Rama, Krishna, Bhim, and Abhimanyu, she introduced him to ideals of courage, duty, and righteousness. Stories of saints and great men taught him humility and respect for all. These narratives inspired him to think beyond himself and prepare for a greater purpose. The emotional and moral lessons from these stories laid the foundation for his future vision of Swaraj and just rule.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: What qualities did Dadaji Konddev have as an administrator?
questions.answer: Dadaji Konddev was faithful, strict, efficient, honest, just, and a strict disciplinarian. He served with devotion and managed the Pune Jagir well.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Dadaji Konddev give concession in land tax to peasants?
questions.answer: Dadaji Konddev gave concession in land tax to peasants to encourage them to settle and cultivate the land, which had become barren due to constant attacks and fleeing of people.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Jijabai resolve that Shivaji would never serve others?
questions.answer: Jijabai resolved that Shivaji would never serve others because she wanted him to establish Swaraj — the rule of his own people — inspired by her own valor and the heroic legacy of her family.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shivaji feel happy when he returned to Pune?
questions.answer: Shivaji felt happy when he returned to Pune because he could see the lofty peaks of the Sahyadri again, reminding him of his childhood on Shivneri, and he saw the town being rebuilt under his mother’s care.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe how Shivaji’s education was shaped by both his father Shahaji Raje and his mother Jijabai.
questions.answer: Shivaji’s education began under Shahaji Raje, who appointed intelligent teachers to teach him reading, writing, Sanskrit, and warfare skills like horse riding, wrestling, and sword use. After returning to Pune, Jijabai supervised his education, teaching him moral values through stories of Rama and Krishna, inspiring him to fight injustice and establish Swaraj. She also ensured the town was rebuilt, temples repaired, and people felt safe. Together, they shaped Shivaji into a brave, just, and visionary leader ready to found the Maratha Empire.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain the role of Dadaji Konddev in the development of Pune Jagir during Shivaji’s absence.
questions.answer: Dadaji Konddev served as the Subhedar of Kondana and managed the Pune Jagir with loyalty and efficiency. He repaired the damage caused by enemies, rebuilt homes and temples, and restored peace. He introduced fair land revenue based on soil quality and gave tax concessions to encourage farming. He raised peasant patrols to protect against wolves and thieves, and his just and disciplined administration made Pune safe and prosperous again, preparing it for Shivaji’s rule.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Swaraj
questions.answer: Swaraj means self-rule or the rule of one’s own people, which Shivaji aimed to establish.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Mavlas
questions.answer: Mavlas were the loyal, hardworking, and quick-footed people of the Maval region who later became the backbone of Shivaji’s army.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how the stories of Rama and Krishna influenced Shivaji’s thinking.
questions.answer: The stories of Rama and Krishna deeply influenced Shivaji’s thinking by showing him how divine heroes fought evil and protected their people. Jijabai told him that he was a descendant of both Rama and Krishna, which inspired him to be brave and just. He began to see himself as a protector of the poor and oppressed, especially the Mavlas. These tales motivated him to stand against injustice and work toward establishing Swaraj. He remembered these heroes whether awake or asleep, striving to emulate their courage and righteousness.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how Pune was transformed from ruins to a thriving town under Jijabai’s care.
questions.answer: When Jijabai and Shivaji returned to Pune, they found it in ruins — houses destroyed, temples collapsed, fields barren, and people frightened. Jijabai took immediate action by repairing the temples and restarting morning and evening worship. She encouraged people to return, settle, and cultivate their lands. With peace restored and basic needs met, the town slowly came back to life. Soon, Pune was again throbbing with people, markets, and activity, symbolizing the dawn of Swaraj.

questions.answer: The royal seal of Shivaji denotes the welfare of the people.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: What was the ideal of Shivaji as mentioned in the chapter?
questions.answer: The ideal of Shivaji was to establish Hindavi Swaraj, where people would have their own kingdom and refuse to live as slaves. He wanted freedom for his people from foreign rule and self-rule based on justice and welfare.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: How did Shivaji win over the Deshmukhs in the Maval valley?
questions.answer: Shivaji visited the Deshmukhs, talked to them, persuaded them to stop their quarrels, and showed them an attractive picture of unity and welfare under his leadership. He won them over through dialogue and vision.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: What is the significance of Shivaji’s royal seal being in Sanskrit?
questions.answer: Shivaji’s royal seal being in Sanskrit was a significant change from the Persian seals used by other rulers. It showed his pride in Indian language and culture, and guaranteed that his government was for the welfare of the people.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shivaji feel unhappy despite the peaceful condition of his Jagir?
questions.answer: Shivaji felt unhappy because, although his Jagir was peaceful, he saw his people suffering as bondmen of foreign sultans, getting killed in wars, and living in slavery. He wanted freedom and self-rule for his people, not just peace under foreign control.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did the Mavlas take the oath of Swaraj at Raireshwar temple?
questions.answer: The Mavlas took the oath at Raireshwar temple because they were deeply inspired by Shivaji’s vision of freedom. The temple, as a sacred place, witnessed their commitment to sacrifice everything for Hindavi Swaraj and refuse to live as slaves anymore.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shivaji’s enthusiasm increase a thousandfold after meeting the Mavlas?
questions.answer: Shivaji’s enthusiasm increased because the Mavlas pledged their full support and readiness to lay down their lives for his cause. Their unity and devotion gave him strength and confidence to pursue the dream of Swaraj with greater determination.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the events that took place at Raireshwar temple and their importance in Shivaji’s life.
questions.answer: In 1645, Shivaji gathered young Mavlas at the Raireshwar temple hidden in the forest. He spoke about his dream of freedom from foreign rule and the suffering of his people. Inspired by his words, the Mavlas took an oath to establish Hindavi Swaraj, promising to work and even sacrifice their lives for this ideal. Shivaji felt renewed strength and returned to Pune to share the joy with his mother Jijabai. This event marked the beginning of organized efforts towards Swaraj, united the Mavlas under his leadership, and turned his dream into a mission. The oath at Raireshwar became a turning point in Shivaji’s life, leading to training, fortification, and eventual foundation of the Maratha Swaraj.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how Shivaji worked to unite the Deshmukhs and prepare for Swaraj after the oath at Raireshwar.
questions.answer: After the oath at Raireshwar, Shivaji visited the Deshmukhs in the Maval valley who were guarding their individual Watans and often quarreling. He persuaded them to stop their useless conflicts, which wasted money and manpower, and presented a vision of unity and welfare under his leadership. He won their trust through sincere talk and became their leader. Simultaneously, he started intensive training in swordsmanship and riding with his comrades, explored secret paths, and surveyed forts and military establishments. His followers helped him gather detailed knowledge of the land. Shivaji also got a special royal seal in Sanskrit, symbolizing that his rule would be for the people’s welfare. These efforts laid the strong foundation for the future Swaraj.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Swaraj
questions.answer: Swaraj means self-rule or independence, where people govern themselves and are not under foreign control.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Watan
questions.answer: Watan refers to a piece of land given to a Deshmukh in lieu of service, which he guards and considers his own.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did the temple at Raireshwar inspire Shivaji and his followers?
questions.answer: The temple at Raireshwar provided a quiet and sacred place where Shivaji could speak freely about his dreams. His passionate speech moved the young Mavlas deeply, making them feel a new vision of freedom. They responded with one voice, promising to follow him and sacrifice everything for the ideal of Hindavi Swaraj. The temple echoed their oath, making it a spiritual commitment witnessed by Lord Raireshwar. This moment filled Shivaji with joy and gave him the strength to work tirelessly toward his goal.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What changes did Shivaji bring in the royal seal and why was it significant?
questions.answer: Shivaji’s royal seal was carved in Sanskrit, unlike the Persian seals used by other rulers at that time. This change showed his pride in Indian language and culture. The seal carried a message that it would grow in splendour like the new moon and denoted the welfare of the people. It was significant because it assured the Mavlas that Shivaji’s government would be just and people-oriented. The seal thus became a symbol of the coming Swaraj.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the geographical advantage of Torana fort that made it difficult to attack.
questions.answer: Torana fort was located on a hill with the only access across the ‘Zunjar Machi’, a narrow passage with high hills on one side and deep valleys on the other. A careless person could easily lose balance and fall into the valley, making it a natural defensive stronghold.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did Shivaji use the wealth found in Torana fort?
questions.answer: Shivaji used part of the treasure found in Torana fort to purchase arms and ammunition for his army. The remaining amount was kept for future use, which he had already planned for another project—strengthening the fort of Murumbdeo (Rajgad).

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shivaji say he had taken the fort for better administration of the countryside?
questions.answer: Shivaji gave this reason to Adilshah to avoid suspicion and justify his action as being in the interest of the Sultan. He claimed there was no evil design and that he was only improving the administration of the Jagir.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What was the composition of the garrison in Torana fort after its capture?
questions.answer: The garrison included Mavlas, Kolis, Ramoshis, Mahars, and brave men from various castes and communities. Shivaji appointed a Maratha Killedar, a Brahmin Sabnis, and a Prabhu Karkhanis to manage the fort, showing inclusivity.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did the workers feel that the discovery of mohurs in Torana fort was a gift from Goddess Bhavani?
questions.answer: The workers felt the discovery was a divine blessing because Shivaji had taken the oath of Swaraj in the temple of Raireshwar seeking the goddess’s grace. Finding wealth at that moment reinforced their belief that Goddess Bhavani had approved and supported his mission of Swaraj.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why was Torana fort considered strategically important despite being neglected by Adilshah?
questions.answer: Torana was strategically important due to its location in the Kanad Valley, natural defences provided by the ‘Zunjar Machi’ passage, and its control over surrounding territory. Though neglected, its strong fortifications and temple made it a valuable asset for Shivaji’s early conquests.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shivaji move swiftly to capture one fort after another after taking Torana?
questions.answer: Shivaji moved swiftly to maintain momentum, prevent enemy retaliation, and inspire confidence among local leaders. Capturing forts quickly helped him consolidate control over Bara Maval and expand the territory under Hindavi Swaraj before Adilshah could respond effectively.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in 6-10 lines. Describe the events of Shivaji’s capture of Torana fort and its significance.
questions.text: Describe how Shivaji captured Torana fort, what he found there, and why this event was important in the foundation of Hindavi Swaraj.
questions.answer: Shivaji selected Torana fort as it was weakly defended and neglected by Adilshah. With a select band of Mavlas, he captured it almost without resistance, hoisting the Maratha flag at the entrance. During repairs, workers discovered four metal pots filled with mohurs, which they believed was a gift from Goddess Bhavani. Shivaji used the wealth to buy arms and ammunition and began planning to capture Murumbdeo. He appointed officers from different communities, reinforcing equality. The fort’s capture boosted morale, marked the beginning of Swaraj, and laid the foundation for future conquests like Rajgad, which became the first capital.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in 6-10 lines. Explain Shivaji’s policy of inclusivity in fort administration after capturing Torana.
questions.text: How did Shivaji ensure that people of all castes and communities were treated equally in the administration of forts like Torana and Rajgad? Give examples from the text.
questions.answer: Shivaji believed in equality and ensured no distinctions were made on the basis of caste in Swaraj. After capturing Torana, he appointed a Maratha as Killedar, a Brahmin as Sabnis, and a Prabhu as Karkhanis, showing trust in merit over birth. The garrison included Mavlas, Kolis, Ramoshis, Mahars, and others from various communities. He declared that in Swaraj, all would be treated alike. This policy strengthened loyalty and unity among diverse groups, which was essential for building a strong and inclusive kingdom.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Machi
questions.answer: A Machi is a fortification of a natural plateau formed on the slope of a hill, used as a defensive structure in hill forts.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Hindavi Swaraj
questions.answer: Hindavi Swaraj means self-rule for the people of India, especially Marathas, free from foreign domination, as envisioned by Shivaji.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how the discovery of wealth in Torana fort motivated Shivaji and his men in their mission of Swaraj.
questions.answer: The discovery of four metal pots filled with mohurs in Torana fort came as a surprise and was seen as a divine blessing from Goddess Bhavani. It greatly elated Shivaji, who felt that the goddess was supporting his efforts. The wealth provided practical help by enabling him to purchase arms and ammunition for his army. It also boosted the morale of his men, reinforcing their belief in the righteousness of their cause. This unexpected gain gave Shivaji added vigour to pursue his ideal of Swaraj with renewed determination.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain why Shivaji’s capture of Torana fort was considered the foundation of Hindavi Swaraj.
questions.answer: The capture of Torana fort was Shivaji’s first major step toward establishing Swaraj. It demonstrated his courage and strategic thinking in challenging powerful enemies like Adilshah. The fort’s location and defences made it a valuable asset for controlling the surrounding region. The discovery of wealth strengthened his resources and morale. Most importantly, it inspired local leaders and people to believe in the possibility of self-rule, marking the beginning of the Maratha empire.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: Describe the role of the Mavlas of Javali in Shivaji's struggle for Swaraj.
questions.answer: The Mavlas of Javali were simple Maratha folk who loved Shivaji more than their lives. They were ready to do his bidding and willing to die for Swaraj. Their loyalty and courage were a strong support to Shivaji in his early struggles.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: How did Shivaji respond to Yeshwantrao Morey's rude reply?
questions.answer: Shivaji replied that Yeshwantrao should give up Javali and his pretensions to kingship. He told him to come before his master with folded hands and accept his service, or risk his life.

questions.text: What happened to Sambhaji Mohite of Supe after he plotted against Shivaji?

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: Why was the conquest of Javali considered a landmark in Shivaji's career?
questions.answer: The conquest of Javali doubled the boundaries of Swaraj under Shivaji. It also brought the strong Rairi fort under his control, which he later renamed Raigad and strengthened further.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did no one cross Morey’s path in the Javali forest?
questions.answer: No one crossed Morey’s path because the Javali forest was covered with thick vegetation that even sunlight could hardly penetrate. It was full of wild animals like tigers, wolves, and bears, making it dangerous and impenetrable. This made it a natural hideout, like a tiger’s den.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shivaji have to fight many battles against Bajaji Naik Nimbalkar?
questions.answer: Shivaji had to fight against Bajaji Naik Nimbalkar because, although he was Shivaji’s brother-in-law, he became impertinent and troublesome after gaining power. He started attacking Shivaji’s territory and harassing the people, posing a threat to Swaraj.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shivaji consider duty more important than relatives?
questions.answer: Shivaji believed that the welfare of Swaraj and his duty as a leader came before personal relationships. When relatives like Sambhaji Mohite or Yeshwantrao Morey betrayed him, he punished them to protect his kingdom and people.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the conquest of Javali and its importance in the growth of Swaraj.
questions.answer: The conquest of Javali was a difficult military operation due to its thick forest and the strong Rairi fort. Shivaji attacked after making thorough preparations. Yeshwantrao Morey held out for a month but suffered heavy losses and escaped to Rairi. Shivaji then laid siege to Rairi fort for three months until Morey surrendered. After conquering Javali, Shivaji doubled the boundaries of Swaraj. The Rairi fort became part of Swaraj and was renamed Raigad. Later, Shivaji built Pratapgad on the Bhorpya hill. This victory strengthened his position, boosted morale, and brought many Maratha sardars into his fold. It marked a turning point in the establishment of Swaraj.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Write about the character and loyalty of the Mavlas of Javali.
questions.answer: The Mavlas of Javali were simple, hardworking Maratha folk who lived in the forests and valleys of the region. They were deeply devoted to Shivaji and loved him more than their own lives. They were always ready to obey his commands and were prepared to sacrifice their lives for the cause of Swaraj. Their loyalty was not based on fear but on genuine admiration for Shivaji’s vision and leadership. They played a crucial role in his early military successes by providing reliable support. Even when others were jealous or plotted against Shivaji, the Mavlas remained steadfast. Their commitment inspired confidence in Shivaji’s mission and helped build a strong foundation for the Maratha Swaraj.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Swaraj
questions.answer: Swaraj means self-rule or independence, especially the goal of establishing a free Hindu kingdom under Shivaji's leadership.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Mavla
questions.answer: A Mavla is a loyal follower or soldier, especially a simple Maratha peasant who served Shivaji with devotion and courage.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how the geography of Javali helped in its defence.
questions.answer: The geography of Javali made it naturally strong and difficult to attack. It was covered with a thick forest that even sunlight could hardly penetrate, making visibility low and movement hard. The forest was full of wild animals like tigers, wolves, and bears, which added to the danger for intruders. This dense vegetation acted as a natural shield, hiding paths and making surprise attacks difficult. As a result, the area became a safe hideout, like a tiger’s den, which only someone as brave and determined as Shivaji could dare to enter.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain why Shivaji renamed the Rairi fort as Raigad.
questions.answer: Shivaji renamed the Rairi fort as Raigad to mark its importance in his kingdom. The name 'Raigad' means 'the fort of the king', symbolizing his sovereignty. After conquering Javali and capturing Rairi, he wanted to establish it as a central seat of power. Renaming it was a way to assert his authority and inspire pride among his people. Later, he strengthened the fort and built new structures, making it the capital of Swaraj. The name Raigad thus became synonymous with Shivaji’s rule and Maratha pride.

questions.answer: Shivaji shifted his headquarters to Pratapgad because Afzalkhan was marching against him and Pratapgad was a safer fort.

questions.answer: Afzalkhan's army was completely unprepared and was destroyed by Shivaji's troops in hot pursuit.

questions.answer: Shivaji told his Sardars to install Sambhaji on the 'gadi' and continue fighting for Swaraj.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe Shivaji's preparations before meeting Afzalkhan at Pratapgad.
questions.answer: Shivaji visited Bhavani's temple and took darshan in the morning. He then wore his ceremonial clothes: surwar, coat of mail, kurta, flowing robe, Jiretope (helmet) with a mandil, and fitted waghnakh on his left hand. He also hid a bichwa in his left sleeve and carried a dandpatta in his hand.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did Shivaji's troops attack Afzalkhan's army after the gun boomed?
questions.answer: On the instant the gun boomed, Shivaji's troops came out of their hiding places and attacked Afzalkhan's army. The enemy army was completely unprepared and caught in difficult terrain, so they could not run away. The Maratha troops chased them in hot pursuit and destroyed the whole of Afzalkhan's powerful army.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What was the outcome of the meeting between Shivaji and Afzalkhan at Pratapgad?
questions.answer: During the embrace, Afzalkhan stabbed Shivaji with a dagger, but Shivaji's coat of mail saved him. Shivaji then attacked Afzalkhan with waghnakh and bichwa, killing him. Jivaji Mahala killed Bada Sayyad, and Shivaji's troops destroyed Afzalkhan's army, leading to a great victory for Swaraj.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Afzalkhan become very angry when he learnt that Shivaji had moved to Pratapgad?
questions.answer: Afzalkhan became very angry because Pratapgad was surrounded by thick forest and high hills, with no proper approach road, making it very difficult to move his artillery. He knew conquering such a fort would be extremely challenging and frustrating for his large army.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shivaji say he was 'guilty of having captured your forts' in his message to Afzalkhan?
questions.answer: Shivaji said this as a clever trick to appear humble and guilty, luring Afzalkhan into a false sense of friendship. By pretending regret, he made Afzalkhan overconfident and willing to meet him at the foothills, where Shivaji had set his trap.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did the Bijapur court feel pleased when Afzalkhan accepted the challenge to bring Shivaji to court?
questions.answer: The Bijapur court felt pleased because they believed Afzalkhan, being a mighty Sardar with great physical prowess and experience, would surely succeed in capturing or killing Shivaji. They thought it was the end of Shivaji's revolt and that he would be brought to Bijapur either alive or dead.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Describe the sequence of events from Shivaji's arrival at the shamiana to the defeat of Afzalkhan's army.
questions.answer: Shivaji arrived at the shamiana and saw Afzalkhan already present, with Bada Sayyad standing by his side. Seeing Bada Sayyad, Shivaji stopped at the entrance, fearing danger. His vakil Pantaji Gopinath requested Bada Sayyad to move away, which he did. Shivaji then entered and embraced Afzalkhan. During the embrace, Afzalkhan stabbed Shivaji with a dagger, but the coat of mail saved him. Shivaji swiftly countered by driving waghnakh into Afzalkhan's stomach and bichwa with his right hand, killing him. Bada Sayyad rushed in to attack Shivaji but was killed by Jivaji Mahala. The gun boomed as a signal, and Shivaji's troops came out of hiding to attack Afzalkhan's army. The enemy was unprepared and trapped in difficult terrain, leading to their complete destruction. Fazalkhan, Afzalkhan's son, escaped with difficulty to Bijapur and reported the disaster, spreading gloom over the whole kingdom.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Explain how Shivaji's careful planning and courage led to victory over Afzalkhan despite being weaker in strength and army size.
questions.answer: Shivaji knew he could not win in an open battle due to Afzalkhan's huge army and his own small forces. So he used strategic thinking: he shifted to the strong fort of Pratapgad, refused to come to the plains, and lured Afzalkhan with a humble message. He prepared himself carefully by wearing protective gear and hiding weapons. During the meeting, he stayed alert, noticed Bada Sayyad's presence, and delayed entry until the threat was removed. When Afzalkhan attacked, Shivaji defended himself and struck back with precision. His timely signal led to a surprise attack by his hidden troops. Thus, through wisdom, courage, and planning, Shivaji turned a dangerous situation into a great victory, proving that brains can win over brute strength.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Waghnakh
questions.answer: Waghnakh is a weapon shaped like tiger's claws, worn on the fingers to stab an enemy.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Shamiana
questions.answer: A shamiana is a large tent or canopy used for holding meetings or ceremonies outdoors.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain why Shivaji's visit to Bhavani's temple before the meeting was important for him and his troops.
questions.answer: Shivaji's visit to Bhavani's temple was important to seek the goddess's blessings for success and protection. It gave him mental strength and confidence before facing a dangerous enemy. By taking darshan, he showed his faith and inspired his troops to believe in divine support. This act also reminded everyone that they were fighting for a righteous cause—Swaraj. The belief that Bhavani would help them succeed boosted morale and courage among Shivaji's followers as they prepared for the meeting.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how the difficult terrain of Pratapgad helped Shivaji in defeating Afzalkhan's army.
questions.answer: The thick forest and high hills surrounding Pratapgad made it hard for Afzalkhan to move his large army and artillery. This slowed down the enemy and prevented them from advancing quickly. When Shivaji's troops attacked, the Afzalkhan's army was caught in this tough terrain with no clear path to escape. They could not run away effectively, making them easy targets. The Maratha troops, familiar with the hills, chased them easily and destroyed the entire army. Thus, the natural disadvantage became a strategic advantage for Shivaji.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: Which plan was hit upon for Shivaji’s escape from the siege of Panhala?
questions.answer: The plan was to use two palanquins: one carrying a look-alike of Shivaji (Shiva Kashid) to deceive the enemy, while the real Shivaji escaped secretly through a difficult route. Shiva Kashid’s palanquin was to leave by Raj-dindi and be captured, making the enemy believe they had caught Shivaji. This would allow the real Shivaji to escape unnoticed.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: What preparation did Baji Prabhu make to halt the enemy in the Ghodkhind pass?
questions.answer: Baji Prabhu divided his soldiers into small groups and posted them at strategic points in the pass. He collected huge boulders and stones to be used as weapons. He instructed his men to stand firm and not leave their posts, using the narrow terrain to their advantage.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: How did Shiva Kashid become immortal in the service of Shivaji?
questions.answer: Shiva Kashid disguised himself as Shivaji and rode out in a palanquin to draw enemy attention. He was captured and killed by Siddi Jauhar’s men, who thought he was the real Shivaji. His sacrifice allowed the real Shivaji to escape, making him a martyr for Swaraj.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: Why did Adilshah throw a fit of wild rage after losing Panhala?
questions.answer: Adilshah was already mourning the death of his general Afzalkhan and the defeat of his army. When Shivaji captured Panhala fort, it added to his humiliation and anger, making him unable to eat or sleep. He immediately sent Siddi Jauhar to take revenge.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shiva Kashid sacrifice his life?
questions.answer: Shiva Kashid sacrificed his life to save Shivaji and the cause of Swaraj. By disguising himself as Shivaji, he drew the enemy’s attack away from the real leader. His death allowed Shivaji to escape safely through the difficult route. He knew the risk but chose loyalty over life.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Baji Prabhu refuse to leave the Ghodkhind pass?
questions.answer: Baji Prabhu refused to leave because he had promised to defend the pass until Shivaji reached Vishalgad safely. He believed that if the pass fell, Shivaji would be captured. His sense of duty and loyalty to Swaraj made him stay and fight, even at the cost of his life.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why is the battle at Ghodkhind considered a turning point in Shivaji’s escape?
questions.answer: The battle at Ghodkhind delayed the enemy long enough for Shivaji to reach Vishalgad safely. Though Baji Prabhu and his men were overwhelmed, their resistance gave Shivaji the crucial time he needed. Without this delay, Shivaji would have been caught before reaching the fort.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the events of Shivaji’s escape from Panhala fort and the role of Baji Prabhu Deshpande in the Battle of Ghodkhind.
questions.answer: Shivaji escaped from Panhala fort by sending a look-alike, Shiva Kashid, in a palanquin to deceive the enemy while he escaped through a difficult route. Shiva Kashid was captured and killed, but this allowed Shivaji to gain a head start. Baji Prabhu Deshpande stayed behind to defend the Ghodkhind pass with a small force. He used boulders and stones to block the enemy and fought bravely for hours. When he heard the gun-fire from Vishalgad, he knew Shivaji was safe and died peacefully. His sacrifice made the pass immortal as Pavan Khind.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain how the bravery of individuals like Shiva Kashid and Baji Prabhu contributed to the success of Shivaji’s mission and the ideal of Swaraj.
questions.answer: Shiva Kashid and Baji Prabhu showed supreme bravery and loyalty by risking their lives for Shivaji and Swaraj. Shiva Kashid disguised himself as Shivaji to mislead the enemy, allowing the real Shivaji to escape. Baji Prabhu held the Ghodkhind pass against a large enemy force, giving Shivaji time to reach Vishalgad. Their sacrifices weakened the enemy’s morale and strengthened the Maratha resolve. Such acts of courage inspired others to join the fight for freedom. Their selflessness became a symbol of patriotism and sacrifice in Maratha history. Because of them, the idea of Swaraj was kept alive and eventually strengthened.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What is meant by 'Swaraj' in the context of Shivaji’s time?
questions.answer: Swaraj means self-rule or independence, especially the dream of establishing a Hindu kingdom free from foreign control.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What is a 'palanquin' as used in the chapter?
questions.answer: A palanquin is a covered carriage carried on poles by bearers, used for transporting a person.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how the monsoon season affected the events at Panhala fort.
questions.answer: Shivaji initially thought that the arrival of the monsoon would force Siddi Jauhar to lift the siege, as rains would make camping difficult and spoil supplies. However, Siddi Jauhar did not lift the siege; instead, he tightened it further despite the rains. The rainy season made movement difficult for both sides, but the enemy remained determined. Shivaji had to rely on deception rather than waiting for natural help. This shows that enemies in war do not always behave as expected.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain why the Ghodkhind pass was strategically important in Shivaji’s escape.
questions.answer: The Ghodkhind pass was a narrow and zigzag mountain passage, making it easy to defend with a small force against a large army. By holding this pass, Baji Prabhu could delay the enemy’s advance toward Vishalgad. The terrain allowed the Mavlas to use boulders and stones effectively as weapons. If the enemy had passed quickly, Shivaji would have been caught before reaching safety. Thus, defending this pass was crucial to buying time for Shivaji’s escape.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe how Shivaji planned and executed his attack on Shaistakhan in Lal Mahal.
questions.answer: Shivaji planned to attack Shaistakhan during a marriage procession in Pune. He joined the procession with his trusted followers to gain entry into the city. At night, he entered Lal Mahal through a hole in the wall, attacked Shaistakhan, cut off three fingers, and escaped to Sinhagad.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain why Aurangzeb sent Shaistakhan to deal with Shivaji.
questions.answer: Aurangzeb was enraged by Shivaji's raids on Mughal territory. He sent his uncle Shaistakhan with a large army to teach Shivaji a lesson and stop his growing power.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What was the significance of Shivaji's attack on Shaistakhan in Lal Mahal?
questions.answer: The attack was a major blow to Mughal prestige, showing that Shivaji could strike at the heart of enemy power. It boosted Maratha morale and announced their strength across Maharashtra.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did the Maratha troops' style of warfare give them an advantage over Shaistakhan's army?
questions.answer: The Marathas moved swiftly on light ponies, lived on simple food like onions and bajra bread, and knew the terrain well. This allowed them to surprise enemies and avoid large, slow Mughal forces.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shaistakhan try to escape through the window during Shivaji's attack?
questions.answer: Shaistakhan tried to escape through the window because he was terrified when Shivaji attacked him with a sword. He thought Shivaji might kill him and wanted to save his life.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Aurangzeb transfer Shaistakhan to Bengal after the Lal Mahal incident?
questions.answer: Aurangzeb transferred Shaistakhan to Bengal because he was furious that Shaistakhan had been attacked in his own residence and lost his fingers, which showed failure in duty.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shivaji choose to attack Shaistakhan at night in Lal Mahal?
questions.answer: Shivaji chose to attack at night because Shaistakhan was asleep and off guard. He also knew the layout of Lal Mahal well, having lived there before, which helped him move secretly.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the events leading to Shivaji's attack on Shaistakhan in Lal Mahal and its impact on the Mughal-Maratha conflict.
questions.answer: Shaistakhan came to Pune with a huge army to defeat Shivaji and made Lal Mahal his headquarters. He troubled the surrounding areas by destroying crops and capturing cattle. Shivaji, knowing the place well, planned a daring attack. On 5th April 1663, he used a marriage procession as cover, entered Lal Mahal, attacked Shaistakhan, and cut off three fingers. Shaistakhan fled, thinking he might lose his life. The attack shocked the Mughals, showed Maratha bravery, and boosted Shivaji's image as a fearless leader. It marked a turning point, proving that even a Mughal commander was not safe in Shivaji's presence.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Write a short narrative of the attack on Lal Mahal from the perspective of one of Shivaji's followers.
questions.answer: I joined Shivaji and our group as part of the marriage procession moving through Pune. Our hearts beat fast as we neared Lal Mahal. After the procession passed, we slipped away silently toward the palace. Shivaji made a hole in the wall and we entered. Everything was quiet; the guards were half-asleep. We tied them up quickly. Shivaji went inside and suddenly came out with his sword stained, having struck Shaistakhan. We heard cries and ran back to Sinhagad. We felt proud and brave, knowing we had struck a big blow to the enemy.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Siege
questions.answer: A siege is when an army surrounds a fort or city to stop people from going in or out and tries to make them surrender by cutting off supplies.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Headquarters
questions.answer: Headquarters is the main place where a leader or army works from and gives orders.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how Shivaji's knowledge of Lal Mahal helped him during the attack.
questions.answer: Shivaji had lived in Lal Mahal before, so he knew its layout very well. He knew where the rooms, doors, windows, and secret passages were. This helped him move quickly and safely inside the building during the attack. He could find Shaistakhan's chamber without wasting time. His knowledge also helped him escape quickly after the attack.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain why the Maratha style of warfare was effective against large armies like Shaistakhan's.
questions.answer: The Marathas fought light and fast, using small ponies and simple food. They did not need big camps or heavy supplies. They could move quickly through hills and valleys where large armies struggled. They used surprise attacks and knew the local terrain. This made it hard for big, slow armies like Shaistakhan's to catch or fight them effectively.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Siege and Treaty of Purandar
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: Describe the raid on Surat carried out by Shivaji.
questions.answer: Shivaji carried out a daring raid on Surat, a rich Mughal trading centre, and brought back a large booty worth lakhs of rupees. He spared churches and mosques and did not show disrespect to women during the raid. The raid angered Aurangzeb, who then decided to destroy the Maratha Kingdom.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Siege and Treaty of Purandar
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: How did Murarbaji show his bravery during the siege of Purandar?
questions.answer: Murarbaji led a fierce attack with five hundred men, broke through the Mughal lines, and entered Dilerkhan's camp, causing havoc. He fought with great courage, shouting 'Har Har Mahadeo', and continued to fight even after being surrounded. His bravery impressed even the enemy.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Siege and Treaty of Purandar
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: What were the terms of the Treaty of Purandar?
questions.answer: As per the Treaty of Purandar, Shivaji agreed to hand over twenty-three forts and a territory yielding four lakh hons annually to the Mughal Emperor. In return, the Emperor guaranteed Shivaji's safe return if he visited Agra. The treaty was signed in 1665.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Siege and Treaty of Purandar
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: Why was Shivaji unwilling to fight the Mughals at the cost of his men's lives?
questions.answer: Shivaji was unwilling to sacrifice his men's lives because he valued their lives and wanted to avoid unnecessary bloodshed. He believed in protecting his people and preferred diplomacy when possible. He wanted to establish Swaraj for the happiness of his people, not through endless war.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Siege and Treaty of Purandar
questions.text: Why did Dilerkhan lay siege to the fort of Purandar?
questions.answer: Dilerkhan laid siege to Purandar because he knew Shivaji could not be defeated as long as he held this strong fort. Purandar was a key Maratha stronghold, and capturing it would weaken Shivaji's power. Dilerkhan wanted to end the Maratha resistance by taking this fort.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Siege and Treaty of Purandar
questions.text: Why did Shivaji agree to go to Agra after signing the treaty?
questions.answer: Shivaji agreed to go to Agra to meet the Emperor as suggested by Mirza Raje Jaising, who assured him of safe return. He wanted to face the situation cautiously and avoid immediate conflict, even though he did not fully trust the Emperor. This was a diplomatic move to buy time and test the Emperor's intentions.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Siege and Treaty of Purandar
questions.text: Why did Murarbaji refuse to join the Mughal side despite Dilerkhan's offer?
questions.answer: Murarbaji refused because he was a loyal servant of Shivaji Maharaj and did not want to betray his master. He questioned why he should accept safety or a jagir from the Mughals when he was ready to die for his king. His loyalty and pride made him reject the offer.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Siege and Treaty of Purandar
questions.instruction: Answer in six to ten lines.
questions.text: Describe the battle between Murarbaji and Dilerkhan, highlighting Murarbaji's bravery and the events that led to his death.
questions.answer: Murarbaji, the commander of Purandar fort, showed extraordinary bravery during the siege. He led a bold attack with five hundred men, broke through the Mughal lines, and entered Dilerkhan's camp, causing chaos. Despite being surrounded, he fought fiercely, shouting 'Har Har Mahadeo'. Impressed by his valour, Dilerkhan asked him to join the Mughal side, offering a jagir and the title of Sardar. Murarbaji refused, declaring his loyalty to Shivaji. He continued to fight but was eventually struck in the neck by an arrow fired by Dilerkhan from his elephant's houdah. Murarbaji fell dead, and his followers carried his body back to the fort. His death was a great loss, but his courage inspired the Marathas to continue fighting.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Siege and Treaty of Purandar
questions.instruction: Answer in six to ten lines.
questions.text: Explain the circumstances that led Shivaji to sign the Treaty of Purandar and his thoughts on the Mughal Emperor's trustworthiness.
questions.answer: After the raid on Surat, Aurangzeb became furious and sent a large army under Mirza Raje Jaising and Dilerkhan to destroy the Maratha Kingdom. Shivaji realized he could not match the Mughal army in open war and risked losing many of his men. He chose diplomacy to avoid further bloodshed and suffering of his people. Although he knew the Emperor had been treacherous to his own brothers and could not be fully trusted, he decided to take the risk and sign the treaty. He agreed to hand over twenty-three forts and four lakh hons in exchange for peace. Shivaji told Jaising that he was willing to go to Agra to meet the Emperor, but only cautiously, showing his wisdom and concern for his people's welfare over pride or revenge.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Siege and Treaty of Purandar
questions.text: What is a 'treaty'?
questions.answer: A treaty is a formal agreement between two or more parties, such as kings or states, to establish peace or set certain terms.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Siege and Treaty of Purandar
questions.text: What does 'Swaraj' mean?
questions.answer: Swaraj means self-rule or independence, where people govern themselves without foreign control.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Siege and Treaty of Purandar
questions.instruction: Explain the following in four or five sentences.
questions.text: Explain why Shivaji did not show disrespect to women or harm holy places during the raid on Surat.
questions.answer: Shivaji followed a strict code of ethics even in warfare. He believed that harming women or attacking places of worship was against dharma and humanity. By sparing churches and mosques, he showed respect for all religions. His actions reflected his values of justice and compassion. This earned him respect even from his enemies and strengthened his image as a righteous leader.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Siege and Treaty of Purandar
questions.instruction: Explain the following in four or five sentences.
questions.text: Explain how the Treaty of Purandar affected Shivaji's future plans for Swaraj.
questions.answer: The Treaty of Purandar was a temporary setback as Shivaji had to surrender many forts and revenue. However, it gave him time to regroup and strengthen his position without losing men in battle. He used the peace to prepare for future challenges and kept his long-term goal of Swaraj alive. Although he handed over territories, he never gave up his vision of self-rule. Later, he worked to regain what was lost and continued his mission with wisdom and courage.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe how Shivaji Maharaj gained the Emperor’s permission to send baskets out of Agra.
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj pretended to be ill and complained of severe stomach pain. Doctors were called to treat him. He then requested permission to send baskets of sweets to Sadhus and Maulavis for his quick recovery, which the Emperor granted.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What did Shivaji Maharaj do before leaving for Agra to ensure the safety of his Swaraj?
questions.answer: Before leaving for Agra, Shivaji Maharaj handed over the administration of his Swaraj to his mother Jijabai and took her blessings. He also left his son Sambhaji Raje in the care of trusted people.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did Hiroji and Madari help Shivaji Maharaj escape from Agra?
questions.answer: Hiroji slept in Shivaji’s bed to deceive the guards, while Madari massaged Shivaji’s feet to make it seem he was resting. This allowed Shivaji and Sambhaji Raje to hide in the baskets of sweets and escape unnoticed.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did the Emperor think Shivaji Maharaj would be isolated after sending back his companions?
questions.answer: The Emperor thought that by sending back the persons who had accompanied Shivaji to Agra, Shivaji would be left alone with no support. He believed this would force Shivaji to remain under his control and not escape.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shivaji Maharaj pretend to be ill in Agra?
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj pretended to be ill to gain the Emperor’s permission to send baskets of sweets out of Agra regularly. He used this routine to hide himself and Sambhaji Raje in the baskets and escape without being checked by the guards.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why was the Emperor’s search for Shivaji after his escape unsuccessful?
questions.answer: The Emperor’s search was unsuccessful because Shivaji escaped in disguise and took a different route toward Maharashtra. He also left Sambhaji Raje safely at Mathura, which misled the spies, and the Marathas helped him evade capture.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the escape of Shivaji Maharaj from Agra in your own words.
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj went to Agra to meet Emperor Aurangzeb but was insulted by being made to stand in the back row. Angry, he decided not to see the Emperor’s face again. He pretended to be ill and gained permission to send baskets of sweets to Sadhus and Maulavis for his recovery. Hiroji and Madari helped him by switching beds and massaging his feet. Shivaji and Sambhaji Raje hid in two of the baskets and escaped at a pre-fixed place. Their servants were waiting with horses. Shivaji reached Rajgad safely, and months later, Sambhaji Raje also arrived. Jijamata was overjoyed to see them back. This escape showed Shivaji’s courage and cleverness.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Write a short paragraph on how Shivaji Maharaj outwitted the Emperor’s plans to keep him in Agra.
questions.answer: The Emperor thought that by keeping Shivaji under surveillance and stopping his requests to return, he could keep him trapped in Agra. But Shivaji outwitted him by pretending to be ill and using the daily basket-sending routine as a cover for escape. He trusted Hiroji and Madari, who risked their lives to help. The Emperor’s spies failed to find him because Shivaji moved in disguise and had already sent Sambhaji Raje to safety. Thus, Shivaji turned the Emperor’s treachery into his own triumph and returned to Maharashtra with dignity and freedom.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Swaraj
questions.answer: Swaraj means self-rule or independence; it was the kingdom Shivaji Maharaj established and governed.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Darbar
questions.answer: Darbar refers to the royal court of the Emperor where official meetings and ceremonies were held.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did Shivaji Maharaj’s escape from Agra show his leadership and courage?
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj’s escape from Agra showed his leadership because he planned carefully, trusted his loyal servants, and kept his mission secret. He showed courage by facing insult and danger without fear. He did not panic when his requests were denied but made a bold plan to escape. He protected his son and ensured the safety of his Swaraj. His success inspired his people and proved that wisdom and bravery can overcome even the strongest enemy.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did the Emperor’s plan to keep Shivaji in Agra fail?
questions.answer: The Emperor’s plan failed because he underestimated Shivaji’s intelligence and determination. He thought stopping Shivaji’s requests would break his spirit, but Shivaji used pretended illness to gain freedom of movement. The Emperor did not suspect the basket routine, which Shivaji turned into an escape route. He also failed to account for the loyalty of Shivaji’s servants like Hiroji and Madari. Thus, Shivaji’s clever planning and the Emperor’s overconfidence led to the failure of the plan.

questions.text: Why did Tanaji refuse to attend his son’s wedding before going to fight for Kondana?
questions.answer: Tanaji believed that capturing Kondana was more important than attending a personal celebration. He said he would first 'perform the marriage of Kondana' by capturing it, and only then could personal events like his son’s wedding take place.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Fort is Won but the Lion is Lost
questions.text: Why did Suryaji cut the rope after reaching the top of the precipice?
questions.answer: Suryaji cut the rope to prevent the Mavlas from retreating, forcing them to either fight or jump to their deaths. This ensured they stayed in battle and turned back to fight the Mughals.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Fort is Won but the Lion is Lost
questions.text: Why is Tanaji remembered as a lion-hearted warrior?
questions.answer: Tanaji is remembered as lion-hearted because he showed extraordinary bravery by scaling a steep precipice at night, fighting fiercely despite being wounded, and sacrificing his life to recapture Kondana fort for Swarajya.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Fort is Won but the Lion is Lost
questions.text: Describe the battle for the recapture of Kondana fort, including Tanaji’s plan, the attack, and the outcome.
questions.answer: Tanaji planned a surprise attack on Kondana fort by scaling an unguarded steep precipice on the western side. He divided his forces: one group led by Suryaji attacked the Kalyan gate, while Tanaji led another to climb the cliff. At night, his men climbed using ropes and rock crevices, reached the top, and lowered ropes for others. They surprised the guards and opened the Kalyan gate. A fierce battle ensued between Tanaji and Udaybhan, both fighting valiantly. Though Tanaji was mortally wounded, his courage inspired Suryaji to rally the troops. The Mavlas ultimately won the fort, but lost their leader. The fort was renamed Sinhagad in his honour.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Fort is Won but the Lion is Lost
questions.text: Write about Jijamata’s role in inspiring the recapture of Kondana fort.
questions.answer: Jijamata played a vital role in motivating Shivaji to recapture Kondana fort. She expressed concern that leaving such a strong fort in enemy hands was dangerous and like a thorn in their side. Her words reminded Shivaji of the importance of securing all forts for Swarajya. She supported Tanaji’s resolve to lead the campaign, even over personal events like his son’s wedding. Her wisdom and courage strengthened the Maratha resolve. After the victory, she shared in the grief of losing Tanaji but celebrated the success of the mission. Her influence helped shape Shivaji’s leadership and determination.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Fort is Won but the Lion is Lost
questions.text: Swarajya
questions.answer: Swarajya means self-rule or independent kingdom, which Shivaji aimed to establish by freeing forts and lands from foreign control.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Fort is Won but the Lion is Lost
questions.text: Precipice
questions.answer: A precipice is a very steep rock face or cliff, often with a vertical drop, which is difficult to climb.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Fort is Won but the Lion is Lost
questions.text: Explain how Tanaji’s personal sacrifice contributed to the success of the Kondana campaign.
questions.answer: Tanaji’s personal sacrifice was crucial to the success of the Kondana campaign. By volunteering to lead the dangerous assault, he inspired courage in his men. His decision to scale the unguarded precipice showed innovative thinking and bravery. Even after being wounded, he fought fiercely, holding the enemy at bay. His death, though tragic, motivated Suryaji to rally the troops and prevent retreat. Ultimately, his sacrifice turned a risky mission into a victorious one, leading to the fort’s capture and renaming as Sinhagad.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.chapter: The Fort is Won but the Lion is Lost
questions.text: Explain why the recapture of Kondana fort was a turning point in Shivaji’s struggle against the Mughals.
questions.answer: The recapture of Kondana fort was a turning point because it was one of the key forts still under Mughal control in the region. Its capture strengthened Shivaji’s hold over the surrounding areas and boosted Maratha morale. It showed that even well-guarded forts could be taken through courage and strategy. The victory discouraged Mughal forces and encouraged more local support for Swarajya. Renaming it Sinhagad also honoured Tanaji’s sacrifice, turning the fort into a symbol of Maratha bravery and resistance.

questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: Why did Shivaji Maharaj have himself crowned? Explain in brief.
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj had himself crowned to give the newly founded Swaraj a firm footing and to gain recognition from other princes and kings. He did it not for personal glory but to establish justice, equality, and happiness for his subjects. The coronation declared that Swaraj had been firmly established in Maharashtra.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: Describe the preparations made by Shivaji Maharaj for his coronation.
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj made detailed preparations for his coronation. He ordered a golden throne studded with precious stones and sent men to bring water from the seven rivers and the sea. Nearly fifty thousand people gathered at Raigad, and spacious shamianas were set up to accommodate the guests.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: What role did Gagabhatt play in the coronation ceremony?
questions.answer: Gagabhatt, a renowned scholar from Varanasi, acted as the chief priest during the coronation ceremony. He held the golden vessel filled with sacred water over Shivaji Maharaj's head and recited the coronation mantras. After the ablution, he proclaimed Shivaji Maharaj as the crowned king.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Answer in two or three sentences.
questions.text: How did the people and the environment react during Shivaji Maharaj's coronation?
questions.answer: During the coronation, musicians played, singers sang, and the air was filled with joy. Guns were fired from fort after fort, and the whole of Maharashtra echoed with the cry 'Shivaji Maharaj Ki Jai'. Everyone present wished victory to Shivaji Maharaj in one voice.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why were Jijamata’s eyes filled with tears of joy after the coronation?
questions.answer: Jijamata’s eyes were filled with tears of joy because her lifelong dream of seeing her son establish a free and just kingdom had finally come true. She had worked hard for thirty years to support Shivaji’s mission of Swaraj. Seeing him crowned as Chhatrapati fulfilled her hopes and brought her immense happiness.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shivaji Maharaj choose Raigad as his capital?
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj chose Raigad as his capital because it is a strong hill fort, naturally protected by steep slopes and difficult terrain. From Raigad, it was easy to keep a watch on enemy movements and administer the kingdom effectively. Its strategic location made it ideal for both defense and governance.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Shivaji Maharaj start a new calendar after his coronation?
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj started a new calendar known as the Coronation Calendar to mark the beginning of a new era in Maharashtra’s history. Just like other great kings, he wanted the coronation to be remembered as a significant event. This calendar helped in recording time from the year of his coronation, symbolizing the firm establishment of Swaraj.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the coronation ceremony of Shivaji Maharaj held at Raigad in 1674.
questions.answer: The coronation ceremony of Shivaji Maharaj took place on a sacred day at Raigad in 1674. The atmosphere was filled with joy as musicians played and singers sang. Shivaji Raje sat on a golden throne in full regalia, with a canopy and fans held over his head. Priests carried vessels of ghee, dahi, and honey, while Gagabhatt held a golden vessel filled with water from the seven rivers—Ganga, Sindhu, Yamuna, Godavari, Krishna, Narmada, Kaveri—and the sea. As the water dripped on Shivaji’s head, mantras were recited. After the ablution, Shivaji bowed before Jijamata, who embraced him with tears of joy. The crowd shouted 'Shivaji Maharaj Ki Jai', guns were fired, and the whole region celebrated. Shivaji then sat on the throne, and his fame spread far and wide.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain why Shivaji Maharaj had himself crowned and what it meant for the people of Maharashtra.
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj had himself crowned not for personal glory but to give the newly founded Swaraj a firm and legitimate footing. He wanted all princes and kings, big and small, to recognize his authority and the independence of Maharashtra. The coronation declared that Swaraj had moved beyond childhood and was now a strong, self-respecting kingdom. It inspired confidence among his subjects that they lived under a just ruler who valued all religions equally and aimed to give them happiness and justice. By striking his own coins and starting a new calendar, Shivaji emphasized the sovereignty of his rule. The ceremony united people in joy and pride, and his fame spread across the land, establishing him as a great king like those whose names mark the beginning of eras.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Swaraj
questions.answer: Swaraj means self-rule or independence, where people govern themselves with justice, equality, and freedom.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Coronation
questions.answer: Coronation is the ceremony in which a king is formally crowned and given the royal authority to rule.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain the significance of the water from the seven rivers and the sea used in Shivaji Maharaj's coronation.
questions.answer: The water from the seven rivers—Ganga, Sindhu, Yamuna, Godavari, Krishna, Narmada, Kaveri—and the sea was collected to symbolize the unity and purity of the entire land. By using this sacred water in the coronation, Shivaji Maharaj showed that his rule was blessed by nature and accepted by all regions. It represented that his sovereignty extended over the whole territory and that he ruled with the consent and goodwill of the people. The ritual of ablution with this water purified him and marked his transformation into a rightful king. It also reflected the cultural and spiritual importance of rivers in Indian tradition, linking his kingship to ancient customs of purification and divine blessing.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how Shivaji Maharaj’s coronation inspired a sense of pride and unity among the people of Maharashtra.
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj’s coronation inspired pride and unity because it marked the establishment of a free and self-respecting kingdom after years of struggle. Seeing their leader crowned with traditional rituals gave people confidence that their culture and values were being upheld. The participation of learned Brahmins, officers, Sardars, and even foreign envoys showed that the coronation was recognized and respected. The joyful celebrations, with music, singing, and the cry of 'Shivaji Maharaj Ki Jai', brought people together in shared happiness. His just rule, respect for all religions, and efforts for public welfare made subjects feel proud to be part of Swaraj. The coronation was not just a personal event but a national milestone that strengthened the bond between the ruler and the people.

questions.text: How did Kutubshah receive Shivaji Maharaj in Golconda?
