questions.answer: त्रिमितीय आकारांचा वापर करून विस्तारत जाणारे आकृतिबंध गहाकार दर्शवितात.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: नक्षी म्हणजे काय?
questions.answer: नक्षी म्हणजे विविध नियमित व अनियमित आकारांचा वापर करून आकर्षक तयार केलेला आकृतिबंध होय.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: टाइलिंगमध्ये रिकामी जागा राहणार नाही हे नियम का महत्वाचे आहे?
questions.answer: टाइलिंगमध्ये रिकामी जागा राहणार नाही हे नियम महत्वाचे आहे कारण तो टुकड्यांचे एकमेकांवर चढणे व फाटणे अवरोधित करते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: त्रिकोणी संख्यांचा आकृतिबंध काय आहे?
questions.answer: त्रिकोणी संख्यांचा आकृतिबंध हे एका पद्धत आहे ज्यामध्ये प्रत्येक पुढील संख्या खालील दोन संख्यांचे बेरीज होते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: सम संख्यांचा आकृतिबंध तयार करण्यासाठी एकक स्थानावरील अंक कोणते येथे?
questions.answer: सम संख्यांचा आकृतिबंध तयार करण्यासाठी एकक स्थानावरील अंक 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 यातून क्रमाने येथे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: त्रिमितीय आकारांचा वापर करून तयार केलेले आकृतिबंध व द्विमितीय आकारांचा वापर करून तयार केलेले आकृतिबंध यांचे फरक सांगा.
questions.answer: त्रिमितीय आकारांचा वापर करून तयार केलेले आकृतिबंध गहाकार असतात, ज्यामध्ये लांबी, रुंद व उंची तीनों दिशा असतात. द्विमितीय आकारांचा वापर करून तयार केलेले आकृतिबंध समतल असतात, त्यामध्ये फक्त लांबी व रुंद असतात. त्रिमितीय आकृतिबंधात घन, गोला, शंकू इत्यादी आकार दिसतात, द्विमितीयात त्रिकोण, चौरस, वृत इत्यादी.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: नक्षी तयार करण्यासाठी भौमितिक आकारांचा वापर का केला जातो?
questions.answer: नक्षी तयार करण्यासाठी भौमितिक आकारांचा वापर केला जातो कारण ते नियमित व सुंदर आकृतिबंध तयार करण्यास मदत करतात. भौमितिक आकारे सोपे होते त्यामुळे त्यांचा वापर सोपे होते. त्यामुळे नक्षी आकर्षक व समजून येणारी होतात.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: टाइलिंगमध्ये रिकामी जागा राहणार नाही हे नियम का पाळला जातो?
questions.answer: टाइलिंगमध्ये रिकामी जागा राहणार नाही हे नियम पाळला जातो कारण तो टुकड्यांचे एकमेकांवर चढणे व फाटणे अवरोधित करते. त्यामुळे टाइलिंग एकरूप व सुरक्षित होतो. हे नियम फर्श व भिंतीच्या टाइलिंगमध्ये महत्त्वाचे आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: त्रिकोणी संख्यांचा आकृतिबंध तयार करण्यासाठी खालील पद्धत सांगा: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15.
questions.answer: त्रिकोणी संख्यांचा आकृतिबंध तयार करण्यासाठी प्रत्येक पुढील संख्या खालील दोन संख्यांचे बेरीज होते. 1 + 2 = 3, 3 + 3 = 6, 6 + 4 = 10, 10 + 5 = 15. त्यामुळे पद्धत हे खालील दोन संख्यांचे बेरीज घेणे आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: त्रिमितीय आकारांचा वापर करून तयार केलेले आकृतिबंध द्विमितीय आकृतिबंधापेक्षा काहे गहाकार दर्शवितात?
questions.answer: त्रिमितीय आकारांचा वापर करून तयार केलेले आकृतिबंध गहाकार दर्शवितात कारण त्रिमितीय आकारे लांबी, रुंद व उंची तीनों दिशा असतात. त्यामुळे त्यात गहापणा व ठोसपणा दिसतो. द्विमितीय आकारे फक्त लांबी व रुंद असतात, त्यामुळे त्यात गहापणा नाही.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: नक्षीमध्ये फक्त नियमित आकारांचा वापर केला जातो का? कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: नक्षीमध्ये फक्त नियमित आकारांचा वापर केला जातो का? नाही, नक्षीमध्ये नियमित व अनियमित आकारांचा दोन्ही वापर केला जातो. नियमित आकारे सुंदर व एकरूप आकृतिबंध तयार करण्यास मदत करतात, अनियमित आकारे वैयक्तिकता व आविष्कार देऊन आकृतिबंधाला रोचक बनवितात.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: टाइलिंगमध्ये टुकड्यांचे आकार एकमेकांवर चढू शकतात का? कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: टाइलिंगमध्ये टुकड्यांचे आकार एकमेकांवर चढू शकतात का? नाही, टाइलिंगमध्ये टुकड्यांचे आकार एकमेकांवर चढू शकत नाहीत. कारण तो टुकड्यांचे एकमेकांवर चढणे व फाटणे अवरोधित करते, ज्यामुळे टाइलिंग एकरूप व सुरक्षित होतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: त्रिमितीय आकारांचा वापर करून तयार केलेले आकृतिबंध व द्विमितीय आकारांचा वापर करून तयार केलेले आकृतिबंध यांचे फरक सांगा व त्यांचे उदाहरण द्या.
questions.answer: त्रिमितीय आकारांचा वापर करून तयार केलेले आकृतिबंध गहाकार असतात, ज्यामध्ये लांबी, रुंद व उंची तीनों दिशा असतात. उदाहरण: घन, गोला, शंकू, सिलिंडर. द्विमितीय आकारांचा वापर करून तयार केलेले आकृतिबंध समतल असतात, त्यामध्ये फक्त लांबी व रुंद असतात. उदाहरण: त्रिकोण, चौरस, वृत, आयत. त्रिमितीय आकृतिबंधात गहापणा व ठोसपणा दिसतो, द्विमितीयात फक्त समतल आकृतिबंध दिसतो. त्रिमितीय आकृतिबंध इमारतीं, मूर्तीं, बर्तनंमध्ये वापरले जाते, द्विमितीय आकृतिबंध चित्रे, नक्षी, कागदावरचे डिझाइनमध्ये वापरले जाते.

questions.text: नक्षी तयार करण्याचे प्रक्रिया सांगा व त्यामध्ये भौमितिक आकारांचा वापर का केला जातो त्याचे कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: नक्षी तयार करण्यासाठी सर्वप्रथम भौमितिक आकारे (त्रिकोण, चौरस, षट्कोन इ.) काढली जातात. त्यानंतर त्यांचा रंग भरून व विविध प्रकारे व्यवस्थित करून आकर्षक आकृतिबंध तयार केला जातो. भौमितिक आकारांचा वापर केला जातो कारण ते नियमित, सुंदर व सोपे असते. त्यामुळे त्यांचा वापर सोपे होते व आकृतिबंध एकरूप होतो. भौमितिक आकारे आकृतिबंधाला संतुलन व सौंदर्य देऊन त्याला आकर्षक बनवितात.

questions.text: Why do planets not twinkle?

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Our Earth and Our Solar System
questions.text: Explain why the moon appears to change its shape every day.
questions.answer: The moon appears to change its shape because we see different parts of its illuminated surface as it orbits the earth. The amount of the lit side visible from earth changes depending on the relative positions of the earth, moon, and sun.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Our Earth and Our Solar System
questions.text: What is the difference between a star and a planet?
questions.answer: A star produces its own light and heat through nuclear reactions, while a planet does not produce its own light and only reflects light from a star. Stars twinkle, but planets do not.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Our Earth and Our Solar System
questions.text: Name two Indian space missions and their objectives.
questions.answer: Chandrayaan-1 was launched to study the moon, and Mangalyaan was launched to study Mars. Both missions aim to gather scientific data about these celestial bodies.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Our Earth and Our Solar System
questions.text: Why is earth considered a unique planet?
questions.answer: Earth is considered unique because it is the only known planet that supports life. It has the right temperature, water, and atmosphere necessary for living organisms.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Our Earth and Our Solar System
questions.text: Why do we not feel the earth moving even though it revolves around the sun?
questions.answer: We do not feel the earth's movement because it moves at a constant speed in a smooth orbit, and everything on earth, including the atmosphere, moves with it. There is no sudden change in motion that we can sense.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Our Earth and Our Solar System
questions.text: Why is life not possible on the moon?
questions.answer: Life is not possible on the moon because it has no atmosphere, no liquid water, and extreme temperature variations. These conditions are not suitable for living organisms to survive.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Our Earth and Our Solar System
questions.text: Why do astronauts wear special suits in space?
questions.answer: Astronauts wear special suits in space to protect themselves from the vacuum, extreme temperatures, and harmful radiation. The suit provides oxygen and maintains pressure around the body.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Our Earth and Our Solar System
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Describe the solar system and mention the position of the earth in it.
questions.answer: The solar system consists of the sun at the centre and eight planets that revolve around it in fixed orbits. The earth is the third planet from the sun. Besides planets, the solar system includes moons, dwarf planets like Pluto, asteroids, and comets. The sun provides light and heat to all these bodies. The earth is unique as it supports life due to its suitable distance from the sun, presence of water, and atmosphere.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Our Earth and Our Solar System
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Explain the importance of artificial satellites and mention any two uses.
questions.answer: Artificial satellites are man-made objects placed in orbit around the earth. They are used for various purposes such as weather forecasting, television broadcasting, and global positioning. They also help in studying the earth's surface and environment. Satellites enable long-distance communication and are vital for disaster management and navigation.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Our Earth and Our Solar System
questions.text: Define: Orbit
questions.answer: Orbit is the fixed path in which a heavenly body revolves around another heavenly body due to gravitational attraction.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Our Earth and Our Solar System
questions.text: Define: Gravity
questions.answer: Gravity is the force of attraction that pulls objects towards the centre of the earth or any other heavenly body.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Our Earth and Our Solar System
questions.text: Explain how rockets help in space travel.
questions.answer: Rockets help in space travel by producing a large amount of thrust through the burning of fuel. This thrust pushes the rocket upwards against the force of gravity. Rockets work on the principle of action and reaction. They carry spacecraft beyond the earth's atmosphere into space. Once in space, they can place satellites in orbit or send probes to other planets.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Our Earth and Our Solar System
questions.text: Explain why the earth does not fall into the sun despite the sun's gravitational pull.
questions.answer: The earth does not fall into the sun because it is moving forward at a high speed in its orbit. The sun's gravity pulls the earth inward, but the earth's forward motion keeps it in a balanced path. This balance between gravity and motion results in a stable orbit. If the earth stopped moving, it would fall into the sun. Thus, it is the combination of gravity and orbital velocity that keeps the earth in orbit.

questions.text: What is a leap year?
questions.answer: A leap year is a year with 366 days, occurring every four years to account for the extra 6 hours in Earth's orbit.

questions.text: What is the equator?
questions.answer: The equator is an imaginary circle around the Earth, equidistant from the North and South Poles, dividing it into northern and southern hemispheres.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how day and night occur on Earth.
questions.answer: Day and night occur due to the Earth's rotation on its axis. As the Earth rotates, the part facing the Sun experiences day, while the part away from the Sun experiences night. One complete rotation takes about 24 hours, which we call a day.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are seasons reversed in the northern and southern hemispheres?
questions.answer: Seasons are reversed because of the tilt of the Earth's axis. When the northern hemisphere tilts toward the Sun, it experiences summer, while the southern hemisphere tilts away and experiences winter, and vice versa.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What is the lunar month and how is it related to tithi?
questions.answer: The lunar month is the time taken by the Moon to complete one revolution around the Earth, lasting about 28-30 days. Each day in the lunar month is called a tithi, and there are 30 tithis in a lunar month.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How does the Earth's inclined axis affect the length of day and night?
questions.answer: Due to the tilt of the Earth's axis, different parts of the Earth receive varying amounts of sunlight throughout the year. This causes the length of day and night to change, with longer days in summer and longer nights in winter in each hemisphere.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we have a leap year every four years?
questions.answer: We have a leap year every four years because the Earth takes approximately 365 days and 6 hours to complete one revolution around the Sun. The extra 6 hours accumulate to one full day every four years, which is added as February 29th to keep the calendar in sync with Earth's orbit.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it summer in the northern hemisphere when it is winter in the southern hemisphere?
questions.answer: It is summer in the northern hemisphere and winter in the southern hemisphere because of the tilt of the Earth's axis. When the North Pole tilts toward the Sun, the northern hemisphere receives more direct sunlight and heat, while the southern hemisphere receives less, causing opposite seasons.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we only see one side of the Moon from Earth?
questions.answer: We only see one side of the Moon because the Moon's period of rotation on its axis is equal to its period of revolution around the Earth. This synchronous rotation means the same side always faces Earth.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Describe the motion of the Earth and its effects on day, night, and seasons.
questions.answer: The Earth has two main motions: rotation and revolution. Rotation is the spinning of the Earth on its axis, which causes day and night. One rotation takes 24 hours. Revolution is the movement of the Earth around the Sun in an elliptical orbit, which takes one year. The Earth's axis is tilted at an angle of about 23.5 degrees. This tilt, combined with revolution, causes different parts of the Earth to receive varying amounts of sunlight throughout the year, leading to the change of seasons. When a hemisphere tilts toward the Sun, it experiences summer; when it tilts away, it experiences winter. The equator divides the Earth into northern and southern hemispheres, which experience opposite seasons at the same time.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the phases of the Moon with the help of a diagram (describe in words).
questions.answer: The phases of the Moon are the changing shapes of the illuminated part of the Moon as seen from Earth. They occur because the Moon revolves around the Earth, and we see different portions of its sunlit side. The cycle begins with the new moon, when the Moon is between the Earth and Sun and its dark side faces us. As it moves, we see a slim crescent (waxing crescent), then half (first quarter), then more than half (waxing gibbous), and finally the full moon, when the entire sunlit side is visible. After full moon, the illuminated part decreases: waning gibbous, last quarter (half), waning crescent, and back to new moon. This cycle takes about 29.5 days and is called a lunar month. Each day in this cycle is called a tithi. The Moon does not produce its own light; we see it only because it reflects sunlight.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define rotation of the Earth.
questions.answer: Rotation of the Earth is the spinning of the Earth on its imaginary axis from west to east, completing one turn in approximately 24 hours, which causes day and night.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define revolution of the Earth.
questions.answer: Revolution of the Earth is its movement around the Sun in an elliptical orbit, completing one revolution in approximately 365 days and 6 hours, which causes the cycle of seasons.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how the Earth's inclined axis leads to the cycle of seasons.
questions.answer: The Earth's axis is tilted at an angle of about 23.5 degrees relative to its orbital plane. As the Earth revolves around the Sun, this tilt causes different hemispheres to receive more or less direct sunlight at different times of the year. When the northern hemisphere tilts toward the Sun, it receives more direct sunlight and experiences summer, while the southern hemisphere tilts away and experiences winter. Six months later, the situation reverses. This annual change in solar exposure due to the tilt and revolution results in the repeating cycle of seasons: spring, summer, autumn, and winter.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the concept of a lunar month and its relation to tithi.
questions.answer: A lunar month is the time taken by the Moon to complete one full revolution around the Earth, lasting approximately 29.5 days. During this period, the Moon goes through all its phases, from new moon to full moon and back to new moon. Each day in the lunar month is called a tithi, and there are typically 30 tithis in a lunar month. The tithis are used in the Hindu calendar to determine auspicious days for festivals and rituals. The lunar month is based on the Moon's synodic period, which is the time between two consecutive new moons as seen from Earth.

questions.chapter: The Earth and its Living World
questions.text: Explain how the water cycle works in nature.
questions.answer: Water from oceans, lakes, and rivers evaporates due to the sun's heat and rises as water vapour. As it rises, it cools and condenses to form clouds. When the droplets become heavy, they fall as rain, which flows back into water bodies, completing the cycle.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: The Earth and its Living World
questions.text: Describe the layers of the atmosphere and name the layer closest to the earth.
questions.answer: The atmosphere has five layers: troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, ionosphere, and exosphere. The layer closest to the earth's surface is the troposphere, where we live and weather occurs.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1

questions.answer: Landforms are natural features of the earth's surface like mountains, plains, hills, and plateaus. Examples include mountains and plains.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: The Earth and its Living World
questions.text: How do living things depend on the spheres of the earth?
questions.answer: Living things depend on the lithosphere for land and minerals, hydrosphere for water, and atmosphere for air. Together, these spheres support life in the biosphere.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: The Earth and its Living World
questions.text: Why do aeroplanes fly in the lower part of the stratosphere?
questions.answer: Aeroplanes fly in the lower part of the stratosphere because the air is stable and there is less turbulence, which makes flying smoother and safer at high altitudes.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: The Earth and its Living World
questions.text: Why is the ozone layer important for living things?
questions.answer: The ozone layer is important because it absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays from the sun, protecting living organisms from skin damage and diseases.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: The Earth and its Living World
questions.text: Why is groundwater important for human use?
questions.answer: Groundwater is important because it is a reliable source of fresh water, especially in areas where surface water is scarce, and it is accessed through wells for drinking and irrigation.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: The Earth and its Living World
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Describe the biosphere and explain how living things interact with the earth's spheres.
questions.answer: The biosphere is the global sum of all ecosystems, where living organisms exist and interact with the lithosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere. Plants take nutrients from the soil (lithosphere) and water from the hydrosphere, and use carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to make food. Animals depend on plants and other animals for food and shelter. Micro-organisms decompose dead matter, returning nutrients to the soil. All living things respire, taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide, thus interacting with the atmosphere. This interdependence maintains the balance of nature.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: The Earth and its Living World
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Explain the water cycle with the help of a diagram. Mention the key processes involved.
questions.answer: The water cycle is the continuous movement of water on, above, and below the earth's surface. It begins with evaporation, where water from oceans, lakes, and rivers turns into vapour due to solar heat. The vapour rises, cools, and condenses to form clouds. When water droplets in clouds become heavy, they fall as precipitation (rain, snow). This water collects in rivers, lakes, and oceans, or seeps into the ground as groundwater. Eventually, it flows back to the oceans, and the cycle repeats. The sun drives this cycle, and it is essential for sustaining life and regulating climate.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: The Earth and its Living World
questions.text: Define lithosphere.
questions.answer: The lithosphere is the rigid outer layer of the earth, consisting of the crust and the upper part of the mantle, made of rock and soil.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: The Earth and its Living World
questions.text: Define atmosphere.
questions.answer: The atmosphere is the thick layer of air surrounding the earth, composed of gases like nitrogen, oxygen, water vapour, and carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: The Earth and its Living World
questions.text: Explain how the ozone layer protects living things on earth.
questions.answer: The ozone layer is located in the stratosphere and contains a high concentration of ozone gas. It absorbs the majority of the sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation, particularly UV-B and UV-C rays. These rays can cause skin cancer, cataracts, and damage to plants and marine life. By absorbing UV radiation, the ozone layer acts as a protective shield for all living organisms. Without it, life on earth would be severely affected by increased radiation exposure.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: The Earth and its Living World
questions.text: Explain the formation of groundwater and how it is accessed by humans.
questions.answer: Groundwater forms when rainwater and surface water seep into the soil and pass through porous layers of rock and sand, accumulating underground. It is stored in aquifers, which are natural underground reservoirs. Humans access groundwater by digging wells or using bore wells to pump it out. This water is often used for drinking, irrigation, and industrial purposes. Groundwater is a vital source of fresh water, especially in dry regions where surface water is limited.

questions.text: How do micro-organisms help in maintaining environmental balance?

questions.text: What happens to the oxygen we breathe out?
questions.answer: Plants use the carbon dioxide we breathe out to make their food and release oxygen back into the air.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What is meant by environmental balance?
questions.answer: Environmental balance is the state where natural cycles like water, oxygen and food chains work uninterrupted, supporting life.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how the water cycle helps maintain environmental balance.
questions.answer: The water cycle ensures a continuous supply of fresh water through evaporation, condensation and precipitation. This water is used by plants, animals and humans for survival. When water is returned to nature, it supports ecosystems and keeps the environment in balance.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important to maintain biodiversity in an area?
questions.answer: Biodiversity ensures that many different living things exist, which strengthens food chains and helps the environment recover from changes. If one species disappears, others can still fulfill their roles. This keeps the ecosystem stable and healthy.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How do plants and animals depend on each other in the environment?
questions.answer: Plants provide food and oxygen to animals, while animals release carbon dioxide that plants use to make food. When plants and animals die, their remains are broken down by micro-organisms, enriching the soil for new plants to grow.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What would happen if micro-organisms were absent from the soil?
questions.answer: Dead plants and animals would not decompose, so nutrients would not return to the soil. Plants would not get the nutrients they need to grow, which would affect the entire food chain. Over time, this would disrupt environmental balance.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is sunlight essential for a food chain to exist?
questions.answer: Sunlight is essential because plants use it to make their food through photosynthesis. Since plants are the first link in most food chains, without sunlight, they cannot produce food, and all other living things that depend on them would not survive.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we say that environmental balance is maintained when natural cycles continue without interruption?
questions.answer: Natural cycles like the water cycle, oxygen-carbon dioxide cycle and decomposition ensure that essential resources are continuously reused. If these cycles stop, resources like water, oxygen and nutrients would run out, making it difficult for living things to survive.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is a food web more stable than a single food chain?
questions.answer: A food web is more stable because one living thing can be part of many food chains. If one species becomes scarce, others can still find food from different sources. This reduces the risk of collapse in the ecosystem.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Describe how various cycles in nature work together to maintain environmental balance.
questions.answer: Environmental balance is maintained by the continuous operation of natural cycles. The water cycle ensures fresh water is available through evaporation and rain. Plants use carbon dioxide from the air and release oxygen during photosynthesis, while animals breathe in oxygen and release carbon dioxide, keeping the air balanced. Micro-organisms break down dead matter in the soil, releasing nutrients that help plants grow. When plants and animals die, their remains return to the soil, completing the nutrient cycle. These cycles are interconnected — for example, water helps plants grow, plants support food chains, and decomposition enriches the soil. As long as these cycles function without disruption, the environment remains balanced and life can continue.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain with an example how a food chain works and what happens if one link is removed.
questions.answer: Consider a simple food chain: Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake. Grass makes food using sunlight. Grasshopper eats grass, frog eats grasshopper, and snake eats frog. Each organism gets energy from the one before it. If frogs disappear due to pollution or disease, grasshoppers may increase in number and eat too much grass, damaging plants. Snakes, losing their food source, may die or move away. This shows how removing one link affects the entire chain. In nature, most organisms are part of multiple chains (forming a food web), which provides some protection, but still, every link is important for balance.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Biodiversity
questions.answer: Biodiversity refers to the variety of living things found in a particular area, including different types of plants, animals and micro-organisms.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Food chain
questions.answer: A food chain is a sequence of living things in which each organism serves as food for the next organism in the sequence.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How do plants contribute to the oxygen-carbon dioxide cycle in nature?
questions.answer: Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air during the process of photosynthesis. Using sunlight, water and this carbon dioxide, they make their food and release oxygen as a byproduct. This oxygen is released into the air and used by animals and humans for breathing. When we breathe out, we release carbon dioxide, which plants again use to make food. This continuous exchange keeps the levels of oxygen and carbon dioxide balanced in the atmosphere.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it necessary to maintain environmental balance for the survival of living things?
questions.answer: Environmental balance ensures that essential resources like water, air and soil remain healthy and available. If natural cycles such as the water cycle or decomposition are disturbed, resources may become scarce or polluted. Living things depend on these resources for food, shelter and reproduction. Without balance, food chains break, biodiversity reduces, and ecosystems may collapse. Therefore, maintaining environmental balance is crucial for the long-term survival of all living things.

questions.text: How does tolerance help in preserving diversity in our country?

questions.text: Give two examples of gender equality in daily life.
questions.answer: Boys and girls being allowed to choose the same toys, like bats and dolls, and both being given equal opportunities to study and play sports are examples of gender equality.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we be honest in our private and public life?
questions.answer: We should be honest because it builds self-confidence and trust in relationships. In private life, it strengthens family bonds, and in public life, it ensures fair use of resources and better services for all.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is co-operation necessary in public life?
questions.answer: Co-operation is necessary because tasks like organizing fairs, rallies, or community projects require collective effort. Without co-operation, such events cannot be successful or well-managed.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important to respect others' opinions in a family?
questions.answer: Respecting others' opinions makes every member feel valued and encourages open discussion. This leads to better decisions that everyone agrees with and strengthens family unity.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe how honesty, co-operation, and tolerance together make our family and community life happy and peaceful.
questions.answer: Honesty builds trust among family and community members, making relationships strong and reliable. Co-operation ensures that everyone works together toward common goals, like preparing for festivals or solving problems. Tolerance allows us to respect differences in opinions, habits, and cultures, preventing conflicts. When these three values are practiced, families communicate better, communities function smoothly, and people feel safe and respected. Together, they create a harmonious environment where everyone can grow and progress.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain how gender equality and tolerance contribute to the progress of boys and girls in society.
questions.answer: Gender equality ensures that boys and girls have equal access to education, sports, and opportunities to grow, without discrimination. When both are treated fairly, they can develop their talents and confidence equally. Tolerance adds to this by encouraging respect for each other’s choices and differences, whether in interests, clothing, or ambitions. Together, they create an inclusive environment where no child is held back due to gender. This leads to better learning, healthier relationships, and a more just society where everyone can contribute to progress.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1

questions.answer: Honesty is the quality of being truthful and sincere in thoughts, words, and actions.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Gender equality

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How does a tolerant attitude help in preserving diversity in our country?
questions.answer: A tolerant attitude means respecting people who are different from us in religion, language, culture, or customs. In our country, people from various backgrounds live together, and tolerance allows them to coexist peacefully. When we accept and respect these differences, we prevent conflicts and promote unity. This helps preserve the rich diversity of our nation, which is a source of strength and beauty. Tolerance, therefore, is essential for maintaining social harmony and national progress.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important for every family member to have a say in decision-making?
questions.answer: When every family member gets a chance to express their opinion, it ensures that decisions are fair and consider everyone’s needs. It makes individuals feel valued and respected, which strengthens family bonds. Discussing different views leads to better solutions, as more ideas are considered. This practice also teaches children responsibility and prepares them to participate in society. Thus, shared decision-making builds trust, unity, and democratic values within the family.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we need to make laws for the protection of the environment?
questions.answer: We need to make laws to protect the environment because natural resources are limited and must be conserved for future generations. Laws ensure that we use resources carefully and prevent pollution and destruction of nature.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Which unjust customs have been banned by law in our country?
questions.answer: Unjust customs such as sati, child marriage, untouchability, and the dowry system have been banned by law in our country. Laws were also made to ban the use of magic for cheating people.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How do customs and traditions help in maintaining the balance of nature?
questions.answer: Many customs and traditions express love and gratitude towards animals and promote non-violence and peace. These values help maintain the balance of nature by encouraging sustainable living and respect for all living beings.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What change occurred in the voting age after Independence?
questions.answer: After Independence, the voting age was 21 years. After 1988, it was lowered to 18 years to allow more young people to participate in democracy.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we obey traffic rules?
questions.answer: We should obey traffic rules to ensure smooth movement of traffic and prevent accidents. Following rules helps maintain order and safety on the roads for everyone.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it wrong to discriminate between boys and girls?
questions.answer: It is wrong to discriminate between boys and girls because it is unjust and deprives girls of good food, education, and equal opportunities for development. Equality is the basis of a fair society.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we say that ‘equality’ is the basis of rules?
questions.answer: We say equality is the basis of rules because rules apply equally to all, and no one is above them. Punishments for breaking rules are the same for everyone, ensuring fairness and justice.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how rules help in making our society disciplined and just.
questions.answer: Rules help make our society disciplined by specifying duties and responsibilities for everyone. When people follow rules, daily life becomes orderly and efficient. Rules also promote justice by ensuring equality—no one is above the law, and punishments are the same for all. They protect the weak, ban harmful customs like untouchability and child labour, and safeguard the environment. Thus, rules create a fair and peaceful society where everyone can live with dignity.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Describe the difference between the rules of society and the laws of nature.
questions.answer: The rules of society are made by humans and can be changed with time and needs, such as lowering the voting age or banning child labour. In contrast, the laws of nature, like gravity or the rising and setting of the sun, are constant and cannot be changed by humans. While society’s rules aim for justice and equality, natural laws govern physical phenomena and always remain the same.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Untouchability
questions.answer: Untouchability was an inhuman and unjust custom where certain people were considered impure and were discriminated against, denied basic rights and social equality.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Natural resources
questions.answer: Natural resources are materials or substances such as water, air, forests, and minerals that occur in nature and are used to fulfill human needs.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How do laws help in combating unjust customs?
questions.answer: Laws help combat unjust customs by banning practices that are harmful or discriminatory, such as sati, child marriage, untouchability, and the dowry system. When a custom is made illegal, people are punished for following it, which discourages such behaviour. Over time, this leads to social change and promotes equality and justice. Laws also create awareness that such customs are wrong and must be abolished for the good of society.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we say that rules are meant for everybody?
questions.answer: We say rules are meant for everybody because they apply equally to all individuals, regardless of their status, wealth, or background. No one is above the law, and everyone must follow the same rules. This ensures fairness and prevents discrimination. When rules are universal, they create a sense of justice and unity in society, helping everyone live together peacefully and with dignity.

questions.chapter: Let us Solve our own Problems
questions.text: What is the significance of the bell rung on International Peace Day at the UN?
questions.answer: The bell, made from coins of about 60 nations, is rung to symbolize global unity and commitment to peace.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Let us Solve our own Problems
questions.text: Explain the concept of cleaning the village through ‘shramdaan’ with reference to Khudawadi village.
questions.answer: In Khudawadi village, people participated in shramdaan by voluntarily offering their labour to clean the village. They first dealt with waste water, then used garbage to make manure through vermiculture, and built toilets in each house. This collective effort improved sanitation and environmental health without external help.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Let us Solve our own Problems
questions.text: How can a suitable environment for peace be created in school and society?
questions.answer: A suitable environment for peace can be created by promoting co-operation, resolving disputes through dialogue, ensuring everyone’s basic needs are met, reducing inequality, and encouraging participation in public life. Learning from peace advocates like Sant Gadgebaba and following their teachings also helps build lasting peace.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Let us Solve our own Problems
questions.text: What are the benefits of peace in family, school, and society?
questions.answer: Peace in family, school, and society leads to happiness, better focus on studies and work, increased co-operation, progress in education and business, and overall development. It creates a positive environment where everyone feels safe and valued, which encourages creativity and hard work.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Let us Solve our own Problems
questions.text: Why is it important to solve problems in time according to the chapter?
questions.answer: It is important to solve problems in time because if ignored, they grow worse and cause more harm. Timely solution prevents loss of unity, stops inconvenience, and maintains harmony in the community.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Let us Solve our own Problems
questions.text: Why should we not turn a blind eye towards problems in civic life?
questions.answer: We should not turn a blind eye towards problems because ignoring them allows them to grow worse over time. Small issues can become big disputes that harm peace and unity. Addressing them early through co-operation prevents larger harm and maintains harmony in society.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Let us Solve our own Problems
questions.text: Why is the ‘Mahatma Gandhi Dispute-Free Village Mission’ considered effective in solving disputes?
questions.answer: This mission is effective because it encourages villagers to solve their own disputes through peaceful discussions instead of going to court. It builds trust, promotes co-operation, and strengthens village unity. Villages that succeed also receive peace awards, which motivates others to follow the same path.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Let us Solve our own Problems
questions.text: Why is cleanliness important for progress according to Sant Gadgebaba?
questions.answer: Sant Gadgebaba believed that progress is impossible without cleanliness because a dirty environment leads to disease, low morale, and lack of self-respect. Cleanliness, along with education and self-reliance, forms the foundation for a healthy and productive society. He showed this by leading cleaning efforts himself.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Let us Solve our own Problems
questions.text: Define ‘issues in civic life’.
questions.answer: Issues in civic life are problems faced by people in their daily living in villages and cities, such as disputes over land, water shortage, or unclean surroundings, which affect peace, harmony, and progress if not solved.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Let us Solve our own Problems
questions.text: Define ‘shramdaan’.
questions.answer: Shramdaan is the voluntary contribution of labour by individuals for community welfare activities like cleaning villages, building toilets, or managing waste, done without expecting payment.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Let us Solve our own Problems
questions.text: Explain how peace contributes to progress in various fields like business, industry, and education.
questions.answer: Peace creates a stable and safe environment where people can focus on their work without fear or distraction. In business and industry, peace allows for smooth production, trade, and investment. In education, students can attend school regularly and concentrate on learning. Peace also encourages innovation, co-operation, and participation in public life, which leads to overall social and economic development. When there is no conflict, resources are used for growth instead of damage control, making progress faster and more sustainable.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Let us Solve our own Problems
questions.text: Explain the role of peacekeepers in maintaining harmony in a village or school.
questions.answer: Peacekeepers help resolve conflicts by listening to all sides, encouraging dialogue, and suggesting fair solutions based on discussion. They promote co-operation, prevent small issues from turning into big disputes, and create a sense of trust and safety. In schools, they can help maintain quiet and respect; in villages, they support efforts like shramdaan and dispute-free initiatives. Their work strengthens unity and ensures that everyone feels heard and valued.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Let us Solve our own Problems
questions.text: Describe how your class can solve a problem like littering in the schoolyard using peaceful methods and co-operation.
questions.answer: Our class can solve the littering problem by first discussing it calmly and identifying why it happens. We can then form a group of student peacekeepers to remind others to use dustbins. We will organize a shramdaan day where everyone volunteers to clean the yard. We can also make posters about cleanliness and request the school to place more bins. By working together and respecting each other, we can keep our school clean and peaceful.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Let us Solve our own Problems
questions.text: Explain how the ‘Dispute-Free Village Mission’ has helped Hiware Bazaar overcome its water shortage and become a model village.
questions.answer: Hiware Bazaar faced severe water shortage, which caused disputes and hindered progress. Under the Dispute-Free Village Mission, villagers came together and used peaceful discussions to decide on solutions. They adopted water conservation methods like rainwater harvesting, recharging groundwater, and growing less water-intensive crops. Through shramdaan, they built check dams and repaired old wells. As water became available, agriculture improved, incomes rose, and the village turned green. Peaceful co-operation solved both the water problem and social conflicts, making Hiware Bazaar a model for other villages.

questions.text: List any four public facilities available in or near your school.
questions.answer: Four public facilities available in or near our school are: classrooms, playground, drinking water facility, and library. Some schools also have toilets, computer lab, and midday meal scheme. These help students learn and stay healthy.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is education considered a fundamental right?
questions.answer: Education is a fundamental right because every child deserves the chance to learn and grow. It helps them become responsible citizens and improves their future. The government ensures free education for children aged 6 to 14 under the Right to Education Act.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How did the students help in the cleanliness drive in their village?
questions.answer: The students prepared posters, presented street plays, and convinced villagers not to spit in public or litter. They worked with the school to spread awareness about cleanliness. Their efforts helped the village win the 'Clean Village' award.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What are the benefits of having a Parent Teacher Association in a school?
questions.answer: The Parent Teacher Association helps parents and teachers work together for the betterment of the school. It allows parents to participate in school activities and stay informed about their child’s progress. This cooperation improves the school environment and student development.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why must we use public facilities responsibly?
questions.answer: We must use public facilities responsibly because they are meant for everyone’s use. If misused or damaged, they may not be available when needed. Responsible use ensures that these facilities last longer and serve the community well.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is the school considered a part of the system of public services?
questions.answer: The school is considered a part of the public services system because it provides education, which is a basic need for all children. Like other public services, it is meant for everyone and contributes to the development of society. It also works with the community, just like other public institutions.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should children with special needs be allowed to go to school up to the age of 18?
questions.answer: Children with special needs may require more time to learn and develop skills due to their conditions. Extending the age limit to 18 ensures they get adequate support and education. This helps them become independent and participate fully in society.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Describe how your school is a part of the public facilities system and how it helps in the development of the community.
questions.answer: Our school is a public facility that provides education to all children, just like hospitals provide health care and buses provide transport. It is open to every child, regardless of background, and helps in their overall growth. The school works with the community — parents, local artists, and experts often help in events, construction, or teaching special skills. Through activities like cleanliness drives, cultural programs, and parent-teacher meetings, the school strengthens community bonds. It also teaches students to be responsible citizens by using public facilities properly. In this way, the school not only educates children but also contributes to the development and unity of the surrounding area.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the role of the community in the growth and development of a school with examples from the chapter.
questions.answer: The community plays a vital role in setting up and improving a school. Many parents volunteer their time and resources to help build classrooms or buy sports equipment. Past students often donate books or funds for laboratories. Artists and scientists may conduct workshops or share knowledge to enrich learning. Industrialists might help in constructing buildings or providing technology. For example, the chapter mentions that parents, artists, sportspersons, and scientists lend a hand in the growth of a school. This collective effort ensures that the school has better facilities and offers a richer learning experience. When the community participates, the school becomes a shared pride and a stronger institution for all.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Public facilities
questions.answer: Public facilities are services and structures provided by the government or community for the use of all people, such as water supply, electricity, schools, hospitals, and transport.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Right to Education
questions.answer: The Right to Education is a fundamental right that ensures every child between the ages of 6 and 14 (and up to 18 for children with special needs) has the opportunity to go to school and receive free and compulsory education.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How do public facilities like bus, railway, and post office help in daily life?
questions.answer: Public facilities like buses and railways help people travel easily from one place to another for work, school, or leisure. The post office allows us to send letters, documents, and parcels to others across the country or world. These services are affordable and available to everyone, making daily life more convenient. They connect people and places, supporting trade, communication, and social interaction. Without such facilities, it would be difficult to access essential services or maintain relationships far away.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important for schools to have facilities like playgrounds, laboratories, and libraries?
questions.answer: Playgrounds help students stay physically active and develop teamwork through sports and games. Laboratories allow students to conduct experiments and understand science concepts practically. Libraries provide access to books and resources that enhance reading skills and knowledge. Together, these facilities support the overall development of a child — physical, mental, and intellectual. They make learning enjoyable, practical, and well-rounded, preparing students for future challenges.

questions.text: Explain how the contour line method shows the slope of the land.
questions.answer: In the contour line method, when contour lines are close together, it indicates a steep slope. When they are far apart, it indicates a gentle slope. This helps us understand the steepness of the land.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are standard signs and symbols used on maps?
questions.answer: Standard signs and symbols are used on maps so that everyone can understand them easily, regardless of language or region. They make maps uniform and easy to read.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What information do physical maps give us about a region?
questions.answer: Physical maps give us information about the height, relief, and slope of a region. They show natural features like mountains, valleys, rivers, and plateaus.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How is the digital elevation model different from the contour line method?
questions.answer: The digital elevation model uses satellite data and computers to show height, while the contour line method uses drawn lines on paper. The digital method is more modern and precise.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are colours used in the layer tinting method?
questions.answer: Colours are used in the layer tinting method to show different heights of land. Each colour represents a specific height range, making it easy to see high and low areas at a glance.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is the Survey of India important for mapmaking?
questions.answer: The Survey of India is important because it makes accurate topographic maps of India, which are used for military, tourism, and development purposes. It has been doing this since 1767.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we need to study the physical set-up of the land?
questions.answer: We need to study the physical set-up of the land to understand our environment better, such as knowing the height, slope, and landforms, which helps in agriculture, construction, and disaster planning.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Describe the three methods of showing height on a map: contour line method, layer tinting method, and digital elevation model.
questions.answer: The contour line method shows height by drawing lines joining places of equal height; close lines mean steep slope, far apart mean gentle slope. The layer tinting method fills the spaces between contour lines with colours, where each colour represents a height range, like blue for water and green for low land. The digital elevation model uses satellite data and computers to show height, giving a detailed and accurate 3D view of the land. All three help us understand the physical set-up of a region.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the importance of conventional signs and symbols in maps with examples.
questions.answer: Conventional signs and symbols are universally accepted marks used on maps to show specific features like temples, hospitals, rivers, and roads. For example, a cross may represent a hospital, a blue line a river, and a green patch a forest. These symbols make maps easy to read and understand by everyone, regardless of language. They are listed in the map's key. Without them, maps would be confusing and hard to interpret.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How do colours help in understanding the height of land on a layer tinted map?
questions.answer: In the layer tinting method, different colours are used between contour lines to show different height ranges. For example, blue is used for water bodies, dark green for low land, yellow for higher land, and so on. This colour coding allows us to quickly identify which areas are high or low without reading numbers. The change in colour gives a visual idea of the land's relief. Thus, colours make the map more informative and easier to interpret.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are physical maps useful in tourism and mountaineering?
questions.answer: Physical maps show the natural features of land such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and slopes, which are essential for tourists and mountaineers. They help in planning safe routes by showing steep slopes, high peaks, and valleys. Tourists can use them to find scenic spots, while mountaineers rely on them to avoid dangerous areas. These maps also show the height of places, helping in preparation for high-altitude travel. Hence, physical maps are vital tools for outdoor activities.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: List three geographical features of India mentioned in the chapter.
questions.answer: India has mountains, plateaus, plains, rivers, islands, deserts, and coastal regions. The Himalayas form the northern border, the Thar Desert is in the west, and the Western and Eastern Ghats run along the coasts.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why does India have a variety of crops, clothing, and festivals?
questions.answer: India has diverse weather conditions due to its large size and varying height above sea level. This leads to different crops being grown in different regions, which in turn affects food, clothing, and festivals.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Name the island groups of India and the seas they are located in.
questions.answer: The Lakshadweep islands are in the Arabian Sea, and the Andaman and Nicobar islands are in the Bay of Bengal. Coastal islands are also found near the mainland.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is the climate different in different parts of India?
questions.answer: The climate varies across India because the country spans a large area with different latitudes and altitudes. The Himalayas block cold winds from the north, while the coastal areas are influenced by the sea. The Thar Desert in the west experiences extreme heat, whereas the northeastern regions receive heavy rainfall.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is rice a primary crop in southern and coastal India?
questions.answer: Rice requires a lot of water and warm temperatures to grow, which are available in the southern and coastal regions of India. These areas receive heavy rainfall and have fertile soil, making them ideal for rice cultivation.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are the Andaman and Nicobar islands strategically important?
questions.answer: The Andaman and Nicobar islands are strategically important because they lie near major sea routes in the Bay of Bengal and help in monitoring maritime activity. They also serve as a defensive outpost for the country.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the physical diversity of India with examples of landforms, water bodies, and vegetation.
questions.answer: India has a rich physical diversity. In the north, there are the lofty Himalayas, which are the source of many rivers like the Ganga and Yamuna. The northern plains are fertile and support wheat and sugarcane. To the west lies the Thar Desert, a dry and sandy region. The central part has plateaus like the Deccan, where jowar and cotton are grown. The Western and Eastern Ghats run along the coasts, supporting evergreen forests. India is surrounded by the Arabian Sea on the west, the Bay of Bengal on the east, and the Indian Ocean to the south. Coastal regions have coconut trees and fishing communities. This diversity in landforms, water, and climate leads to a variety of plants, animals, crops, and cultures across the country.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain how the physical features of India influence the lifestyle and culture of its people.
questions.answer: The physical features of India greatly influence how people live. In the mountainous regions like the Himalayas, people wear woolen clothes, practice terrace farming, and follow unique traditions. In the desert areas of Rajasthan, people live in mud houses, wear bright clothes to reflect heat, and celebrate festivals like Desert Festival. In the fertile plains of Punjab and Uttar Pradesh, wheat and rice farming are common, leading to dishes like roti and dal. Coastal regions such as Kerala and Goa have coconut-based cuisine, fishing as a livelihood, and festivals like Onam and Carnival. The availability of water, soil type, and climate determines the crops grown, which in turn shapes food, clothing, housing, and celebrations. Thus, India’s diverse geography leads to a rich variety of lifestyles and cultures.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the course of the Ganga river from its origin to its mouth.
questions.answer: The Ganga river originates from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas of Uttarakhand. It flows southward through the states of Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Jharkhand. Along its course, it is joined by many tributaries like the Yamuna, Ghaghara, and Kosi. The river then flows through West Bengal and finally empties into the Bay of Bengal. The Ganga forms a large delta known as the Sundarbans before meeting the sea.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain why India is called a land of diversity.
questions.answer: India is called a land of diversity because it has a wide variety of landforms, climates, languages, religions, cultures, and traditions. The country stretches from the snow-covered Himalayas in the north to the tropical coasts in the south. Different regions have different crops, clothing, food, and festivals. Over 22 official languages and hundreds of dialects are spoken. People follow various religions such as Hinduism, Islam, Christianity, Sikhism, and Buddhism. This rich mix of natural and cultural differences makes India unique and diverse.

questions.answer: Homeless people lack shelter and often live on footpaths, under bridges, or in temporary shelters. They also face difficulties in getting food, clean water, and safety.

questions.answer: Using solar energy, recycling water and garbage, and avoiding artificial materials and colours are three eco-friendly practices that can be followed in a house.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it necessary to use non-exhaustible sources of energy in house construction and use?
questions.answer: Non-exhaustible sources like solar and wind energy are available in plenty and do not get depleted. Using them reduces pollution and saves natural resources like coal and oil for future generations.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we need to protect the environment while building houses?
questions.answer: Protecting the environment ensures that natural resources like trees, water, and soil are not destroyed. It also prevents pollution and maintains ecological balance for all living beings.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we avoid using artificial materials in eco-friendly houses?
questions.answer: Artificial materials often cause pollution during production and disposal. They are not biodegradable and can harm the environment, so avoiding them helps in keeping the house eco-friendly.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe how the type of house built in a region depends on the climate and available materials. Give examples.
questions.answer: The type of house built in a region depends on the local climate and the materials easily available there. In heavy rainfall areas, houses have sloping roofs to drain water and are built on raised platforms to avoid flooding. In desert regions, houses have thick walls and small windows to keep the inside cool during hot days. In mountainous areas, stone and wood are used because they are readily available and provide insulation against cold. Using local materials reduces cost and effort, and the design ensures comfort and protection from weather conditions.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain what an eco-friendly house is and list any four features that make a house eco-friendly.
questions.answer: An eco-friendly house is one that is built and used in a way that causes minimum harm to the environment. It uses natural resources wisely and avoids pollution. Features of an eco-friendly house include the use of solar or wind energy, recycling of water and garbage, use of natural and locally available materials, and provision for natural light and ventilation. Such houses also avoid artificial materials and colours that can pollute. Building eco-friendly houses helps in conserving energy and protecting nature for future generations.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how construction work can lead to different types of pollution.
questions.answer: Construction work can cause air pollution due to dust from digging and smoke from machinery. It leads to noise pollution from loud equipment and vehicles. Water pollution can occur when waste materials or chemicals mix with nearby water bodies. Soil pollution happens when harmful substances are dumped on the land. All these affect the health of people and living things in the area.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important to use locally available materials for building houses?
questions.answer: Using locally available materials reduces the need for transportation, which saves fuel and lowers pollution. It is also cost-effective as the materials are easily accessible. It helps in preserving the local environment and supports the use of natural resources in a sustainable way.

questions.answer: The rabi season is the agricultural season from October to March when crops are watered by retained rainwater, dew, and retreating monsoons.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What is drip irrigation?
questions.answer: Drip irrigation is a method where water drips slowly near the roots of plants through pipes with small holes.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is storing grain important?
questions.answer: Storing grain is important to protect it from pests, moisture, and fungus so it can be used later when needed.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What is the Green Revolution?
questions.answer: The Green Revolution was a period of increased foodgrain production in India due to improved seeds, modern irrigation, and better farming techniques.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What are the advantages of using improved seeds?
questions.answer: Improved seeds give higher yield, resist pest attacks, and some varieties ripen faster. They also produce good yield even with less water. This helps farmers get more crop from the same land.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What are the modern methods of irrigation? State one advantage of each.
questions.answer: The modern methods of irrigation are drip irrigation and sprinkle irrigation. Drip irrigation saves water by dripping it near the plant roots. Sprinkle irrigation sprays water like rain, covering a wide area evenly.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How can damage to stored grain be prevented?
questions.answer: Damage to stored grain can be prevented by keeping it dry and airy, using neem leaves or safe chemicals to repel insects, and storing it in clean, pest-free places. Regular checking also helps avoid fungus and rodent damage.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What are natural fertilizers? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Natural fertilizers, also called manures, are obtained from plant and animal waste. Examples include compost and animal dung.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should chemical fertilizers not be used in excess?
questions.answer: Excessive use of chemical fertilizers makes the soil saline and reduces its fertility. It can also pollute water sources and harm useful organisms in the soil. Over time, the land becomes less productive and may need costly treatment to recover.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is the rabi season suitable for growing wheat?
questions.answer: The rabi season has cool temperatures and water from retained soil moisture, dew, and retreating monsoons, which are ideal for wheat growth. Wheat requires less water and grows well in these conditions.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is food storage important for disaster management?
questions.answer: During disasters like floods or droughts, fresh food production may stop. Stored surplus grain can be used to feed affected people. It helps prevent hunger and supports relief efforts in emergencies.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how improved methods of agriculture have increased food production in India.
questions.answer: Improved methods of agriculture have increased food production in India through the use of high-yielding and pest-resistant seeds, modern irrigation like drip and sprinkle systems, and better use of fertilizers and pesticides. Farmers now get timely weather and farming advice from agricultural assistance centres. Mechanization has reduced manual labour and increased efficiency. These improvements led to the Green Revolution, making India self-reliant in foodgrains and even allowing exports. Proper storage and distribution systems like Fair Price shops also ensure food reaches everyone.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Describe the importance of food storage and mention two ways to protect stored grain from damage.
questions.answer: Food storage is important to ensure food availability during off-seasons, natural disasters, or emergencies. It helps maintain food security and stable prices. To protect stored grain, it should be dried well and kept in airy, dry places to prevent fungus. Neem leaves or approved chemicals can be mixed with grain to repel insects. Storing in sealed but ventilated sacks or warehouses also keeps rodents away. Regular inspection ensures early detection of spoilage.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define: Kharif season
questions.answer: The Kharif season is the agricultural season from June to October when crops are sown with the onset of monsoon and are mainly watered by rain.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define: Food security
questions.answer: Food security means that all people have access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food to meet their dietary needs for an active and healthy life.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how overuse of water and fertilizers can harm the soil.
questions.answer: Overuse of water can lead to waterlogging and make the soil saline, especially in areas with poor drainage. Excess fertilizers, particularly chemical ones, accumulate in the soil and alter its natural balance. This reduces the soil’s fertility and harms useful microbes. Over time, the land becomes less productive and may need expensive treatment to restore. Hence, water and fertilizers should be used only as needed.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the role of Agricultural Assistance Programmes in helping farmers.
questions.answer: Agricultural Assistance Programmes provide farmers with information about improved seeds, modern irrigation, and proper use of fertilizers and pesticides. They offer weather forecasts and training on new farming techniques. Farmers can learn about organic farming and market trends through these centres. Agricultural schools and exhibitions also help in spreading awareness. This support enables farmers to increase yield, reduce costs, and adopt sustainable practices.

questions.text: How does drying help in preserving food?

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is food kept in a refrigerator less likely to spoil quickly?

questions.text: Give one example of a food preserved by adding salt and sugar.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain why food spoils and how we can prevent it.
questions.answer: Food spoils when micro-organisms like fungus and bacteria grow in it, especially when air, moisture, and warmth are present. We can prevent spoilage by drying, cooling, boiling, or using preservatives like salt and sugar. These methods either destroy micro-organisms or create conditions where they cannot grow.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are fruits and vegetables preserved in different seasons?
questions.answer: Fruits and vegetables are available in abundance only during certain seasons. To enjoy them throughout the year, we preserve them when they are plentiful using methods like drying, making jams, or pickling. This ensures supply and prevents wastage.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What changes occur in food when it gets spoiled?
questions.answer: Spoiled food may show changes like foul smell, change in colour, or growth of fuzzy patches (fungus). It may taste sour or bitter and can cause stomach ache, diarrhoea, or vomiting if eaten. Its nutritional value also decreases.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How does keeping food in airtight containers help in preservation?
questions.answer: Airtight containers prevent the entry of air, moisture, and micro-organisms from the outside. This stops new contamination and helps keep the food safe for a longer time. It is especially effective for dry foods like grains and pickles.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we boil milk before storing it?
questions.answer: We boil milk to destroy the micro-organisms present in it that can cause spoilage. Boiling kills these harmful microbes, making the milk safe to store for a few hours without getting spoiled immediately. This helps in keeping milk fresh until the next use.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are onions and potatoes dried in the sun before storage?
questions.answer: Onions and potatoes are dried in the sun to remove surface moisture, which prevents the growth of fungus and bacteria during storage. Moisture encourages spoilage, so drying helps in keeping them dry and safe for a longer period. This traditional method ensures they remain usable till the next season.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why does chapati kept in a closed box get spoiled faster than one kept in the fridge?
questions.answer: The closed box traps warmth and moisture, creating ideal conditions for micro-organisms like fungus to grow rapidly. In contrast, the fridge has low temperature which slows down microbial growth. Hence, the chapati in the box spoils faster due to favourable conditions for microbes.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Describe the different methods of preserving food with examples.
questions.answer: Food can be preserved by several methods: Drying removes water from food, as seen in papads, wheat, and daals. Cooling in a refrigerator slows microbial growth, used for milk, vegetables, and cooked food. Boiling destroys micro-organisms, applied to milk and curries before storage. Airtight sealing prevents entry of air and moisture, used in jam and pickle bottles. Preservatives like salt, sugar, oil, and vinegar stop microbial growth and are added to pickles, jams, and sauces. These methods ensure food remains safe, nutritious, and available throughout the year.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain why food preservation is necessary in our daily life.
questions.answer: Food preservation is essential because crops and seasonal foods are available only at certain times of the year. Without preservation, we would not have access to grains, fruits, or vegetables during off-seasons. It prevents wastage of surplus produce and ensures a steady food supply. Preserved food also helps during travel, emergencies, or when fresh food is not accessible. Moreover, it maintains nutritional value and protects us from eating spoiled food that can cause illness. Thus, preservation supports health, food security, and convenience in daily life.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Preservatives
questions.answer: Preservatives are substances like salt, sugar, oil, and vinegar that are added to food to prevent the growth of micro-organisms and thus stop spoilage.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Spoiled food
questions.answer: Spoiled food is food that has undergone undesirable changes due to the growth of micro-organisms, such as foul smell, change in colour or texture, and reduced nutritional value, making it unfit for consumption.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How does cooling help in preserving food?
questions.answer: Cooling reduces the temperature of food, which slows down the metabolic activities of micro-organisms. At lower temperatures, bacteria and fungus grow very slowly or remain inactive. This delay in microbial growth keeps food fresh for a longer period. Refrigerators are commonly used to cool and store perishable items like milk, cooked food, and vegetables. Thus, cooling is an effective and widely used method of food preservation.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we use salt and sugar as preservatives in pickles and jams?
questions.answer: Salt and sugar act as preservatives by drawing out moisture from food through osmosis, making it unavailable for micro-organisms. They create an environment where bacteria and fungus cannot survive or grow. In pickles, salt prevents spoilage and enhances flavour, while in jams, sugar helps in setting and long-term preservation. These substances are natural, safe, and have been used traditionally for generations. Hence, salt and sugar are effective and commonly used preservatives in Indian households.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: List three advantages of using a bicycle for short-distance travel.
