questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: State two harmful effects of air pollution on plants.
questions.answer: Air pollution causes the leaves of plants to shrivel and fall, and it affects the growth and development of plants adversely. It can also scorch sprouts and damage plant health.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important to maintain vehicles regularly?
questions.answer: Timely maintenance and repair of vehicles help reduce smoke and harmful gas emissions. It also ensures the vehicle runs efficiently and safely, reducing the risk of accidents and pollution.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Give two advantages of modern means of transport.
questions.answer: Modern means of transport help in saving time and effort, and they facilitate trade and tourism. They also connect different parts of the world and improve people's lifestyle by making goods and services easily available.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do vehicles using fuel cause air pollution?
questions.answer: Vehicles using fuel cause air pollution because burning fuel releases harmful gases like carbon monoxide, nitrogen dioxide, and sulphur dioxide, along with minute particles of carbon and lead into the air. These substances lower the quality of air and damage the environment.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is walking recommended for short distances?
questions.answer: Walking is recommended for short distances because it saves fuel, does not cause pollution, and provides physical exercise. It also helps reduce traffic congestion and is economical.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we use public transport as far as possible?
questions.answer: We should use public transport as far as possible because it reduces the number of private vehicles on the road, thereby lowering air and noise pollution. It also saves time, effort, and fuel for individuals.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Write a paragraph on the advantages and disadvantages of using automobiles.
questions.answer: Automobiles offer advantages such as saving time and effort, providing comfort, and enabling travel over long distances quickly. They facilitate trade, tourism, and access to education and healthcare. However, they have disadvantages like causing air and noise pollution due to fuel burning, leading to health problems. They also contribute to traffic congestion, require fuel, and can cause accidents. Regular maintenance and using cleaner fuels like CNG can help reduce their harmful effects.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Suggest four remedies to reduce pollution caused by transport in your locality.
questions.answer: To reduce transport pollution, we can use public transport more often, walk or bicycle for short distances, and use vehicles only when necessary. Regular maintenance of vehicles helps reduce smoke emissions. Using cleaner fuels like CNG or LPG instead of petrol or diesel lowers pollution. Planting trees along roadsides helps absorb pollutants. Encouraging carpooling and spreading awareness about pollution through street plays or posters can also be effective remedies.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define air pollution.
questions.answer: Air pollution is the presence of harmful substances like smoke, poisonous gases, and dust particles in the air, which lowers its quality and harms living beings and the environment.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define transport.
questions.answer: Transport is the movement of people, animals, or goods from one place to another using various means such as walking, bicycles, automobiles, trains, ships, or aeroplanes.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how the use of fuel in vehicles leads to air and noise pollution.
questions.answer: When fuel is burned in vehicle engines, it produces smoke and harmful gases such as carbon monoxide, nitrogen dioxide, and sulphur dioxide. Minute particles of carbon and lead are also released into the air. These pollutants lower the air quality and cause respiratory and eye problems in humans and animals. The constant movement and engines of vehicles create loud sounds, leading to noise pollution, which causes stress, headaches, and lack of concentration. Together, air and noise pollution from vehicles harm the environment and human health.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain why using a bicycle is beneficial for both health and the environment.
questions.answer: Using a bicycle provides physical exercise, which improves cardiovascular health and strengthens muscles. It helps in maintaining a healthy weight and reduces the risk of lifestyle diseases. Environmentally, a bicycle does not use fuel, so it does not emit smoke or harmful gases. It also produces no noise, helping to reduce noise pollution. Additionally, bicycles take up less space on roads, reducing traffic congestion and promoting cleaner, quieter cities.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How do artificial satellites help in watching live events and talking to people far away?
questions.answer: Artificial satellites receive signals from one place and transmit them to another very quickly. This allows us to watch live telecast of events happening anywhere in the world and talk to people in other countries through mobile phones and TV.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we use telecommunication devices sensibly and not excessively?
questions.answer: We should use telecommunication devices sensibly because excessive use can cause health problems like eye strain, ear disorders, back pain and psychological issues such as isolation. It also leads to neglect of physical activities and affects appetite and weight.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Give two examples of how mass media helps in the implementation of government schemes.
questions.answer: Mass media helps in spreading information about government schemes to people in remote areas. It also raises awareness about the benefits of such schemes, encouraging public participation and successful implementation.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is excessive use of television harmful to physical health?
questions.answer: Excessive use of television leads to long hours of sitting, which reduces physical activity and affects fitness. It also causes eye strain and can lead to poor posture, resulting in back and neck problems. Lack of outdoor play and overeating while watching TV can further lead to weight gain and related health issues.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are artificial satellites important for national communication?
questions.answer: Artificial satellites are important because they allow the President or Prime Minister to address the entire nation at the same time through TV or radio. They enable live telecast of events across the country and help in quick delivery of signals from one place to another. This ensures that information reaches everyone quickly and uniformly.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why does mass media help in improving people's way of life?
questions.answer: Mass media spreads awareness about important matters like food, clothes, shelter, education and health. When people are informed, they make better choices regarding their lifestyle, hygiene and habits. This leads to improved living conditions and overall well-being.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the role of mass media in education and awareness with examples.
questions.answer: Mass media plays a vital role in education by providing informative programmes on channels like Discovery and National Geographic. It helps students learn about science, nature and history in an engaging way. Through news and documentaries, it raises awareness about social issues such as gender equality, cleanliness and environmental protection. Educational programmes like Dnyanadarshana support school learning. Mass media also informs people about government schemes, health campaigns and safety measures during disasters. Thus, it empowers people with knowledge and helps build a well-informed society.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain the advantages and disadvantages of using mobile phones and television.
questions.answer: Mobile phones and television have many advantages. They help us stay connected with family and friends far away. We can watch live events, access educational content and get timely warnings about natural disasters. They also provide entertainment and help in learning. However, excessive use has disadvantages. It can cause eye strain, ear problems and back pain due to poor posture. It may lead to psychological issues like isolation and anxiety. Spending too much time on screens reduces time for outdoor games and physical activity, affecting health and fitness. Therefore, it is important to use these devices wisely and in moderation.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Communication
questions.answer: Communication is the exchange of information, ideas or feelings between people through speaking, writing or using other mediums.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Mass media
questions.answer: Mass media refers to various means of communication that reach a large audience, such as television, radio, newspapers and the internet.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How do artificial satellites help in modern communication?
questions.answer: Artificial satellites are launched into space using rockets and orbit the Earth. They receive signals from one location, such as a TV studio or mobile tower, and transmit them to another location far away. This allows live telecast of events, mobile phone calls and internet data to be sent across cities, countries and continents. Satellites like INSAT in India help in broadcasting TV programmes and enabling communication in remote areas. Without satellites, long-distance communication would be much slower and less reliable.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What are the educational uses of mass media?
questions.answer: Mass media is used for education through informative TV programmes on channels like Discovery, National Geographic and Dnyanadarshana. These programmes teach students about science, nature, history and social issues in an engaging way. Educational videos and documentaries help in understanding complex topics visually. Radio programmes are used for distance learning and adult education. The internet, as part of mass media, provides access to e-books, online classes and educational websites. Thus, mass media supports both formal and informal learning for people of all ages.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how rainwater harvesting helps in meeting water needs during dry periods.
questions.answer: Rainwater harvesting involves collecting and storing rainwater or allowing it to seep into the ground. This increases groundwater levels, which can be used through wells and tanks during dry periods. It ensures water availability even after the rainy season ends.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it dangerous to let untreated waste water into rivers and lakes?
questions.answer: Untreated waste water contains harmful substances, poisonous chemicals, and disease-causing micro-organisms. When let into water bodies, it pollutes the water, making it unsafe for drinking or other uses. It can also harm aquatic life and spread diseases to humans and animals.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Describe the simple filtration method using a plastic bottle, sand, and powdered coal.
questions.answer: In this method, a plastic bottle is cut and layered with powdered coal at the bottom, fine sand in the middle, and coarse sand at the top. Muddy water is poured slowly into the bottle, and as it passes through the layers, impurities are trapped, making the water appear cleaner. However, it may still contain micro-organisms and needs further treatment for safe drinking.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What steps are taken by the government during a famine to help people and animals?
questions.answer: During a famine, the government temporarily moves people and animals from affected areas to safe places where they can get water, foodgrain, and fodder. Fodder camps are set up to care for domestic animals. These steps help reduce suffering and prevent loss of life due to scarcity.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is chlorine added to water during purification?
questions.answer: Chlorine is added to water to kill germs and micro-organisms that can cause diseases. It ensures the water is safe for drinking by destroying harmful biological contaminants. This process is called disinfection and is essential for public health.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why does water look muddy when some substances are mixed in it?
questions.answer: Water looks muddy when insoluble substances like soil or sand are mixed in it because these particles float or remain suspended in the water. They scatter light and make the water appear unclean or turbid. Such impurities can be removed by sedimentation and filtration.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important to read the date of bottling on a water bottle?
questions.answer: It is important to read the date of bottling to know until when the water is safe to use. After that period, the water may get contaminated or lose its quality. Once opened, the water should not be stored for long to avoid bacterial growth.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the process of water purification at water-works in the correct order.
questions.answer: The purification of water at water-works involves several steps in a specific order. First, the water is allowed to stand in large tanks during the settling process, where undissolved impurities like sand and soil settle at the bottom; alum is added to speed up this process. Next, the water passes through filtration layers of coarse sand, fine sand, and powdered coal to remove remaining impurities. Then, chlorine is added in the chlorination step to kill germs and make the water safe from diseases. Finally, oxygenation is done by mixing air with water using pumps to increase the dissolved oxygen, which improves the taste and supports aquatic life. After these steps, the water is clean, transparent, and germ-free, and is then supplied to the public for drinking and other uses.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What is drought? Explain its effects on humans, animals, plants, and agriculture.
questions.answer: Drought is a condition that occurs when there is no rainfall for a very long period, leading to acute water scarcity. As a result, the water level in rivers, wells, lakes, and dams falls, and some may even dry up. The land also dries up due to increased evaporation, making it unsuitable for cultivation. Humans and animals suffer from lack of drinking water, and there is no water available for agriculture, leading to crop failure. Fodder becomes scarce for domestic animals, and grains are in short supply, causing hardship. This condition, when severe, is called a famine, which is a natural disaster affecting all living beings in the region.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define water pollution.
questions.answer: Water pollution is the contamination of water bodies by harmful substances such as chemicals, waste, or micro-organisms, making the water unsafe for living things and unfit for drinking or other uses.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define water management.
questions.answer: Water management refers to the practices of stopping, storing, or allowing rainwater to seep into the ground so that water remains available for use even after the rainy season ends.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how natural processes help in the purification of flowing river water.
questions.answer: Flowing river water gets purified to some extent by natural processes as it moves over stones and gravel, which helps in filtering out larger impurities. The movement of water increases aeration, allowing more oxygen from the air to dissolve, which supports the breakdown of organic matter by beneficial microorganisms. Sedimentation occurs naturally when the water flows slowly, letting heavier particles settle. Exposure to sunlight also helps in killing some germs. However, these natural processes are slow and cannot cope with large amounts of pollution from human activities.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain why it is necessary to stop rainwater from flowing away and instead let it seep into the ground.
questions.answer: Stopping rainwater from flowing away helps increase groundwater levels, which ensures water availability in wells and tanks during dry periods. When rainwater seeps into the soil, it recharges underground water reserves that can be used later for drinking, agriculture, and daily needs. This prevents water scarcity and reduces dependence on erratic rainfall. It also helps in growing trees and cultivating land, as plants get a steady supply of moisture. Such practices are part of water management and are essential to face droughts and ensure long-term water security.

questions.text: Explain how the clothing of early humans changed over time.
questions.answer: In prehistoric times, man did not wear clothes. Later, he used bark and leaves of trees. After that, he began to use animal skins from hunted animals. Finally, after learning to make yarn from cotton wool, he started using cotton cloth in various ways.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we see a variety of clothes in different regions of India?
questions.answer: The variety of clothes in different regions of India is due to diverse climatic conditions. For example, woolen clothes are used in cold regions like Jammu and Kashmir, while cotton clothes are preferred in hot regions like Rajasthan. Traditional practices and local availability of raw materials also influence clothing choices.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What are the specialities of Solapur and Ichalkaranji in the textile industry?

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How can wanting too many clothes lead to a problem?
questions.answer: Wanting too many clothes when we do not need them turns into greed. This can lead to wastage of resources and unnecessary spending. It is important to distinguish between need and desire and use clothes only as per requirement.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we give priority to our needs and not desires when it comes to clothes?
questions.answer: We should give priority to our needs because nature can fulfill everyone’s basic needs, but it cannot satisfy endless desires. If we focus only on desires, it leads to greed and overuse of resources. By focusing on needs, we ensure that nature can take care of us all and maintain balance.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why did textile mills flourish in Mumbai?
questions.answer: Textile mills flourished in Mumbai because the humid weather there helped in the manufacture of long thread, which is essential for making cloth. This favourable climate attracted workers from all over the country, leading to the growth of the textile industry in the city.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important to visit elderly people to learn about old clothes?
questions.answer: It is important to visit elderly people because they can share knowledge about clothes used in the past, which are no longer in common use. This helps us understand how clothing has changed over time due to technology, tradition, and availability of materials. Their experiences help preserve cultural heritage related to clothing.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the evolution of clothing from prehistoric times to modern days, mentioning the materials used at each stage.
questions.answer: In prehistoric times, man did not wear clothes and relied on body hair for protection. As body hair reduced, he began to use bark and leaves of trees. Later, after hunting animals, he used their skins for clothing. With the invention of spinning, he learned to make yarn from cotton wool and began to use cotton cloth in various ways. Over time, different fabrics like silk and wool were developed. Today, we have a wide variety of clothes made from natural and synthetic fibres, influenced by climate, culture, and fashion. This evolution shows how human needs and intelligence have shaped clothing over thousands of years.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain the importance of textiles in our lives and how they reflect the diversity of our country.
questions.answer: Textiles are essential for protection, comfort, and cultural expression. They protect us from weather, help in hygiene, and are used in traditions and festivals. The diversity of textiles in India reflects the variety of climates, traditions, and local resources. For example, Paithani sarees from Maharashtra, Kashmiri wool from the north, and cotton clothes from Gujarat show regional specialities. With better transport, these fabrics are now available across the country. This variety in clothing is a part of India’s rich cultural diversity and highlights how geography and lifestyle influence what we wear.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define 'necessity' in the context of clothes.
questions.answer: Necessity refers to clothes that are essential for protection from weather, heat, cold, or rain, and for maintaining hygiene and dignity.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define 'greed' as mentioned in the chapter.
questions.answer: Greed is the excessive desire to have more clothes than needed, driven by attraction to advertisements or fashion, rather than actual requirement.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how advertisements influence our desire for clothes and why this can be harmful.
questions.answer: Advertisements show attractive clothes on TV, hoardings, and social media, which create a wish to own them even if we do not need them. This attraction can turn into desire and then greed, making us want more clothes than necessary. As a result, we may spend money unnecessarily and neglect our real needs. The chapter explains that wanting things we do not need is not necessity but desire. It emphasizes that we must use things only as we need them, not as per greed, so that nature can fulfill everyone’s needs.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the role of climate in determining the type of clothes people wear in different regions of India.
questions.answer: Climate plays a major role in deciding the type of clothes people wear. In hot regions like Rajasthan, light and loose cotton clothes are preferred to stay cool. In cold regions like Jammu and Kashmir, woolen clothes are worn to retain body heat. In areas with heavy rainfall, such as Kerala, clothes that dry quickly are useful. The local climate affects the choice of fabric, colour, and style of clothing. Thus, the diversity in clothing across India is largely due to the diverse climatic conditions found in different parts of the country.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how deforestation affects the water cycle and leads to droughts.
questions.answer: Deforestation reduces the number of trees that absorb water from the soil and release it into the air through transpiration. This decreases atmospheric moisture, leading to less rainfall. As a result, water sources dry up and droughts occur.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important to protect biodiversity parks and sanctuaries?
questions.answer: Biodiversity parks and sanctuaries protect and conserve various species of plants and animals. They help maintain ecological balance and prevent extinction. They also provide opportunities for study and recreation.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How does pollution of water sources affect aquatic life?
questions.answer: Polluted water reduces the oxygen available for aquatic plants and animals. Toxic substances in the water can poison them. This leads to a decrease in their numbers and can cause extinction.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What steps can individuals take to prevent environmental degradation?
questions.answer: Individuals can use resources frugally, recycle used articles, avoid littering, and spread awareness. They can also participate in tree plantation and support conservation efforts.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why does the proportion of carbon dioxide in the air rise due to deforestation?
questions.answer: Trees absorb carbon dioxide during photosynthesis. When forests are cut down, fewer trees are available to absorb carbon dioxide. At the same time, burning of fuels releases more carbon dioxide. As a result, the proportion of carbon dioxide in the air increases.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do flamingos migrate to Mayani lake?
questions.answer: Flamingos migrate to Mayani lake because it provides a suitable habitat with water and food. They build nests and lay eggs there. The lake’s environment supports their breeding cycle.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it necessary to conserve plants in the environment?
questions.answer: Plants produce oxygen and absorb carbon dioxide, maintaining air quality. They provide food and shelter to animals. They also prevent soil erosion and support the water cycle. Conserving plants ensures the survival of many living things.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Describe the impact of large-scale deforestation on the environment and suggest measures to prevent it.
questions.answer: Large-scale deforestation leads to loss of biodiversity as animals lose their habitats. It disrupts the water cycle, causing reduced rainfall and droughts. Increased carbon dioxide levels contribute to global warming. Soil erosion increases due to lack of tree roots. To prevent this, we must stop unnecessary cutting of trees, promote tree plantation, use paper and wood wisely, and support conservation efforts like biodiversity parks and sanctuaries. Awareness and strict enforcement of environmental laws are also essential.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how human activities like industrialization and agriculture affect the environment and what steps can be taken to maintain ecological balance.
questions.answer: Industrialization leads to air and water pollution through smoke and waste discharge. Agriculture using chemical fertilizers and pesticides pollutes soil and water. Clearing forests for farms and industries destroys habitats. To maintain balance, we should treat waste before discharge, use eco-friendly fuels, practice organic farming, and protect forests. Recycling, using renewable energy, and creating awareness are vital. Everyone must act responsibly to protect nature for future generations.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Biodiversity
questions.answer: Biodiversity refers to the variety of living things found in a particular area, including different species of plants, animals, and microorganisms.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Deforestation
questions.answer: Deforestation is the large-scale cutting down of forests for purposes like agriculture, housing, industry, or building roads and railways.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How does pollution of air and water affect living things?
questions.answer: Air pollution causes respiratory problems in animals and humans and damages plants. It also increases global warming due to excess carbon dioxide. Water pollution makes water unfit for drinking and harms aquatic life by reducing oxygen and introducing toxins. Polluted water seeps into the soil, making it infertile and affecting plant growth. Over time, pollution leads to a decline in the number of living things and can cause extinction.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are Devrais considered important for environmental conservation?
questions.answer: Devrais are sacred groves where no tree or plant is ever cut, as they are believed to be reserved for god. This belief has protected them from destruction for many years. They provide shelter to various plants and animals, preserving biodiversity. Devrais act as natural sanctuaries and help maintain ecological balance. They are examples of traditional conservation practices that are still effective today.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the importance of a balanced diet with examples.
questions.answer: A balanced diet includes carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals in the right amounts. It gives us energy to work and play, helps in growth and repair of body parts, protects us from diseases, and keeps us healthy. For example, eating roti (carbohydrates), dal (protein), ghee (fat), and vegetables (vitamins and minerals) together makes a balanced diet. Without balance, we may feel weak, fall sick often, or not grow properly.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What is malnutrition? Explain its causes and effects.
questions.answer: Malnutrition is a condition caused by lack of proper food constituents in the diet over a long period. It can happen due to deficiency of proteins, vitamins, or minerals. Effects include stunted growth, weakness, tiredness, poor resistance to diseases, and disorders like anaemia or night-blindness. Eating a variety of fresh foods prevents malnutrition.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Carbohydrates

questions.text: Roughage
questions.answer: Roughage is another name for fibre, which helps in digestion and formation of stool.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How do fats help in protecting our body?
questions.answer: Fats help protect our body by forming a layer under the skin that shields internal organs from injury. They also help in keeping the body warm by preventing heat loss. Fats are stored and used as energy when food is scarce. Additionally, they help in the absorption of certain vitamins. Thus, fats serve multiple protective and functional roles in the body.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are vitamins and minerals called protective nutrients?
questions.answer: Vitamins and minerals are called protective nutrients because they help the body resist diseases and maintain normal functioning. Though needed in small quantities, they are essential for processes like immunity, blood clotting, bone strength, and vision. A deficiency in any of them can lead to specific health disorders. For example, vitamin C prevents scurvy, and calcium strengthens bones. Hence, they play a vital role in protecting our health.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What is meant by 'coping with emotions'?
questions.answer: Coping with emotions means being aware of our feelings, controlling them when necessary, and expressing them in a reasonable and healthy way. It involves not letting emotions like anger or sadness overpower our thoughts and actions. This helps us maintain balance in our behaviour and relationships.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What are the harmful effects of anger on our body and mind?
questions.answer: Harmful effects of anger include headaches, loss of sleep, dullness, and increased stress on the mind. It can also make us short-tempered and stubborn, leading to hurtful behaviour toward others. Over time, uncontrolled anger can damage our health and relationships.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why must we know our flaws as well as our talents?
questions.answer: We must know our flaws so that we can try to improve upon them and grow as better individuals. Knowing our talents helps us to build confidence and use our strengths effectively. Together, this self-awareness leads to personal development and a balanced personality.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How can we change aspects of our nature that bother us or others?
questions.answer: We can change such aspects by becoming aware of them, making a conscious effort to improve, and practicing better behaviour over time. For example, if we talk too much, we can consciously listen more and speak less. With consistent effort and support from friends or teachers, these aspects can be transformed into strengths.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we not lose our temper when we get angry?
questions.answer: We should not lose our temper because it can lead to saying or doing things we later regret. Losing our temper harms our relationships and can cause mental stress and physical discomfort like headaches. Controlling anger helps us think clearly and act in a fair and kind manner.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why does Neha’s behaviour change when she realises her friends avoid her?
questions.answer: Neha changes her behaviour because she realises that talking too much prevents others from speaking, which makes them feel ignored. Her friends’ avoidance makes her aware of her flaw, motivating her to correct it. She then tries to listen more and speak less to improve her relationships.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important to express emotions in a reasonable manner?
questions.answer: Expressing emotions in a reasonable manner helps us communicate our feelings without hurting others or causing conflict. It allows us to be honest while maintaining respect and understanding in relationships. This emotional balance supports mental well-being and healthy social interactions.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Answer in 6-10 lines. Describe how you would react in the following situation.
questions.text: Your friend got a big prize in a school competition, but you did not win anything. How will you react?
questions.answer: I will feel happy for my friend and congratulate them sincerely, even if I feel a little disappointed inside. I will not show jealousy or sadness openly, as that might hurt my friend’s feelings. Instead, I will appreciate their effort and talent, and think about how I can improve for next time. I may talk to my teacher or parents to understand where I can work harder. This way, I turn my emotion into motivation rather than letting it turn into resentment. By reacting positively, I strengthen my friendship and grow emotionally.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Answer in 6-10 lines. Explain the importance of emotional balance in daily life.
questions.text: Emotional balance is important because it helps us think clearly and make good decisions, even when we feel strong emotions like anger or joy. When our emotions are balanced, we can cooperate with others, understand their feelings, and maintain good relationships. For example, if we are angry but control it, we can talk calmly instead of fighting. Emotional balance also protects our health by reducing stress, headaches, and sleeplessness. It allows us to enjoy happiness without becoming overly excited or careless. Similarly, we can feel sadness without becoming hopeless. Students with emotional balance focus better in studies and participate well in group activities. They are ready to help others and accept feedback positively. Thus, emotional balance makes us responsible, kind, and successful individuals in school and life.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define 'emotions'.
questions.answer: Emotions are strong feelings such as anger, joy, sorrow, fear, or jealousy that arise in response to what happens around us or within us.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define 'coping with emotions'.
questions.answer: Coping with emotions means being aware of our feelings, controlling them when needed, and expressing them in a healthy and reasonable way.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how knowing our flaws and talents helps us in life.
questions.answer: Knowing our flaws helps us understand where we need to improve and avoid repeating mistakes. It encourages humility and a willingness to learn from others. Recognising our talents builds confidence and motivates us to use our strengths in studies, sports, or arts. When we accept both, we develop a realistic and positive self-image. This self-awareness leads to better decisions, stronger relationships, and personal growth over time.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain why we must maintain a balance between thoughts and emotions.
questions.answer: A balance between thoughts and emotions ensures that we do not act only on impulse or only on logic, but with wisdom. If we follow only emotions, we may act angrily or selfishly without thinking. If we rely only on thoughts, we may become insensitive to others’ feelings. When thoughts and emotions work together, we can make kind, fair, and sensible decisions. This balance helps us stay calm during conflicts and joyful without being careless. It leads to a peaceful mind and healthy relationships with family, friends, and teachers.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Busy at Work – our Internal Organs
questions.text: Describe the process of digestion in the stomach.
questions.answer: In the stomach, food is churned and mixed with digestive juices. These juices break down proteins and kill harmful germs. The food turns into a thin slurry before moving to the small intestine.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Busy at Work – our Internal Organs
questions.text: How does the diaphragm help in breathing?
questions.answer: When the diaphragm moves down, the chest cavity expands and air rushes into the lungs. When it moves up, the cavity shrinks and air is pushed out. This movement causes inhalation and exhalation.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Busy at Work – our Internal Organs
questions.text: Why is drinking water important during digestion?
questions.answer: Water helps dissolve nutrients so they can be absorbed into the blood. It also keeps food moving smoothly through the alimentary canal and prevents constipation.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Busy at Work – our Internal Organs
questions.text: What are the main parts of the respiratory system?
questions.answer: The main parts of the respiratory system are the nose, trachea, lungs, and diaphragm. Air enters through the nose, passes through the trachea to the lungs, and the diaphragm helps in breathing.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Busy at Work – our Internal Organs
questions.text: Why should we not eat in a hurry?
questions.answer: We should not eat in a hurry because food may enter the windpipe instead of the food pipe, causing choking. The windpipe remains closed during swallowing only if we eat slowly and carefully.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Busy at Work – our Internal Organs
questions.text: Why is the nervous system important for the body?
questions.answer: The nervous system is important because it coordinates all body functions. It ensures that organs work together at the right time and in the right way, like walking, thinking, and digesting.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Busy at Work – our Internal Organs
questions.text: Why do we feel hungry?
questions.answer: We feel hungry when the body needs energy and nutrients. The brain receives signals from the stomach and blood sugar levels, indicating it's time to eat.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Busy at Work – our Internal Organs
questions.text: Explain how the respiratory and circulatory systems work together to provide energy to the body.
questions.answer: The respiratory system brings oxygen into the body through breathing. Oxygen enters the blood in the alveoli of the lungs. The circulatory system, led by the heart, pumps this oxygen-rich blood to all body cells. In the cells, oxygen helps break down digested food to release energy. This energy is used for all body activities like movement, growth, and repair. Thus, both systems work together to supply energy.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Busy at Work – our Internal Organs
questions.text: Describe the journey of food from the mouth to the anus.
questions.answer: Food enters the mouth where it is chewed and mixed with saliva to form a bolus. The bolus passes through the oesophagus into the stomach. In the stomach, it is churned and mixed with digestive juices. It then moves to the small intestine where nutrients are absorbed into the blood. The remaining waste goes to the large intestine where water is absorbed. The waste is stored in the rectum and finally expelled through the anus.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Busy at Work – our Internal Organs
questions.text: What is a system?
questions.answer: A system is a group of organs that work together to perform a specific function in the body.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Busy at Work – our Internal Organs
questions.text: What is alveoli?
questions.answer: Alveoli are tiny air sacs in the lungs where the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide takes place.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Busy at Work – our Internal Organs
questions.text: Explain how smoking affects the respiratory system.
questions.answer: Smoking introduces toxic substances into the respiratory tract. These substances damage the alveoli and reduce their surface area for gas exchange. A sticky layer of tar forms inside the lungs, making breathing difficult. Over time, this leads to reduced lung efficiency and increases the risk of diseases like bronchitis and lung cancer. Smoking also harms people nearby through passive smoking.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Busy at Work – our Internal Organs
questions.text: Explain the process of blood circulation in the body.
questions.answer: The heart pumps oxygen-rich blood to all parts of the body through arteries. As blood travels, it delivers oxygen and nutrients to cells and picks up carbon dioxide and waste. The deoxygenated blood returns to the heart through veins. The heart then pumps it to the lungs to release carbon dioxide and pick up fresh oxygen. This cycle continues non-stop to keep the body alive and functioning.

questions.text: Explain how practice helps in improving a skill. Give one example from daily life.
questions.answer: When we repeat a task many times, our body and mind get used to it, making it easier and more accurate. For example, the more we practice writing, the neater and faster our writing becomes.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it said that human beings learn more skills than animals?
questions.answer: Animals learn only a limited number of skills needed for survival, such as finding food and protecting themselves. Human beings, however, continue to learn many skills throughout life, like reading, writing, and using computers, which help in personal and social development.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What are two factors that support healthy growth and development in children?
questions.answer: Adequate nutritious food and regular physical exercise are two essential factors that support healthy growth and development. Without proper food, a child may suffer from malnutrition, and without exercise, physical strength and fitness may not develop well.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How does doing personal tasks ourselves help in our development?
questions.answer: Doing personal tasks like dressing, washing, or eating independently builds confidence and self-reliance. It also improves coordination and responsibility, which are important parts of personality development.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do we say that the first 18 years are the growing years for all boys and girls?
questions.answer: The first 18 years are called the growing years because during this period, children experience significant increases in height and weight. After this age, most people reach their adult height and physical growth slows down or stops.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it important to put good thoughts into practice for personality development?
questions.answer: Personality is not just about knowing what is good, but about behaving in a good way. When we put good thoughts into action—like helping others or being honest—our character becomes strong and our personality develops positively.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do children in Std V show more skills than children in pre-primary classes?
questions.answer: Children in Std V are older and have had more time to learn and practice skills. They have been taught by parents and teachers and have gained experience through daily activities, which helps them perform more complex tasks independently.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Answer in 6-10 lines. Include key points.
questions.text: Describe how a child develops from infancy to adulthood in terms of physical growth, skill learning, and personality development.
questions.answer: From infancy, a child grows rapidly in height and weight, especially during the first 18 years. Initially, babies depend entirely on caregivers and can only cry or move limbs randomly. Over time, they gain control over movements, learning to hold objects, sit, crawl, and walk. As they grow, they learn skills like speaking, eating independently, dressing, and later, reading, writing, and playing games. These skills are learned through practice and guidance from parents and teachers. Alongside physical and skill development, personality grows as children learn to distinguish right from wrong, form interests, and express emotions. Good habits, values, and efforts shape a unique personality. Heredity influences physical traits, but environment and personal effort determine how skills and character develop. Thus, development is a lifelong process of growing in body, mind, and character.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: Answer in 6-10 lines. Include key points.
questions.text: Explain the concept of development with reference to the story of the industrialist and his three assistants. What does it teach us about true progress?
questions.answer: The story shows that true development is not just about saving or increasing money, but about using resources to improve the well-being of others. The first assistant kept the money safe but did nothing productive. The second doubled workers’ bonus and gave a feast, bringing short-term happiness. The third invested in machines, built a canteen, and created a welfare fund, leading to increased production, better quality, worker satisfaction, and long-term profit. This reflects real development: using resources wisely to create lasting benefits for individuals and society. Just as the industrialist chose the third assistant, we learn that progress comes from investing in health, education, and welfare—helping people grow skills and live better lives. Thus, development means holistic improvement in life, not just material gain.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Heredity
questions.answer: Heredity is the passing of physical and mental traits from parents to their children through genes.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Skill
questions.answer: A skill is the ability to do something well, learned through practice and experience.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How does learning new skills reduce our dependence on others?
questions.answer: As we learn new skills, we become capable of doing more tasks by ourselves, such as dressing, eating, or studying without help. This increases our independence and confidence. For example, once a child learns to tie shoelaces, they no longer need an adult to do it for them. Each skill mastered reduces the need to rely on others for that task. Over time, learning many skills helps us manage our daily life and responsibilities independently. Thus, skill learning is a key step toward becoming self-reliant and responsible.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is it said that human beings go on learning many more skills throughout life compared to animals?
questions.answer: Animals learn only a limited set of skills essential for survival, such as hunting, avoiding danger, and caring for young, which they mostly learn in early life. Human beings, however, are not limited to survival skills; we learn for personal growth, social interaction, and cultural development. We continue to learn new skills like languages, arts, technology, and professions at any age. Our brains remain capable of learning and adapting throughout life. This lifelong learning ability allows us to innovate, improve society, and lead rich, varied lives. Hence, human development is marked by continuous and diverse skill acquisition.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Infectious Diseases and how to Prevent them
questions.text: List the four mediums through which infectious diseases spread.
questions.answer: Infectious diseases spread through air, water, food, and insect bites. These are the main carriers of germs from an infected person to a healthy one. Preventing contact with these mediums helps stop the spread.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Infectious Diseases and how to Prevent them
questions.text: What steps should be taken to prevent the spread of cholera?
questions.answer: To prevent cholera, drink only boiled or purified water, avoid eating uncovered food, and maintain proper sanitation. Wash hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet. Avoid defecating near water sources.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Infectious Diseases and how to Prevent them
questions.text: Why is it important to wash hands before eating?
questions.answer: Washing hands before eating removes germs that may have stuck to them from touching dirty surfaces or objects. These germs can enter the body through food and cause diseases like diarrhoea or typhoid. Clean hands help prevent food-borne illnesses.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Infectious Diseases and how to Prevent them
questions.text: What is an epidemic? Give one example.
questions.answer: An epidemic occurs when many people in a particular area get the same infectious disease at the same time. For example, during a cholera outbreak, many people may fall ill due to contaminated water supply.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Infectious Diseases and how to Prevent them
questions.text: Why should we not spit in the open?
questions.answer: We should not spit in the open because spit may contain germs of diseases like tuberculosis. When others breathe in the air near the spit, they may inhale these germs and get infected. Spitting in public spreads diseases through the air.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Infectious Diseases and how to Prevent them
questions.text: Why are patients with tuberculosis kept in separate wards in hospitals?
questions.answer: Patients with tuberculosis are kept in separate wards to prevent the spread of germs through coughing or sneezing. This isolation protects other patients, visitors, and hospital staff from inhaling the infected droplets. It is a key measure to control epidemics.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Infectious Diseases and how to Prevent them
questions.text: Why should food be kept covered?
questions.answer: Food should be kept covered to prevent flies, dust, and dirt from settling on it. Flies can carry germs from garbage or faeces and transfer them to food. Eating contaminated food can lead to food poisoning or diarrhoea.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Infectious Diseases and how to Prevent them
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain how infectious diseases spread and what we can do to prevent them.
questions.answer: Infectious diseases spread through air (coughing, sneezing), water (contaminated drinking water), food (uncovered or handled with dirty hands), and insect bites (mosquitoes, flies). To prevent spread, we should cover our mouth when coughing, drink boiled water, keep food covered, wash hands regularly, avoid stagnant water to stop mosquito breeding, and get vaccinated. Cleanliness and awareness are key to staying healthy.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Infectious Diseases and how to Prevent them
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the vaccination schedule for a newborn baby as mentioned in the lesson.
questions.answer: Soon after birth, a baby is given the tuberculosis vaccine. At one and a half months, the first dose of the triple vaccine (for diphtheria, whooping cough, and tetanus) and polio vaccine is given. Two more doses of these vaccines are given at one-month intervals. The polio vaccine is given orally, while others are injections. This schedule helps build immunity early in life.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Infectious Diseases and how to Prevent them
questions.text: Define infectious disease.
questions.answer: An infectious disease is a disease caused by micro-organisms (germs) that can spread from an infected person to a healthy person through air, water, food, or insect bites.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Infectious Diseases and how to Prevent them
questions.text: Define vaccination.
questions.answer: Vaccination is the process of administering a vaccine to help the body develop resistance to a specific disease without causing the disease itself.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Infectious Diseases and how to Prevent them
questions.text: Explain how malaria spreads from one person to another.
questions.answer: Malaria spreads when a mosquito bites a person who has malaria, sucking blood that contains the malaria germs. These germs grow inside the mosquito. When the same mosquito bites another person, the germs enter that person’s blood through the mosquito’s saliva. The person then develops malaria. Thus, the mosquito acts as a carrier of the disease.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.chapter: Infectious Diseases and how to Prevent them
questions.text: Explain why boiling water prevents water-borne diseases.
questions.answer: Boiling water kills harmful micro-organisms like those causing cholera, typhoid, and diarrhoea. These germs cannot survive high temperatures. When water is boiled for at least 10 minutes, it becomes safe to drink. This prevents the germs from entering the body through drinking water. Boiling is a simple and effective method, especially during epidemics.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Describe the three states of water and how the arrangement of particles differs in each.
questions.answer: Water is found as solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (steam) in nature. In solid, particles are tightly packed; in liquid, they are loose and can flow; in gas, they are far apart and move freely. The particles themselves remain the same, only their arrangement changes.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How do we obtain energy from substances like petrol and diesel?
questions.answer: When petrol or diesel burns in a vehicle, the stored energy is released as heat. This heat energy is then converted into motion (kinetic energy) that moves the vehicle. When the fuel finishes, the vehicle stops.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we use minimum electricity according to the chapter?
questions.answer: We should use minimum electricity because producing it uses natural resources like coal and water, which are limited. Also, some methods of electricity generation can harm the environment. Saving electricity helps conserve resources and reduce pollution.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do naphthalene balls become smaller after a few days?
questions.answer: Naphthalene balls become smaller because they continuously change into tiny gaseous particles. These particles escape into the air and settle on clothes or other surfaces. As the particles leave the ball, its size reduces and it slowly disappears.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why do moving things have kinetic energy?
questions.answer: Moving things have kinetic energy because energy in the form of motion is called kinetic energy. Any object that is moving possesses this energy due to its motion. For example, blowing wind has kinetic energy that can turn windmills.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are substances like coal and petrol called fuels?
questions.answer: Substances like coal and petrol are called fuels because they release energy when burned. This energy is obtained in the form of heat, which can be used to run machines or produce electricity. They store energy that is released during combustion.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the particle theory of matter as given in the chapter. Include how it explains the states of substances and gives examples from daily life.
questions.answer: The particle theory states that all substances are made up of very tiny particles that cannot be seen with the naked eye. These particles behave differently in solid, liquid, and gas states. In solids, particles are tightly packed and vibrate in place; in liquids, they are loose and slide past each other; in gases, they are far apart and move freely. The theory explains everyday observations: when we write with chalk, its particles stick to the board; when we pound sugar, it becomes powder as particles separate; naphthalene balls shrink as particles escape into air; and we feel wet under a roof due to bouncing raindrops breaking into tiny droplets. This theory was first proposed by Kanaad Maharshi, who named the tiny particle 'peelav'.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Describe how we get energy from various sources and mention the importance of using non-exhaustible sources.
questions.answer: We obtain energy from substances like coal, diesel, petrol, and LPG when they burn, releasing heat energy. This heat can run vehicles or generate electricity. Electricity itself is a form of energy used to run fans, TVs, and machines. The chapter highlights that sunlight, wind, and flowing water are non-exhaustible sources of energy because they are naturally replenished and do not get depleted. Unlike coal and mineral oil, which are limited and cause pollution, solar and wind energy are clean and sustainable. Therefore, we should use sunlight, wind, and water to the maximum extent as alternative sources to conserve resources and protect the environment.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Substance
questions.answer: A substance is a form of matter made up of tiny particles and has a definite composition. Examples include chalk, sugar, iron, and water.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Object
questions.answer: An object is a thing made from one or more substances and has a definite shape. Examples include a chair made of wood or a pot made of clay.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How does the chapter explain that liquids are made of small particles?
questions.answer: The chapter explains that liquids are made of small particles by observing rain. When raindrops fall on the road, they bounce and break into tiny droplets. These droplets, though small, are still made of even tinier water particles that cannot be seen. These particles make us wet when they reach us. This shows that liquids, like water, are composed of minute particles. Even though we cannot see them, their effect (like making us wet) proves their presence.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What is kinetic energy and give two examples from daily life where it is used?
questions.answer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion. It is the energy of motion. For example, when wind blows, it has kinetic energy that turns the blades of a windmill. Similarly, a moving car has kinetic energy that allows it to travel from one place to another. Even flowing water in a river has kinetic energy that can be used to rotate turbines in a dam to produce electricity. Thus, any moving object possesses kinetic energy.

questions.text: What are the threats to community health mentioned in the chapter?
questions.answer: The threats to community health include pollution, squalor, epidemics, infectious diseases, addiction, insect-borne diseases, and carelessness regarding hygiene.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: How can good community health be achieved?
questions.answer: Good community health can be achieved through habits of cleanliness and good health on the part of all individuals in a community, including nutritious food, personal hygiene, exercise and pursuit of hobbies.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What are the ill effects of alcoholism on the body?
questions.answer: Alcoholism causes diseases of the liver, intestines and urinary bladder, leads to drowsiness and confusion, and makes a person lose control over their actions.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should one avoid tobacco and alcohol addiction?
questions.answer: One should avoid tobacco and alcohol addiction because they harm health, lead to serious diseases like cancer and liver damage, waste money and time, and destroy family happiness and peace.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why is there a ban on spitting in public places?
questions.answer: There is a ban on spitting in public places to prevent the spread of diseases through germs present in spit.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why should we be alert about health and hygiene?
questions.answer: We should be alert about health and hygiene to protect ourselves and others from diseases and to maintain a happy and healthy life.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Why are mass media used in community welfare programmes?
questions.answer: Mass media are used to educate people about issues such as taking care of drinking water and food to promote community health.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Describe the ill effects of tobacco addiction and suggest ways to avoid it.
questions.answer: Tobacco addiction causes ulcers in the mouth, which can develop into tumours and eventually cancer. It leads to restlessness, inability to focus, and spending excessive time and money on tobacco. Addicts often spit in public, making surroundings dirty. To avoid it, one must stay firm, say 'No!' to peer pressure, seek help from counsellors if needed, and engage in healthy hobbies and sports.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how wholesome living leads to good personal and social health.
questions.answer: Wholesome living, which includes nutritious food, personal hygiene, exercise, and pursuing hobbies, keeps the body and mind healthy. It reduces stress, increases happiness, and builds strength. When people live healthily, social tensions decrease and feelings of friendship grow. A healthy community progresses better as people are energetic and productive. Thus, wholesome living improves both personal well-being and social harmony.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Define community health.
questions.answer: Community health refers to the health and well-being of all individuals in a community, achieved through cleanliness, good habits, and collective efforts to prevent disease.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: What is wholesome living?
questions.answer: Wholesome living means leading a healthy and balanced life by taking care of physical health through proper food, exercise, hygiene, and maintaining a peaceful mind by avoiding hatred and envy.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain how addiction to tobacco or alcohol affects the family.
questions.answer: Addiction to tobacco or alcohol not only harms the individual but also deeply affects the family. The addict becomes neglectful and may spend all money on the habit, leaving the family in financial trouble. The family suffers emotional stress and shame, and often has to care for the sick addict. Over time, the home loses peace and happiness, and the family’s health and well-being are ruined.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: Explain the importance of safe drinking water and clean food for community health.
questions.answer: Safe drinking water and clean food are essential to prevent diseases like cholera and food poisoning. Contaminated water or food can quickly spread illness among many people, especially in crowded areas. Ensuring safety means treating water properly, storing food hygienically, and washing hands before eating. When the community has access to safe water and food, overall health improves and epidemics can be avoided. Thus, these are basic needs for a healthy community.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्यमालेत ग्रह व तारांची फरक सांगा.
questions.answer: ग्रह स्वतःप्रकाशित नाहीत, तारं स्वतःप्रकाशित आहेत. ग्रह सूर्याभोवती फिरतात, तारे स्थिर दिसतात. ग्रहांचा आकार मोठा व गोल असतो, तारे दिसण्याने लहान व चमकदार वाटतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्यमालेत उपग्रहांचा महत्त्व सांगा.
questions.answer: उपग्रह ग्रहाभोवती परिभ्रमण करतात. ते पृथ्वीवरील हवामान, पाणी, खनिज संपत्तीचा शोध घेतात. ते संदेशवहन व नकाशे तयार करण्यात मदत करतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्यमालेत लघुग्रह काय आहे व ते किधर असते?
questions.answer: लघुग्रह सूर्याभोवती फिरणारे लहान खगोलीय वस्तूंचा पट्टा आहे. ते मंगळ व गुरू ग्रहांच्या दरम्यान असते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्यमालेची आकृतीत दाखवलेली वस्तू काय आहेत?
questions.answer: सूर्यमालेची आकृतीत सूर्य, त्याभोवती परिभ्रमण करणारे ग्रह (पृथ्वी व इतर), आणि पृथ्वीचा उपग्रह चंद्र दाखवले आहेत.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्य दिवसात मोठा व चमकदार दिसतो का?
questions.answer: सूर्य पृथ्वीपासून जवळ असल्याने मोठा व चमकदार दिसतो. इतर तारे खूप दूर असल्याने लहान व मंद दिसतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: चंद्र रात्रीत पृथ्वीपासून जवळ दिसतो का?
questions.answer: चंद्र पृथ्वीपासून जवळ असल्याने रात्रीत मोठा व चमकदार दिसतो. दिवसात सूर्याच्या प्रखर प्रकाशामुळे चंद्राची ओझा हो जाते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्यमालेत ग्रह लुकलुकत नाहीत का?
questions.answer: ग्रह स्वतःप्रकाशित नाहीत. त्यांना सूर्याकडून प्रकाश मिळतो, त्यामुळे त्यांचा प्रकाश स्थिर राहतो, लुकलुकत नाही.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्यमाला काय आहे? त्यात कोणती खगोलीय वस्तू समावेश आहेत?
questions.answer: सूर्यमाला सूर्य आणि त्याभोवती परिभ्रमण करण्या खगोलीय वस्तूंचा समूह आहे. त्यात सूर्य (एक तारा), आठ ग्रह (बुध, शुक्र, पृथ्वी, मंगळ, गुरू, शनि, युरेनस, नेपच्यून), ग्रहांचे उपग्रह (जसे की चंद्र), लघुग्रह (मंगळ व गुरू दरम्यानचा पट्टा), आणि बट॒ग्रह (सूर्याभोवती फिरणारे लहान खगोलीय वस्तू) समावेश आहेत. सर्व वस्तू सूर्याभोवती फिरतात, त्यांची पातळी कक्षा म्हणतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्यमालेची आकृती चित्रावर दाखवली जाते. त्यात कोणती माहिती दाखवली जाते?
questions.answer: सूर्यमालेची आकृती चित्रात मध्यभागी सूर्य दाखवला जातो. त्याभोवती परिभ्रमण करणारे ग्रह (पृथ्वी व इतर) त्यांच्या कक्षेत दाखवले जातात. पृथ्वीचा उपग्रह चंद्र पृथ्वीभोवती फिरतो. ग्रह, उपग्रह, लघुग्रह, बट॒ग्रह यांचा समावेश होतो. चित्रात प्रत्येक वस्तूचे नाव व त्यांचे स्थान दर्शवले जाते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: ग्रह परिभाषा लिहा.
questions.answer: ग्रह हे स्वतःप्रकाशित नाहोणारी खगोलीय वस्तू आहे जी सूर्याभोवती फिरते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: उपग्रह परिभाषा लिहा.
questions.answer: उपग्रह हे खगोलीय वस्तू आहे जी ग्रहाभोवती परिभ्रमण करतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्यमालेत तारे लुकलुकतात, पण ग्रह लुकलुकत नाहीत. स्पष्टीकरण द्या.
questions.answer: तारे स्वतःप्रकाशित असतात, त्यांचे प्रकाश कमी-जास्त होतामुळे लुकलुकत दिसतात. ग्रह स्वतःप्रकाशित नाहीत, त्यांना सूर्याकडून स्थिर प्रकाश मिळतो, त्यामुळे त्यांचा प्रकाश लुकलुकत नाही.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्यमालेची आकृतीत फक्त पृथ्वीचा उपग्रह दाखवला आहे का?
questions.answer: सूर्यमालेची आकृतीत फक्त पृथ्वीचा उपग्रह (चंद्र) दाखवला आहे कारण हे अध्यायमध्ये पृथ्वी व त्याच्या उपग्रहाचा विस्तृत अभ्यास केला आहे. इतर ग्रहांचे उपग्रह हे शैक्षणिक स्तरावरून ओळखले जातात, पण चित्रात स्पष्टता साठी फक्त चंद्र दाखवला जातो.
