questions.text: संपर्कामुळे फैलणाऱ्या रोग टाळण्यासाठी काय उपाय घ्यावे?
questions.answer: संपर्कामुळे फैलणाऱ्या रोग टाळण्यासाठी हात स्वच्छ धुणे, इतरांच्या कपडे वापरणे टाळणे व व्यक्तिगत स्वच्छता टाळणे आवश्यक आहे.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: हवेतून फैलणाऱ्या रोगात थुंकताना रुमाल धरणे आवश्यक आहे का? कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: हवेतून फैलणाऱ्या रोगात थुंकताना रुमाल धरणे आवश्यक आहे, कारण थुंक्याने रोगजंतू हवेत पसरतात आणि रुमाल धरण्याने ते फैलणे टाळता येते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: पाण्यामार्फत फैलणाऱ्या रोग टाळण्यासाठी पाणी उकळून पिणे आवश्यक आहे का? कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: पाण्यामार्फत फैलणाऱ्या रोग टाळण्यासाठी पाणी उकळून पिणे आवश्यक आहे, कारण उकळण्याने पाण्यातील रोगजंतू मारे जातात व त्यामुळे रोगाची लागण टाळली जाते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: कीटकांमुळे फैलणाऱ्या रोग टाळण्यासाठी डासांची पैदास रोखणे आवश्यक आहे का? कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: कीटकांमुळे फैलणाऱ्या रोग टाळण्यासाठी डासांची पैदास रोखणे आवश्यक आहे, कारण डासे रोगजंतू वाहतात व त्यांची पैदास रोखण्याने रोगप्रसार टाळता येते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: संसर्गजन्य रोग म्हणजे काय? त्यांचे प्रसाराचे माध्यम कोणती आहेत? त्यांची अडथळा बसविण्यासाठी काय उपाय घ्यावे?
questions.answer: संसर्गजन्य रोग हे सूक्ष्मजीवामुळे होणाऱ्ये रोग आहेत जे एका व्यक्तीने दुसऱ्याने फैलतात. त्यांचे प्रसाराचे माध्यम हवेतून (थुंकणे, शिंकणे), पाण्यामार्फत (दूषित पाणी), अन्नामार्फत (दूषित अन्न), कीटकांमार्फत (डास, माश्या) आणि संपर्कामुळे (स्पर्श, कपडे) आहेत. अडथळा बसविण्यासाठी हात धुणे, पाणी उकळून पिणे, अन्न झाकून ठेवणे, रुमाल धरणे, डासांची पैदास रोखणे व व्यक्तिगत स्वच्छता टाळणे उपाय आहेत.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: लसीकरण म्हणजे काय? त्याचे फायदे काय आहेत? रोगप्रतिबंधात लसीकरणाचा महत्त्व काय आहे?
questions.answer: लसीकरण म्हणजे शरीरात रोगप्रतिकार क्षमता वाढविणे. त्याचे फायदे रोगांची लागण टाळणे, रोगातील कष्ट कमी करणे व दीर्घकालीन संरक्षण आहे. रोगप्रतिबंधात लसीकरणाचा महत्त्व त्यामध्ये आहे की ते विशिष्ट रोगांशी लढण्याची शक्ती विकसित करते, त्यामुळे रोगप्रसार टाळतो व सामाजिक आरोग्य सुधारतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: संसर्गजन्य रोग परिभाषित करा.
questions.answer: संसर्गजन्य रोग हे सूक्ष्मजीवामुळे होणाऱ्ये रोग आहेत जे एका व्यक्तीने दुसऱ्याने हवेतून, पाण्यामार्फत, अन्नामार्फत, कीटकांमार्फत व संपर्कामुळे फैलतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: रोगप्रतिबंध परिभाषित करा.
questions.answer: रोगप्रतिबंध म्हणजे रोगाची लागण टाळण्यासाठी केलेले उपाय, जसे की स्वच्छता, लसीकरण, पाणी शुध्दीकरण व व्यक्तिगत स्वच्छता.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: हवेतून फैलणाऱ्या रोगांचे प्रसार कसे होतो? त्यात रोगजंतू कसे फैलतात?
questions.answer: हवेतून फैलणाऱ्या रोगात रोगजंतू रोग्याच्या थुंक्याने, शिंकण्याने व खोकल्याने हवेत पसरतात. ते हवेत फुसक्यांसह गळतात व आसपासच्या लोकांचे श्वास घेण्याने त्यांच्या शरीरात प्रवेश करतात. त्यामुळे एकाच वेळी अनेक लोकांना रोग होऊ शकतो, विशेषतः भीड जाग्यांमध्ये.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: पाण्यामार्फत फैलणाऱ्या रोगांचे प्रसार कसे होतो? त्यात रोगजंतू कसे पसरतात?
questions.answer: पाण्यामार्फत फैलणाऱ्या रोगात रोगजंतू दूषित पाण्यात शिरतात. जे लोक हे दूषित पाणी पिणे ते रोगजंतूंचा शरीरात प्रवेश होतो व रोगाची लागण होते. दूषित पाण्याचे मुख्य स्रोत दूषित नदी, कुंए व अपूर्णपणे शुध्द केलेले पाणी आहेत.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पदार्थ सूक्ष्म _______ पासून बनलेले असतात.
questions.answer: कणां

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याची स्थायू अवस्था _______ असे म्हणतात.
questions.answer: बर्फ

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पदार्थांमध्ये ऊर्जा मिळविण्याचा एक महत्त्वाचा साधन _______ आहे.
questions.answer: इंधन

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्याची उष्णता, वारा, पाणी हे _______ ऊर्जा स्रोत आहेत.
questions.answer: पयावरणीय

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: गतिमान वस्तूमध्ये असलेली ऊर्जा _______ ऊर्जा म्हणतात.
questions.answer: गतिज

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सर्व पदार्थे निसर्गात फक्त स्थायू अवस्थेत असतात.
questions.answer: चूक

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याचे थेंब पाण्याचे सूक्ष्म कणे असतात.
questions.answer: बरोबर

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: डांबरगोळ्या कपड्यांमध्ये ठेवलेली असतील तर त्यांचा वास कपड्यांवर बसलेल्या कणामुळे येतो.
questions.answer: बरोबर

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: ऊर्जेचा रूप प्रकाश असताना तो ध्वनी ऊर्जा म्हणून कार्य करतो.
questions.answer: चूक

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: खडूने फळ्यावर लिहिताना फळ्यावर पडलेले खडूचे कण काय होतात?
questions.answer: खडूचे कण

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पदार्थांचे जे लहान कण दिसतात ते काय असतात?
questions.answer: सूक्ष्म कण

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: खालीलपैकी कोणता द्रव पदार्थ नाही?
questions.answer: लोखंड

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्याची उष्णता, वारा, पाणी हे कोणते ऊर्जा स्रोत आहेत?
questions.answer: पयावरणीय

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पदार्थांचे सूक्ष्म भाग काय म्हणतात?
questions.answer: कण

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याची स्थायू अवस्था काय म्हणतात?
questions.answer: बर्फ

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: गतिज ऊर्जा म्हणजे कोणती ऊर्जा?
questions.answer: गतीची

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: डांबरगोळ्याचा वास कपड्यांवर काय बसतो?
questions.answer: कण

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: ऊर्जा म्हणजे काय?
questions.answer: कार्य करण्याची क्षमता

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पदार्थे काय बनलेली असतात?
questions.answer: पदार्थे सूक्ष्म कणांपासून बनलेली असतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याची कोणती अवस्थे निसर्गात आढळतात?
questions.answer: पाण्याची स्थायू, द्रव आणि वायू तीनों अवस्थे निसर्गात आढळतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: डांबरगोळ्या कपड्यांमध्ये ठेवली असतील तर त्याचा वास कशामुळे येतो?
questions.answer: डांबरगोळ्यांचे लहान कण कपड्यावर बसल्यामुळे त्याचा वास येतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: गतिज ऊर्जा म्हणजे काय?
questions.answer: गतिमान वस्तूमध्ये असलेली ऊर्जा गतिज ऊर्जा म्हणतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पदार्थ आणि वस्तू यातील फरक काय आहे?
questions.answer: पदार्थ म्हणजे काही जणूनी बनलेला असतो, ज्याचे कण एकसारखे असतात. वस्तू म्हणजे पदार्थापासून बनीली विशिष्ट आकार आणि उपयोग असलेली चीज, जसे बेंच, कपडे.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पाण्याची तीन अवस्थे काय आहेत आणि त्यांचे उदाहरण द्या?
questions.answer: पाण्याची तीन अवस्थे स्थायू (बर्फ), द्रव (पाणी) आणि वायू (भाप) आहेत. उदाहरण: शीतात पाणी बर्फ होते, उकलीत पाणी पाणी राहते, उकलीत पाणी भाप बनतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: धावणाऱ्या व्यक्तीतील गतिज ऊर्जा काय होऊ शकतो?
questions.answer: धावणाऱ्या व्यक्तीतील गतिज ऊर्जा श्वास वाढणे, हात पाय हिलवणे, पसी येत होना इत्यादींमध्ये रूपांतर होते. त्यामुळे शरीरातील क्रिया करण्याकी शक्ती मिळते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्याची उष्णता, वारा, पाणी हे पयावरणीय ऊर्जा स्रोत कसे?
questions.answer: सूर्याची उष्णता, वारा, पाणी हे पयावरणीय ऊर्जा स्रोत आहेत जे न संपणारे, स्वच्छ आणि पुणरावर्तनीय आहेत. त्यांचा वापर करण्याने प्रदूषण होत नाही.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: खडूने फळ्यावर लिहिताना फळ्यावर पडलेले खडूचे कण खाल्यावर पडणे कसा होतो?
questions.answer: खडूने लिहिताना फळ्यावर खडूचे कण चिकटले. फळ्याला पुसल्यानंतर ते कण फळ्यापासून मोकळे झाले आणि गुरुत्वाकर्षणामुळे खाल्यावर पडले. हे कण खडूचे असल्यामुळे त्याचा रंग दिसला.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: डांबरगोळ्या कपड्यांमध्ये ठेवलेली असतील तर त्यांचा वास कपड्यांवर कशामुळे येतो?
questions.answer: डांबरगोळ्या कपड्यांमध्ये ठेवलेली असतील तर ते सतत वायुरूपातील लहान कणांत रूपांतर होतात. त्यांचे लहान कण कपड्यावर बसतात. त्यामुळे कपड्यांना डांबरगोळीचा वास येतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सूर्याची उष्णता, वारा, पाणी हे पयावरणीय ऊर्जा स्रोत म्हणून वापरण्याने फायदा काय आहे?
questions.answer: सूर्याची उष्णता, वारा, पाणी हे न संपणारे, स्वच्छ आणि पुणरावर्तनीय ऊर्जा स्रोत आहेत. त्यांचा वापर करण्याने प्रदूषण होत नाही आणि पर्यावरण संतुलित राहतो. त्यामुळे भविष्यातील पीढींसाठी ऊर्जा conserved राहते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पदार्थांची अवस्थे काय आहेत? त्यांचे गुणधर्म कसे बदलतात? उदाहरण सaha लिहा.
questions.answer: पदार्थांची तीन मूलभूत अवस्थे स्थायू, द्रव आणि वायू आहेत. स्थायू अवस्थेत कण एकत्र बंधलेले असतात, त्यामुळे पदार्थाचा निश्चित आकार आणि आयतन असतो. द्रव अवस्थेत कण स्वतंत्रपणे बहते पण एकत्र राहतात, त्यामुळe पदार्थाचा निश्चित आयतन असतो पण आकार बदलतो. वायू अवस्थेत कण खूप अंतरावर असतात आणि स्वतंत्रपणे गामवते, त्यामुळे पदार्थाचा न तो निश्चित आकार नाही न निश्चित आयतन. उदाहरण: पाणी स्थायू अवस्थेत बर्फ, द्रव अवस्थात पाणी, वायू अवस्थात भाप असतो. अवस्थे बदलली पण पाण्याचे कण एकसारखे राहतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: ऊर्जा म्हणजे काय? त्यांचे कोणते कोणते रूप असतात? त्यांचा वापर काय करतो?
questions.answer: ऊर्जा म्हणजे कार्य करण्याची क्षमता. ऊर्जेचे विविध रूप असतात जसे गतिज ऊर्जा (गतीचा रूप), उष्णता ऊर्जा (वाटेचा रूप), प्रकाश ऊर्जा (देखण्याचा रूप), ध्वनी ऊर्जा ( ऐकण्याचा रूप), विद्युत ऊर्जा (विद्युत प्रवाहाचा रूप). गतिज ऊर्जा धावणाऱ्या व्यक्ती, फERRING व्हीलमध्ये असते. उष्णता ऊर्जा इंधन ज्वलनातून मिळते, ज्यामुळे पाणी उकळतो. प्रकाश ऊर्जा सूर्यप्रकाशातून मिळते, ज्यामुळे वनस्पती फोटोसिंथेसिस करतात. ध्वनी ऊर्जा बाजूस वजवण्यात असते. विद्युत ऊर्जा घरातील पंखे, लांब, टीव्हीमध्ये काम करते. सर्व रूपांतरांत ऊर्जा conserved राहते, फक्त रूप बदलते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पदार्थ
questions.answer: पदार्थ म्हणजे काही जणूनी बनलेला असतो, ज्याचे सूक्ष्म कण एकसारखे असतात आणि त्याने द्रव्यमान आणि घेते असते.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: ऊर्जा
questions.answer: ऊर्जा म्हणजे कार्य करण्याची क्षमता. ते विविध रूपांतरात असतात जसे गतिज, उष्णता, प्रकाश, ध्वनी, विद्युत इत्यादी.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: पदार्थांच्या अवस्थेत बदल झाल्यावर त्यांचे कण कसे बदलत नाहीत?
questions.answer: पदार्थांच्या अवस्थेत बदल झाल्यावर त्यांचे कण एकसारखे राहतात. फक्त कणांचे व्यवस्थिती बदलते. स्थायू अवस्थेत कण एकत्र बंधलेले असतात, द्रव अवस्थेत कण स्वतंत्रपणे बहते पण एकत्र राहतात, वायू अवस्थेत कण खूप अंतरावर असतात आणि स्वतंत्रपणे गामवते. अवस्थे बदलली पण प्रत्येक कणाचे द्रव्यमान, रचना आणि गुणधर्म एकाच राहतात. उदाहरण: पाण्याचे कण बर्फ, पाणी आणि भापतील सर्वात एकसारखे असतात. त्यामुळे पदार्थाचे मूलभूत कण अवस्थे बदलली जाणून बदलत नाहीत.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य धोक्यात आणणाऱ्या मुख्य घटकांमध्ये _______ शाश्वत आहे.
questions.answer: व्यसनाधीनता

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: स्वच्छ पाण्याची उपलब्धता न झाल्यामुळे _______ आजार फैलू शकतो.
questions.answer: कोलरा

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्यसाठी महत्त्वाचे घटक _______ आहे.
questions.answer: पोषक आहार

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सार्वजनिक ठिकाणी थुंकण्यास कायद्याने _______ आहे.
questions.answer: दंडनीय

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: तंबाखू खाण्यामुळे तोंडात _______ पडू शकतो.
questions.answer: व्रण

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील वाक्य चूक की बरोबर ते सांगा.
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य धोक्यात आणणाऱ्या घटकांसाठी प्रदूषण, अस्वच्छता, साथीचे आजार, कीटकदंशापासून होणारे आजार शमील नाहीत.
questions.answer: चूक

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील वाक्य चूक की बरोबर ते सांगा.
questions.text: व्यक्तिगत आरोग्य व सवयीतून आपल्याला समाजाचे आरोग्य व सार्वजनिक आरोग्य प्राप्त करता येते.
questions.answer: बरोबर

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील वाक्य चूक की बरोबर ते सांगा.
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य चांगले राहण्यासाठी प्रत्येकाला व्यसनांपासून दूर राहणे आवश्यक नाही.
questions.answer: चूक

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील वाक्य चूक की बरोबर ते सांगा.
questions.text: मद्यपान व तंबाखू सेवनामुळे यकृताचे, आतड्याचे तसेच मूत्राशयाचे रोग होतात.
questions.answer: बरोबर

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: खालील बायांमध्ये दिलेल्या सामाजिक आरोग्य धोक्यात आणणाऱ्या घटकांना दायांमध्ये दिलेल्या परिणामांशी जोडा.
questions.answer: प्रदूषण – श्वसन आजार, अस्वच्छता – पाणीत जनून फैलणारे आजार, साथीचे आजार – जुळण्याचा आजार, कीटकदंशापासून होणारे आजार – मलेरिया, डेंगू, व्यसनाधीनता – कर्करोग, यकृताचा रोग

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य धोक्यात आणणाऱ्या खालीलपैकी कोणतीं सवयी नाही?
questions.answer: व्यायाम

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्यसाठी खालीलपैकी कोणतीं आवश्यक नाही?
questions.answer: अधिक स्क्रीन टाइम

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सार्वजनिक स्वच्छता वाटण्यासाठी खालीलपैकी कोणतीं योग्य उपाय आहे?
questions.answer: सार्वजनिक स्वच्छतागृहांचा वापर करणे

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य चांगले राहण्यासाठी खालीलपैकी कोणतीं छंद जोपासावी?
questions.answer: फुटबॉल खेळणे

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील पर्यायांमधील विसम anomalous शोधा आणि कारण सांगा.
questions.text: पोषक आहार, व्यायाम, स्वच्छता, तंबाखू
questions.answer: तंबाखू - हे सामाजिक आरोग्य धोक्यात आणणाऱ्या घटक आहे, शेषे आरोग्य वर्धक छंद.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील पर्यायांमधील विसम anomalous शोधा आणि कारण सांगा.
questions.text: स्वच्छ पाणी, पोषक आहार, व्यक्तिगत स्वच्छता, अस्वच्छता
questions.answer: अस्वच्छता - हे सामाजिक आरोग्य धोक्यात आणणाऱ्या घटक आहे, शेषे आरोग्यसाठी आवश्यक गोष्टी.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य धोक्यात आणणाऱ्या तंबाखू युक्त पदार्थाचे एक उदाहरण सांगा.
questions.answer: गुटखा

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्यसाठी आवश्यक स्वच्छ पाण्याचे स्रोत कोणता?
questions.answer: प्यावळ

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य चांगले राहण्यासाठी जोपासण्यायोग्य छंदाचे एक उदाहरण सांगा.
questions.answer: जोगिंग

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सार्वजनिक ठिकाणी थुंकण्याने होणारा परिणाम कोणता?
questions.answer: प्रदूषण

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य धोक्यात आणणाऱ्या व्यसनामुळे होणारा गंभीर आजार कोणता?
questions.answer: कर्करोग

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य म्हणजे काय?
questions.answer: सामाजिक आरोग्य म्हणजे समाजातील सर्व लोकांचे शारीरिक, मानसिक व सामाजिक आरोग्य.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य धोक्यात आणणाऱ्या खालीलपैकी दोन घटक सांगा.
questions.answer: प्रदूषण आणि अस्वच्छता सामाजिक आरोग्य धोक्यात आणणाऱ्या घटक आहेत.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: व्यक्तिगत आरोग्य व सामाजिक आरोग्य यांचे संबंध काय आहे?
questions.answer: व्यक्तिगत आरोग्य सुधरली तर सामाजिक आरोग्य देखील सुधरतो, आणि विपर्यय.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्यसाठी स्वच्छ पाण्याची काळजी कशे घ्यावी?
questions.answer: पाण्याचे शुद्धीकरण करा, सुरक्षित स्रोतापासून पाणी पिऊन, पाण्याचे भांडे स्वच्छ ठेवा.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: तंबाखू खाण्याचे एक घातक परिणाम सांगा.
questions.answer: तंबाखू खाण्यामुळे कर्करोग होऊ शकतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य धोक्यात आणणाऱ्या मुख्य घटकांमध्ये प्रदूषण व अस्वच्छता यांचे परिणाम काय आहेत?
questions.answer: प्रदूषणामुळे श्वसन आजार, हृदय रोग वाढतात. अस्वच्छतामुळे पाणीत जनून फैलणारे आजार जसे कोलरा, टायफायड फैलतात, ज्यामुळे लोकांचा आरोग्य खराब होतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य चांगले राहण्यासाठी व्यक्ती काय प्रयत्न करू शकतो?
questions.answer: व्यक्ती पोषक आहार घेऊ शकतो, नियमित व्यायाम करतो, व्यक्तिगत स्वच्छता टाकतो, व्यसनांपासून दूर राहतो, आणि सार्वजनिक स्वच्छतेचा पालन करतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सार्वजनिक स्वच्छता वाटण्यासाठी समाज काय करू शकतो?
questions.answer: समाज सार्वजनिक शौचालयांचा वापर करतो, कचरा उचित ठिकाणी टाकतो, रस्त्यावर थुंकणे बंद करतो, आणि स्वच्छता अभियानात सहभागी होतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: व्यसनाधीनता सामाजिक आरोग्याला कसे प्रभावित करते?
questions.answer: व्यसनाधीनता यामुळे व्यक्तीचा शारीरिक व मानसिक आरोग्य खराब होतो, त्यामुळे तो समाजाला आर्थिक व सामाजिक बोझ बनतो, आणि इतरांना देखील व्यसनाचा प्रभाव होतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य धोक्यात आणणाऱ्या तंबाखू खाण्याचे घातक परिणाम काय आहेत? कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: तंबाखू खाण्यामुळे तोंडात व्रण पडतात, जो कर्करोगाला अडावा देतात. तंबाखूच्या धूमामुळे फुफ्फुसांची क्षमता घटते, ज्यामुळे श्वसन आजार होतात. तंबाखूचे सेवन यकृताचे व रक्तवाहिन्यांचे रोग वाढवतो. त्यामुळे मृत्यूचे जोखيم वाढतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: स्वच्छ पाण्याची उपलब्धता सामाजिक आरोग्यसाठी कशे आवश्यक आहे? कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: स्वच्छ पाण्याची उपलब्धता न झाल्यामुळे पाणीत जनून फैलणारे आजार जसे कोलरा, टायफायड फैलतात, ज्यामुळे सर्वसामान्य जनतेचा आरोग्य खराब होतो. स्वच्छ पाण्याने हात धुणे, पाकपदार्थे धुणे, पिणे यामुळे आजारांचे फैलाव टाळता येतो. त्यामुळे आरोग्य जोपासना वाढते आणि समाज निरामय राहतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: व्यक्तिगत स्वच्छता सामाजिक आरोग्यसाठी कशे महत्वाची आहे? कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: व्यक्तिगत स्वच्छता टाकण्यामुळे हात धुणे, स्नान करणे, कपडे धुणे यामुळे शरीरावरून आजारांची जुळणे टाळली जाते. जणू हात धुण्याने पाणीत जनून फैलणारे आजार टाळता येतो. त्यामुळे घरातील व शाळेतील लोकांचा आरोग्य सुधरतो, ज्यामुळे सामाजिक आरोग्य देखील वाढतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य धोक्यात आणणाऱ्या घटकांमध्ये प्रदूषण, अस्वच्छता, व्यसनाधीनता यांचे प्रभाव व त्यांचे उपाय सांगा.
questions.answer: प्रदूषणामुळे हवा दूषित होते, ज्यामुळे श्वसन आजार, हृदय रोग वाढतात. उपाय: जामिनीच्या वाहतूकच्या वापराला कमी करणे, वृक्ष लावणे, उद्योगांचे धुळे नियंत्रण करणे. अस्वच्छतामुळे पाणी व मातीचा दूषण होतो, ज्यामुळे पाणीत जनून फैलणारे आजार फैलतात. उपाय: स्वच्छ शौचालयांची उपलब्धता, कचरेचे उचित निपटारा, पाण्याचे शुद्धीकरण करणे. व्यसनाधीनता यामुळे तंबाखू, मद्यपान, नशे यामुळे कर्करोग, यकृताचा रोग, मानसिक रोग होतात. उपाय: जागरूकता अभियान, परामर्श केंद्रे, व्यसनमुक्तीसाठी मदत, शाळेत शिक्षण. यामुळे सामाजिक आरोग्य सुधरतो आणि समाज निरामय राहतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य चांगले राहण्यासाठी व्यक्ती व समाजाला काय प्रयत्न करणे आवश्यक आहे? विस्तृत उत्तर लिहा.
questions.answer: व्यक्तीला पोषक आहार घेणे, नियमित व्यायाम करणे, व्यक्तिगत स्वच्छता टाकणे, व्यसनांपासून दूर राहणे, मानसिक आरोग्यासाठी ध्यान व शेअर करणे आवश्यक आहे. समाजाला स्वच्छ पाणीपुरवठा उपलब्ध करवणे, सार्वजनिक शौचालयांची व्यवस्था करणे, कचरा व्यवस्थापन सुधारणे, प्रदूषण नियंत्रण करणे, आरोग्य जागरूकता अभियान चलवणे, शाळेत आरोग्य शिक्षण देणे, व्यसनमुक्तीसाठी साधे उपलब्ध करवणे आवश्यक आहे. यामु�्के व्यक्तीचा व societyscha आरोग्य वाढतो, ज्यामुळे राष्ट्रीय प्रगती व विकास होतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य
questions.answer: सामाजिक आरोग्य म्हणजे समाजातील सर्व लोकांचे शारीरिक, मानसिक व सामाजिक आरोग्याची अवस्था, ज्यामुळे ते निरामय व आनंदी जीवन जीता येऊ शकतात.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: व्यसनाधीनता
questions.answer: व्यसनाधीनता म्हणजे काय पणे पदार्थ किंवा व्यवहार अशी इच्छा जणू न थांबवली जाऊ शकते, ज्यामुळे व्यक्तीचा शारीरिक, मानसिक व सामाजिक जीवन खराब होतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्य धोक्यात आणणाऱ्या साथीचे आजार कसे फैलतात व त्याचे परिणाम काय आहेत?
questions.answer: साथीचे आजार जसे टीबी, इन्फ्लुएंजा हवा मध्ये घोललेली सूक्ष्मजीवांद्वारे फैलतात, ज्यामुहे एका व्यक्तीने खांसणे, जुके मारणे वा हात धुणे न करण्यामुळे इतरांशी फैलते. त्यामुळे शाळा, कार्यालय, घरातील लोकांमध्ये आजार फैलते, ज्यामुळे उपस्थिती व उत्पादनता घटते. दीर्घकालीन आजामुळे गंभीर आरोग्य समस्या होऊ शकते. त्यामुळे सामाजिक आरोग्य धोक्यात येतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 1
questions.text: सामाजिक आरोग्यसाठी पोषक आहाराची भूमिका काय आहे?
questions.answer: पोषक आहारामुळे शरीराला आवश्यक पोषक तत्व जसे प्रोटीन, विटामिन, खनिज मिळतात, ज्यामुळे वाढ, ऊर्जा व रोग प्रतिरोधक क्षमता वाढते. पोषक आहार न झाल्यामुळे कुपोषण होतो, ज्यामुळे शारीरिक व मानसिक विकास अडथळे पडतो. पोषक आहारामुळे रोगांचे जोखيم घटते व निरामयता वाढते. त्यामुळे सामाजिक आरोग्य वाढतो.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: The science that tries to understand past events is called _______.
questions.answer: history

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: History is not written solely on the basis of _______.
questions.answer: imagination

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: The time that has already gone by is called the _______.
questions.answer: past

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: The time that we are in now is called the _______.
questions.answer: present

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: The time that is yet to come is called the _______.
questions.answer: future

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: State whether the following statement is true or false.
questions.text: History is a science that tells us about events in the future.
questions.answer: False

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: State whether the following statement is true or false.
questions.text: The scientific method of history involves testing evidence through repeated experiments.
questions.answer: True

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: State whether the following statement is true or false.
questions.text: Oral sources of history include books and manuscripts.
questions.answer: False

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: State whether the following statement is true or false.
questions.text: Studying history helps us understand how to shape a good future.
questions.answer: True

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Match the following sources of history with their correct type.
questions.answer: Coins – Material sources, Letters – Written sources, Folk songs – Oral sources, Stone inscriptions – Material sources

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a type of source of history?
questions.answer: Digital sources

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What does the study of history help us understand about past societies?
options: Their way of life and progress

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why is history considered a scientific discipline?
questions.answer: History is considered a scientific discipline because it uses the scientific method to test and verify evidence. Evidence from material, written, and oral sources is collected and examined for reliability. This process ensures that historical accounts are based on facts, not just imagination.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How are the past, present, and future linked according to the chapter?
questions.answer: The past, present, and future are linked by a continuous chain of events. Present actions are influenced by past events, and future developments depend on past discoveries and inventions. For example, today’s technology is built on the foundation of past innovations.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What are the three types of sources of history? Give one example of each.
questions.answer: The three types of sources of history are material, written, and oral. Material sources include coins and pots; written sources include books and manuscripts; oral sources include folk songs and traditional stories.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How does studying history inspire us?
questions.answer: Studying history inspires us by telling the life stories of great people and their struggles. It motivates us to learn from their courage and dedication. It also teaches us about the progress of human civilization through cooperation and innovation.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why can we not conduct experiments to recreate past events in history?
questions.answer: We cannot conduct experiments to recreate past events because they have already happened and cannot be repeated. Unlike in sciences like physics or chemistry, we cannot control or redo historical events in a laboratory. Therefore, historians rely on evidence from sources to understand the past.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why is it important to examine evidence from different sources when studying history?
questions.answer: It is important to examine evidence from different sources because different people may narrate the same event differently. Comparing multiple sources helps us check for consistency and reliability. This ensures that the historical account is accurate and not biased.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why does history help us shape a good future?
questions.answer: History helps us shape a good future by teaching us from past mistakes and successes. It shows us how human actions affect society and the environment. By understanding this, we can make better decisions today to create a favourable future.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how the study of history helps us understand the progress of human civilization.
questions.answer: The study of history shows how human civilization has progressed over time. We learn that early humans made tools from natural materials, learned to use fire, and invented the wheel. Each generation built upon these discoveries, leading to advancements in agriculture, transportation, and communication. History also teaches us how cooperation in villages and cities led to better living conditions. Inventions of today are possible only because of the foundations laid by past innovations. Thus, history reveals a continuous chain of development where past events shape the present and future.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the scientific method of history with reference to how evidence is collected and used.
questions.answer: The scientific method of history involves a systematic process of collecting, examining, and organizing evidence from the past. First, historians gather evidence from material sources like coins and pots, written sources like books and inscriptions, and oral sources like folk tales. This evidence is then carefully examined to check its reliability — whether it is authentic and accurate. Historians may also take help from other sciences like archaeology to verify findings. Once the evidence is confirmed as reliable, it is arranged in a proper sequence to understand how events happened. Finally, a historical account is written based on this verified evidence. This method ensures that history is not based on imagination but on facts that can be tested and verified, just like in other sciences.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Define 'sources of history'.
questions.answer: Sources of history are the materials, records, or traditions from which we obtain information about past events.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Define 'scientific method' in the context of history.
questions.answer: The scientific method in history is the process of testing and verifying evidence from the past to determine its reliability before using it to write a historical account.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how history helps us understand the relationship between human actions and their consequences on society.
questions.answer: History shows that every human action, whether individual or collective, has consequences that affect society. For example, when people in a village work together, the village progresses; when they do not cooperate, development is hindered. Similarly, historical events like India’s struggle for Independence were the result of collective action and led to freedom. By studying such events, we learn that positive actions lead to favourable outcomes, while conflict and neglect create obstacles. This understanding helps us make better choices in our daily lives to promote harmony and progress.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain why the study of history is important for understanding the present and shaping the future.
questions.answer: The study of history is important because it helps us understand how past events have shaped the present world we live in. It shows us the roots of current systems, cultures, and challenges. By learning from past successes and mistakes, we can make informed decisions today. History also teaches us that the future is built on the foundation of past discoveries and inventions. Therefore, knowing history enables us to shape a better future by avoiding errors and repeating what worked well.

questions.text: Explain how the Carbon-14 dating method works to determine the age of ancient objects.
questions.answer: After the death of an organism, the Carbon-14 in its body begins to decrease. By measuring the remaining C-14 in a sample like wood or bone in a laboratory, we can estimate how long ago the organism died. This helps determine the approximate age of the object and the culture it belonged to.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe how the earth's rotation causes day and night.
questions.answer: As the earth rotates around its axis, the part facing the sun experiences daylight while the part away from the sun is in darkness. One full rotation takes approximately 24 hours, which we divide into day and night.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What are the units of measuring time mentioned in the chapter? List them in increasing order.
questions.answer: The units of measuring time mentioned are second, minute, hour, day, week, fortnight, month, year, century, and millennium. In increasing order: second < minute < hour < day < week < fortnight < month < year < century < millennium.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Differentiate between the Prehistoric and Historic periods.
questions.answer: The Prehistoric period is the time for which no written records are available, so we rely on archaeological evidence. The Historic period is the time for which written records exist, allowing us to write history based on those records.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why do we divide time into periods like years, centuries, and millennia?
questions.answer: We divide time into larger periods for convenience, as it is difficult to grasp vast spans of time all at once. Dividing time helps us understand and organize historical events in a systematic way.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why is the Christian Era also called the Common Era?
questions.answer: The Christian Era is called the Common Era because it is widely used across the world for measuring time, regardless of religious beliefs, making it a common reference point.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why are tree rings useful in determining the age of a wooden artefact?
questions.answer: A new ring forms in the trunk of a tree each year as it grows in girth. By counting the rings in a cross-section of wood, we can determine the age of the tree when it was cut, which gives the age of the artefact.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain the scientific methods used to measure time and establish the age of ancient objects. Give examples.
questions.answer: Scientific methods like Carbon-14 analysis and Tree-ring analysis (Dendrochronology) are used to estimate the age of ancient objects. Carbon-14 dating measures the remaining radioactive carbon in once-living materials like wood, bone, or charcoal to determine how long ago the organism died. Tree-ring dating counts the annual growth rings in a tree’s trunk to determine its age, which can be applied to wooden artefacts. These methods help place objects on a unilinear timeline and understand the period of the culture they belonged to. For example, if an earthen pot is found to be 5000 years old via Carbon-14, it belongs to around 3000 BC.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the division of time into day, night, week, month, year, century, and millennium with examples from daily life or history.
questions.answer: Time is divided based on natural and cultural cycles. A day consists of daytime and nighttime, caused by Earth’s rotation. Seven days make a week, roughly based on lunar phases. Four weeks make a month, and twelve months make a year, based on Earth’s revolution around the sun. One hundred years make a century, and ten centuries make a millennium. For example, we say 'It is morning' at sunrise, 'It is Monday' to start the week, 'It is January' for the month, and '2024' for the year. Historical periods like the first century CE (1-100 CE) or the third millennium BCE show how we group years to study history in a structured way.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Define 'Common Era'.
questions.answer: The Common Era is the system of numbering years that begins from the year traditionally believed to be the birth of Jesus Christ, denoted as CE or AD, and is used globally for measuring time.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Define 'Before Common Era'.
questions.answer: Before Common Era (BCE or BC) refers to the period of time before the start of the Common Era, with years counted in reverse order, such as 100 BCE, 50 BCE, leading up to 1 BCE.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how we use the date to specify a particular day.
questions.answer: To specify a particular day, we write the date which includes three parts: the serial number of the day, the name or number of the month, and the serial number of the year. For example, 10 June 2024 means the 10th day of the 6th month of the year 2024. This system allows us to uniquely identify any day in the unilinear timeline. It helps in recording events, planning activities, and understanding historical sequences. The date is based on the Common Era system, which provides a common reference point across cultures.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain why it is necessary to divide the vast period of Earth's history into stages.
questions.answer: The span of 4.5 billion years since Earth's formation is too vast to understand all at once. Dividing it into stages like eras, periods, and epochs helps us study changes in a manageable way. It allows scientists and historians to focus on specific developments, such as the formation of continents, appearance of life, or evolution of humans. This staged approach makes it easier to compare events and understand cause and effect over time. Just as we use years and centuries for human history, we use geological time scales for Earth's long history.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2

questions.answer: Mars is considered a possible candidate for past life because it has features similar to Earth, such as volcanoes, valleys, deserts, and polar ice caps. Although its atmosphere is mostly carbon dioxide and lacks liquid water today, scientists believe it may have had water in the past, making ancient life a possibility.

questions.text: Explain why some species of dinosaurs became extinct.
questions.answer: Some species of dinosaurs became extinct due to sudden natural disasters or major environmental changes that they could not adapt to. Their inability to survive these changes led to their extinction. Fossil evidence suggests that such events wiped out large dinosaur species suddenly.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What are the characteristics of most mammals?
questions.answer: Most mammals have the following characteristics: the baby grows in the mother's womb for some time before birth, and after birth, the baby is fed on the mother's milk for some time. They are warm-blooded and have hair or fur on their bodies.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did winged dinosaurs contribute to the evolution of birds?
questions.answer: Fossils of dinosaurs with wings have been found, suggesting that some two-legged, winged dinosaurs gradually evolved into birds. Over generations, their wings became more adapted for flight, and other bird-like features developed. This transition shows how birds evolved from certain dinosaur species.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why are mammals considered the most evolved animals among vertebrates?
questions.answer: Mammals are considered the most evolved because they show advanced care for their young. The baby develops inside the mother's womb, ensuring protection, and after birth, it is fed with mother's milk, which provides essential nutrients and strengthens the mother-offspring bond. This increases the chances of survival of the young.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why do some species become extinct during the process of evolution?
questions.answer: Some species become extinct because they fail to adapt to changing environmental conditions. When internal changes do not help them survive new challenges like climate shifts, food scarcity, or natural disasters, they cannot compete or survive. Over time, such species die out while better-adapted ones continue to evolve.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why is the platypus considered an exception among mammals?
questions.answer: The platypus is an exception because, although it is a mammal, it lays eggs instead of giving birth to live young. However, like other mammals, it feeds its young with milk. This unique combination of reptilian and mammalian traits makes it an evolutionary exception.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the stages of evolution of animals as learnt in the lesson.
questions.answer: The evolution of animals began with unicellular organisms called protozoa. These gradually evolved into multicellular organisms. Over time, various forms of life appeared in sequence: first came invertebrates like worms and mosquitoes, then vertebrates such as fish (aquatic animals). Next evolved amphibians like frogs that live both in water and on land. After that, reptiles such as snakes appeared, which crawl on land. Then came birds, which evolved from winged dinosaurs. Finally, mammals evolved, showing advanced traits like internal development of young and feeding them with mother's milk. Humans evolved from ape-like mammals, first appearing in Africa.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how Charles Darwin contributed to our understanding of evolution.
questions.answer: Charles Darwin gave the first systematic explanation of evolution through his observations and studies. In 1859, he published 'On the Origin of Species', where he proposed that species evolve gradually through natural selection. He explained that organisms best adapted to their environment survive and pass on their traits. Before Darwin, Carl Linnaeus had classified organisms, but Darwin explained how they change over time. Later, in 'The Descent of Man' (1871), he suggested humans evolved from tailless apes in Africa. He pointed to vestigial structures like the tailbone and wisdom teeth as evidence of evolution. Although evidence was limited in his time, later discoveries supported his theory. His work laid the foundation for modern biology.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Evolution
questions.answer: Evolution is the gradual and continuous change in the characteristics of living organisms over generations, leading to the formation of new species.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Vertebrates
questions.answer: Vertebrates are animals that have a backbone or spinal column.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How do fossils help us understand the evolution of animals?
questions.answer: Fossils are the preserved remains or traces of ancient organisms found in rocks. They provide direct evidence of life forms that existed in the past. By studying fossils, scientists can see how the structure of animals has changed over time. For example, fossils of dinosaurs with wings show a link between dinosaurs and birds. Fossils also help determine when certain species lived and how they may have become extinct. Thus, fossils are crucial in tracing the evolutionary history of animals.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why are humans considered to have evolved from ape-like ancestors?
questions.answer: Humans are considered to have evolved from ape-like ancestors because of structural and genetic similarities. Charles Darwin noted that although humans lack tails, the last bone of the human spine is a vestige of a tail, suggesting an evolutionary remnant. Other non-functional structures like wisdom teeth also point to evolutionary changes. Fossil evidence shows a gradual change from ape-like skulls to human skulls over time. The first human-like forms appeared in Africa, supporting the idea of African origin. These observations together support the theory that humans evolved from earlier primates.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the tools made by Homo habilis and their uses.
questions.answer: Homo habilis made stone choppers and scrapers. These tools were used to break bones to get marrow and to scrape meat from animal hides. They were not suitable for hunting big animals.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did Homo erectus differ from Homo habilis in terms of physical and mental development?
questions.answer: Homo erectus had a more developed brain and stood fully erect, unlike Homo habilis whose spine was slightly bent. Homo erectus also made symmetrical tools like hand-axes and used fire, which Homo habilis did not master.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Mention two ways in which Neanderthals used animal hides.
questions.answer: Neanderthals used scrapers made from stone flakes to clean meat from animal hides. They also made clothing from animal hide to protect themselves from cold.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What changes occurred in human lifestyle after the development of agriculture?
questions.answer: After agriculture, humans began to grow foodgrains and domesticate animals. This led to a settled life, increased food production, and technological progress over time.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Neanderthals become extinct?
questions.answer: Neanderthals became extinct due to their inability to adapt to environmental changes, competition with Homo sapiens for resources, and possibly conflict with them. Their reliance on hunting big animals made survival difficult when climate changed.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why could Homo sapiens produce a variety of sounds?
questions.answer: Homo sapiens had a well-developed larynx, flexible tongue, and strong facial muscles, which allowed them to produce subtle and varied sounds necessary for speech.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why are humans called 'makers' of tools?
questions.answer: Humans are called 'makers' because they design and create tools to perform tasks that other animals cannot, using their intelligence and hand skills.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the evolution of man from Homo habilis to Homo sapiens sapiens with reference to tool use, lifestyle, and mental development.
questions.answer: Homo habilis was the first to use stone tools like choppers and scrapers for foraging. Homo erectus stood upright, made symmetrical hand-axes, and learned to use fire. Neanderthals lived in caves, made advanced tools from flakes, wore hide clothing, and buried their dead with rituals. Homo sapiens developed art, language, and better tools like blades fixed in handles. Homo sapiens sapiens further developed agriculture, settled life, and technology due to enhanced thinking capacity. This progression shows increasing intelligence, adaptability, and cultural development.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how the development of the human hand and brain contributed to tool making and cultural progress.
questions.answer: The human hand evolved with an opposable thumb, allowing a firm grip and precise movements essential for making tools. Walking upright freed the hands for tool use. Simultaneously, the human brain grew larger and more complex, enhancing thinking, planning, and imagination. This enabled humans to design better tools, learn from experience, and pass knowledge to future generations. Over time, tool making improved from simple choppers to advanced blades and eventually to machines. The brain also led to language, art, agriculture, and culture. Thus, the coordination of hand and brain drove human progress.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Heredity
questions.answer: Heredity is the transmission of genetic traits from parents to offspring.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Fossil
questions.answer: A fossil is the preserved remains or impression of an ancient organism found in rock.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how the use of fire changed the life of early humans.
questions.answer: The use of fire provided warmth, allowing early humans to survive in cold climates. It enabled them to cook food, making it easier to digest and safer to eat. Fire also provided protection from wild animals at night. Early humans used fire to harden wooden tools and later to make pottery. Over time, gathering around fire encouraged social interaction and sharing of ideas.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain why Homo sapiens sapiens is considered more advanced than earlier human species.
questions.answer: Homo sapiens sapiens had a highly developed brain capable of complex thinking, planning, and imagination. They developed a clear language system to express thoughts and emotions. They created art, such as cave paintings, and made advanced tools like blades fixed in handles. They began agriculture and domestication of animals, leading to settled life. These abilities allowed them to adapt, innovate, and build culture, making them the most advanced human species.

questions.text: How did early humans choose the right tool for a task?
questions.answer: Early humans chose tools based on the availability of resources, the need to minimize time and energy, maximum efficiency, and skill acquired through practice. They matched the tool to the demand of the task, such as using a pointed stone to dig or a scraper to clean hides.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the percussion technique used in making stone tools.
questions.answer: The percussion technique involved striking a large pebble against another stone to obtain stone flakes. These flakes were then shaped into tools like choppers, scrapers, or borers. This method was used by Homo habilis and Homo erectus in the Old Stone Age.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What changes occurred in human life during the Middle Stone Age?
questions.answer: During the Middle Stone Age, humans began to harvest wild foodgrains, domesticate animals like the dog, and adapt to climate changes. They also started making smaller, more precise tools like microliths for arrows and fish-hooks, reflecting a more varied lifestyle.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why are stone tools more commonly found than tools made of wood or bone?
questions.answer: Stone tools are more commonly found because stone does not decompose easily, unlike wood, bone, twigs, or sticks which rot over time. This durability allows stone tools to survive for thousands of years and be discovered by archaeologists.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Homo sapiens start making a variety of tools in the New Stone Age?
questions.answer: Homo sapiens started making a variety of tools because they had settled into agriculture and animal husbandry, which required different tasks like harvesting, grinding grain, and clearing land. This led to the need for specialized tools such as sickles, grinders, and axes, each suited to a specific job.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why are microliths considered an advancement in tool-making technology?
questions.answer: Microliths are considered an advancement because they are very small and precise, allowing them to be fixed onto sticks to make arrows, spears, or sickles. Their small size made them lightweight and efficient, showing improved skill and planning in tool design during the Middle Stone Age.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why is the fossil of a human skull found near Hathnora important?
questions.answer: The fossil of a human skull found near Hathnora is important because it provides evidence of Homo sapiens living in India during the Old Stone Age. It helps us understand early human migration, lifestyle, and tool use in the Indian subcontinent.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the life and tools of Homo erectus during the Old Stone Age.
questions.answer: Homo erectus lived during the Old Stone Age and made more advanced tools than Homo habilis. They used the percussion technique to create stone flakes and shaped them into symmetrical tools like hand-axes and cleavers. These tools were sharper and more efficient, showing that Homo erectus could plan and visualize tools before making them. They hunted animals, gathered food, and used tools for scraping hides, chopping wood, and sharpening sticks. Their ability to adapt tools to different tasks marked a significant progress in early human intelligence and survival skills.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how the Stone Age is divided into three periods and give one example of a tool from each period.
questions.answer: The Stone Age is divided into three periods based on the type and shape of tools found: Old Stone Age (Palaeolithic), Middle Stone Age (Mesolithic), and New Stone Age (Neolithic). In the Old Stone Age, tools like choppers and hand-axes were made by Homo habilis and Homo erectus using the percussion technique. In the Middle Stone Age, humans made microliths — small stone blades used as tips of arrows and fish-hooks. In the New Stone Age, polished stone tools such as axes and sickles were introduced, reflecting the shift to agriculture and settled life. Each period shows a gradual improvement in tool-making skills and human lifestyle.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Microliths
questions.answer: Microliths are very small stone blades, about the size of a nail or slightly bigger, used in the Middle Stone Age to make tools like arrows, spears, and sickles by fixing them onto wooden or bone handles.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Percussion technique
questions.answer: The percussion technique is a method of making stone tools by striking a large pebble against another stone to break off flakes, which are then shaped into tools such as choppers, scrapers, or borers.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did the invention of polished stone tools change human life in the Neolithic Age?
questions.answer: The invention of polished stone tools in the Neolithic Age made tools smoother, stronger, and more durable. This allowed humans to clear forests more effectively for farming, dig soil better, and harvest crops with tools like sickles. Polished axes were used to cut wood for building huts and making ploughs. These improvements supported the shift from hunting-gathering to farming and animal husbandry. As a result, people could settle in one place, store food, and develop villages, leading to the growth of early civilizations.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did early humans need to choose tools according to the task?
questions.answer: Early humans needed to choose tools according to the task to save time and energy and get the best results. Using the wrong tool, like a blunt stone to dig or a sharp one to scrape, would be inefficient. They observed that different tasks — such as breaking nuts, cutting hides, or sharpening sticks — required different tool shapes and strengths. Over time, they learned to match tools to specific jobs through practice and experience. This smart selection helped them survive and improve their way of life.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did the changing climate affect the lifestyle of Homo sapiens during the Middle Stone Age?
questions.answer: As the climate warmed, big animals like mammoths declined, so Homo sapiens turned to fishing and gathering seasonal foods. They moved their camps according to the availability of food and seasons. This led to a more varied diet and greater mobility.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What are two ways Neanderthals protected themselves from the cold?
questions.answer: Neanderthals protected themselves from the cold by wearing leather clothing and making use of fire. They also built huts in the open and erected tents inside caves using animal hides for warmth.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did agriculture change the way of life in the New Stone Age compared to earlier ages?
questions.answer: In the New Stone Age, humans became producers of foodgrains through cultivation, which allowed them to store food. This made it possible to stay in one place for longer periods, leading to permanent village-settlements, unlike the nomadic life of earlier ages.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What evidence shows that climate changes affected early human migration and settlement?
questions.answer: During glacial periods, cold and dry conditions made life difficult, while interglacial periods brought warmer, humid climates that supported plant and animal life. As the last glacial ended about 11,000 years ago, the warmer climate allowed agriculture to begin, leading to permanent settlements.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did Homo sapiens turn to fishing during the Middle Stone Age?
questions.answer: Homo sapiens turned to fishing because big animals like mammoths were declining due to environmental changes and overhunting. As the climate changed, these animals could not survive, reducing their numbers. This forced humans to find other food sources, and fishing became a reliable alternative.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did people in the New Stone Age settle in one place for longer periods?
questions.answer: People settled in one place because agriculture allowed them to grow and store foodgrains. This reduced the need to constantly move in search of food. Staying in one place also made it easier to look after crops and build permanent homes.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why is the interglacial period important in the history of human culture?
questions.answer: The interglacial period is important because the warmer and more humid climate supported the growth of plants and animals. This made food more available and allowed humans to begin agriculture. About 11,000 years ago, the start of the current interglacial coincided with the beginning of the New Stone Age and farming.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the life of humans in the New Stone Age village-settlements.
questions.answer: In the New Stone Age, humans began practicing agriculture and became producers of foodgrains. They cleared forests, cultivated crops, and stored food for longer use. This allowed them to live permanently in one place, forming village-settlements. They built houses using mud, wood, and thatch. Life became more stable as they no longer had to move constantly for food. They also domesticated animals and developed new tools. Over generations, these villages grew and laid the foundation for future civilizations.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain how seasonal changes influenced the movement and food habits of Homo sapiens in the Middle Stone Age.
questions.answer: In the Middle Stone Age, Homo sapiens moved their camps according to seasons to follow food sources. They hunted animals in favorable seasons and migrated to warmer areas during cold periods. They harvested wild grains, fruits, and roots when available. As big animals declined, they relied more on fishing and gathering. They used knowledge of seasons to plan their movements and survival. This seasonal adaptation helped them survive in changing environments. Their lifestyle was flexible and closely tied to nature’s cycles.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Interglacial period
questions.answer: An interglacial period is the time between two glacial periods when the climate becomes warmer, ice melts, and sea levels rise.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: New Stone Age
questions.answer: The New Stone Age is the period when humans began agriculture, started producing foodgrains, and established permanent village-settlements.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did the end of the last glacial period lead to the beginning of agriculture and the New Stone Age?
questions.answer: About 11,000 years ago, the last glacial period ended and the current interglacial began. The climate became warmer and more humid, which helped plants grow better. As ice melted, new land became available for settlement. These favorable conditions allowed humans to experiment with growing crops. They began to cultivate wild grains and store food. This shift from gathering to farming marked the start of the New Stone Age.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: In what ways was the life of Neanderthals different from that of Homo sapiens in the Middle Stone Age?
questions.answer: Neanderthals mainly lived in caves and relied on hunting large animals in cold European climates. They used leather clothing and fire for warmth. In contrast, Homo sapiens in the Middle Stone Age lived in varied environments and adapted by building tents and huts. They turned to fishing and gathering as big animals declined. Homo sapiens were more mobile and used seasonal knowledge to survive. Their diet and lifestyle were more diverse than that of Neanderthals.

questions.text: How did agriculture lead to the development of special skills?
questions.answer: Agriculture produced surplus food, giving people spare time to develop special skills like pottery and tool-making.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why were protective walls and moats built around village-settlements?
questions.answer: They were built to protect the village from floods, wild animals, and outsiders who stole cattle.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain how the domestication of animals helped early humans in their daily life.
questions.answer: Domesticated animals provided milk, meat, and wool. They helped in hunting and guarding homes. Animals like bullocks were used to pull ploughs and carry loads, making farming and transport easier.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the structure of houses at the beginning of the New Stone Age.
questions.answer: The houses were made of wattle and daub, where walls were woven from sticks or bamboo and plastered with mud or cow-dung. They were often round or quadrangular and built close to each other. Some had more than one room.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did the barter system help in the exchange of goods in village-settlements?
questions.answer: The barter system allowed people to exchange surplus goods like foodgrains for raw materials or finished objects they needed. Salt was often traded for other articles. This system helped spread trade and cooperation between settlements.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What changes occurred in village-settlements when food became available in plenty?
questions.answer: With surplus food, people had spare time to develop crafts and special skills. The population grew, settlements became permanent, and people began building quadrangular houses. Social systems and rules for cooperation developed.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did people begin to worship nature and deities for good crops?
questions.answer: People depended on agriculture for food and survival. They believed that pleasing nature and deities would ensure good rainfall, fertile soil, and protection from pests, leading to better harvests.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why were craftsmen paid in foodgrains or articles instead of coins?
questions.answer: Coins were not in use during the New Stone Age. The economy was based on barter, so craftsmen received payment in the form of foodgrains, pots, or other useful articles they needed.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did the idea of extended family become important in village-settlements?
questions.answer: People in the village-settlement were closely related and lived near each other. They shared resources, followed common rules, and supported one another, making the entire settlement function like an extended family.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the life of people in a New Stone Age village-settlement.
questions.answer: People lived in close-knit village-settlements where they practiced agriculture and animal husbandry. They built houses of wattle and daub, often close together. Surplus food allowed some to develop special skills like pottery and tool-making. They exchanged goods through the barter system. Rules were made for sharing water and fields, and chiefs were chosen to maintain order and protect the village. Dead were buried with articles, showing belief in life after death. The settlement grew into a permanent community based on cooperation and kinship.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain the importance of domesticated animals in early settled life with examples.
questions.answer: Domesticated animals were very useful in early settled life. Dogs helped in hunting and guarding. Goats and sheep provided milk, meat, and wool. Cattle and buffalo were used to pull ploughs and carry heavy loads. Animals also gave dung for fuel and plaster. Their domestication made farming easier and life more secure. This marked the beginning of animal husbandry, which supported the growth of permanent villages.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Animal husbandry
questions.answer: Animal husbandry is the process of taming, keeping, and breeding animals for human use such as for milk, meat, work, or wool.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Barter system
questions.answer: The barter system is a method of exchange where goods or services are directly traded for other goods or services without using money.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did agriculture lead to the development of village administration?
questions.answer: Agriculture led to surplus food, which allowed people to stay in one place permanently. As villages grew, there was a need to manage shared resources like water, fields, and storage. People began to make rules for fair use and protection. Those who enforced these rules became chiefs, responsible for order and safety. This marked the beginning of village administration and leadership.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What were the essential things that gained importance in village-settlements due to agriculture?
questions.answer: With agriculture, sharing of agricultural tasks and water resources became essential for fair use. The security of the village-settlement gained importance to protect crops, cattle, and stored food from wild animals and outsiders. People built walls and moats for protection. They also developed rules for cooperation and chose leaders to maintain peace. These factors led to a stable, organized community life based on mutual help.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe how the potter’s wheel improved pottery making.
questions.answer: The potter’s wheel allowed potters to shape pots more quickly and uniformly. It enabled mass production of symmetrical pots with beautiful designs. This led to increased production and trade of pottery.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Explain why trade and transport led to the rise of cities.
questions.answer: As trade expanded, people engaged in different occupations came together in one place. This led to the growth of settlements into cities. Centres of large-scale production and record-keeping also developed in these cities.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What is the Chalcolithic Age? Give an example of evidence found at such sites.
questions.answer: The Chalcolithic Age is the period when both copper and stone tools were used. Evidence includes copper objects found alongside stone tools at ancient sites.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did the invention of the wheel impact transport in ancient times?
questions.answer: The wheel was first used by potters and later adapted for carts and chariots. This made transport of goods faster and easier over long distances, boosting trade.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why is the period of copper tools not called the 'Copper Age' in regions where copper was rare?
questions.answer: In regions where copper was rare, people continued to use stone tools even though they knew copper. Copper objects were found only in small numbers, so these sites are called Chalcolithic, not Copper Age.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did the Harappan civilization develop a script?
questions.answer: The Harappan civilization developed a script to keep permanent records of expanding trade and growing production, which became necessary as urban centres grew.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why is bronze harder than copper?
questions.answer: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin; adding tin to copper makes it sufficiently hard for making tools and weapons, whereas pure copper is too soft.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the social organization in ancient cities as discussed in the chapter.
questions.answer: In ancient cities, social organization became more elaborate due to rise in trade. Chiefs of temples became administrators, and later the roles of temple head and king were combined in one person. This system had roots in the faith systems of village settlements from the New Stone Age. Festivals and social life continued to be based on agricultural faiths. Grand temples were built, and their chiefs gained importance. This marked the beginning of ancient urban civilizations.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain the sequence of events that led from the use of metals to the development of script in ancient times.
questions.answer: The use of metals began with gold, followed by copper and iron, leading to better tools and increased production. This growth in production and trade required efficient transport, which led to the invention of the wheel. As trade expanded, people from different occupations gathered, forming cities. To manage records of trade and production, signs and symbols were used, which gradually evolved into scripts. Each culture developed its own script for record-keeping, such as hieroglyphs in Egypt.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Chalcolithic Age
questions.answer: The Chalcolithic Age is the period when both copper and stone tools were used by humans.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Three Age System
questions.answer: The Three Age System is a method of classifying ancient objects into Stone Age, Copper Age, and Iron Age based on the materials used for tools.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did the discovery of copper lead to social changes in ancient settlements?
questions.answer: The discovery of copper led to the Copper Age, where stronger tools could be made. This improved agriculture and craftsmanship. Skilled craftsmen began to live close to each other in villages, forming industrial areas. As production increased, trade expanded, requiring better transport and record-keeping. These changes brought people together, leading to the rise of cities and complex social organization.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the role of the Rosetta Stone in the decipherment of Egyptian hieroglyphs.
questions.answer: The Rosetta Stone, discovered in 1799, contains the same text in three scripts: hieroglyphs, Demotic, and Greek. Scholars used the known Greek script to understand the Demotic, and then the hieroglyphs. Jean Francois Champollion used foreign names in the text to build a chart of hieroglyphic letters. This enabled him to read the entire inscription. Thus, the Rosetta Stone became the key to unlocking ancient Egyptian language and history.

questions.text: What is a Balag?
questions.answer: A Balag is a stringed musical instrument made of gold, used in ancient Mesopotamia.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe how ancient Egyptians used the flood water of the Nile.
questions.answer: Ancient Egyptians built embankments to store the flood water of the Nile. After the water settled, they used the moist soil for agriculture. This made the land very fertile for growing crops.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: What are two special features of Harappan city planning?
questions.answer: Harappan cities had well-planned layouts with houses built in blocks formed by parallel roads crossing at right angles. They also had a covered drainage system and separate areas for administrators and common people.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Mention any two sports or games played in ancient civilizations.
questions.answer: Wrestling and hunting were important sports in ancient civilizations. Games like Senat, played with a board and gamesmen, were also popular.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did early civilizations develop in river valleys?
questions.answer: Early civilizations developed in river valleys because of fertile soil and constant water supply, which were essential for agriculture. Rivers also supported trade, transport, and daily life needs.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why is the Harappan Civilization called 'Protohistoric'?
questions.answer: The Harappan Civilization is called Protohistoric because although they had a developed script, scholars have not been able to decipher it. Hence, we rely on archaeological findings rather than written records to understand their history.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why did humans in the New Stone Age process food before eating?
questions.answer: Humans processed food by roasting or cooking to make it digestible and safe to eat, unlike animals who eat food in its natural form. This processing was part of their cultural development.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why were Harappan towns divided into two to four parts?
questions.answer: Harappan towns were divided into separate parts for better organization, such as separating the administrative area from the residential area of common people. Each part had its own wells and facilities.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Describe the characteristics of early civilizations.
questions.answer: Early civilizations had permanent agricultural settlements near rivers. They used copper and bronze, had developed technology and craft specialization. They managed water through irrigation systems and produced surplus food. They developed writing, engaged in long-distance trade, and used wheeled vehicles and boats. Cities were planned with walls, paved roads, and separate zones. They had advanced architecture, sculpture, and progress in science like mathematics and medicine.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Write about the Harappan Civilization’s town planning and daily life.
questions.answer: Harappan cities showed excellent town planning with grid-like layouts, houses made of baked bricks, and covered drainage systems. Homes had bathrooms and latrines. Public and private wells were carefully built. People wore cotton and wool, used bronze tools, and played games like Senat. They traded with Mesopotamia and worshipped deities like Pashupati and a Mother Goddess. Artifacts show their skill in pottery, bead-making, and sculpture.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Culture
questions.answer: Culture is the way of life founded on knowledge, arts, skills, and traditions passed from one generation to the next.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Riverine Civilization
questions.answer: A Riverine Civilization is an ancient civilization that developed in a river valley, depending on the river for water, agriculture, transport, and trade.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: How did the rise of ancient civilizations lead to the development of arts and skills?
questions.answer: With the rise of ancient civilizations, people began to produce surplus food, which allowed some to specialize in crafts like pottery, metalwork, and weaving. They developed new skills to meet their needs and used available natural materials. Over generations, these skills and artistic traditions were passed down, enriching culture. This continuous exchange of ideas led to progress in arts, music, dance, and technology. Thus, civilization laid the foundation for cultural growth.

questions.subject: EVS Part 2
questions.text: Why is the Indus Valley Civilization also called the Harappan Civilization?
questions.answer: The Indus Valley Civilization is called the Harappan Civilization because the first site of this civilization to be discovered was Harappa, in 1921-22. Since it was found there first, the civilization was named after the site. Later, other sites like Mohen-jo-daro, Lothal, and Kalibangan were found. But the name Harappan remained as it was the type-site. Hence, both names refer to the same ancient civilization.
