questions.answer: The cuckoo's behaviour changes according to the season. In spring (April-May), it is active and sings to attract mates. In early summer (June), it varies its call. In mid-summer (July-August), it prepares to migrate. This shows how birds adapt to weather and breeding cycles.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why the poem mentions specific months for the cuckoo's actions.
questions.answer: The poem mentions specific months to show the cuckoo's annual cycle. Each action matches the season: singing in spring, migrating in summer. This helps children learn about bird behaviour and the months of the year in a rhythmic way.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Describe the sequence of events in the story from threshing the wheat to eating the bread.
questions.answer: First, the Little Red Hen threshed the wheat and asked for help to grind it, but no one helped. She ground the wheat herself. Then she asked for help to bake the bread into flour, and again no one helped, so she baked it herself. Finally, when the bread was ready, the duck, cat, and dog wanted to eat it, but she refused and ate it with her chicks.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why the Little Red Hen did not share the bread with the duck, cat, and dog.
questions.answer: The Little Red Hen did not share the bread because the duck, cat, and dog refused to help her at every stage—grinding, baking, and preparing. Since they did not contribute to the work, she felt it was fair that only those who helped, like her chicks, should enjoy the bread.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: What would have happened if the duck, cat, and dog had helped the Little Red Hen?
questions.answer: If the duck, cat, and dog had helped, the work would have been easier and faster for the Little Red Hen. They would have shared in the effort and, according to the story's lesson, would have deserved to eat the bread too. This would have changed the ending to a more cooperative and joyful one.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: How does the story show the value of hard work?
questions.answer: The story shows that the Little Red Hen worked hard alone to turn wheat into bread, while others refused to help. In the end, she enjoyed the reward of her labor, teaching that hard work leads to personal satisfaction and rightful ownership of the results.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Give reason for your answer in 3-4 sentences.
questions.text: Why did the Little Red Hen say 'I will' each time when asked who would do the work?
questions.answer: The Little Red Hen said 'I will' each time because no one else volunteered to help. She was determined to complete the task herself rather than wait for others who kept refusing. Her repeated 'I will' shows her sense of responsibility and perseverance. Despite being alone, she chose to act instead of complain or give up.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Give reason for your answer in 3-4 sentences.
questions.text: Give reason why the duck, cat, and dog were not allowed to eat the bread.
questions.answer: The duck, cat, and dog were not allowed to eat the bread because they refused to help the Little Red Hen at any stage of making it. They said 'Not I' when asked to grind, bake, or prepare the wheat. Since they did not contribute any effort, the Little Red Hen felt it was unfair for them to enjoy the result. She believed only those who work should enjoy the rewards.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Give reason for your answer in 3-4 sentences.
questions.text: Explain why the story is titled 'The Little Red Hen'.
questions.answer: The story is titled 'The Little Red Hen' because the main character is a small, red-colored hen who does all the work. Her color and size make her distinct and memorable. The title focuses attention on her actions and personality. Naming the story after her highlights her role as the hardworking protagonist.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Summarize the story 'The Little Red Hen' in your own words.
questions.answer: The Little Red Hen found some wheat and decided to make bread. She asked the duck, cat, and dog to help her grind the wheat, but they all said 'Not I'. She ground it herself. Then she asked for help to make flour and bake the bread, but again, no one helped. She did all the work alone. When the bread was ready, the duck, cat, and dog wanted to eat it, but she refused and said she would eat it herself. She called her chicks, and they all enjoyed the lovely loaf together. The story teaches that hard work brings its own reward and that one should not expect to benefit without contributing.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Describe the character of the Little Red Hen based on her actions in the story.
questions.answer: The Little Red Hen is hardworking, responsible, and self-reliant. She does not wait for others to help but takes initiative to complete her tasks. Even when refused help, she does not give up or complain. She is fair and believes that rewards should go to those who work. She is also caring, as she shares the bread with her chicks. Her determination and honesty make her a role model for doing one's duty sincerely.

questions.text: Explain how the story teaches the importance of helping others.
questions.answer: The story shows that when everyone helps, the work becomes easier and faster for all. The Little Red Hen had to do all the work alone because others refused to help, which made her tired and burdened. If the duck, cat, and dog had helped, they would have shared the effort and also enjoyed the bread together. Helping others builds teamwork and friendship. The story teaches that refusing to help leads to missing out on the rewards of collective effort.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why the Little Red Hen felt it was fair to eat the bread herself.
questions.answer: The Little Red Hen felt it was fair because she was the only one who worked from the beginning to the end. She ground the wheat, made the flour, and baked the bread without any help. The others refused to contribute at any stage, so they had no right to enjoy the result. She believed in the principle that effort should be rewarded. Eating the bread herself was her just reward for hard work and patience.

questions.answer: Aman fell ill and did not attend college for three days. His best friend Ronak, who is rich, offered to take him home in his car and wished him to get well soon. True friendship means being present during tough times, helping without hesitation, and expressing kindness and concern for the friend’s well-being.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Describe the qualities of a true friend using examples from the conversation.
questions.answer: A true friend is someone who stands by you in difficult times, shows care, and helps without being asked. A true friend also visits when you are unwell, as this brings comfort and hope. On the other hand, Aman is not a true friend because he did not even ask about Munna when he fell ill. True friendship involves empathy, responsibility, and kindness.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: How can small acts of kindness strengthen friendship? Explain with reference to the text.
questions.answer: Small acts of kindness, like visiting a sick friend or helping with their work, can greatly strengthen friendship. In the text, Munna felt much better just because someone came to see him when he was ill. This small act of care made him feel valued and loved. Similarly, Ronak’s act of working in the shop to do Munna’s job, without being asked, shows deep loyalty and concern. Such actions build trust and show that you are willing to sacrifice for your friend. These small gestures create emotional bonds and make friendships last longer. They remind us that friendship is not just about fun times, but also about being there when it matters most.

questions.text: What lesson does the story 'Friendly Plans' teach students?
questions.answer: The story teaches that true friendship involves helping others without expecting anything in return. It shows that friends should support each other during difficult times. It also highlights the importance of kindness, empathy, and selflessness in relationships.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: How did Munna respond after he felt better?
questions.answer: After feeling better, Munna said he would go back to work the next day. He also thanked Ronak for his money and acknowledged Aman's help. His response shows gratitude and a sense of responsibility.

questions.text: Why did Ronak say that Aman showed him what true friendship is?

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why is the story titled 'Friendly Plans'?
questions.answer: The story is titled 'Friendly Plans' because it shows how friends plan to help each other—Aman planned to do Munna's work so he could rest. questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the character of Aman based on his actions in the story.
questions.answer: Aman is a kind, helpful, and selfless friend. When Munna fell ill, Aman immediately offered to do his work so Munna could rest and recover. He did not wait to be asked or expect anything in return. His words, 'Don't worry, I'll do your work for you,' show empathy and concern. Aman's actions reflect true friendship—putting a friend's well-being before his own convenience. He is responsible, caring, and reliable. Through his behavior, Aman teaches us the value of compassion and support in relationships. He serves as a role model for how friends should treat one another.

questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Narrate the story 'Friendly Plans' in your own words.
questions.answer: Munna was feeling unwell and could not work. His friend Aman saw this and kindly offered to do Munna's work so he could go home and rest. Munna then thanked Ronak and said that Aman had shown him what true friendship really means. The story highlights kindness, support, and the importance of helping friends in need.

questions.text: What are the three degrees of comparison? Give one example.
questions.answer: The three degrees of comparison are positive, comparative, and superlative. For example: tall (positive), taller (comparative), tallest (superlative).

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Give reason for your answer in 3-4 sentences.
questions.text: Why is 'best' the superlative form of 'good'?
questions.answer: Because 'best' expresses the highest degree of quality among three or more things. It is used when something is better than all others in a group. For example, 'This is the best book I have read.' It shows excellence compared to others.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Give reason for your answer in 3-4 sentences.
questions.text: Why do we use 'doesn’t' with 'she'?
questions.answer: We use 'doesn’t' with 'she' because it is a third person singular subject. In English, for present simple negative, we use 'does not' or 'doesn’t' with he, she, it. Using 'don’t' would be grammatically incorrect here.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Give reason for your answer in 3-4 sentences.
questions.text: Why is 'worse' the comparative form of 'bad'?
questions.answer: Because 'worse' shows a lower quality when comparing two things. It is used to say that one thing is less good than another. For example, 'This weather is worse than yesterday.’ It compares two states.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain the difference between comparative and superlative degrees with examples.
questions.answer: Comparative degree is used to compare two things or people, showing which has more or less of a quality. For example, 'She is taller than her brother.' Superlative degree is used to compare three or more things, showing the highest or lowest degree. For example, 'She is the tallest girl in the class.' We add -er or use 'more' for comparative, and -est or 'most' for superlative.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain how to make negative sentences in present simple tense.
questions.answer: To make a negative sentence in present simple, we use 'do not' or 'does not' (don’t/doesn’t) before the base verb. For I, you, we, they, we use 'do not'. For he, she, it, we use 'does not'. For example: I do not like tea. She does not eat meat. We do not watch TV. It does not bark.

questions.text: Describe the journey of the trains as described in the poem.
questions.answer: The trains run over mountains, plains, and rivers. They carry passengers, mail, and precious loads. They run without fail through day and night, dusk and dawn.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why does the poet say trains run 'without fail'?
questions.answer: The poet says trains run 'without fail' to show their reliability and consistency. They operate regularly in all conditions—day or night, fair weather or foul. This highlights their importance in transportation.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: What imagery is used in the poem to show the movement of trains?
questions.answer: The poem uses imagery of trains moving over natural landscapes like mountains, plains, and rivers. It also mentions time of day—day, darkness, dusk, and dawn—to show continuous movement. The image of 'thousands of freight cars rushing' adds to the sense of steady, powerful motion.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: What is the main idea of the poem 'Over the mountains'?
questions.answer: The main idea is that trains are reliable and hardworking, transporting people, mail, and valuable goods across all kinds of terrain and at all times. The poem praises their constant service and contribution to society.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why does the poem mention 'through day and darkness'?
questions.answer: The poem mentions 'through day and darkness' to emphasize that trains operate continuously, regardless of time. This shows their dedication and importance in daily life, as they never stop serving people and transporting goods.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why are freight cars important in the poem?
questions.answer: Freight cars are important because they carry precious loads, showing that trains transport not just people but also valuable goods. This highlights the broader role of trains in trade and daily life.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why does the poet repeat 'Over the mountains, Over the plains, Over the rivers'?
questions.answer: The poet repeats these lines to create rhythm and emphasize the wide reach of trains. It shows that trains travel across diverse landscapes, symbolizing their extensive and uninterrupted service.

questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Imagine you are a train driver. Describe your journey as you pass through mountains, plains, and rivers. Mention what you see, what you carry, and how you feel.
questions.answer: I am a train driver, and every day I feel proud as I steer my train through tall mountains, wide plains, and flowing rivers. I carry passengers going to work, children to school, and mail with important letters. My freight cars are full of goods like food, clothes, and toys. As the sun rises, I see birds flying over the fields, and at dusk, the sky turns orange. I feel happy knowing I am helping people and connecting places. Even in the dark, my lights shine bright, and I move forward without fail. Being a train driver is a big responsibility, but I love it because I get to see beautiful views and be part of so many journeys.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Write a summary of the poem 'Over the mountains' in your own words.
questions.answer: The poem 'Over the mountains' by James S. Tippett describes how trains run continuously over mountains, plains, and rivers. They carry passengers, mail, and precious goods without stopping, whether it is day or night, dusk or dawn. The poem highlights the reliability, strength, and importance of trains in our lives. It praises their hard work and constant service, showing how they connect people and places. The repeated lines create a rhythmic feel, like the steady movement of a train. Overall, the poem is a tribute to the dedication and power of trains.

questions.subject: English

questions.answer: The poem repeats the lines 'Over the mountains, Over the plains, Over the rivers' to create a musical rhythm. questions.subject: English
questions.text: What lesson does the story of the little babul tree teach us?
questions.answer: The story teaches us to be happy with what we have and not to keep wishing for things that may not suit us. It shows that our own qualities, even if they seem small or unattractive, can be the best for us in the long run.

questions.text: How did the wind affect the babul tree's glass leaves?

questions.text: Why do goats not like the babul tree?

questions.text: Imagine you are the little babul tree. Write about your feelings when you wished for big leaves, then lost them to the goat, and finally how you felt when you got your own leaves and thorns back.
questions.answer: I was sad and jealous seeing the mango trees with their big green leaves. I wished for big leaves too, and when I got them, I felt happy for a moment. But my happiness did not last long when a goat came and ate all my big leaves. I felt sad and foolish. Then I wished for gold leaves, thinking they would be safe, but a thief stole them. I felt angry and helpless. When I got glass leaves, I loved how they shone in the sun, but the wind broke them and I felt heartbroken. Finally, when I got my own small leaves and sharp thorns back, I felt peaceful and safe. I realized that being myself was the best thing. I was never so happy as I was then, standing strong in the grove with my true leaves and thorns.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Summarize the story of the little babul tree in your own words, highlighting the wishes, the problems faced, and the final realization.
questions.answer: The little babul tree in a mango grove was unhappy because it had small leaves and thorns while other trees had big leaves. It wished for big leaves, which it got, but a goat ate them. Then it wished for gold leaves to avoid goats, but a thief stole them. Next, it wished for glass leaves to avoid thieves, but the wind broke them. Each wish brought a new problem. Finally, it wished for its own thorns and small leaves back. When it got them, it realized that its natural form was safest—goats didn’t eat the thorns, thieves didn’t want them, and the wind didn’t harm them. The tree learned to be happy with what it had and understood that self-acceptance brings true happiness.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why the babul tree was never truly happy with the leaves it wished for, even though it got what it wanted.

In each case, the wish was fulfilled, but the outcome was unhappy because the leaves were not suited to its environment or nature. The tree failed to consider that its own small leaves and thorns were naturally protected. True happiness came only when it accepted itself and stopped chasing what others had or what seemed valuable.

questions.text: Why do children like flowers but not thorns?
questions.answer: Children like flowers because they are beautiful, colorful, and soft to touch. They do not like thorns because thorns are sharp and can hurt or prick the skin. Flowers bring joy, while thorns cause pain.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why is 'a bunch of keys' a correct phrase but 'a bundle of keys' is not commonly used?
questions.answer: Keys are usually held together on a ring, not tied in a bundle, so 'a bunch of keys' is the natural phrase. 'Bundle' implies tying with a string or cloth, which is not how keys are typically grouped. Usage follows real-life practice.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why is 'a list of names' used during prize distribution?
questions.answer: A list of names is used because it organizes names in a clear, readable order, one below the other. It helps the teacher or announcer to call each name easily without confusion. It ensures no name is missed and the process is fair.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph of 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the different 'Lots of Things' phrases from the chapter and their uses in daily life.
questions.answer: The chapter 'Lots of Things' teaches us phrases like bundle, bunch, row, chain, and list to describe grouped items. A bundle of sticks or clothes is tied for carrying. A bunch of flowers or grapes is tied or grows together. A row of children stands in a line during assembly. A chain of flowers is linked for decoration. A list of names is written for records or announcements. These phrases help us speak clearly and correctly in English.

questions.subject: English

questions.text: Imagine you are going to a market. Write about the things you see using phrases from the chapter.
questions.answer: At the market, I saw a bunch of fresh grapes hanging from the stall. Nearby, a bundle of coriander was tied with a string for freshness. A row of children stood with their mothers, waiting for their turn. A lady wore a chain of jasmine flowers in her hair. The shopkeeper had a list of prices written on a board. These phrases helped me describe what I saw neatly.

questions.answer: These phrases give specific meanings to how things are grouped. 'Bundle' shows things tied for carrying, like sticks. 'Bunch' shows things tied or growing together, like flowers or grapes. 'Row' shows things in a straight line, like children. 'Chain' shows things linked one after another, like flowers in a garland. 'List' shows things written in order, like names. Using the right word makes our speech clear and correct.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why is it important to learn fixed phrases like 'a bunch of flowers' instead of making our own?
questions.answer: Learning fixed phrases helps us speak English naturally and correctly. If we say 'a group of flowers', it may be understood but sounds awkward. Native speakers use 'a bunch of flowers' as a set expression. Using the right collocation makes our speech fluent and avoids mistakes. It also helps in writing and understanding stories or instructions better.

questions.text: Why is hygiene important for good health? Give two reasons.
questions.answer: Hygiene helps remove germs that can cause illness. Keeping the body clean prevents infections and promotes overall well-being.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Describe what happens when we cough and why it can spread germs.
questions.answer: When we cough, air from our lungs rushes out at about 9 km/h. This fast-moving air can carry tiny droplets containing germs to nearby people or surfaces.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: How does the body heal a broken bone?
questions.answer: After a fracture, the body starts producing new bone cells to bridge the break. Over time, the bone grows back and becomes strong again, especially when kept immobile with a plaster-cast.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why do doctors use a plaster-cast for a broken bone?
questions.answer: Doctors use a plaster-cast to keep the broken bone pieces in the correct position. It prevents movement that could disrupt healing. The cast supports the bone as it grows back naturally. This ensures proper and timely recovery.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why is it said that 'Health is wealth'?
questions.answer: Good health allows a person to work, study, and enjoy life fully. Without health, even riches cannot bring happiness or productivity. Thus, being healthy is the truest form of wealth.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why should we cover our mouth when we cough?
questions.answer: Covering the mouth stops germs from spreading into the air. It protects others from inhaling infected droplets. This simple act helps prevent diseases like cold and flu. It shows care for public health.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Write a short paragraph on 'How to Keep Your Body Healthy'.
questions.answer: To keep the body healthy, we should eat nutritious food like fruits, vegetables, and grains. Regular exercise such as walking, running, or playing sports keeps muscles and bones strong. Drinking enough water and getting proper sleep are also essential. We must keep our body clean by bathing daily and washing hands. Avoiding junk food and harmful habits like smoking is important. Regular check-ups help detect problems early. A healthy body supports a sound mind, leading to a happy and active life.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the journey of a bone from baby to adult, including what happens when it breaks.
questions.answer: A baby is born with about 300 soft bones made of cartilage and bone. As the child grows, many of these bones fuse together, especially in the skull and spine. By adulthood, the number reduces to 206 stronger bones. If a bone breaks, the body immediately starts healing by forming a clot and then new bone tissue. Doctors often use a plaster-cast to keep the bone stable during healing. Over weeks or months, the bone regrows and becomes strong again. This shows the amazing ability of the body to repair itself.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain how the body repairs a broken bone.
questions.answer: When a bone breaks, blood vessels rupture and form a clot at the site. This clot is replaced by soft callus made of collagen and cartilage. Over time, osteoblasts build new bone tissue to replace the callus. The bone gradually becomes hard and strong again. This process can take several weeks and is helped by rest and proper alignment, often with a plaster-cast.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why maintaining personal hygiene is important for health.
questions.answer: Personal hygiene removes dirt, sweat, and germs from the body surface. Washing hands prevents the spread of infections to others and oneself. Bathing regularly keeps the skin healthy and prevents skin diseases. Clean clothes and teeth avoid bad odors and dental problems. Good hygiene habits build confidence and contribute to overall physical and mental well-being.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: What lesson does the story of Alyonushka teach about responsibility and kindness?

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why did Alyonushka thank each character after they helped her?

questions.subject: English

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why is Alyonushka considered brave in the story?
questions.answer: Alyonushka is considered brave because she went alone to rescue her baby brother despite being scared. She faced the witch Baba Yaga and ran through fields and woods to save Ivanushka, showing courage and love.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Describe Alyonushka’s journey to find her brother, including the characters she met and how they helped her.
questions.answer: Alyonushka’s journey began when she realized her baby brother Ivanushka was taken by geese. She ran after them and met the oven, which asked her to eat wheat bread before showing the way. She obeyed and was guided onward. Next, she met the apple tree, which asked for a wild apple; after eating it, the tree showed her the path. Then she reached the milk river, which asked for milk; she drank it and was shown the way. The river later hid her and her brother from the geese. She also met the apple tree again, which hid them in its branches. Finally, she reached Baba Yaga’s hut, rescued her brother, and ran home with help from the natural friends who concealed them from the geese.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Write a character sketch of Alyonushka based on her actions in the story.
questions.answer: Alyonushka is a loving and responsible elder sister who deeply cares for her baby brother Ivanushka. Though she initially forgets her duty and plays with friends, she quickly realizes her mistake and feels remorse. She shows determination by running after the geese without hesitation. Alyonushka is polite and respectful—she apologizes to the oven, apple tree, and milk river when she initially refuses their food, then accepts their help. She is brave, facing the witch Baba Yaga to save her brother. Her honesty, kindness, and perseverance make her a role model for young readers.

questions.text: Explain how Alyonushka’s attitude changed from the beginning to the end of the story.
questions.answer: At the beginning, Alyonushka was careless and forgot her duty to look after her baby brother as she went to play with friends. When she realized Ivanushka was missing, she felt guilty and upset, sobbing and weeping. Then she became determined and took responsibility, deciding to bring him back no matter what. During her journey, she learned to be polite and humble, accepting help from nature by eating what was offered. By the end, she was brave, focused, and successful in rescuing her brother, showing growth in maturity and courage.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain the role of nature (oven, apple tree, milk river) in helping Alyonushka on her journey.
questions.answer: Nature in the story acts as a kind and helpful guide to Alyonushka. The oven, apple tree, and milk river each ask her to partake of their gift—wheat bread, wild apple, and milk—before showing her the way. This teaches her humility and gratitude. Later, they actively protect her by hiding her and her brother from the geese. Their help shows that nature responds to kindness and respect. Through them, Alyonushka learns that cooperation and politeness can overcome difficulties.

questions.answer: The story teaches that one should focus on one task at a time, like Alyonushka focusing on protecting her brother. It shows that doing things carefully and step by step leads to safety and success. The title reminds us not to rush or multitask when responsibility is involved. Alyonushka’s attention to her duty helped her make the right decisions.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Give reason for your answer in 3-4 sentences.
questions.text: Why were the geese unable to find the children?
questions.answer: The geese could not find the children because they were hidden inside the oven, which the geese did not think to check. The oven provided a concealed space that looked ordinary from outside. Alyonushka’s quick thinking led her to a safe place the geese overlooked. Thus, the children remained safe due to clever hiding.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Imagine you are Alyonushka. Describe how you felt when the geese were chasing you and how you felt after hiding in the oven.
questions.answer: When the geese started chasing me, I felt very scared and my heart beat fast. I was worried not just for myself but more for my baby brother, whom I had to protect. I ran as fast as I could, looking for a safe place. When I saw the oven, I felt a little hope and quickly asked it to hide us. Inside the oven, it was dark and quiet, but I felt safe and relieved. I held my brother close and waited until I knew the geese had gone. When I came out, I felt happy and brave, and I ran home with my brother, thankful for the oven’s help.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Write a short summary of the story 'One Thing at a Time' in your own words.
questions.answer: Alyonushka was asked by her mother to look after her baby brother while she went out to play. While playing, she saw geese flying toward them and got scared. She ran with her brother to escape, and the geese chased them. She reached an oven and asked it to hide them. The oven opened and hid both children inside. The geese could not find them and flew away. After some time, Alyonushka came out with her brother and ran home. Soon, their parents also came home and were happy to see them safe. The story teaches us to be responsible and calm in danger.

questions.text: Explain how the oven helped Alyonushka and her brother in the story.
questions.answer: The oven helped Alyonushka and her brother by providing a safe hiding place when they were being chased by the geese. When Alyonushka politely asked the oven to hide them, it opened and allowed them to go inside. Inside the oven, they were completely hidden from view, so the geese could not find them. The oven kept them safe until the danger passed. This shows how quick thinking and help from unexpected places can save us in difficult times.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why it was important for Alyonushka to look after her brother.
questions.answer: It was important for Alyonushka to look after her brother because her mother had trusted her with this responsibility. Her brother was young and could not protect himself from dangers like the geese. By taking care of him, Alyonushka showed love, maturity, and duty. If she had not watched him, he might have been harmed or lost. Her care and attention kept him safe and brought peace to her family.

questions.answer: First, introduce yourself by saying hello and sharing your name, standard, and that you are looking for a pen-friend. questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why is it important to write letters in English when having a pen-friend?
questions.answer: It is important to write letters in English because the chapter specifies that we have to write letters in English to our pen-friends. This helps in practicing the language and ensures both friends can understand each other.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: What are some examples of favourite things you can discuss with a pen-friend?
questions.answer: You can discuss your favourite colour, game, subject, teacher, book, movie, TV programme, and dish with your pen-friend. These topics help you get to know each other better.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: How should you behave when making a pen-friend to keep the friendship healthy?
questions.answer: You should be polite, listen to your pen-friend, avoid starting quarrels, and be the last one to argue. Being kind and respectful helps maintain a good friendship.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why should we not start a quarrel with our pen-friend?
questions.answer: We should not start a quarrel with our pen-friend because it can hurt their feelings and damage the friendship. Since pen-friends communicate through letters, misunderstandings can last longer. Being kind helps maintain a long-lasting and joyful friendship.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why is it important to exchange information like birthday and favourite things with a pen-friend?
questions.answer: Exchanging information helps pen-friends get to know each other better and builds trust. Sharing personal details like birthday and favourites makes the friendship more meaningful and fun. It also gives more topics to write about in letters.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why do we look for pen-friends in Std V or Std VI?
questions.answer: We look for pen-friends in Std V or Std VI because students in these standards are of similar age and can relate to each other's experiences. This makes it easier to share thoughts and understand each other. It also ensures they are studying at a comparable level.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Imagine you have made a new pen-friend. Write a paragraph describing your first letter to them.
questions.answer: In my first letter, I would start with a greeting like 'Hello' or 'Hi'. I would then introduce myself by sharing my name, that I am in the fifth standard, and where I live. I would mention my hobbies, such as reading books and playing cricket, and ask about theirs. I would talk about my favourite subject, which is English, and why I like it. I would end the letter by saying I am excited to be their pen-friend and hope to hear from them soon, signing off with 'Your friend'.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Describe the qualities of a good pen-friend based on the chapter.
questions.answer: A good pen-friend is someone who writes letters regularly and in English. They are polite, kind, and respectful in their communication. They share information about themselves honestly and show interest in their friend's life. A good pen-friend avoids starting quarrels and is patient and understanding. They enjoy exchanging thoughts about favourite things like books, games, and school. Such a friendship brings joy and helps improve writing skills.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why writing letters to pen-friends helps in learning English.
questions.answer: Writing letters to pen-friends helps in learning English because it gives regular practice in writing sentences and using new words. When we write about our favourite things, we learn to describe them in English. Reading replies from our pen-friend improves our understanding of the language. It also helps us learn correct spelling and grammar through real use. Over time, this builds confidence in writing and speaking English.

questions.text: Describe how a fish moves in water.
questions.answer: A fish moves in water by swinging its tail from side to side. Its fins help it to balance, steer, and stop. The streamlined shape of its body reduces resistance in water.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain how a bird flies.
questions.answer: A bird flaps its wings to push air downwards, which lifts its body up. The shape of its wings helps it to glide and change direction. Birds also use their tail to balance while flying.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: How does a snake move without legs?
questions.answer: A snake moves by contracting and relaxing its muscles in waves. It pushes against the ground with its scales to move forward. This movement is called crawling.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why do fish have fins?
questions.answer: Fish have fins to help them swim, balance, change direction, and stop in water. Without fins, they would not be able to move properly or survive in their aquatic habitat.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why can birds fly but humans cannot?
questions.answer: Birds have lightweight bones, strong wing muscles, and feathers that help them lift and stay in the air. Humans lack these adaptations and are too heavy to fly with arm movements alone.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why does a snake move in a zigzag pattern?
questions.answer: A snake moves in a zigzag pattern to push against the ground and move forward efficiently. This motion helps it gain grip and propel its body without legs.

questions.answer: Different creatures move in different ways according to their body structure and habitat. Fish swim in water using their fins and tail. Birds fly in the air by flapping their wings. Snakes crawl on land by moving their bodies in curves. Kangaroos hop on their strong hind legs. Each movement helps them survive in their environment.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Explain why movement is important for animals. Give examples.
questions.answer: Movement is important for animals to find food, escape from enemies, find shelter, and reproduce. For example, a deer runs to escape a tiger, a bird flies to search for worms, and a fish swims to catch small plants. Without movement, animals cannot survive in nature.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain how a fish is adapted for swimming.
questions.answer: A fish has a streamlined body that reduces resistance in water. Its fins help in balancing, steering, and stopping. The tail moves from side to side to push the fish forward. Gills help it breathe underwater. These adaptations make swimming easy and efficient.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain how a bird’s body helps it to fly.
questions.answer: Birds have hollow bones that make their body light. Their wings are shaped to lift the body when flapped. Strong muscles move the wings up and down. Feathers reduce air resistance and help in steering. The tail helps to balance and change direction during flight.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: What should you include in the body of a letter to your friend about a movie you watched?
questions.answer: In the body, you should write the name of the movie, when and where you watched it, what you liked or disliked about it, and why you are telling your friend about it. You can also ask if they have seen it or would like to watch it.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why it is important to write the date in a letter.
questions.answer: Writing the date helps the receiver know when the letter was written. It is useful for keeping a record and replying in time. It also makes the letter look complete and proper.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: How can you make your letter sound friendly and warm?
questions.answer: You can make your letter friendly by using kind words, asking about the receiver's well-being, sharing personal news, and closing with warm wishes like 'With love' or 'Your friend'.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Give reason for your answer in 3-4 sentences.
questions.text: Why should we not use 'Dear Sir' in a letter to our close friend?
questions.answer: We should not use 'Dear Sir' in a letter to a close friend because it is too formal and sounds distant. A letter to a friend should be warm and personal. Using 'Dear Sir' might make the friend feel that we are not close or are being unfriendly. It is better to use 'Dear friend' or their name to show affection.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Give reason for your answer in 3-4 sentences.
questions.text: Why is it important to check spelling and punctuation in a letter?
questions.answer: Checking spelling and punctuation makes the letter easy to read and understand. It shows that we have taken care and respect in writing. Mistakes can change the meaning or make the letter look careless. A well-written letter creates a good impression on the receiver.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Give reason for your answer in 3-4 sentences.
questions.text: Why do we leave space between the paragraphs in the body of a letter?
questions.answer: Leaving space between paragraphs makes the letter look neat and organized. It helps the reader to pause and understand each idea clearly. Without spaces, the letter looks crowded and hard to follow. Proper spacing improves the overall presentation.

questions.text: Write a letter to your friend telling them about a funny incident that happened in your class last week.
questions.answer: Your address Date Dear friend, I hope you are doing well. I want to tell you about something funny that happened in our class last week. During the English period, our teacher asked us to read a poem aloud. When it was Rohan’s turn, he started reading very seriously, but suddenly he misread a word and said ‘cat’ instead of ‘cap’. The whole class started laughing, and even the teacher smiled. Rohan laughed at himself too and said, ‘Sorry, I saw a cat in my mind!’ We all laughed for a long time. It made the class very lively. I wish you were there to enjoy it with us. Please write back and tell me if anything funny happened in your class too. Your friend, [Your Name]

questions.text: Write a letter to your cousin inviting them to spend the weekend at your house.
questions.answer: Your address Date Dear cousin, I hope you are fine. I am writing to invite you to come to my house this weekend. My parents have said yes, and we have planned many fun activities. On Saturday, we can go to the park in the morning and play cricket or fly kites. In the afternoon, we will watch a cartoon movie together and eat popcorn. In the evening, we can play board games or draw pictures. On Sunday, after breakfast, we can visit the nearby garden or help my mother in the kitchen. I have saved your favorite chocolate for you. Please come and bring your night suit and toothbrush. I am really excited to spend time with you. Please tell your parents and let me know if you can come. Your loving cousin, [Your Name]

questions.text: Describe how different animals move as mentioned in the poem.
questions.answer: The lion walks on padded paws, the squirrel leaps from limb to limb, and flies crawl straight up a wall. Seals dive and swim, worms wiggle all around, and monkeys swing by their tails. Birds leap, dance, walk, and run, showing a variety of movements in nature.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: How is the fun of boys and girls different from that of animals in the poem?
questions.answer: While animals move in specific ways like walking, leaping, or swimming, boys and girls have much more fun by hopping on the ground. Their fun is described as greater and more varied compared to the animals’ movements. The poem highlights their joyful and active play.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: List the movements of any three animals from the poem.
questions.answer: The lion walks on padded paws. The squirrel leaps from limb to limb. The seal dives and swims in the water. These movements show how each animal adapts to its environment.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why do you think the poet says boys and girls have more fun?
questions.answer: The poet says boys and girls have more fun because they can hop freely on the ground, showing joy and energy. Their activities are playful and not limited to survival movements like animals. This highlights the happiness and freedom in children's play.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why does the worm wiggle all around?
questions.answer: The worm wiggles all around to move through the soil, as it does not have legs. This movement helps it burrow and navigate underground. It is a natural way for worms to travel and find food.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why can seals dive and swim well?
questions.answer: Seals have streamlined bodies and flippers that help them move easily in water. They are adapted to aquatic life, which allows them to dive deep and swim long distances. This helps them catch food and escape predators.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why do birds leap and dance?
questions.answer: Birds leap and dance as part of their natural behavior, often to attract mates or show joy. These movements are seen during courtship or play. It reflects their agility and lively nature.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the movements of animals and children as given in the poem. What message does the poet give about fun and activity?
questions.answer: The poem describes various animals and their unique movements: the lion walks on soft paws, the squirrel jumps between tree limbs, flies crawl up walls, seals dive and swim, worms wiggle, monkeys swing by tails, and birds leap, dance, walk, and run. In contrast, boys and girls enjoy hopping on the ground and are said to have much more fun. The poet conveys that while animals move for survival, children’s play is full of joy, freedom, and energy. The message is that happiness comes from active, playful movement, and children’s fun is special and vibrant.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Imagine you are a squirrel. Describe your day using movements from the poem.
questions.answer: I am a squirrel, and my day begins with leaping from limb to limb in the tall trees. I run along branches, sometimes pausing to sit and wiggle my nose. I jump down to the ground to search for nuts, then quickly scamper back up to safety. I chase my friends, twisting and turning in the air, and sometimes hang upside down by my tail. At sunset, I curl up in my nest, tired but happy from all the jumping and playing. Being a squirrel means moving fast, staying alert, and enjoying every leap and run.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain how the poem shows different ways of living and moving in nature.
questions.answer: The poem shows that each creature moves in a way suited to its body and habitat. The lion walks on padded paws for quiet movement on land, while the squirrel leaps between limbs to stay safe in trees. Flies crawl up walls using tiny hairs, and seals use flippers to dive and swim in water. Worms wiggle through soil, monkeys swing from branches, and birds use wings and legs for varied movement. This diversity shows how life adapts to different environments through unique forms of motion.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why the poet says boys and girls have more fun than animals.
questions.answer: The poet believes boys and girls have more fun because their movements are free, playful, and not driven by survival. While animals move to find food, escape danger, or live, children hop, run, and play just for joy. Their activities are imaginative and full of energy, not limited by instinct. The poet highlights the happiness and creativity in children’s play, which goes beyond basic needs. This makes their fun richer and more varied than the purposeful movements of animals.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why is 'falls' an action word?
questions.answer: 'Falls' is an action word because it shows what rain does — it describes movement or happening. Action words are also called verbs. They tell us about actions or states.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why is 'sky' not an action word?
questions.answer: 'Sky' is not an action word because it names a thing, not an action. It is a noun. Action words show doing, while nouns name people, places, or things.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why do we say 'many lions' and not 'many lion'?
questions.answer: We say 'many lions' because 'many' is used with plural nouns. 'Lion' is singular, so it becomes 'lions' to match 'many'. This follows the rule of number agreement in English.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: I speak, I say, I talk
questions.text: Explain the difference between 'speak', 'say', and 'talk' with one example each.
questions.answer: 'Speak' is used for using language in general, e.g., She speaks English. 'Say' is used to report exact words, e.g., He said, 'Hello.' 'Talk' means to converse informally, e.g., They talked about their holidays.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: I speak, I say, I talk
questions.text: Why is it important to use the right word among speak, say, and talk?
questions.answer: Using the right word makes our meaning clear. 'Speak' focuses on language ability, 'say' on the words uttered, and 'talk' on the conversation. Wrong use can confuse the listener.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: I speak, I say, I talk
questions.text: Give two situations where we use 'express' instead of 'speak' or 'say'.
questions.answer: We use 'express' when showing feelings, like expressing happiness through words. We also use it when sharing ideas, such as expressing an opinion in a meeting.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: I speak, I say, I talk
questions.text: Can 'talk' be used for one-way communication? Explain.
questions.answer: No, 'talk' usually means two-way communication, like a conversation. For one-way, we use 'speak' or 'say', such as in a speech or announcement.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: I speak, I say, I talk
questions.instruction: Give reason for your answer in 3-4 sentences.
questions.text: Why do we say 'I say' when quoting someone’s exact words?
questions.answer: We use 'I say' to show that we are repeating someone’s exact words. It helps the listener know that the words are not our own but are being reported. This makes the communication clear and honest. It is common in storytelling or when sharing news.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: I speak, I say, I talk
questions.instruction: Give reason for your answer in 3-4 sentences.
questions.text: Why is 'talk' not used in formal speeches?
questions.answer: 'Talk' suggests an informal, casual conversation between people. Formal speeches are planned and delivered to an audience, so we use 'speak' instead. Using 'talk' might make the speech seem less serious. Therefore, 'speak' is more appropriate for formal settings.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: I speak, I say, I talk
questions.instruction: Give reason for your answer in 3-4 sentences.
questions.text: Why can we 'express' ideas without speaking?
questions.answer: We can express ideas through writing, art, or signs, not just speech. For example, a painting can express sadness without any words. This shows that expression is broader than speaking. So, 'express' includes non-verbal ways of sharing thoughts.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: I speak, I say, I talk
questions.text: Explain how 'speak', 'say', 'talk', and 'express' are related but used in different contexts.
questions.answer: All four words involve communication using language. 'Speak' is general and refers to using voice in a language. 'Say' focuses on the exact words uttered. 'Talk' means informal conversation between two or more people. 'Express' is broader and includes showing feelings or ideas through words, art, or actions. Choosing the right word depends on what aspect of communication we want to highlight.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: I speak, I say, I talk
questions.text: Explain why it is important to learn the differences between similar words like speak, say, and talk.
questions.answer: Learning the differences helps us use language more accurately and clearly. It prevents misunderstandings when we speak or write. It also improves our listening and reading skills because we understand nuances better. Using the right word makes our speech more effective and impressive. Finally, it builds confidence in using English in different situations.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Describe what happened when the villagers threw the turtle into the river.
questions.answer: The villagers threw the turtle into the river, believing he was a thief. Instead of crying or sinking, the turtle laughed and swam away happily. This surprised the villagers and showed the turtle was innocent and clever.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why the chief said, 'You must protect the river.'
questions.answer: The chief said this because the villagers were harming innocent creatures like the turtle by throwing them into the river out of suspicion. He wanted them to realize that the river and its life should be protected, not abused. His words were meant to teach them kindness and responsibility.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: What lesson does the grizzly bear poem teach us?
questions.answer: The poem teaches us that we should never disturb or provoke a grizzly bear by asking unnecessary questions. It warns that interfering with a wild animal can be dangerous and may lead to harm. The message is to respect wildlife and leave them alone.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: How did the turtle show wisdom in the story?
questions.answer: The turtle showed wisdom by not getting angry or scared when falsely accused. Instead, he reacted with calmness and humor, laughing and swimming away. This taught the villagers a lesson without violence or fear.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why did the turtle laugh when thrown into the river?
questions.answer: The turtle laughed because he knew he was innocent and the villagers had made a mistake. He was not afraid, as he could swim safely in the river. His laughter showed his confidence and cleverness in turning a bad situation into a peaceful escape.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why should we never ask a grizzly bear where he is going or what he is doing?
questions.answer: We should never ask a grizzly bear such questions because it may anger or disturb him. Grizzly bears are wild animals and need their space; interfering can make them feel threatened. The poem warns that doing so could lead to danger, as we might never meet another bear safely.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why did the chief tell the villagers to protect the river?
questions.answer: The chief told them to protect the river because they were harming innocent life in it, like the turtle, based on false suspicions. He wanted them to realize their actions were cruel and unjust. Protecting the river meant respecting nature and living in harmony with it.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Answer in 6-10 lines. Describe the incident of the turtle and the villagers in your own words.
questions.text: Describe the incident of the turtle and the villagers in your own words.
questions.answer: The villagers saw a turtle and, without knowing the truth, accused him of being a thief. They became angry and threw him into the river to punish him. However, instead of sinking or crying, the turtle laughed and swam away happily. This surprised everyone and showed that the turtle was innocent and clever. The chief then stepped in and told the villagers to protect the river and not harm its creatures. The incident taught the villagers not to judge quickly and to be kind to all living things. It also showed that wisdom and calmness can overcome false accusations.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Answer in 6-10 lines. Write a short paragraph on the message of the grizzly bear poem.
questions.text: Write a short paragraph on the message of the grizzly bear poem.
questions.answer: The grizzly bear poem gives a clear message: never disturb a wild animal, especially a grizzly bear, by asking unnecessary questions like where he is going or what he is doing. Such actions may provoke the bear and lead to danger. The poem uses repetition to emphasize that we must never, ever dare to interfere. It teaches respect for wildlife and the importance of leaving animals in peace. By doing so, we stay safe and allow nature to thrive. The poem is a gentle reminder that curiosity should not override caution and respect for nature.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain how the story of the turtle teaches a lesson about judging others.
questions.answer: The story teaches that we should not judge others based on suspicion or appearance. The villagers assumed the turtle was a thief without any proof and punished him harshly. This shows how quick judgments can lead to unfair treatment. The turtle’s calm and clever reaction—laughing and swimming away—showed his innocence and wisdom. In the end, the chief corrected the villagers, teaching them to protect life and avoid blind accusations.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why the grizzly bear poem uses repetition of 'never, ever, ever'.
questions.answer: The poem uses repetition to strongly emphasize the warning and make it memorable. By repeating 'never, ever, ever', it creates a rhythmic and urgent tone that grabs the reader’s attention. This repetition reinforces the idea that the warning is absolute and must not be ignored. It also makes the poem enjoyable to read aloud, especially for young learners. The poetic device helps the message stick in the mind: never disturb a grizzly bear.

questions.answer: Wind is helpful in many ways. It helps boats sail and kites fly. It also turns windmills to grind grain or produce electricity.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: When can wind be harmful? Explain with examples.
questions.answer: Wind can be harmful when it blows very hard. It can break trees, damage houses, and cause dust storms that make it hard to see or breathe.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: What do we use to measure wind direction and speed?
questions.answer: We use a wind vane to know the direction from which the wind is blowing. To measure how fast the wind is blowing, we use an anemometer.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why do leaves and paper fly when wind blows?
questions.answer: Leaves and paper are light in weight. When wind blows, it pushes them easily because they offer little resistance, so they fly or flutter in the air.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why can we not see the wind but only feel it?
questions.answer: We cannot see wind because air is transparent and has no colour or shape of its own. We only know it is there when it moves things like leaves, dust, or our hair. The movement of these things shows us that wind is blowing.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why is wind important for farmers?
questions.answer: Wind helps farmers in many ways. It helps in pollination by carrying pollen from one flower to another. It also helps in spreading seeds of crops and grasses over large fields. Sometimes, wind brings rain clouds which are useful for crops.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why do we feel cool when wind blows on a hot day?
questions.answer: When wind blows, it carries away the hot air surrounding our body. It also helps sweat evaporate faster from our skin, which makes us feel cooler.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Describe how wind is both useful and harmful in our daily life.
questions.answer: Wind plays an important role in our lives. It is useful because it helps boats sail, kites fly, and windmills work. It spreads seeds and helps in pollination. Wind also brings cool air on hot days and helps dry clothes. However, when wind blows very hard, it can be harmful. Strong winds can break trees, damage roofs, and cause dust storms. In extreme cases, they lead to cyclones that destroy homes and farms. So, wind is helpful when gentle but dangerous when strong.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Imagine you are a leaf. Write about what you feel and see when the wind blows.
questions.answer: I am a small leaf hanging from a tree. When the wind starts to blow, I feel a gentle push. I begin to sway and dance in the air. I see the world moving fast — the ground, other leaves, and birds flying by. Sometimes the wind is strong and I tumble far from my tree. I feel scared but also free, flying like a bird without wings. When the wind stops, I float down slowly and rest on the ground, waiting for the next breeze to come.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain how wind helps in the dispersal of seeds.
questions.answer: Wind helps plants spread their seeds to new places so they can grow without competing with the parent plant. Many seeds are light or have wings, hairs, or parachutes that help them float in the air. When the wind blows, it carries these seeds far away. Some seeds can travel hundreds of kilometres before landing on the ground. This way, wind helps plants grow in new areas and survive better.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why wind is considered a natural resource.
questions.answer: Wind is called a natural resource because it is freely available in nature and can be used without being used up. We can use wind energy to turn windmills and generate electricity. Unlike coal or oil, wind does not cause pollution when used for energy. It is renewable, meaning it will keep blowing as long as the sun shines and the earth turns. Using wind helps save other fuels and protects the environment.

questions.answer: The minister was annoyed because the blacksmith and carpenter continued their work in their new houses, which were now exchanged. questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Describe the sequence of events in the story 'The Golden Touch' from the minister’s request to the final outcome.
questions.answer: The minister wanted peace and quiet, so he asked the blacksmith and carpenter to move their houses. Both agreed happily and said they would move the next day. The minister felt pleased, thinking he would finally rest. The next morning, however, he woke up to loud noises of tong, tong, tong and krrr, kirr, krrr. He sent his servants to check, who reported that the blacksmith had moved to the carpenter’s house and the carpenter to the blacksmith’s house. They had exchanged homes and were working day and night. The minister realized he did not get peace but more noise because the work continued nearby. He offered food to his neighbours and said goodbye, still troubled by the sounds.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Explain the irony in the situation where the minister sought peace but got more disturbance.
questions.answer: The irony lies in the fact that the minister tried to avoid noise by sending the blacksmith and carpenter away, but his plan backfired. He thought distance would reduce the sound, but instead, the workers exchanged houses and set up right near him. The blacksmith moved to the carpenter’s house and vice versa, bringing their noisy work closer to his home. As a minister, he expected obedience to bring peace, but their clever exchange defeated his purpose. The situation shows how well-intentioned actions can fail due to lack of foresight. The minister’s desire for quiet led to greater disturbance, highlighting the unintended consequences of his decision.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Describe the position and characteristics of Earth in the solar system.
questions.answer: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only known planet to support life. It has one natural satellite, the Moon, and its atmosphere contains oxygen and nitrogen. Earth's distance from the Sun allows liquid water to exist, making life possible.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: What are comets? Where do they come from?
questions.answer: Comets are icy bodies that release gas and dust, forming a glowing coma and tail when they approach the Sun. They originate from the Kuiper Belt and the Oort Cloud, located far beyond Neptune. As they orbit the Sun, their tails always point away from the Sun due to solar wind.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why life is not possible on Mercury.
questions.answer: Mercury has no atmosphere to regulate temperature, leading to extreme heat during the day and freezing cold at night. It also lacks liquid water and has high levels of radiation from the Sun. These conditions make it impossible for life as we know it to survive.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: What is the difference between a star and a planet?
questions.answer: A star produces its own light and heat through nuclear fusion, while a planet does not and only reflects light from a star. Stars are much larger and hotter than planets. Planets orbit stars, but stars do not orbit planets.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why is Venus hotter than Mercury even though it is farther from the Sun?
questions.answer: Venus is hotter than Mercury because it has a thick atmosphere filled with carbon dioxide, which traps heat through the greenhouse effect. Mercury, being closer to the Sun, has no atmosphere to retain heat, so it loses heat quickly at night. Thus, Venus maintains a consistently high temperature.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why do we see different shapes of the Moon from Earth?
questions.answer: We see different shapes of the Moon because of its changing position relative to the Earth and Sun as it orbits Earth. The portion of the Moon illuminated by the Sun that we can see varies, causing the phases. This cycle repeats approximately every 29.5 days.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why is Pluto no longer classified as a planet?
questions.answer: Pluto is no longer classified as a planet because it has not cleared its orbital path of other debris, which is one of the three criteria set by the IAU for planethood. It shares its orbit with many objects in the Kuiper Belt. Therefore, it is classified as a dwarf planet.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Describe the solar system. Include the Sun, planets, and their key features.
questions.answer: The solar system consists of the Sun at its center and eight planets that orbit it. The Sun is a massive star that provides light and heat. The inner planets—Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars—are rocky and small. The outer planets—Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune—are large gas giants, with Jupiter being the largest. Earth is the only planet known to support life due to its suitable temperature, water, and atmosphere. Many planets have moons; for example, Earth has one, while Jupiter has over 90. The solar system also includes dwarf planets, asteroids, comets, and other celestial bodies.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Imagine you are an astronaut visiting Mars. Describe what you would see and feel.
questions.answer: As an astronaut on Mars, I would see a reddish-orange landscape covered with dust and rocks, under a pale pinkish sky. The Sun would appear smaller and less bright than on Earth. I would feel much lighter due to Mars' weaker gravity—about one-third of Earth's. The temperature would be very cold, often below freezing, and the air would be too thin to breathe without a suit. I might see signs of ancient riverbeds and volcanoes like Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the solar system. The silence would be profound, with no sound traveling through the thin air. Overall, Mars would feel like a lonely, ancient world full of mysteries waiting to be explored.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: How does the Earth's movement cause day and night?
questions.answer: Earth rotates on its axis once every 24 hours, causing different parts to face the Sun or face away from it. When a part of Earth faces the Sun, it experiences daylight; when it faces away, it is night. This rotation is responsible for the cycle of day and night. The side facing the Sun gets sunlight and warmth, while the opposite side is in darkness. This continuous rotation ensures that all places on Earth experience both day and night over time.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why is Jupiter called a gas giant?
questions.answer: Jupiter is called a gas giant because it is primarily made up of hydrogen and helium gases, with no solid surface like Earth. Its massive size and strong gravity allow it to hold onto these light gases. Unlike rocky planets, Jupiter does not have a well-defined surface; its atmosphere gradually becomes denser toward the core. It also has a thick layer of clouds and storms, such as the Great Red Spot. These features make it a classic example of a gas giant in our solar system.

questions.text: Describe the experiment with the magnet and iron clips. What do you observe when you try it through air, glass, and water?
questions.answer: When I bring the magnet near iron clips in air, the clips jump and stick to the magnet. When I place the clips in a glass bowl and bring the magnet near the glass, the clips still move and stick to the magnet through the glass. Even when I pour water into the bowl with the clips, the magnet attracts them through the water. This shows that magnetic force can pass through glass, water, and air. The magnet does not need to touch the clips to pull them. It works invisibly through these materials. I find it amazing that the magnet works without direct contact. This experiment shows that magnetism is a non-contact force.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-10 lines.
questions.text: Write a summary of the poem 'O wind, a-blowing all day long' in your own words.
questions.answer: The poem describes the wind as a mysterious force that blows all day long and sings a loud song. The poet feels the wind pushing and calling but cannot see it. He wonders if the wind is a beast, a child, or something strong and cold. The wind’s presence is known by its actions — moving kites, birds, and grass — but it remains unseen. The repeated lines emphasize its constant motion and song. The poet is amazed by the wind’s power and invisibility. The poem highlights how we can feel and hear the wind but never see it directly. It makes us think about invisible forces in nature.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain how static electricity makes the balloon stick to the wall.
questions.answer: When you rub the balloon on your head, electrons transfer from your hair to the balloon, giving it a negative charge. The wall has a neutral charge, but the negative balloon repels electrons in the wall’s surface, making that area positively charged. Opposite charges attract, so the negatively charged balloon sticks to the positively charged area on the wall. This is static electricity at work. The balloon stays stuck until the charge slowly disappears.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why we can feel and hear the wind but not see it.
questions.answer: Wind is moving air, and air is transparent, so we cannot see it directly. However, when wind moves, it pushes against things like leaves, hair, or kites, which we can see moving. We also hear wind when it vibrates objects or rushes past our ears, creating sound. These effects — movement and sound — let us know the wind is there. So, although wind is invisible, we know it exists by what it does.

questions.text: Describe Carver's early life as mentioned in the chapter.
questions.answer: George Washington Carver was born in 1861 and lost his parents at a young age. He loved plants from childhood and was called the 'plant doctor'. He moved from place to place in search of education.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: What were Carver's major contributions to agriculture?
questions.answer: Carver found many uses for peanuts and sweet potato, which helped farmers diversify crops. He taught farmers in Alabama how to enrich their soil, improving crop yields. His work promoted sustainable farming practices.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why is Carver remembered as an important scientist?
questions.answer: Carver is remembered for his innovative research on peanuts and sweet potato, creating over 300 products from them. He helped poor farmers improve their livelihoods through better farming methods. His dedication to science and service made him a role model.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: How did Carver's love for plants influence his life's work?
questions.answer: Carver's love for plants began in childhood and led him to study agriculture deeply. He used this passion to help farmers by discovering new uses for crops and improving soil health. His lifelong devotion to plants brought lasting benefits to many communities.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why did people call George Washington Carver the 'plant doctor'?
questions.answer: People called him the 'plant doctor' because he had deep knowledge about plants and could heal sick plants, just like a doctor treats sick people. He understood plant needs and helped them grow better. His work with plants earned him this respectful nickname.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why did Carver go from place to place to find a college?
questions.answer: Carver went from place to place because, as an African American in the 1800s, he faced racial discrimination and many colleges refused to admit him. He kept searching until he found an institution that would accept him. His determination helped him overcome barriers to education.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Why did Carver's work help farmers in Alabama?
questions.answer: Carver's work helped farmers because he taught them to rotate crops like peanuts and sweet potato, which restored nutrients to the soil. This made the soil rich and improved crop yields. Farmers could grow more food and earn better incomes.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: Write a short paragraph on the life and work of George Washington Carver.
questions.answer: George Washington Carver was born in 1861 and overcame many hardships, including losing his parents and facing racial prejudice. He loved plants from childhood and became known as the 'plant doctor'. He went on to teach at the Tuskegee Institute in Alabama, where he researched peanuts and sweet potato, discovering over 300 uses for them. He taught farmers how to enrich their soil through crop rotation, helping them grow better crops and improve their lives. Carver died in 1943, but his legacy of science, service, and kindness continues to inspire people around the world.

questions.subject: English
questions.instruction: Write a short paragraph in 6-8 lines.
questions.text: How did George Washington Carver contribute to the lives of farmers?
questions.answer: George Washington Carver contributed greatly to farmers' lives by teaching them sustainable farming methods. He encouraged crop rotation with peanuts and sweet potato to prevent soil depletion. He discovered hundreds of uses for these crops, creating new markets and income sources for farmers. His work at the Tuskegee Institute included giving practical advice and conducting workshops. By improving soil health and crop diversity, he helped farmers become more self-reliant and prosperous. Carver’s efforts brought lasting change to agriculture in the American South.

Losing his parents early made him self-reliant and determined to succeed through education. His search for a college taught him perseverance in the face of rejection. questions.subject: English
questions.text: Explain why crop rotation with peanuts and sweet potato helps the soil.
questions.answer: Peanuts and sweet potato are legume-like plants that have the ability to fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. This process enriches the soil with essential nutrients that other crops need to grow. When farmers rotate these crops with cotton or corn, the soil does not get depleted. It prevents the need for chemical fertilizers and keeps the land fertile for longer. Thus, Carver’s advice helped maintain healthy, productive farmland.

questions.chapter: Question Bank / Dice for your Game
questions.text: How is the game played using the dice?
questions.answer: Players throw the dice and look at the words on the top faces. They read the action corresponding to those words and perform it in one minute. For each correct action, they get one mark. The star means a free mark without action.
