questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: कवेत अंबर घेणे व धोंडा यांचे अर्थ लिहा.
questions.answer: कवेत अंबर घेणे म्हणजे अशक्य गोष्ट शक्‍य करणे. धोंडा म्हणजे भंडावून सोडणे. यातील पहिला अक्षयता दर्शवितो, दुसरा त्याग दर्शवितो.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: हिरिरीने भाग घेणे व समकालीन यांचे अर्थ लिहा.
questions.answer: हिरिरीने भाग घेणे म्हणजे उत्साहाने भाग घेणे. समकालीन म्हणजे समान काळातील. पहिला प्रवृत्ती दर्शवितो, दुसरा समयसंबंधी.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: गुलामी व काळीज काढून देणे यांचे अर्थ लिहा.
questions.answer: गुलामी म्हणजे दास्यत्व. काळीज काढून देणे म्हणजे प्रिय गोष्ट दुसऱ्याला देणे, समर्पण करणे. पहिला जबर्दस्ती, दुसरा स्वेच्छा.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: ठणकावून सांगणे व सुगावा लागणे यांचे अर्थ लिहा.
questions.answer: ठणकावून सांगणे म्हणजे न घाबरता सांगणे. सुगावा लागणे म्हणजे शोध लागणे. पहिला साहस दर्शवितो, दुसरा जिज्ञासा.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: कवेत अंबर घेणे म्हणजे अशक्य गोष्ट शक्‍य करणे असे सांगणे का?
questions.answer: कवेत अंबर घेणे म्हणजे कवेत (आकाशात) अंबर (धोके) घेणे. अंबर सामान्यपणे मिळत नाही, त्यामुळे हे अशक्य गोष्ट माणली जाते. पण कवितेत असे सांगणे अशक्य गोшт शक्‍य करणे याची इच्छा दर्शवितो. यामुळे मानवी इच्छाशक्तींची क्षमता ओळखली जाते.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: धोंडा म्हणजे भंडावून सोडणे असे सांगणे का?
questions.answer: धोंडा म्हणजे काही वस्तू भंडवून तिचा ठिकाण बदलून सोडणे. भंडवून सोडणे म्हणजे वस्तूंचा संग्रह करून त्याला इतर ठिकाणी ठेवणे. यामुळे वस्तूंचा अस्तित्व व त्याचे वापर दोन्ही बदलतात. यामुळे त्याचा अर्थ भंडावून सोडणे होतो.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: हिरिरीने भाग घेणे म्हणजे उत्साहाने भाग घेणे असे सांगणे का?
questions.answer: हिरिरी म्हणजे हिरहिर वाजणारा आवाज, जे उत्साह व ऊर्जा दर्शवितो. हिरिरीने भाग घेणे म्हणजे हिरहिर वाजताना भागणे. यामुळे भागणे उत्साहाने होतो, फक्त शारीरिक नाही. त्यामुळे हिरिरीने भाग घेणे म्हणजे उत्साहाने भाग घेणे.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: कवेत अंबर घेणे, धोंडा, हिरिरीने भाग घेणे, समकालीन यांचे अर्थ लिहा व त्यांचे एकत्रित संदेश स्पष्ट करा.
questions.answer: कवेत अंबर घेणे म्हणजे अशक्य गोष्ट शक्‍य करणे, धोंडा म्हणजे भंडावून सोडणे, हिरिरीने भाग घेणे म्हणजे उत्साहाने भाग घेणे, समकालीन म्हणजे समान काळातील. यातील पहिल्यांतीन अक्षयता, त्याग, उत्साह दर्शवितो, चौथा वेळेबंध दर्शवितो. एकत्रित संदेश असेल की, मानवी इच्छाशक्तीने अशक्य गोष्ट शक्‍य केली जाऊ शकते, त्यासाठी त्याग व उत्साह आवश्यक आहे, आणि हे सर्व समकालीन संदर्भात लागू आहे. यामुळे व्यक्तीला सकारात्मक दृष्टीकोन व साहसाने जीवण यात्याने प्रेरणा मिळते.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: गुलामी, काळीज काढून देणे, ठणकावून सांगणे, सुगावा लागणे यांचे अर्थ लिहा व त्यांचे मानवी गुणधर्मांशी संबंध स्पष्ट करा.
questions.answer: गुलामी म्हणजे दास्यत्व, काळीज काढून देणे म्हणजे प्रिय गोष्ट दुसऱ्याला देणे, समर्पण करणे, ठणकावून सांगणे म्हणजे न घाबरता सांगणे, सुगावा लागणे म्हणजे शोध लागणे. गुलामी जबर्दस्ती, काळीज काढून देणे स्वेच्छा समर्पण, ठणकावून सांगणे साहस, सुगावा लागणे जिज्ञासा दर्शवितो. यातील पहिला नकारात्मक, शेष तीन सकारात्मक गुणधर्म. यामुळे मानवी जीवनात स्वेच्छा, साहस व जिज्ञासा महत्त्वाचे आहेत, ज्यामुळे व्यक्ती विकास करतो.

questions.answer: हिरिरीने भाग घेणे म्हणजे उत्साहाने भाग घेणे, जे ऊर्जा व उत्साह दर्शवितो. समकालीन म्हणजे समान काळातील, जे वेळेबंध दर्शवितो. यातील पहिला व्यक्तिगत गुणधर्म, दुसरा सामाजिक संदर्भ. एकत्रित त्यांनी सांगितले की, समकालीन वातावरणात उत्साहाने कार्य करणे आवश्यक आहे. यामुळे त्यांचे अभ्यास सामाजिक जागतिकतेसाठी उपयुक्त आहे.

questions.answer: संत तुकारामांच्या अभंग्यांमध्ये विसरलेली दोन मुख्य वैशिष्ट्ये आहेत: १) सरल भाषा, २) वित्ठोबाच्या भक्तीचा अनुभव.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: संतवाणीमध्ये ज्ञान आणि भक्तीचा संबंध कसे वर्णन केले जाते?
questions.answer: संतवाणीमध्ये ज्ञान व भक्ती एकमेकांचे पूरक माने जाते; ज्ञान बिना भक्ती शुष्क होते, भक्ती बिना ज्ञान अंधविश्वासी होऊ शकतो.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: संत चोखामेला यांचे उपदेश सामाजिक समानतेसाठी कसे उपयुक्त आहेत?
questions.answer: संत चोखामेला यांनी सर्व मनुष्यांमध्ये एकात्मता व देवाच्या एकता सांगितली, ज्यामुळे जातीची पट्टी टूटली.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: संत तुकारामांच्या अभंग्यांमध्ये ओवी फक्त कम देखील का?
questions.answer: संत तुकारामांच्या अभंग्यांमध्ये ओवी फक्त कम आहेत कारण त्यांचा उद्देश भक्तीचे सरल व अनुभवात्मक अभिव्यक्ती करणे होता, ज्यामध्ये ओवींचा शास्त्रिय पद्धतिक वापर आवश्यक नव्हता.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: संतवाणीमध्ये सामाजिक सुधाराचे संदेश कदाचित अधिक प्रामाणिक कसे मातरे?
questions.answer: संतवाणीमध्ये सामाजिक सुधाराचे संदेश अधिक प्रामाणिक मातरे कारण ते संतांच्या वैयक्तिक अनुभव व समाजातील अन्यायाचे प्रत्यक्ष दृष्टीकोनाने उद्भवले होते, त्यामुळे ते वास्तविक व प्रेरक होते.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: संत ज्ञानेश्वराने मराठीमध्ये ज्ञानेश्वरी लिहिणे आवश्यक का?
questions.answer: संत ज्ञानेश्वराने मराठीमध्ये ज्ञानेश्वरी लिहिणे आवश्यक होता कारण तेव्हा संस्कृत फक्त ब्राह्मणांचे भाषा होती, मराठीमध्ये ज्ञानेश्वरी लिहून सर्व manus्यांना वेदांचा ज्ञान सुलभ केला गेला.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: संतवाणीमध्ये दर्शवित मूल्यांचे स्पष्टीकरण द्या आणि त्यांचा आजच्या जीवनातील महत्त्व सांगा.
questions.answer: संतवाणीमध्ये दर्शवित मूल्यांचा मुख्य सारांश: १) भक्तीद्वारा देवाशी संबंध, २) ज्ञानद्वारा विवेक, ३) सामाजिक समानता, ४) सरल जीवनशैली. आजच्या जीवनातील महत्त्व: भक्तीने तणाव कमी होतो, ज्ञानाने योग्य निर्णय घेणे सोयते, समानतेमुळे सामाजिक एकता वाढते, सरलतेमुळे शांती मिळते. यामुळे व्यक्तिगत व सामाजिक विकास होतो.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: संत तुकारामांच्या अभंग्यांमध्ये विसरलेली तीन मुख्य वैशिष्ट्ये सांगा आणि त्यांचे प्रभाव स्पष्ट करा.
questions.answer: संत तुकारामांच्या अभंग्यांमध्ये विसरलेली तीन मुख्य वैशिष्ट्ये: १) सरल व बोलचालची भाषा, २) वित्ठोबाच्या भक्तीचा अनुभवात्मक वर्णन, ३) सामाजिक hypocrisy चा विरोध. त्यांचे प्रभाव: सर्व manus्यांना समजण्यायोग्य, भक्तीचा प्रवेश सोयला, सामाजिक जागृती वाढली, मराठी साहित्यातील भक्ती धारा मजबूत झाली.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: संतवाणीमध्ये 'निरगुण भक्ती' अवधारणे स्पष्ट करा.
questions.answer: संतवाणीमध्ये निरगुण भक्ती म्हणजे निराकार देवाशी भक्ती. त्यात देवाची कोणतीही मूर्ती वाचली जाणारी नाही, फक्त अनुभव व प्रेम आधारित असते. हे भक्ती सर्वात शुद्ध माणली जाते कारण ते रूपवanta बंधन मुक्त असते. ज्ञानेश्वर व तुकाराम यांनी हे उपदेश दिले.

questions.subject: Marathi
questions.text: संतवाणीमध्ये सामाजिक संदेशाचे प्रभाव स्पष्ट करा.
questions.answer: संतवाणीमध्ये सामाजिक संदेशाने जातीची पट्टी, अंधविश्वास व ऊंच-नीच भावना टूटली. संत चोखामेला, तुकाराम व इतरांनी सर्व manus्यांना एक मानली. हे संदेश आज देखील सामाजिक एकता व न्यायासाठी प्रेरणादायी आहे. त्यामुळे शैक्षणिक व सामाजिक क्षेत्रेतील सुधार होते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain how you would construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment of 6 cm.
questions.answer: To construct the perpendicular bisector of a 6 cm line segment, first draw the segment. Then, with a compass set to more than half the length (say 4 cm), draw arcs from each endpoint above and below the segment. Finally, draw a line through the two intersection points of the arcs. This line is the perpendicular bisector.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe the steps to construct a triangle when two sides and the included angle are given.
questions.answer: First, draw the base using the given length of one side. At one endpoint, use a protractor to construct the given angle. From the vertex of the angle, mark an arc with radius equal to the length of the second side. Connect this point to the other endpoint of the base to complete the triangle.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the incentre of a triangle always located inside the triangle?
questions.answer: The incentre is the intersection of the angle bisectors, and since each angle bisector lies inside the triangle, their point of intersection must also be inside. This holds true for all types of triangles—acute, obtuse, or right.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: How can you verify that a line is the perpendicular bisector of a segment?
questions.answer: To verify, measure the angles between the line and the segment—they should be 90°. Also, measure the two halves of the segment from the intersection point—they should be equal in length.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why can a triangle not be constructed if the sum of two given angles is 180° or more?
questions.answer: If the sum of two angles is 180° or more, the third angle would be 0° or negative, which is not possible in a triangle. Since the sum of all three interior angles must be exactly 180°, having two angles sum to 180° or more leaves no valid measure for the third angle.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why are the perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle concurrent?
questions.answer: The perpendicular bisectors are concurrent because any point on the perpendicular bisector of a segment is equidistant from its endpoints. The point where two such bisectors meet is equidistant from all three vertices, so it must also lie on the third perpendicular bisector.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the circumcentre of an obtuse triangle located outside the triangle?
questions.answer: In an obtuse triangle, the perpendicular bisectors of the sides intersect at a point outside the triangle because the sides are angled such that the bisectors extend outward to meet. This happens due to the obtuse angle causing the triangle to be 'wide' enough that the equidistant point lies outside.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain the construction of a right-angled triangle when the hypotenuse and one side are given. Include the steps and the reasoning behind each step.
questions.answer: To construct a right-angled triangle given the hypotenuse and one side: 1. Draw the given side as the base. 2. At one endpoint of the base, use a protractor to draw a perpendicular ray (90°). 3. From the other endpoint of the base, draw an arc with radius equal to the hypotenuse. 4. Mark the point where the arc intersects the perpendicular ray. 5. Connect this point to the other endpoint of the base. The triangle formed is right-angled because we constructed a 90° angle. The hypotenuse is the given length from the arc, and the base is the given side. The third side is formed by the intersection. This satisfies the Pythagorean theorem implicitly.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe the properties of the incentre and circumcentre of a triangle. How are they constructed? Where do they lie in different types of triangles?
questions.answer: The incentre is the point of concurrency of the angle bisectors and is equidistant from all sides of the triangle. It is constructed by drawing the bisectors of any two angles; their intersection is the incentre. It always lies inside the triangle, regardless of its type. The circumcentre is the point of concurrency of the perpendicular bisectors of the sides and is equidistant from all three vertices. It is constructed by drawing the perpendicular bisectors of any two sides. In an acute triangle, it lies inside; in a right triangle, it lies at the midpoint of the hypotenuse; in an obtuse triangle, it lies outside the triangle.

questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with proper steps.
questions.text: Construct a triangle ABC such that AB = 5 cm, BC = 4 cm, and ∠ABC = 60°. Measure AC and write its length.
questions.answer: Steps of construction: 1. Draw line segment AB = 5 cm. 2. At point B, use a protractor to construct an angle of 60° and draw ray BX. 3. From point B, cut an arc of radius 4 cm on ray BX to mark point C. 4. Join points A and C to form triangle ABC. 5. Measure side AC with a ruler. On measurement, AC is found to be approximately 4.4 cm. (Note: Exact value by Law of Cosines: AC² = 5² + 4² - 2×5×4×cos60° = 25 + 16 - 20 = 21 → AC = √21 ≈ 4.58 cm. Due to practical drawing, 4.4–4.6 cm is acceptable.)

questions.text: Draw a line segment PQ = 8 cm. Construct its perpendicular bisector. Measure the lengths of the two parts of PQ and the angle between the bisector and PQ.
questions.answer: Steps: 1. Draw segment PQ = 8 cm. 2. With P as centre and radius >4 cm (say 5 cm), draw arcs above and below PQ. 3. With Q as centre and same radius, draw arcs intersecting the previous ones. 4. Draw a line through the two intersection points — this is the perpendicular bisector. 5. Let it intersect PQ at point M. On measurement: - PM = MQ = 4 cm - Angle between bisector and PQ = 90° Thus, verified: it bisects PQ and is perpendicular to it.

questions.text: Construct a triangle XYZ such that XY = 6 cm, ∠YXZ = 45°, and ∠XYZ = 60°. Find the measure of ∠XZY.
questions.answer: Steps: 1. Draw base XY = 6 cm. 2. At point X, construct ∠YXZ = 45° and draw ray XZ. 3. At point Y, construct ∠XYZ = 60° and draw ray YZ. 4. Mark the intersection of rays XZ and YZ as point Z. 5. Triangle XYZ is formed. Now, sum of angles in triangle = 180° So, ∠XZY = 180° - (∠YXZ + ∠XYZ) = 180° - (45° + 60°) = 180° - 105° = 75° Answer: ∠XZY = 75°

questions.answer: Steps: 1. Draw line segment AB = 5 cm. 2. With A as centre and radius 5 cm, draw an arc. 3. With B as centre and radius 5 cm, draw another arc intersecting the first at C. 4. Join AC and BC. 5. Triangle ABC is equilateral. Now, measure each angle with a protractor: - ∠A = 60° - ∠B = 60° - ∠C = 60° All angles are equal, confirming the triangle is equilateral.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with proper steps.
questions.text: Draw a triangle with sides 5 cm, 6 cm, and 7 cm. Construct the perpendicular bisector of the longest side. Does it pass through the opposite vertex?
questions.answer: Steps: 1. Draw the longest side, say BC = 7 cm. 2. With B as centre and radius 5 cm, draw an arc. 3. With C as centre and radius 6 cm, draw another arc intersecting the first at A. 4. Join AB and AC to form triangle ABC. 5. Now, construct the perpendicular bisector of BC: - From B and C, draw arcs of equal radius (>3.5 cm) above and below BC. - Join the intersection points to get the bisector line. 6. Let it meet BC at point M. On observation: The perpendicular bisector of BC does NOT pass through vertex A (unless the triangle is isosceles with AB = AC, which it is not). Hence, it does not pass through the opposite vertex.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with proper steps.
questions.text: Construct a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse = 10 cm and one side = 6 cm. Measure the other side.
questions.answer: Steps: 1. Draw the given side, say AB = 6 cm. 2. At point A, construct a 90° angle and draw ray AX. 3. From point B, draw an arc of radius 10 cm (hypotenuse) cutting ray AX at point C. 4. Join B and C. 5. Triangle ABC is right-angled at A. Now, measure side BC. By Pythagoras: BC² = AC² - AB² → AC is hypotenuse = 10 cm, AB = 6 cm So, BC² = 10² - 6² = 100 - 36 = 64 → BC = 8 cm On measurement, BC ≈ 8 cm. Answer: The other side is 8 cm.

questions.text: Explain the rules of multiplication and division of integers with examples for each case.
questions.answer: The product of two positive integers is positive, e.g., 3 × 4 = 12. The product of two negative integers is positive, e.g., (-3) × (-4) = 12. The product of a positive and a negative integer is negative, e.g., 3 × (-4) = -12. In division, the quotient of two integers with the same sign is positive, e.g., (-12) ÷ (-3) = 4. The quotient of two integers with opposite signs is negative, e.g., 12 ÷ (-3) = -4. Division by zero is not defined. These rules are consistent with the number line and patterns in multiplication tables.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: How can the concept of debt be used to understand multiplication of negative integers? Explain with an example.
questions.answer: If a person borrows ₹5 each day for 3 days, the total debt is ₹15, represented as (-5) × 3 = -15. If the borrowing continues for negative time (i.e., reversing the debt), removing a debt of ₹5 three times means gaining ₹15, so (-5) × (-3) = 15. This shows that removing a negative (debt) multiple times results in a positive gain, justifying why the product of two negatives is positive.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain the prime factorisation method to find HCF and LCM of 24 and 36 with an example.
questions.answer: First, find the prime factors of each number: 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3, 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. For HCF, take the common prime factors with the lowest powers: 2 × 2 × 3 = 12. For LCM, take all prime factors with the highest powers: 2³ × 3² = 8 × 9 = 72. Thus, HCF = 12 and LCM = 72. Verify: HCF × LCM = 12 × 72 = 864, and 24 × 36 = 864, so the relation holds.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe how to find the smallest number that leaves a remainder of 3 when divided by 8, 10, and 12.
questions.answer: To find such a number, first compute the LCM of the divisors 8, 10, and 12. Prime factors: 8 = 2³, 10 = 2 × 5, 12 = 2² × 3. LCM = 2³ × 3 × 5 = 8 × 3 × 5 = 120. Since the remainder is 3 in each case, the required number is LCM + remainder = 120 + 3 = 123. Verify: 123 ÷ 8 = 15 rem 3, 123 ÷ 10 = 12 rem 3, 123 ÷ 12 = 10 rem 3. Hence, 123 is the smallest such number.

questions.text: What is a linear pair of angles?
questions.answer: A linear pair is a pair of adjacent angles whose non-common arms are opposite rays.

questions.answer: An exterior angle of a triangle is formed when one side of the triangle is extended, and it lies outside the triangle.

questions.answer: The sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral is 360°.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain how you can determine if two angles are complementary using an example.
questions.answer: Two angles are complementary if their sum is 90°. For example, 35° and 55° are complementary because 35° + 55° = 90°. To check, add the two angles and see if the total equals 90°.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Differentiate between adjacent angles and vertically opposite angles with examples.
questions.answer: Adjacent angles share a common vertex and a common arm, and lie next to each other, e.g., ∠AOB and ∠BOC. Vertically opposite angles are formed when two lines intersect and are opposite each other, e.g., ∠AOD and ∠BOC, and they are always equal.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: How do you find the supplement of an angle? Give an example.
questions.answer: To find the supplement of an angle, subtract its measure from 180°. For example, the supplement of 70° is 180° - 70° = 110°. So, 70° and 110° are supplementary angles.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain why two acute angles cannot form a supplementary pair.
questions.answer: An acute angle is less than 90°, so the sum of two acute angles is less than 90° + 90° = 180°. Since supplementary angles must sum to exactly 180°, two acute angles cannot be supplementary.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: In the figure, ∠AOC and ∠COB share vertex O and arm OC, and their other arms OA and OB are opposite rays. Give reason why ∠AOC and ∠COB form a linear pair.
questions.answer: ∠AOC and ∠COB form a linear pair because they are adjacent (share vertex O and arm OC) and their non-common arms OA and OB are opposite rays, meaning they lie on a straight line. Hence, their sum is 180°.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: If two lines intersect and one of the angles formed is 110°, what is the measure of its vertically opposite angle? Give reason.
questions.answer: The vertically opposite angle is also 110°. This is because vertically opposite angles are always equal in measure when two lines intersect.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Can an angle be both complementary and supplementary to another angle? Give reason.
questions.answer: No, an angle cannot be both complementary and supplementary to the same angle. Complementary angles sum to 90°, supplementary to 180°. For the same pair, this would require 90° = 180°, which is impossible.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Define complementary angles.
questions.answer: Complementary angles are two angles whose measures add up to exactly 90°.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Define a linear pair of angles.
questions.answer: A linear pair is a pair of adjacent angles formed when two lines intersect, such that their non-common arms are opposite rays, and their sum is always 180°.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: Answer in 6-10 lines. Include key points.
questions.text: Explain the different types of angle pairs covered in this chapter: complementary, supplementary, adjacent, linear pair, and vertically opposite angles. For each, state the definition and give one example.
questions.answer: Complementary angles are two angles whose sum is 90°, e.g., 40° and 50°. Supplementary angles sum to 180°, e.g., 110° and 70°. Adjacent angles share a common vertex and common arm with separate interiors, e.g., ∠AOB and ∠BOC. A linear pair is a pair of adjacent angles whose non-common arms form a straight line, e.g., ∠AOB and ∠BOC when A-O-C is a line. Vertically opposite angles are formed by intersecting lines and are equal, e.g., ∠AOD and ∠BOC when lines AB and CD intersect at O.

questions.instruction: Answer in 6-10 lines. Include key points.
questions.text: State and explain the property of an exterior angle of a triangle with the help of a diagram and example.
questions.answer: The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of its two remote interior angles. For example, in triangle ABC, if side BC is extended to D, then exterior angle ∠ACD = ∠A + ∠B. This is because ∠ACD and ∠ACB form a linear pair (sum 180°), and ∠A + ∠B + ∠ACB = 180° (angle sum property), so substituting gives ∠ACD = ∠A + ∠B. This property helps in solving for unknown angles in triangles.

questions.instruction: Solve the following problem. Show all steps of your working.
questions.text: Two complementary angles are such that one is twice the other. Find the measures of both angles.
questions.answer: Let the smaller angle be x°. Then the larger angle is 2x°. Since they are complementary, x + 2x = 90 3x = 90 x = 30 So, the angles are 30° and 2×30 = 60°. Answer: 30° and 60°.

questions.text: The difference between two supplementary angles is 40°. Find the measures of the angles.
questions.answer: Let one angle be x°. Then the other angle is x + 40° (since difference is 40°). As they are supplementary, x + (x + 40) = 180 2x + 40 = 180 2x = 140 x = 70 So, the angles are 70° and 70 + 40 = 110°. Answer: 70° and 110°.

questions.text: Find the measure of an angle which is equal to its complement.
questions.answer: Let the angle be x°. Its complement is (90 - x)°. Given: x = 90 - x 2x = 90 x = 45 So, the angle is 45°. Answer: 45°.

questions.text: An angle is 30° less than its supplement. Find the measure of the angle.
questions.answer: Let the angle be x°. Its supplement is (180 - x)°. Given: x = (180 - x) - 30 x = 150 - x 2x = 150 x = 75 So, the angle is 75°. Answer: 75°.

questions.text: In a right-angled triangle, one acute angle is 35°. Find the other acute angle.
questions.answer: In a right-angled triangle, one angle is 90°. Let the other acute angle be x°. Then, 90 + 35 + x = 180 125 + x = 180 x = 55 So, the other acute angle is 55°. Answer: 55°.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain why subtraction of rational numbers is not commutative, with an example.
questions.answer: Subtraction of rational numbers is not commutative because changing the order of the numbers changes the result. For example, 1/2 - 1/3 = 1/6, but 1/3 - 1/2 = -1/6, and 1/6 ≠ -1/6.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: How do you add two rational numbers with different denominators? Explain with an example.
questions.answer: To add two rational numbers with different denominators, first find a common denominator, preferably the LCM of the denominators. Then convert each fraction to an equivalent fraction with that denominator, add the numerators, and keep the common denominator. For example, to add 1/4 and 1/6, LCM of 4 and 6 is 12. So, 1/4 = 3/12 and 1/6 = 2/12. Sum = 3/12 + 2/12 = 5/12.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: What is a terminating decimal? Give an example of a rational number that has a terminating decimal form.
questions.answer: A terminating decimal is a decimal number that has a finite number of digits after the decimal point. For example, 1/4 = 0.25 is a terminating decimal because the division ends after two decimal places.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain how to find a rational number between two given rational numbers using the averaging method.
questions.answer: To find a rational number between two given rational numbers, add the two numbers and divide the sum by 2. This gives the midpoint, which is a rational number lying between them. For example, between 1/3 and 2/3, the sum is 1, and half of 1 is 1/2, which lies between 1/3 and 2/3.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is every integer a rational number?
questions.answer: Every integer is a rational number because it can be expressed as a fraction with denominator 1. For example, the integer 5 can be written as 5/1, which is in the form p/q where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0. Hence, it satisfies the definition of a rational number.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the division of rational numbers not commutative?
questions.answer: Division of rational numbers is not commutative because changing the order of the numbers changes the result. For example, (1/2) ÷ (1/4) = (1/2) × (4/1) = 2, but (1/4) ÷ (1/2) = (1/4) × (2/1) = 1/2. Since 2 ≠ 1/2, the operation is not commutative.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why does the rational number 1/3 have a recurring decimal form?
questions.answer: The rational number 1/3 has a recurring decimal form because when 1 is divided by 3, the remainder keeps repeating (1, then 10÷3 gives remainder 1 again), causing the digit 3 to repeat infinitely in the quotient. Hence, 1/3 = 0.333..., which is a recurring decimal.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain the closure property of rational numbers under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division (except by zero).
questions.answer: Rational numbers are closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division (by non-zero rational numbers). This means that when you perform any of these operations on two rational numbers, the result is always a rational number. For addition: if a/b and c/d are rational, then a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/bd, which is rational since numerator and denominator are integers and bd ≠ 0. For subtraction: a/b - c/d = (ad - bc)/bd, similarly rational. For multiplication: (a/b)×(c/d) = (ac)/(bd), rational. For division: (a/b) ÷ (c/d) = (a/b)×(d/c) = ad/(bc), provided c ≠ 0, so bc ≠ 0, hence rational. However, division by zero is undefined, so closure does not apply when dividing by zero. Thus, rational numbers form a closed system under the four basic operations, excluding division by zero.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe the difference between terminating and recurring decimal forms of rational numbers, and explain how to determine which type a given rational number will have based on its denominator in simplest form.
questions.answer: A terminating decimal is a decimal that ends after a finite number of digits, such as 0.25 or 0.125. A recurring decimal has one or more digits that repeat infinitely after the decimal point, such as 0.333... or 0.142857142857.... A rational number in its simplest form p/q has a terminating decimal if and only if the prime factors of the denominator q are only 2 and/or 5. If q has any prime factor other than 2 or 5, the decimal form will be recurring. For example, 1/8 = 0.125 terminates because 8 = 2³. But 1/6 = 0.1666... recurs because 6 = 2×3, and 3 is not 2 or 5. This rule helps predict the decimal form without performing the division.

questions.text: If x = 2/3 and y = -3/4, find the value of x² + y².
questions.answer: Step 1: Calculate x² = (2/3)² = (2²)/(3²) = 4/9 Step 2: Calculate y² = (-3/4)² = (-3)²/(4)² = 9/16 Step 3: Add x² + y² = 4/9 + 9/16 Step 4: Find LCM of 9 and 16. Since 9=3² and 16=2⁴, LCM = 3²×2⁴ = 9×16 = 144 Step 5: Convert fractions: 4/9 = (4×16)/(9×16) = 64/144 9/16 = (9×9)/(16×9) = 81/144 Step 6: Add: 64/144 + 81/144 = (64+81)/144 = 145/144 Step 7: The fraction 145/144 is already in simplest form (GCD of 145 and 144 is 1). Answer: 145/144

questions.text: Multiplicative inverse
questions.answer: The multiplicative inverse of a non-zero rational number a/b is the rational number b/a such that their product is 1. For example, the multiplicative inverse of 3/4 is 4/3 because (3/4) × (4/3) = 12/12 = 1.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Recurring decimal
questions.answer: A recurring decimal is a decimal number in which a digit or a group of digits repeats infinitely after the decimal point. It is represented by placing a dot over the repeating digit or a bar over the repeating group. For example, 1/3 = 0.333... = 0.3̇ and 1/7 = 0.142857142857... = 0.1̄42857̄.

questions.answer: Any non-zero number raised to the power 0 is 1 because of the division law: aᵐ ÷ aᵐ = aᵐ⁻ᵐ = a⁰. But aᵐ ÷ aᵐ = 1, so a⁰ = 1. This holds for any a ≠ 0.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the square root of a number considered to have two values, but we usually take only the positive one?
questions.answer: Both a positive and a negative number, when squared, give the same positive result (e.g., 3² = 9 and (-3)² = 9). Hence, every positive number has two square roots. However, in most practical contexts, the principal (non-negative) square root is taken for consistency and to avoid ambiguity.

questions.text: Why is 10⁸ used to express 384,000,000 in standard form?
questions.answer: To express 384,000,000 in standard form, we write it as a number between 1 and 10 multiplied by a power of 10. Moving the decimal point 8 places to the left gives 3.84, so we multiply by 10⁸ to get back the original number: 3.84 × 10⁸ = 384,000,000.

questions.text: Explain the laws of indices for multiplication and division with the same base, and give two examples for each.
questions.answer: The law for multiplication: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ. Example: 2³ × 2⁴ = 2⁷ = 128; 5² × 5³ = 5⁵ = 3125. The law for division: aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ (for m > n). Example: 6⁵ ÷ 6² = 6³ = 216; 10⁴ ÷ 10² = 10² = 100. These laws simplify calculations with powers.

questions.text: Describe how to find the square root of a number using the prime factorization method, with an example.
questions.answer: Step 1: Find the prime factors of the number. Step 2: Pair the identical factors. Step 3: Take one factor from each pair. Step 4: Multiply these factors to get the square root. Example: √144. Prime factors: 144 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. Pairs: (2×2), (2×2), (3×3). Take one from each: 2, 2, 3. Product: 2 × 2 × 3 = 12. Hence, √144 = 12.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe the steps to choose a scale for the Y-axis when drawing a joint bar graph.
questions.answer: First, find the highest value in the data to be represented. Then, choose a convenient unit (like 5, 10, 20) such that the highest value can be easily marked on the graph paper. Finally, ensure that the scale allows clear marking of all values without overcrowding.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: How does a joint bar graph help in comparing the wheat production of Ajay and Vijay over the years?
questions.answer: A joint bar graph places the bars for Ajay and Vijay side by side for each year, making it easy to visually compare their production. One can quickly see in which year one produced more than the other or if they were equal. It also saves space compared to drawing two separate graphs.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: What precautions should be taken while drawing a joint bar graph to ensure it is neat and accurate?
questions.answer: One must use graph paper, draw axes with a ruler, keep equal width for all bars, maintain equal distance between consecutive sets of bars, choose an appropriate scale, and use different colours or shading for the two data sets. Labels on axes and a title should also be included.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is it necessary to keep the distance between two consecutive sets of joint bars equal?
questions.answer: Equal distance between sets ensures that the graph is visually balanced and prevents misinterpretation. If distances are unequal, it may appear that certain data points are more closely related than others, leading to wrong conclusions about patterns or trends.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why should different colours be used for the two sets of data in a joint bar graph?
questions.answer: Using different colours helps in clearly distinguishing between the two data sets being compared. Without colour differentiation, it would be difficult to know which bar belongs to which entity, especially when bars are placed side by side.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is a joint bar graph considered useful for comparative study?
questions.answer: A joint bar graph allows two related data sets to be displayed side by side for the same categories, making direct visual comparison easy. It helps in quickly identifying similarities, differences, and trends between the two sets across different categories.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain the importance of joint bar graphs in representing data. Give two examples from daily life where such graphs can be used.
questions.answer: Joint bar graphs are important because they allow comparison of two related data sets across the same categories in a single, compact graph. They save space, make comparisons easier, and help in drawing quick conclusions. For example, they can be used to compare the monthly electricity bills of two consecutive years in a household. Another example is comparing the number of boys and girls participating in different sports in a school. They are also useful in showing temperature changes (max and min) over a week for two different cities.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe the process of drawing a joint bar graph to show the number of vaccinated children in Solapur and Pune for different vaccines. Include all steps from preparing the axes to labelling the graph.
questions.answer: First, take graph paper and draw the X-axis and Y-axis intersecting at the origin. On the X-axis, mark the names of the vaccines (D.P.T., Polio, Measles, etc.) with equal spacing. On the Y-axis, choose a scale such as 1 cm = 10 children, since the highest value is 89. Mark the values accordingly. For each vaccine, draw two vertical bars side by side: one for Solapur and one for Pune. Keep the width of all bars equal and the distance between each set of bars equal. Use different colours or shading to distinguish between Solapur and Pune. Label the X-axis as 'Vaccine', Y-axis as 'Number of Children', and give the title 'Vaccination in Solapur and Pune'. Finally, include a key indicating which colour/shading represents which city.

questions.answer: Ajay's wheat production in 2011 = 40 quintals Vijay's wheat production in 2011 = 30 quintals Difference = Ajay's production - Vijay's production = 40 - 30 = 10 quintals Therefore, Ajay's production exceeded Vijay's by 10 quintals in 2011.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.chapter: Algebraic Expressions and Operations on them
questions.text: Explain the process of adding algebraic expressions with examples.
questions.answer: To add algebraic expressions, we combine like terms by adding their coefficients while keeping the variable part unchanged. Unlike terms are written as they are. For example, to add (3x + 4y) and (2x - 5y), we group like terms: (3x + 2x) + (4y - 5y) = 5x - y. Another example: (7a² - 3ab + 2b) + (4a² + 5ab - b) = (7a² + 4a²) + (-3ab + 5ab) + (2b - b) = 11a² + 2ab + b. The key is to identify terms with the same variables and exponents.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.chapter: Algebraic Expressions and Operations on them
questions.text: Describe the different types of algebraic expressions based on the number of terms, with examples.
questions.answer: Algebraic expressions are classified based on the number of terms they contain. A monomial has one term, e.g., 5x or -3. A binomial has two terms, e.g., 2x + 3y or 7 - 4x. A trinomial has three terms, e.g., x² + 2x + 1 or 3a - 4b + 5. Expressions with more than three terms are called polynomials, e.g., 2x³ - x² + 4x - 7. Each term may be a number, a variable, or a product of numbers and variables. The classification helps in understanding and performing operations like addition and subtraction.

questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: If the length of a rectangle is (2x + 3) cm and its breadth is (x - 1) cm, find its area in terms of x.
questions.answer: Area = length × breadth = (2x + 3)(x - 1) = 2x(x) + 2x(-1) + 3(x) + 3(-1) = 2x² - 2x + 3x - 3 = 2x² + x - 3 Hence, the area is (2x² + x - 3) cm².

questions.answer: The product of two negative integers is positive because multiplying two negatives cancels out the negative signs, following the rule of signs in multiplication: (−) × (−) = (+).

questions.text: Differentiate between direct and inverse proportion with one example each.
questions.answer: In direct proportion, both quantities increase or decrease together (e.g., cost and number of items). In inverse proportion, one increases while the other decreases (e.g., number of workers and time taken to complete a job).

questions.text: A car travels 180 km in 3 hours. How long will it take to travel 300 km at the same speed?
questions.answer: First, speed = 180 km / 3 h = 60 km/h. Then, time = 300 km / 60 km/h = 5 hours. So, it will take 5 hours to travel 300 km.

questions.text: If 24 workers can build a wall in 15 days, how many workers are needed to build the same wall in 10 days?
questions.answer: Using inverse proportion: 24 × 15 = x × 10 → x = (24 × 15) / 10 = 36. So, 36 workers are needed.

questions.text: Why is the relationship between the number of spokes in a wheel and the angle between consecutive spokes an example of inverse proportion?
questions.answer: As the number of spokes increases, the angle between consecutive spokes decreases, and their product (number of spokes × angle) remains constant at 360°, which is the condition for inverse proportion.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why do we say that the number of men working on a task and the time taken to complete it are in inverse proportion?
questions.answer: Because increasing the number of men decreases the time required to finish the work, and the product of the number of men and the time taken remains constant for the same amount of work.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the cost of vegetables and their weight considered to be in direct proportion?
questions.answer: Because if the weight of vegetables increases, the cost increases at the same rate (assuming fixed price per kg), so the ratio of cost to weight remains constant.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain the concept of direct proportion with two different examples from daily life and show how to solve a problem based on it.
questions.answer: Direct proportion occurs when two quantities increase or decrease together such that their ratio remains constant. Example 1: If 5 kg of apples cost ₹200, then 1 kg costs ₹40, so 8 kg will cost 8 × 40 = ₹320. Example 2: A car travels 60 km in 1 hour; at the same speed, it will travel 180 km in 3 hours. To solve such problems, we find the value for one unit and then scale up or down. For instance, in the apple problem, cost per kg = ₹200/5 = ₹40, then cost for 8 kg = 8 × 40 = ₹320. This method is called the unitary method.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain inverse proportion with two examples and solve one problem using the concept.
questions.answer: Inverse proportion occurs when one quantity increases and the other decreases such that their product remains constant. Example 1: If 6 taps can fill a tank in 30 minutes, then 10 taps will take (6×30)/10 = 18 minutes. Example 2: A vehicle covers a fixed distance; if its speed doubles, the time taken halves. To solve: 6 taps × 30 min = 180 (constant). For 10 taps, time = 180 / 10 = 18 minutes. This shows that more taps mean less time, confirming inverse proportion.

questions.text: If 18 goats can graze a field in 12 days, how many days will 24 goats take to graze the same field?

questions.text: A train travels 360 km in 5 hours. How long will it take to travel 540 km at the same speed?

questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: Rohit deposited ₹8000 in a bank at 7% p.c.p.a. for 3 years. Find the simple interest and the total amount he will get after 3 years.
questions.answer: Principal (P) = ₹8000 Rate (R) = 7% p.c.p.a. Time (T) = 3 years Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) / 100 I = (8000 × 7 × 3) / 100 I = (168000) / 100 I = ₹1680 Amount = Principal + Interest Amount = 8000 + 1680 = ₹9680 Therefore, the simple interest is ₹1680 and the total amount after 3 years is ₹9680.

questions.text: A sum of money amounts to ₹6500 in 2 years and ₹7000 in 3 years at simple interest. Find the principal and the rate of interest.
questions.answer: Amount after 2 years = ₹6500 Amount after 3 years = ₹7000 Interest for 1 year = 7000 - 6500 = ₹500 Interest for 2 years = 500 × 2 = ₹1000 Principal = Amount after 2 years - Interest for 2 years Principal = 6500 - 1000 = ₹5500 Now, I = (P × R × T) / 100 For 1 year: 500 = (5500 × R × 1) / 100 500 = (5500R) / 100 500 × 100 = 5500R 50000 = 5500R R = 50000 / 5500 = 100/11 ≈ 9.09% Therefore, Principal = ₹5500 and Rate of interest = 100/11% or approximately 9.09% p.c.p.a.

questions.text: At what rate percent per annum will a sum of money double itself in 8 years?
questions.answer: Let Principal = P Then Amount = 2P (since it doubles) So, Interest = Amount - Principal = 2P - P = P Time = 8 years I = (P × R × T) / 100 P = (P × R × 8) / 100 Divide both sides by P (P ≠ 0): 1 = (R × 8) / 100 1 = 8R / 100 8R = 100 R = 100 / 8 = 12.5 Therefore, the rate of interest is 12.5% per annum.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain the different types of bank accounts mentioned in the chapter and state which account is suitable for which purpose.
questions.answer: The chapter discusses four main types of bank accounts: Current Account, Savings Account, Recurring Deposit Account, and Fixed Deposit Account. A Current Account is ideal for traders and businesses who need to deposit and withdraw money frequently; it does not earn interest. A Savings Account is for individuals who want to save money and earn interest on their balance, with some withdrawal restrictions. A Recurring Deposit Account encourages regular savings by depositing a fixed amount monthly and offers higher interest than a savings account. A Fixed Deposit Account is for depositing a lump sum for a fixed period to earn a higher interest rate, with senior citizens getting slightly more. Each account serves a different financial need based on liquidity, returns, and saving habits.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: What is simple interest? Explain how it is calculated and give an example to illustrate its use in real-life banking.
questions.answer: Simple interest is the interest calculated uniformly on the original principal for the entire time period. It does not compound, meaning interest is not earned on interest. The formula for simple interest is I = (P × R × T) / 100, where P is principal, R is rate of interest per annum, and T is time in years. For example, if ₹5000 is deposited at 6% p.c.p.a. for 2 years, the interest is (5000 × 6 × 2)/100 = ₹600. The total amount returned is ₹5600. This method is used in savings accounts, fixed deposits, and short-term loans where the interest remains fixed each year based on the initial amount.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain how you would find the circumference of a circle if you know its diameter.
questions.answer: To find the circumference of a circle when the diameter is known, multiply the diameter by π (pi). The formula is c = πd. If π is taken as 22/7, then c = (22/7) × d.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Differentiate between a minor arc and a major arc of a circle.
questions.answer: A minor arc is an arc of a circle that measures less than 180°, while a major arc measures more than 180°. The minor and major arcs corresponding to the same chord together make the complete circle.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the value of π taken as 22/7 in many school-level problems?
questions.answer: The value of π is taken as 22/7 in school-level problems because it is a simple fractional approximation that is close to the actual value of π (3.14159...) and makes manual calculations easier without a calculator.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: How does the circumference of a circle change if its radius is halved?
questions.answer: If the radius of a circle is halved, its circumference also becomes half, since circumference is directly proportional to radius (c = 2πr).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the measure of a semicircular arc 180°?
questions.answer: A semicircular arc is formed by a diameter, which divides the circle into two equal parts. Since the complete circle measures 360°, each half measures 360°/2 = 180°. Hence, the measure of a semicircular arc is 180°.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the ratio of circumference to diameter constant for all circles?
questions.answer: The ratio of circumference to diameter is constant for all circles because all circles are similar figures. This constant ratio is defined as π (pi), which is a universal geometric constant.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why can a diameter be considered a special type of chord?
questions.answer: A diameter is a chord that passes through the centre of the circle. Since it connects two points on the circle and lies entirely within it, it satisfies the definition of a chord, making it a special case.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain the relationship between the circumference, diameter, and radius of a circle. Include the formulas and the role of π.
questions.answer: The circumference of a circle is the distance around it. It is directly proportional to both the diameter and the radius. The ratio of circumference to diameter is a constant denoted by π (pi), approximately 22/7 or 3.14. Therefore, circumference c = πd. Since diameter d = 2r, substituting gives c = π × 2r = 2πr. These formulas allow us to calculate any one quantity if the other is known. The value of π remains the same for all circles, regardless of size.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe how to find the radius of a circle if its circumference is given. Use an example to illustrate your answer.
questions.answer: To find the radius from the circumference, use the formula c = 2πr. Rearranging gives r = c / (2π). Substitute the given value of circumference and the value of π (usually 22/7 or 3.14) to calculate the radius. For example, if the circumference is 88 cm and π = 22/7, then r = 88 / (2 × 22/7) = 88 × 7 / 44 = 14 cm. Thus, the radius is 14 cm.

questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: A bicycle wheel makes 500 rotations to travel a distance of 1.1 km. Find the radius of the wheel. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.answer: Total distance = 1.1 km = 1100 m Number of rotations = 500 Distance per rotation = 1100 / 500 = 2.2 m This is the circumference: c = 2.2 m c = 2πr 2.2 = 2 × (22/7) × r 2.2 = (44/7) × r r = 2.2 × (7/44) = (2.2/44) × 7 = 0.05 × 7 = 0.35 m Answer: Radius = 0.35 m or 35 cm

questions.text: Explain how doubling the side of a square affects its perimeter and area.

questions.text: How is the area of a right-angled triangle related to the area of a rectangle?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why do we need to know the surface area of a box before painting it?
questions.answer: We need to know the surface area to calculate how much paint is required. The total area to be painted determines the cost based on the rate per square unit.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the perimeter of a square not affected by its area?
questions.answer: Perimeter depends only on the length of the sides, while area depends on the square of the side. Two different squares can have the same perimeter but different areas, or vice versa, so they are independent properties.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain why the area of a pathway around a garden is found by subtracting the inner area from the outer area.
questions.answer: The pathway forms a border around the garden. The area of the pathway is the region between the outer rectangle (including path) and the inner rectangle (garden only). Subtracting the inner area from the outer gives the area of the pathway alone.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the surface area of a cube calculated as 6 × side²?
questions.answer: A cube has six identical square faces. The area of one face is side², so the total surface area is six times the area of one face, i.e., 6 × side².

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe the activity to find the area of a leaf using graph paper. Explain the steps and how the area is estimated.
questions.answer: Place the leaf on a graph paper and trace its outline. Count the number of complete squares inside the outline. For squares more than half inside, count them as full. Ignore squares less than half inside. Add the count of full and more-than-half squares to get the approximate area in square units. This method gives a good estimate of irregular shapes.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain how to find the cost of fencing a rectangular field and tiling its floor, given the rate per metre for fencing and per square metre for tiling.
questions.answer: First, find the perimeter of the field to calculate the length of fencing needed. Multiply perimeter by the rate per metre to get fencing cost. Then, find the area of the field to determine the number of tiles required. Multiply area by the rate per square metre to get tiling cost. Add both costs for total expenditure.

questions.text: The length of a rectangle is 3 times its breadth. If the perimeter is 64 cm, find its length and breadth.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: A ladder 13 m long reaches a window 12 m above the ground. Find the distance of the foot of the ladder from the wall.
questions.answer: Let the distance from the wall be x m. By Pythagoras’ theorem: x² + 12² = 13² → x² + 144 = 169 → x² = 25 → x = 5 m. So, the foot of the ladder is 5 m from the wall.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Check whether the numbers 10, 24, 26 form a Pythagorean triplet.
questions.answer: Calculate: 10² = 100, 24² = 576, 26² = 676. Now, 100 + 576 = 676, which equals 26². Hence, 10, 24, 26 form a Pythagorean triplet.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: The hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle is 15 cm and one side is 9 cm. Find the length of the other side.
questions.answer: Let the unknown side be x cm. Then, x² + 9² = 15² → x² + 81 = 225 → x² = 144 → x = 12 cm. So, the other side is 12 cm long.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the hypotenuse always the longest side in a right-angled triangle?
questions.answer: Because the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides (by Pythagoras’ theorem), it must be greater than each individual side. Hence, the hypotenuse is longer than either of the other two sides.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why can’t Pythagoras’ theorem be applied to an acute-angled triangle?
questions.answer: Pythagoras’ theorem is based on the presence of a right angle. In an acute-angled triangle, all angles are less than 90°, so the relationship (hypotenuse)² = (base)² + (height)² does not hold, as there is no hypotenuse defined in the same way.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the triangle with sides 7 cm, 10 cm, 12 cm not right-angled?
questions.answer: The longest side is 12 cm. Check: 7² + 10² = 49 + 100 = 149, and 12² = 144. Since 149 ≠ 144, the condition of Pythagoras’ theorem is not satisfied. Hence, it is not a right-angled triangle.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe the activity to verify Pythagoras’ theorem using cut-out triangles and squares as described in the textbook.
questions.answer: Cut out eight identical right-angled triangles with hypotenuse ‘a’ and sides ‘b’ and ‘c’. Draw two squares each of side (b + c). In the first square, place four triangles so that they form an inner square of side ‘a’. In the second square, place the remaining four triangles to leave two squares of sides ‘b’ and ‘c’. The area of the large square is (b + c)². This equals the area of the four triangles plus the inner square: 4 × (½bc) + a² = 2bc + a². Also, (b + c)² = b² + 2bc + c². Equating: a² + 2bc = b² + 2bc + c² → a² = b² + c². Hence, Pythagoras’ theorem is verified.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain the concept of Pythagorean triplets with examples and state how they help in identifying right-angled triangles.
questions.answer: A Pythagorean triplet consists of three natural numbers such that the square of the largest is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two. Examples: (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (8,15,17), (7,24,25). If the sides of a triangle are in such a ratio, the triangle is right-angled. This helps in quickly verifying right angles without measuring. For instance, a triangle with sides 6 cm, 8 cm, 10 cm is similar to 3:4:5, so it is right-angled. These triplets are useful in construction, navigation, and problem-solving where right angles are needed.

questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is 25 cm and one side is 15 cm. Find the length of the other side.
questions.answer: Let the unknown side be x cm. By Pythagoras’ theorem: ( hypotenuse )² = (side₁)² + (side₂)² 25² = 15² + x² 625 = 225 + x² x² = 625 – 225 = 400 x = √400 = 20 cm Hence, the length of the other side is 20 cm.

questions.answer: The diagonal of a rectangle forms a right-angled triangle with the length and width. Let diagonal = d m. By Pythagoras’ theorem: d² = 24² + 18² = 576 + 324 = 900 d = √900 = 30 m Hence, the length of the diagonal is 30 m.

questions.answer: Let the length of the ladder be l m. The ladder, wall, and ground form a right-angled triangle. By Pythagoras’ theorem: l² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100 l = √100 = 10 m Hence, the length of the ladder is 10 m.

questions.text: Find the length of the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle whose sides are 9 cm and 40 cm.
questions.answer: Let hypotenuse = h cm. By Pythagoras’ theorem: h² = 9² + 40² = 81 + 1600 = 1681 h = √1681 = 41 cm Hence, the hypotenuse is 41 cm long.

questions.text: If the sides of a triangle are in the ratio 5:12:13, and its perimeter is 90 cm, find the length of each side.
questions.answer: Let the sides be 5x, 12x, and 13x cm. Perimeter = 5x + 12x + 13x = 30x = 90 → x = 90 / 30 = 3 So, sides are: 5x = 5 × 3 = 15 cm 12x = 12 × 3 = 36 cm 13x = 13 × 3 = 39 cm Hence, the sides are 15 cm, 36 cm, and 39 cm.

questions.text: Explain how to expand (x + y)² using the area of a square.
questions.answer: Consider a square of side (x + y). Its area is (x + y)². This square can be divided into four regions: a square of area x², two rectangles each of area xy, and a square of area y². Adding these gives x² + xy + xy + y² = x² + 2xy + y², which is the expansion.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: How can you verify the formula (a - b)² = a² - 2ab + b² using a = 5, b = 3?
questions.answer: Substitute a = 5 and b = 3 into (a - b)²: (5 - 3)² = 2² = 4. Now compute a² - 2ab + b² = 25 - 2×5×3 + 9 = 25 - 30 + 9 = 4. Both sides are equal, so the formula is verified.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is (x + y)² not equal to x² + y²?
questions.answer: Because (x + y)² includes the cross term 2xy, which comes from the two rectangles formed when the square is divided. Ignoring this term gives an incomplete area, so x² + y² is less than the actual area unless x or y is zero.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why does (a + b)(a - b) simplify to a² - b² and not a² + b²?
questions.answer: When expanding (a + b)(a - b), we get a·a + a·(-b) + b·a + b·(-b) = a² - ab + ab - b². The -ab and +ab cancel, leaving a² - b². The middle terms cancel due to opposite signs, so no +b² term remains.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is the expansion of (a - b)² equal to a² - 2ab + b² and not a² + 2ab + b²?
questions.answer: Because (a - b)² = (a - b)(a - b) = a·a + a·(-b) + (-b)·a + (-b)·(-b) = a² - ab - ab + b² = a² - 2ab + b². The two middle terms are both negative, so they add to -2ab, not +2ab.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain the expansion of (x + y)² with the help of a diagram. Describe how the areas of the parts relate to the algebraic expression.
questions.answer: Draw a square with side (x + y). Divide it by drawing a line parallel to one side at distance x from one corner, and another line parallel to the adjacent side at distance y from the same corner. This divides the square into four parts: a square of side x (area x²), two rectangles each of size x by y (area xy each), and a square of side y (area y²). The total area is x² + xy + xy + y² = x² + 2xy + y². Since the area of the big square is also (x + y)², we conclude (x + y)² = x² + 2xy + y². This visual method helps understand why the cross term appears.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain how the formula (a + b)(a - b) = a² - b² can be used to calculate 97 × 103. Show all steps.
questions.answer: Notice that 97 = 100 - 3 and 103 = 100 + 3. So 97 × 103 = (100 - 3)(100 + 3). Using the formula (a + b)(a - b) = a² - b² with a = 100 and b = 3, we get (100)² - (3)² = 10000 - 9 = 9991. This method avoids direct multiplication and uses the difference of squares identity. It is especially useful when numbers are close to a round number like 100, 1000, etc. The formula simplifies calculation and reduces chances of error.

questions.answer: List the scores in ascending order in the first column. For each score, put a tally mark in the second column for every occurrence. Count the tally marks and write the frequency in the third column. Add all frequencies to get N.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why can the average be a fractional number even when all data points are whole numbers?
questions.answer: The average is the sum divided by the count. Even if the sum is a whole number, division by the count may not result in a whole number, leading to a fraction or decimal.

questions.text: How did Priya use the frequency table to find the average number of peas in a pod?
questions.answer: Priya multiplied each number of peas by its frequency (e.g., 2×8, 3×15, etc.), added all the products to get the total sum of peas, and divided by the total number of pods (50) to find the average.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why is it necessary to convert all distances to the same unit before finding the average distance?
questions.answer: It is necessary to convert all distances to the same unit because adding different units (like metres and kilometres) is meaningless. Only like quantities can be added to get a correct total, which is required for calculating a meaningful average.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why do we use tally marks instead of writing numbers directly when making a frequency table?
questions.answer: We use tally marks because they provide a simple, visual way to count occurrences as we read the data. Grouping them in fives reduces errors and makes counting faster and more accurate than writing numbers repeatedly.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Why can the average number of jumps per minute be a decimal when the actual jumps are always whole numbers?
questions.answer: The average can be a decimal because it is calculated by dividing the total number of jumps (a whole number) by the number of days. Unless the total is exactly divisible by the number of days, the result will be a fraction or decimal, representing the mean value over the period.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain the concept of average and frequency table with the help of an example from daily life.
questions.answer: The average is a representative value that shows the central tendency of a data set. It is calculated by dividing the sum of all values by the number of values. For example, if a student scores 80, 85, and 90 in three tests, the average is (80+85+90)/3 = 85. A frequency table organises data by listing each unique value, its tally marks, and how often it occurs (frequency). This is useful when data is large. For instance, if we record the number of absentees in a class over 20 days and many days have the same count, a frequency table avoids repeated addition. We can then compute the average by multiplying each score by its frequency, summing the products, and dividing by the total number of days (N). This method saves time and reduces errors.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Describe the process of making a frequency table and using it to find the average, using the pea pod activity as an example.
questions.answer: Priya observed the number of peas in 50 peapods and recorded each count. To organise this data, she made a frequency table with three columns: number of peas, tally marks, and frequency. She listed the possible scores (2 to 8 peas) in ascending order. As she read each pod’s pea count, she added a tally mark in the corresponding row. After every four tallies, she drew a diagonal line to complete a group of five. She then counted the tally marks for each score and wrote the frequency. For example, 8 pods had 2 peas, so frequency of 2 is 8. She calculated the total number of pods (N) by adding all frequencies, which was 50. To find the average, she multiplied each pea count by its frequency (2×8, 3×15, etc.), summed these products to get 206, and divided by 50. The average was 4.12, meaning about 4 peas per pod on average. This method avoided adding 50 numbers individually.

questions.text: The daily temperatures (in °C) recorded in a city for six consecutive days were: 28, 30, 32, 29, 31, 30. Find the average temperature.
questions.answer: Step 1: Add all the temperatures. 28 + 30 + 32 + 29 + 31 + 30 = 180 Step 2: Count the number of days = 6 Step 3: Divide the sum by the number of days Average = 180 ÷ 6 = 30 Therefore, the average temperature is 30°C.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: Explain the concept of simple interest with an example. How is it different from compound interest?
questions.answer: Simple interest is calculated only on the principal amount for the entire time period. For example, if 1000 rupees are deposited at 10% p.a. for 2 years, simple interest = (1000 × 10 × 2)/100 = 200 rupees. In compound interest, interest is calculated on the principal plus accumulated interest. For the same example, compound interest would be higher because interest in the second year is earned on 1100 rupees. Simple interest grows linearly, while compound interest grows exponentially.

questions.text: A rectangular garden of length 40 m has an area of 1000 sq m. It is to be fenced with 3 rounds of wire, leaving an entrance of 4 m. Find the cost of fencing at 250 rupees per metre.

questions.text: Ten men take 4 days to complete the task of tarring a road. How many days would 8 men take?
questions.answer: Total work = number of men × number of days = 10 × 4 = 40 man-days. Let the number of days for 8 men be x. Then, 8 × x = 40 → x = 40 / 8 = 5 days.

questions.instruction: Solve the following problem with full working.
questions.text: The area of a rectangular garden of length 40 m is 1000 sq m. Find the breadth of the garden and its perimeter.
questions.answer: Area = length × breadth → 1000 = 40 × breadth → breadth = 1000 / 40 = 25 m. Perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth) = 2 × (40 + 25) = 2 × 65 = 130 m.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: कोनदुभाजक कोनाचे दोन समान भाग करतो हे कशासाठी सत्य आहे?
questions.answer: कोनदुभाजक म्हणजे कोनाच्या बिंदूतील रेषा जी कोनाचे दोन कोन मापे समान करतो. त्यामुळे कोनदुभाजक कोनाचे दोन समान भाग करतो. हे कंपास व पट्टी वापरून काढता येते. त्यामुळे कोनदुभाजक चे गुणधर्म सत्य आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: त्रिकोणातील तीन कोनदुभाजक एकसंपाती असतात हे कशासाठी सत्य आहे?
questions.answer: त्रिकोणातील तीन कोनदुभाजक प्रत्येक कोनाचे दोन समान भाग करतात. त्यामुळे त्यांचे संपात बिंदू एकाच बिंदूतील जातो. हे कंपास व पट्टी वापरून काढता येते. त्यामुळे त्रिकोणातील तीन कोनदुभाजक एकसंपाती असतात हे सत्य आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: त्रिकोणाच्या बाजूंचे लंबदुभाजक एकसंपाती असतात हे कशासाठी सत्य आहे?
questions.answer: त्रिकोणाच्या बाजूंचे लंबदुभाजक प्रत्येक बाजूच्या मध्यबिंदूद्वारा लांब काढतात. त्यामुळे त्यांचे संपात बिंदू एकाच बिंदूतील जातो. हे कंपास व पट्टी वापरून काढता येते. त्यामुळे त्रिकोणाच्या बाजूंचे लंबदुभाजक एकसंपाती असतात हे सत्य आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: कोनदुभाजक, लंबदुभाजक, त्रिकोणाचे कोनदुभाजक व त्रिकोणाच्या बाजूंचे लंबदुभाजक यांचे गुणधर्म व रचना पद्धती सांगा.
questions.answer: कोनदुभाजक म्हणजे कोनाचे दोन समान भाग करणारी रेषा. लंबदुभाजक म्हणजे रेषाखंडाच्या मध्यबिंदूद्वारा लांब काढली जाणारी रेषा. त्रिकोणातील तीन कोनदुभाजक एकसंपाती असतात, त्यांचे संपात बिंदू अंतर्मध्य असेल. त्रिकोणाच्या बाजूंचे लंबदुभाजक एकसंपाती असतात, त्यांचे संपात बिंदू परिमध्य असेल. कोनदुभाजक काढण्यासाठी कोनाच्या बिंदूतील कंपास घेऊन दोन चाप काढते व त्यांचे छेदनबिंदू जोडतो. लंबदुभाजक काढण्यासाठी रेषाखंडाच्या दोन बिंदूतील कंपास घेऊन दोन चाप काढते व त्यांचे छेदनबिंदू जोडतो. हे पद्धती कंपास व पट्टी वापरून केली जाते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: वर्तुळांची एकरूपता व रेषाखंडांची एकरूपता यांचे गुणधर्म सांगा. त्यांचे उदाहरण द्या.
questions.answer: वर्तुळांची एकरूपता त्यांच्या त्रिज्या समान असल्याने निर्धारित होते. उदा. त्रिज्या 2 सेमी व 2 सेमी चे वर्तुळे एकरूप आहेत. रेषाखंडांची एकरूपता त्यांच्या लांबी समान असल्याने निर्धारित होते. उदा. रेषा 4 सेमी व रेषा 4 सेमी एकरूप आहेत. वर्तुळांची एकरूपता काढण्यासाठी कंपासाची त्रिज्या समान ठेवते. रेषाखंडांची एकरूपता काढण्यासाठी पट्टी व पेंसिल वापरून लांबी मोजते. हे गुणधर्म भौमितिक रचना वापरून सिद्ध केली जाते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील समस्या हलवा. पूर्ण कार्य दाखवा.
questions.text: 4 सेमी लांबीचा रेषाखंड काढा. त्याचा लंबदुभाजक काढा. लंबदुभाजक रेषा लांब किती असते?
questions.answer: रेषाखंड 4 सेमी लांबीचा काढला. त्याचा मध्यबिंदू 2 सेमी दुर असतो. लंबदुभाजक म्हणजे मध्यबिंदूद्वारा लांब रेषा. लंबदुभाजक रेषा लांब असीमित असते, पण कागदावर काढल्यास ते रेषाखंडाच्या लांबीवर अवलंबून असते. लंबदुभाजक रेषा लांब मोजण्यासाठी कोणतीही लांब असू शकते, पण典型पर्यंत 10 सेमी लांब काढली जाऊ शकतो. त्यामुळे लंबदुभाजक रेषा लांब 10 सेमी (उदाहरणार्थ) असते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील समस्या हलवा. पूर्ण कार्य दाखवा.
questions.text: 60° कोन काढा. त्याचा कोनदुभाजक काढा. कोनदुभाजक द्वारा बनेले दोन कोनांचे मापे काय आहेत?
questions.answer: 60° कोन काढला. त्याचा कोनदुभाजक काढला. कोनदुभाजक कोनाचे दोन समान भाग करतो. त्यामुळे प्रत्येक कोन 60° / 2 = 30° असतो. त्यामुळे कोनदुभाजक द्वारा बनेले दोन कोनांचे मापे 30° व 30° आहेत.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील समस्या हलवा. पूर्ण कार्य दाखवा.
questions.text: त्रिकोण ABC चे कोन A = 50°, B = 60° असतील. कोन C चा माप काय आहे? कोन C चा दुभाजक काढा. दुभाजक द्वारा बनेले दोन कोनांचे मापे काय आहेत?
questions.answer: त्रिकोणातील तीन कोनांचे बेरीज 180° असतो. त्यामुळे कोन C = 180° - (50° + 60°) = 70°. कोन C चा दुभाजक काढला. दुभाजक कोनाचे दोन समान भाग करतो. त्यामुळे प्रत्येक कोन 70° / 2 = 35° असतो. त्यामुळे दुभाजक द्वारा बनेले दोन कोनांचे मापे 35° व 35° आहेत.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील समस्या हलवा. पूर्ण कार्य दाखवा.
questions.text: त्रिकोण XYZ चे बाजू XY = 5 सेमी, YZ = 6 सेमी, ZX = 7 सेमी असतात. त्रिकोणाच्या बाजूंचे लंबदुभाजक काढा. लंबदुभाजकांचे संपात बिंदू परिमध्य असेल. परिमध्य बिंदूने त्रिकोणाच्या शिरोबिंदूंपर्यंतची दूरी समान असते. हे दूरी काय आहे?
questions.answer: त्रिकोण XYZ चे बाजू XY = 5 सेमी, YZ = 6 सेमी, ZX = 7 सेमी. त्रिकोणाच्या बाजूंचे लंबदुभाजक काढले. त्यांचे संपात बिंदू परिमध्य असेल. परिमध्य बिंदूने त्रिकोणाच्या शिरोबिंदूंपर्यंतची दूरी समान असते. हे दूरी परिमध्य त्रिज्या असेल. परिमध्य त्रिज्या R = (abc) / (4Δ) असते, ज्या a=5, b=6, c=7. त्रिकोणACHE क्षेत्रफळ Δ = sqrt[s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)], ज्या s = (5+6+7)/2 = 9. Δ = sqrt[9(4)(3)(2)] = sqrt[216] = 6√6 ≈ 14.7. R = (5*6*7) / (4 * 14.7) = 210 / 58.8 ≈ 3.57 सेमी. त्यामुळे परिमध्य त्रिज्या ≈ 3.6 सेमी (अंदाजे).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील समस्या हलवा. पूर्ण कार्य दाखवा.
questions.text: त्रिकोण PQR चे कोन P = 80°, Q = 70° असतील. कोन R चा माप काय आहे? कोन R चा दुभाजक काढा. दुभाजक द्वारा बनेले दोन कोनांचे मापे काय आहेत?
questions.answer: त्रिकोणातील तीन कोनांचे बेरीज 180° असतो. त्यामुळे कोन R = 180° - (80° + 70°) = 30°. कोन R चा दुभाजक काढला. दुभाजक कोनाचे दोन समान भाग करतो. त्यामुळे प्रत्येक कोन 30° / 2 = 15° असतो. त्यामुळे दुभाजक द्वारा बनेले दोन कोनांचे मापे 15° व 15° आहेत.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील समस्या हलवा. पूर्ण कार्य दाखवा.
questions.text: 5 सेमी लांबीचा रेषाखंड काढा. त्याचा लंबदुभाजक काढा. लंबदुभाजक रेषा व रेषाखंड 90° कोन बनवते का? खालील पद्धतीनुसार लंबदुभाजक काढा व त्याचा कोन मोजा.
questions.answer: 5 सेमी लांबीचा रेषाखंड AB काढला. त्याचा मध्यबिंदू M शोधला. कंपासमध्ये 3 सेमी अंतर घेऊन A व B वर चाप काढले. त्यांचे छेदनबिंदू C व D मिळाले. CD रेषा काढली. CD रेषा लंबदुभाजक आहे. लंबदुभाजक रेषा CD व रेषाखंड AB 90° कोन बनवते. त्यामुळे लंबदुभाजक रेषा व रेषाखंड 90° कोन बनवते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.answer: 50 ÷ (-10) चा भागाकार -5 आहे. धन पूर्णांक ला क्रण पूर्णांकाने भागविल्याने परिणाम क्रण असतो, आणि 50 ला 10 भागविल्याने 5 मिळतो, त्यामुळे -5.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: (-5) x (-4) चा परिणाम धन क्यों होतो?
questions.answer: दोनों क्रण पूर्णांकांचा गुणाकार धन असतो हे पूर्णांकांच्या गुणाकाराचे नियम आहे. कारण दोन ऋणे एकत्र जोडल्याने त्यांचा प्रभाव उलट होतो, जसे की कर्ज काढून टाकणे पैसे मिळवणे जसे. त्यामुळe (-5) x (-4) = +20, ज्यामध्ये धन परिणाम मिळतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: 0 ÷ (-7) चा भागाकार शून्य क्यों होतो?
questions.answer: शून्य ला कोणतेही शून्येतर संख्या भागविल्याने परिणाम शून्य असतो, कारण शून्य कदाचितही भागले जाऊ शकत नाही. त्यामुळे 0 ला -7 द्वारा भागविल्याने बाहेर येतो 0. हे भागाकाराचे मूलभूत नियम आहे.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: (-8) ÷ 2 चा भागाकार क्रण क्यों होतो?
questions.answer: एक क्रण पूर्णांक ला धन पूर्णांकाने भागविल्याने परिणाम नेहमी क्रण असतो, कारण चिन्हे विरुद्द असल्यामुळे भागाकाराचा चिन्ह क्रण होतो. त्यामुळe (-8) ÷ 2 = -4, जिथे 8 ला 2 भागविल्याने 4 मिळतो आणि चिन्ह क्रण राहतो.

questions.subject: Maths

questions.text: पूर्णांकांच्या गुणाकार व भागाकारच्या नियमांचा सांख्यिक उदाहरणे द्यून समजावा.
questions.answer: पूर्णांकांच्या गुणाकार व भागाकारचे नियम एकसमान असतात. दोन धन पूर्णांकांचा गुणाकार/भागाकार धन असतो, जसे की 6 x 4 = 24, 24 ÷ 6 = 4. एक धन व एक क्रण पूर्णांक यांचा गुणाकार/भागाकार क्रण असतो, जसे की 5 x (-3) = -15, (-15) ÷ 5 = -3. दोन क्रण पूर्णांकांचा गुणाकार/भागाकार धन असतो, जसे की (-4) x (-5) = 20, (-20) ÷ (-4) = 5. कोणतेही पूर्णांक शून्याने गुणलेल्यास परिणाम शून्य असतो, जसे की 7 x 0 = 0. शून्य ला कोणतेही शून्येतर पूर्णांकाने भागविल्याने परिणाम शून्य असतो, जसे की 0 ÷ (-9) = 0. हे नियम संख्यारेषेवर दिशा बदलण्याने देखील स्पष्ट होतात, जसे की दोन उलट दिशा एकत्र येवलील तेव्हा उजवीक दिशा होईल.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची उत्तर 6-10 ओळींचा पैराग्राफ लिहा.
questions.text: मयूरीचे कर्ज व परतफेडण्याचा उदाहरण घेऊन पूर्णांकांच्या गुणाकार व भागाकारचे व्यावहारिक अर्थ स्पष्ट करा.
questions.answer: मयूरीने तीन मित्रांनी पाच- पाच रुपये घेतले, ज्यामुळे तिच्याजबळ 15 रुपयांचा कर्ज झाला, ज्याला आपण -15 असा दर्शवतो. तेव्हा तिला आईकडून 15 रुपये मिळले व तिच्याने प्रत्येकाला परत केले, ज्यामुळे कर्ज 0 झाला. यामध्ये (-5) x 3 = -15 दर्शवितो की तीन मित्रांच्या पाच- पाच रुपयांचे कर्ज एकत्र 15 रुपयांचे कर्ज देतात. पुढे, (-15) ÷ 3 = -5 दर्शवितो की 15 रुपयांचा कर्ज तीन मित्रांमध्ये बराबर बांवले गेले, ज्यामुळे प्रत्येकाला 5 रुपये परत द्यावे लागले. यामुळे गुणाकार व भागाकारचे नियम कर्ज व परतफेडण्यामुळे स्पष्ट होतात, जसे की कर्ज वाढवणे (गुणाकार) आणि कर्ज घटवणे (भागाकार) पूर्णांकांच्या चिन्हे निर्धारित करतात.

questions.text: किसी भी शून्येतर संख्या का शून्य घातांक हमेशा 1 क्यों होता है?
questions.answer: घातांक के नियम aᵐ / aᵐ = a^(m-m) = a⁰ के अनुसार, किसी संख्या को खुद से भाग देने पर 1 प्राप्त होता है, इसलिए a⁰ = 1 माना जाता है। यह नियम सभी शून्येतर संख्याओं पर लागू होता है। उदाहरण: 5³ / 5³ = 125 / 125 = 1, और नियम के अनुसार 5^(3-3) = 5⁰ = 1।

questions.subject: Maths

questions.answer: किसी संख्या का वर्ग उसे घातांक 2 से उठाने पर प्राप्त होता है, जैसे 4² = 16, और इसे संख्या का वर्ग कहा जाता है। इसी प्रकार, किसी संख्या का घन उसे घातांक 3 से उठाने पर प्राप्त होता है, जैसे 3³ = 27, और इसे संख्या का घन कहा जाता है। ये概念 ज्यामिति में भी उपयोगी हैं: वर्ग का क्षेत्रफल भुजा² होता है, और घन का आयतन भुजा³ होता है। उदाहरण: यदि एक वर्ग की भुजा 5 सेमी है, तो उसका क्षेत्रफल 5² = 25 वर्ग सेमी है। यदि एक घन की भुजा 3 सेमी है, तो उसका आयतन 3³ = 27 घन सेमी है। इन अवधारणाओं को समझने से बीजगणित और मापन में सहायता मिलती है।

questions.answer: दोन जोडस्तंभांचे अंतर समान ठेवण्यामुळे तुलना स्पष्ट व सोपी होईल, आणि भ्रम घालण्याची शक्यता कमी होईल.

questions.answer: दोन जोडस्तंभांचे अंतर समान ठेवणे आवश्यक आहे, ज्यामुळे तुलना सोपी व स्पष्ट होईल. अंतर वेगळे असल्यास, कोणती माहिती जास्त आहे हे ओळखणे कठीण होईल.

questions.answer: वेगळे रंगे दाखवणyat येतात, त्यामुळे कोणती माहिती कोणते स्तंभ दर्शवते तात्काळ ओळखता येईल. हे विशेषतः विद्यार्थ्यांसाठी उपयोगी आहे, ज्यामुळे त्रुटी होण्याची शक्यता कमी होईल.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: जोडस्तंभालेखाचा अर्थ सांगा व त्याचे दोन फायदे व दोन नियम सांगा.
questions.answer: जोडस्तंभालेख म्हणजे दोन किंवा अधिक माहितींची तुलना करण्यासाठी वापरले जाने वाला आलेख. फायदे: 1) दोन माहितींची सोपी तुलना होईल. 2) कम जागेत जास्त माहिती दाखवता येईल. नियम: 1) प्रत्येक इयत्तेतील दोन स्तंभांचे अंतर समान ठेवायचे. 2) प्रत्येक स्तंभाची रुंदी समान असावी.

questions.text: बैजिक राशी 5x + 3y मध्ये x व y सजातीय पदे नाहीत का?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: बैजिक राशींची बेरीज व घटाव की प्रक्रिया स्पष्ट करा व सजातीय पदांची भूमिका स्पष्ट करा.
questions.answer: बैजिक राशींची बेरीज करताना, पहिले सजातीय पदे ओळखली जातात. सजातीय पदे म्हणजे त्यांचे चल व घातांक समान असलेले पद. त्यांचे गुणांक एकत्र केला जातो व त्यापुढे सामान्य चल लिहितो. घटावसाठी, दुसरी राशीतील प्रत्येक पदाचे चिन्ह बदलले जातात (धनात्मक ऋणात्मक व oppositely) व त्यानंतर बेरीज केली जाते. उदा.: (3x + 4y) - (2x - 5y) = 3x + 4y - 2x + 5y = (3-2)x + (4+5)y = x + 9y. सजातीय पदांची ओळख बेरीज व घटावच्या प्रक्रियेचा आधार होते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: ल.स.ब. व ग.स.ब. यांचे概念 सांगा. (75, 135) साठी ल.स.ब. व ग.स.ब. काढा व त्यांचे वापर सांगा.
questions.answer: ल.स.ब. (Least Common Multiple) म्हणजे दोन किंवा त्यापेक्षा अधिक संख्यांचा सर्वोत्तम छोटा सामान्य गुणाकार. ग.स.ब. (Greatest Common Divisor) म्हणजे सर्वोत्तम बड़ा सामान्य गुणाकार. (75, 135) साठी: 75 = 3×5×5, 135 = 3×3×3×5. ल.स.ब. = 3×3×3×5×5 = 675. ग.स.ब. = 3×5 = 15. ल.स.ब. चा वापर भिन्नांचे जोड-घट, घटनाक्रम, दिवसांच्या गणनेत केला जातो. ग.स.ब. चा वापर भिन्नांचे सादर रूप, वाटप, टाकण्यांचे समस्या समाधानात केला जातो.

questions.answer: वर्ग म्हणजे ककड्याला स्वतःशी गुणाकार केल्याने मिळता परिणाम. वर्गमूळ म्हणजे तो संख्या ज्या च वर्ग करण्याने दिली संख्या मिळते. 784 चा वर्गमूळ 28 (28×28=784), 225 चा 15 (15×15=225), 1296 चा 36 (36×36=1296), 2025 चा 45 (45×45=2025), 256 चा 16 (16×16=256). वर्गमूळ चा वापर क्षेत्रफळ, भुजा, त्रिकोणमिती, बीजगणित, वास्तुशास्त्र, इंजिनियरिंगमध्ये केला जातो. उदाहरण: वर्गाकार मैदानाचा क्षेत्रफळ जाणवली तर भुजा वर्गमूळ द्वारा काढली जाते.

questions.answer: समप्रमाण

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: समप्रमाण व व्यस्तप्रमाणातील फरक सांगा.
questions.answer: समप्रमाणात दोन राशींचा गुणोत्तर स्थिर राहतो, ज्यामुळे एका राशीची वाढ दुसरी राशीची वाढ होते. व्यस्तप्रमाणात दोन राशींचा गुणाकार स्थिर राहतो, ज्यामुळे एका राशीची वाढ दुसरी राशीची घट होते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: एक उदाहरण द्या जिथे समप्रमाण दिसतो.
questions.answer: व्यास व वर्तुळाचे भाग: जसे व्यासाची संख्या वाढते, तसे वर्तुळाचे भाग देखील वाढते, त्यामुळे त्यांचा गुणोत्तर स्थिर राहतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: एक उदाहरण द्या जिथे व्यस्तप्रमाण दिसतो.
questions.answer: स्वयंसेवकांची संख्या व खड्डे खणण्यासाठी लागणारे दिवस: जसे स्वयंसेवकांची संख्या वाढते, तसे दिवस घटते, त्यामुळे त्यांचा गुणाकार स्थिर राहतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: समप्रमाणातील दोन राशींचा गुणोत्तर कसे शोधता येते?
questions.answer: समप्रमाणातील दोन राशींचा गुणोत्तर शोधण्यासाठी एका राशीची मात्रा दुसरी राशीची मात्राने भागवली जाते. जर हा गुणोत्तर सर्व अवलंबुन स्थिर राहिल्यास, तेव्हा राशी समप्रमाणात असतात.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: जसे मजूरांची संख्या वाढते, तसे काम पूर्ण होण्याचा आवश्यक वेळ घटतो. हे काय प्रमाण दर्शवितात?
questions.answer: हे व्यस्तप्रमाण दर्शवितात, कारण मजूरांची संख्या व काम पूर्ण होण्याचा आवश्यक वेळ यांचा गुणाकार स्थिर राहतो. जसे मजूरांची संख्या वाढते, तसे प्रत्येक मजूर कमी काम करतो, त्यामुळे काम जल्दी पूर्ण होतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: जसे विद्यार्थ्यांची संख्या घटते, तसे प्रत्येकाला मिळणारे लाडू देखील घटते. हे काय प्रमाण दर्शवितात?
questions.answer: हे समप्रमाण दर्शवितात, कारण विद्यार्थ्यांची संख्या व प्रत्येकाला मिळणारे लाडू यांचा गुणोत्तर स्थिर राहतो. जसे विद्यार्थ्यांची संख्या घटते, तसे एकत्र लाडूंची संख्या स्थिर राहिल्यामुळे प्रत्येकाला मिळणारे लाडू देखील घटते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: जसे गाडीचा वेग वाढते, तसे निश्चित अंतर तयार करण्यास लागणारा वेळ घटतो. हे काय प्रमाण दर्शवितात?
questions.answer: हे व्यस्तप्रमाण दर्शवितात, कारण गाडीचा वेग व लागणारा वेळ यांचा गुणाकार स्थिर राहतो. जसे वेग वाढते, तसे समान अंतर तयार करण्यास कम वेळ लागतो, त्यामुळे त्यांचा गुणाकार स्थिर राहतो.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: समप्रमाण व व्यस्तप्रमाण स्पष्ट करा. प्रत्येकासाठी दोन-दोन उदाहरण द्या.
questions.answer: समप्रमाण म्हणजे दोन राशींचा गुणोत्तर स्थिर राहणारा संबंध. उदा. 1: व्यास व वर्तुळाचे भाग. जसे व्यास वाढते, तसे भाग देखील वाढते. उदा. 2: विद्यार्थी संख्या व प्रत्येकाला मिळणारे लाडू. व्यस्तप्रमाण म्हणजे दोन राशींचा गुणाकार स्थिर राहणारा संबंध. उदा. 1: मजूरांची संख्या व कामाचे तास. जसे मजूर वाढते, तसे तास घटते. उदा. 2: गाडीचा वेग व लागणारा वेळ. जसे वेग वाढते, तसे वेळ घटते.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.text: भागीदारीतील नफ्याचा वाटप भांडवलाच्या प्रमाणात केला जातो. हे स्पष्ट करा व एक उदाहरण द्या.
questions.answer: भागीदारीतील नफा भांडवलाच्या प्रमाणात वाटला जातो, कारण प्रत्येक भागीदारचा नफा त्याच्या गुंतवणूकेचे प्रमाणानुसार हота पाहिजे. उदा. दोन मित्र 3:2 प्रमाणात गुंतवणूक केली व 36000 रुपये नफा झाला. तर नफा 3:2 प्रमाणात वाटला, ज्यामुळे एकाला 21600 व दुसऱ्याला 14400 रुपये मिळाले.
