questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: समोच्च रेषा नकाशावर दोन समोच्च रेषांतील अंतर जास्त असल्यास भूरूपेचा काय वाटतो?
questions.answer: समोच्च रेषा नकाशावर दोन समोच्च रेषांतील अंतर जास्त असल्यास भूरूपेचा ढलान तीव्र वाटतो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: समोच्च रेषा नकाशा म्हणजे काय? त्याचा उपयोग कसा होतो?
questions.answer: समोच्च रेषा नकाशा म्हणजे समान उंचीच्या ठिकाणे जोडून तयार केलेला नकाशा. त्याचा उपयोग भूरूपेचे स्वरूप समजणे, उचाई मापणे, पाण्याचे प्रवाह दिशा ओळखणे व हवेच्या दाबाचे वितरण समजण्यासाठी होतो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: समुद्रसपाटीपासूनची उंची कसे मोजली जाते? त्याचे महत्त्व काय आहे?
questions.answer: समुद्रसपाटीपासूनची उंची समुद्रसपाटीला शून्य मीटर मानून मोजली जाते. त्याचे महत्त्व हे की हा सर्व उंची मापण्याचा आधार बिंदू होतो, ज्यामुळे सर्व ठिकाणांची उंची एकसमान पद्धतीने तुलना केली जाऊ शकते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: समोच्च रेषा नकाशा तयार करताना प्रत्येक समोच्च रेषेतील अंतर कसे ठेवले जाते? त्याचा परिणाम काय होतो?
questions.answer: समोच्च रेषा नकाशा तयार करताना प्रत्येक समोच्च रेषेतील अंतर पचास मीटर घेतले जाते. त्यामुळे नकाशावर उंचीच्याऐकटीची माहिती स्पष्टपणे दिसते व भूरूपेचा ढलान सहजपणे समजून घेतला जाऊ शकतो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: समोच्च रेषा नकाशावर कोणती भूरूपे ओळखली जाऊ शकतात? त्यांचे लक्षण सांगा.
questions.answer: समोच्च रेषा नकाशावर पठार, डोंगर, घाटी, मैदान इ. भूरूपे ओळखली जाऊ शकतात. पठारवरील समोच्च रेषा फक्तली असतात, डोंगरवरील चढते असतात, घाटीवरील खाली उडकलेली असतात, मैदानवरील समोच्च रेषा खूप फक्तली असतात.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: समोच्च रेषा एकमेकांशी कधी पण कटते नाहीत, का?
questions.answer: समोच्च रेषा एकमेकांशी कधी पण कटते नाहीत, कारण प्रत्येक रेषा समान उंचीच्या ठिकाणे जोडते. दोन वेगवेगळ्या उंचीच्या रेषा कटली तर त्याचा अर्थ होईल की एकाच ठिकाणी दोन वेगवेगळ्या उंची आहेत, जो असंभव आहे.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: समुद्रसपाटीपासूनची उंची शून्य मीटर मानून मोजली जाते, का?
questions.answer: समुद्रसपाटीपासूनची उंची शून्य मीटर मानून मोजली जाते, कारण समुद्रसपाटी सर्वात स्थिर व सार्वभौमिक आधार बिंदू आहे. त्यामुळे सर्व देशे एकसमान पद्धतीने उंची मापतील व त्यामुळे नकाशे तुलनेयोग्य होतात.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: समोच्च रेषा नकाशा तयार करताना प्रत्येक समोच्च रेषेतील अंतर पचास मीटर घेतले जाते, का?
questions.answer: समोच्च रेषा नकाशा तयार करताना प्रत्येक समोच्च रेषेतील अंतर पचास मीटर घेतले जाते, कारण हे अंतर पर्याप्त मोठा असतो की भूरूपेचे मुख्य आकार (जसे डोंगर, पठार, घाटी) स्पष्टपणे दिसतील, तर तरलच लहान असता तर नकाशा जटिल होईल व वाचणे कठीण होईल.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: समोच्च रेषा नकाशा म्हणजे काय? त्याचे उपयोग काय-काय आहेत? समुद्रसपाटीपासूनची उंची कसे मोजली जाते? समोच्च रेषा नकाशा तयार करताना प्रत्येक समोच्च रेषेतील अंतर कसे ठेवले जाते? त्यांचे भूरूपेच्या अभ्यासातील महत्त्व सांगा.
questions.answer: समोच्च रेषा नकाशा म्हणजे समान उंचीच्या ठिकाणे जोडून तयार केलेला नकाशा. त्याचे उपयोग: भूरूपेचे स्वरूप (डोंगर, पठार, घाटी, मैदान) ओळखणे, उचाई मापणे, पाण्याचे प्रवाह दिशा ओळखणे, हवेच्या दाबाचे वितरण समजणे, रस्ता व बांधकाम योजनेसाठी उपयोजन. समुद्रसपाटीपासूनची उंची समुद्रसपाटीला शून्य मीटर मानून मोजली जाते, ज्यामुरे सर्व ठिकाणांची उंची एकसमान पद्धतीने मापली जाऊ शकते. समोच्च रेषा नकाशा तयार करताना प्रत्येक समोच्च रेषेतील अंतर पचास मीटर घेतले जाते, ज्यामुळे नकाशा सोपे व स्पष्ट राहतो व भूरूपेचे मुख्य आकार स्पष्टपणे दिसतात. त्यांचे भूरूपेच्या अभ्यासातील महत्त्व हे की विद्यार्थी नकाशा वाचून भूप्रवाह, जलस्रोत, खेतीची शक्यता, वासस्थळाची योग्यता इ. निर्णय घेतले जाऊ शकते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: समोच्च रेषा नकाशावर पाहून कोणती भूरूपे ओळखली जाऊ शकतात? त्यांचे लक्षणे सांगा. समोच्च रेषा नकाशा तयार करताना कोणती सावधाणी बरवी हवी?
questions.answer: समोच्च रेषा नकाशावर पाहून पठार, डोंगर, घाटी, मैदान इ. भूरूपे ओळखली जाऊ शकतात. पठारवरील समोच्च रेषा फक्तली असतात (उचाई समान), डोंगरवरील समोच्च रेषा चढते असतात (उचाई वाढते जाते), घाटीवरील समोच्च रेषा खाली उडकलेली असतात (उचाई कमी होते जाते), मैदानवरील समोच्च रेषा खूप फक्तली असतात (खूप कमी उचाई वर्तन). समोच्च रेषा नकाशा तयार करताना सावधाणी: प्रत्येक समोच्च रेषेतील अंतर समान (पचास मीटर) ठेवा, रेषा एकमेकांशी कटविणे नाही, उचाई अचूकपणे मोजा, नकाशावर स्पष्टपणे लabele करा, leyenda (की) तयार करा की कोणती रेषा कोणती उंची दर्शवते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: समोच्च रेषा
questions.answer: समोच्च रेषा म्हणजे नकाशावर समान उंचीच्या ठिकाणे जोडणारी रेषा.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: समुद्रसपाटी
questions.answer: समुद्रसपाटी म्हणजे समुद्राची पातळी, ज्याची उंची शून्य मीटर मानून मोजली जाते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: समोच्च रेषा व समदाब रेषा
questions.answer: समोच्च रेषा: नकाशावर समान उंचीच्या ठिकाणे जोडणारी रेषा. समदाब रेषा: नकाशावर समान वायुदाब असलेली ठिकाणे जोडणारी रेषा. समोच्च रेषा भूरूपेचे अभ्यासासाठी वापरते, समदाब रेषा हवामानाचे अभ्यासासाठी वापरते. समोच्च रेषा उचाई दर्शवते, समदाब रेषा दाब दर्शवते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: पठार व डोंगर
questions.answer: पठार: वरील भाग समतल व उंच असलेला पठारी प्रदेश. डोंगर: उंच व ढालू असलेला भूरूपा. पठारवरील समोच्च रेषा फक्तली असतात, डोंगरवरील चढते असतात. पठारवरील उचाई अधिक समान असते, डोंगरवरील उचाई चढते जाते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील आकृती काढा व लेबल लिहा.
questions.text: समुद्रसपाटीपासूनची उंची दर्शवणारा सरल आकार काढा.
questions.answer: समुद्रसपाटी (शून्य मीटर), वरील दिशेने उंची दर्शवणारी रेषा (उदाहरण: 50 मीटर, 100 मीटर), लेबल: समुद्रसपाटी, 50 मीटर समोच्च रेषा, 100 मीटर समोच्च रेषा, उचाई दिशा

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील आकृती काढा व लेबल लिहा.
questions.text: डोंगराची सरल आकृती काढा व त्यावर समोच्च रेषा दाखवा.
questions.answer: डोंगराची आकृती (आधार खालील, वरील शिखर), समोच्च रेषा: आधारातून 50 मीटर, 100 मीटर, 150 मीटर, शिखरावर 200 मीटर, लेबल: आधार, 50 मीटर रेषा, 100 मीटर रेषा, 150 मीटर रेषा, शिखर, उचाई दिशा

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What do material sources include?
questions.answer: Material sources include forts, monuments, coins, inscriptions, sculptures, and copper plates.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What is meant by 'oral sources'?
questions.answer: Oral sources are those traditionally passed on from generation to generation, such as folk songs, powadas, and myths.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why do history books differ over time?
questions.answer: History books differ because new sources and information come to light through continuous research, requiring history to be rewritten.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What information do we get from coins?
questions.answer: Coins provide information about the rulers, their period, governance, religious ideas, and economic conditions of that time.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Mention the types of forts.
questions.answer: The major types of forts are hill forts, forest forts, sea forts, and forts on the plains.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What do we learn from inscriptions?
questions.answer: Inscriptions help us understand features like the language, script, and social life of a particular period. They are considered a reliable source of history.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What is a Bakhar?
questions.answer: A Bakhar is a type of chronicle that originated in Maharashtra. It helps in understanding contemporary political happenings, linguistic transactions, and social conditions.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What precautions should be taken while using historical sources?
questions.answer: We must examine the authenticity of sources, verify if they are genuine or fake, and analyze the integrity and personal interests of the writers.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: A stone inscription is considered to be an authentic source of history. Give reason.
questions.answer: Stone inscriptions are carved directly onto stone or walls, making them permanent and difficult to alter. They provide direct, contemporary evidence of the language, script, and social life of the period.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Oral sources reveal various aspects of people's lives. Give reason.
questions.answer: Oral sources like folk songs, powadas, and myths are created by the people themselves. They reflect the traditions, beliefs, and daily experiences of the common people across generations.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: It is necessary to evaluate sources of history. Give reason.
questions.answer: Historical sources can be one-sided, contradictory, or exaggerated. Critical analysis is required to ensure the information is neutral, impartial, and accurate before it is used to write history.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the importance of written sources in understanding medieval history.
questions.answer: Written sources include scripts like Devanagari, Arabic, Persian, and Modi. They consist of bhurjapatras, religious manuscripts, treatises, edicts, decrees, and biographies. These sources provide detailed information about food items, attire, rules of conduct, and festivals. Travelogues by foreign travellers help us understand the administrative systems and diplomatic relations of the rulers. Chronicles like Bakhars provide insights into political and social conditions of the time.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: How do coins act as a source of history?
questions.answer: Coins are vital material sources. They reveal the names of rulers, their period of governance, and their religious ideas. For example, images of Ram-Sita or Shiva-Parvati on coins show religious coordination. The metals used, like gold or silver, indicate the economic prosperity of the kingdom. Furthermore, the language used on coins, such as Arabic or Persian on Peshwa coins, sheds light on the linguistic trends of that era.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Material Sources'.
questions.answer: Material sources are physical objects from the past, such as forts, monuments, coins, sculptures, and utensils, which provide insights into the architecture, art, and standard of living of a specific period.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Written Sources'.
questions.answer: Written sources are historical records preserved in written form, including manuscripts, biographies, travelogues, and chronicles, which help us understand the social, political, and cultural life of the medieval period.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the importance of evaluating historical sources.
questions.answer: Evaluating sources is crucial because not all historical documents are unbiased. Authors may have personal interests or political pressures. Information might be exaggerated or one-sided. By verifying sources against internal standards and other contemporary evidence, historians ensure the accuracy and neutrality of the historical account.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the role of foreign travellers in writing medieval history.
questions.answer: Foreign travellers visited India during the medieval period and documented their observations in travelogues. These accounts provide an outsider's perspective on Indian society, food, attire, and administration. Writers like Al Biruni, Ibn Batuta, and Niccolao Manucci recorded details that help historians understand the diplomatic relations and political systems of the rulers of that time.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the naval strength of the Chola dynasty.
questions.answer: The Cholas were powerful at sea. Using their naval strength, they conquered the Maldive Islands and Sri Lanka, demonstrating their dominance in maritime trade and warfare.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the administrative reforms of Mahmud Gawan?
questions.answer: Mahmud Gawan paid soldiers in cash instead of land grants to ensure loyalty. He also brought discipline to the army and introduced significant reforms in the land revenue system.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why is the struggle of Rani Durgavati noteworthy?
questions.answer: Rani Durgavati was an excellent administrator who fought bravely against Akbar's forces. She laid down her life in battle rather than surrendering, becoming a symbol of courage.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What happened to the Bahamani kingdom after the death of Mahmud Gawan?
questions.answer: After his death, factionalism increased among the Sardars. The kingdom eventually disintegrated into five small powers: Imadshahi, Baridshahi, Adilshahi, Nizamshahi, and Qutubshahi.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: The Bahamani kingdom disintegrated into five fragments.
questions.answer: After the death of Mahmud Gawan, internal factionalism grew among the Sardars. Additionally, constant conflicts with the Vijaynagar kingdom weakened the central authority, causing provincial governors to act independently.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Aurangzeb imprisoned Guru Teghbahaddar.
questions.answer: Guru Teghbahaddar, the ninth Guru of the Sikhs, strongly protested against Aurangzeb's policy of religious intolerance. This defiance led Aurangzeb to imprison and eventually behead him.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: The Rajputs fought against the Mughals.
questions.answer: Aurangzeb failed to maintain the amicable relations that Akbar had established with the Rajputs. By annexing Marwad and interfering in their succession, he forced the Rajputs to revolt to protect their independence.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Write a short note on the achievements of Krishnadevaraya.
questions.answer: Krishnadevaraya ascended the throne of Vijaynagar in 1509 CE. He was a powerful ruler who expanded his kingdom from Cuttak to Goa and from Raichur Doab to the Indian Ocean. He defeated the combined forces of the Bahamani Sultans. He was also a scholar who wrote 'Amuktamalyada' and patronized the construction of the Hazar Ram and Vitthal temples.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the religious policy of Akbar.
questions.answer: Akbar was a liberal and tolerant ruler who believed in equal treatment for people of all religions. He secured the cooperation of Rajputs through amicable relations. He founded Din-i-Ilahi, which incorporated noble principles from various religions, though he never forced anyone to adopt it. His policy helped in maintaining stability and harmony in his vast empire.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Swaraj'.
questions.answer: Swaraj refers to self-rule or independence, established in Maharashtra under the leadership of Shivaji Maharaj to defend the people's freedom against foreign powers like the Mughals.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Guerilla technique'.
questions.answer: A guerilla technique is a form of irregular warfare where small groups of combatants use hit-and-run tactics, ambushes, and mobility to defeat a larger, less mobile army, as used by the Ahoms against the Mughals.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the significance of the First Battle of Panipat.
questions.answer: The First Battle of Panipat in 1526 CE marked the end of the Delhi Sultanate and the establishment of Mughal power in India. Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi using artillery effectively for the first time in India. This victory paved the way for the long-lasting Mughal dynasty, which significantly influenced Indian history and administration.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the conflict between Aurangzeb and the Marathas.
questions.answer: After the death of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Aurangzeb came to the Deccan with the intention of conquering the entire South. However, the Marathas offered stiff resistance to his forces. They defended their independence and prevented Aurangzeb from establishing a permanent foothold in the South, leading to a prolonged struggle that exhausted the Mughal treasury.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Write a short note on the 'Harihar' idols.
questions.answer: During the medieval period, there were attempts to consider Shiva and Vishnu as one. Consequently, 'Harihar' idols, which depict half Vishnu and half Shiva, were produced on a large scale to represent this unity.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the impact of the Bhakti movement on regional languages?
questions.answer: The Bhakti movement used the common people's language instead of Sanskrit. This shift helped significantly in the development and enrichment of various regional languages across India.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the role of the 'Anubhava Mantapa'?
questions.answer: The 'Anubhava Mantapa' was a hall where religious discussions were conducted. It allowed men and women belonging to all castes to participate in these discussions, promoting equality.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Mention the contribution of the Sufi sect to Indian music.
questions.answer: The Sufi saints believed in love and devotion to reach God. Their musical traditions and compositions have made a valuable and lasting contribution to Indian music.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why did the Bhakti movement facilitate religious synthesis?
questions.answer: The Bhakti movement did not give undue importance to hierarchies or caste differences. By using the language of the common people and emphasizing devotion to God, it brought different social strata together, thus facilitating religious synthesis.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why is the work of Guru Nanak considered a great attempt at religious synthesis?
questions.answer: Guru Nanak visited holy places of both Hindus and Muslims, including Mecca. He taught that all persons should be treated equally and aimed at achieving unity between the two communities, making his work a great attempt at synthesis.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why did the common people find the Bhakti movement close to their hearts?
questions.answer: The path of Bhakti was easy to follow and did not require complex rituals. Furthermore, the Sants expressed their thoughts in the language of the common people, making the movement accessible and relatable to everyone.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the teachings and impact of Sant Kabir.
questions.answer: Sant Kabir was a prominent saint of the Bhakti movement. He rejected idol worship, pilgrimages, and rituals, believing that Truth is God. He advocated for the equality of all human beings regardless of caste or religion. He strongly criticized orthodox practices in both Hindu and Muslim religions. His teachings aimed at fostering unity and brotherhood among all people, leaving a lasting impact on Indian society.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the significance of the Mahanubhav Panth in Maharashtra.
questions.answer: Founded by Chakradhar Swami in the 13th century, the Mahanubhav Panth preached devotion to Krishna. It played a crucial role in the development of the Marathi language as Chakradhar Swami preferred Marathi over Sanskrit. The sect promoted equality and opposed the caste system, welcoming men and women from all backgrounds. It spread across Vidarbha, Marathwada, and even reached Punjab and Afghanistan. Its literature, including 'Leelacharitra', remains a significant contribution to Marathi culture.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Secularism' in the context of the Indian Constitution.
questions.answer: Secularism is the principle adopted by the Indian Constitution that ensures the state treats all religions equally and does not discriminate against any religion, respecting the diversity of the Indian society.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Bhakti Marg'.
questions.answer: Bhakti Marg is the 'path of devotion' that emerged in the medieval period, replacing the emphasis on complex rituals and brahmadnyan with a direct, personal, and loving devotion to God.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the role of Mahatma Basaveshwar in social reform.
questions.answer: Mahatma Basaveshwar spread the Lingayat stream of thought in Karnataka. He strongly opposed the caste system and emphasized the 'dignity of labour' through his saying 'Kayakave Kailas' (Work is worship). He encouraged women's participation in his movement and religious discussions. By conveying his teachings in the common language, Kannada, through 'Vachana' literature, he made his message accessible to all, significantly impacting society.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the concept of religious harmony as depicted by the Sants.
questions.answer: The Sants of the Bhakti and Sufi movements worked to bridge the gap between different religions. They taught that God is one and does not discriminate based on caste or creed. For example, Sant Eknath wrote about the unity of Hindus and Muslims, and Guru Nanak visited holy places of both faiths to promote peace. Their teachings emphasized love, humanity, and tolerance, which helped in creating a more harmonious society.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the duties of a Patil?
questions.answer: The Patil tried to bring maximum land under cultivation. He also resolved disputes in the village and maintained peace.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the role of the Kulkarni?
questions.answer: The Kulkarni helped the Patil in his administrative work. He kept the records of the revenue collected in the village.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the impact of the famine of 1630 CE?
questions.answer: The famine caused a severe scarcity of foodgrains, leading to the destruction of families and cattle. Agriculture was devastated, and financial transactions came to a standstill.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the significance of the Varkari movement?
questions.answer: The Varkari movement propagated equality through bhajans and keertans. It united people from all strata of society and provided moral support during difficult times.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: The famine was a great calamity.
questions.answer: The famine caused crops to fail, leading to a severe scarcity of food and fodder. People were forced to leave their villages, and the entire social and economic life was destroyed.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Sants faced opposition from orthodox people.
questions.answer: The Sants preached equality and criticized blind beliefs and rituals. This challenged the authority and dogmatic views of the orthodox people, leading to opposition.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: The Deshmukh and Deshpande were important officers.
questions.answer: They acted as the link between the people and the government. They were responsible for revenue collection and representing the grievances of the people to the government.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the work of the Sants in Maharashtra.
questions.answer: Sants taught humanity and equality. They preached harmony and love. They helped society face invasions and natural calamities. They used simple language to explain complex religious ideas. They developed the moral sensibilities of society and created self-confidence among the people.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the administrative structure of a Pargana.
questions.answer: A Pargana was made up of many villages. The Deshmukh was the chief of the Patils, and the Deshpande was the chief of the Kulkarnis. These watandar officers acted as a link between the people and the government. They were responsible for revenue and representing the people's grievances.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define Baluta.
questions.answer: Baluta was the share of agricultural produce given by peasants to the village artisans for the services they rendered to the village community.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define Vatan.
questions.answer: Vatan is an Arabic word used in Maharashtra to refer to hereditary land for which the holder does not have to pay revenue.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the role of Shete and Mahajan in a peth.
questions.answer: The Shete and Mahajan were the watandars of the peth. It was their responsibility to set up a peth. They received land from the government and rights from the villagers for this work. The Mahajan was responsible for maintaining the accounts of the peth.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the teachings of Sant Tukaram.
questions.answer: Sant Tukaram stressed that devotion should be coupled with morality. He criticized hypocrisy and superstition in society. He believed in finding God by showing love to the unhappy and tormented. He taught that all are equal before God.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What did Shivaji Maharaj do after escaping from Panhala fort?
questions.answer: After escaping from Panhala fort, Shivaji Maharaj proceeded to Vishalgad and later entered into a treaty with the Adilshah.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the role of Veermata Jijabai in Shivaji Maharaj's life and his mission of establishing Swaraj.
questions.answer: Veermata Jijabai played a crucial role in shaping Shivaji Maharaj's character by instilling values like courage, truthfulness, and fearlessness. She ensured he received excellent education and training in weapons and administration. She constantly guided and encouraged him to fulfil his dream of establishing Swaraj.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain how the geographical features of the Maval region helped Shivaji Maharaj in founding Swaraj.
questions.answer: The Maval region, with its hills and valleys, was not easily accessible, which Shivaji Maharaj used to his advantage for guerrilla warfare and strategic movements. He skilfully used the terrain to build trust among local people and launch surprise attacks on enemies. This helped him establish a strong foundation for Swaraj.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What happened during the encounter between Shivaji Maharaj and Afzalkhan at Pratapgad?
questions.answer: Afzalkhan attempted treachery during the meeting at Pratapgad, but Shivaji Maharaj killed him in self-defence. He then routed the Adilshahi army, rewarded his brave soldiers, and compensated the wounded. This victory greatly increased Shivaji's strength and confidence.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why did Shivaji Maharaj feel the need to build a navy?
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj realised that to counter the Siddi, Portuguese, and British powers on the Western Coast, a strong naval force was necessary. He therefore concentrated on building a navy to protect his coastline and challenge foreign powers at sea.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why is Shahajiraje termed a Swaraj visionary?
questions.answer: Shahajiraje is termed a Swaraj visionary because he foresaw the need for self-rule and resisted Mughal and Adilshahi domination to protect Deccan's independence. He laid the foundation by providing Shivaji with education, training, and values essential for leadership. His efforts to save Nizamshahi and guide Shivaji towards Swaraj show his visionary outlook.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why did Shivaji Maharaj enter into a treaty with the Adilshah after reaching Vishalgad safely?
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj entered into a treaty with the Adilshah to secure his position and avoid fighting on two fronts—against the Adilshahi in the south and the Mughals in the north. The treaty allowed him to consolidate his gains and focus on strengthening Swaraj. It was a strategic move to ensure long-term stability.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why was the capture of Javali a turning point in Shivaji Maharaj's career?
questions.answer: The capture of Javali provided Shivaji Maharaj with a huge amount of wealth and strategic control over a key region. It increased his strength in all respects and enabled him to expand his activities in the Konkan region. This victory also led to the construction of Pratapgad fort and brought him into contact with European powers, prompting him to build a navy.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the efforts made by Veermata Jijabai in the education and upbringing of Shivaji Maharaj.
questions.answer: Veermata Jijabai took special care in the education and upbringing of Shivaji Maharaj. She ensured he received training in weaponry, horse riding, and military tactics. She also provided him with knowledge of administration, religion, and ethics. She instilled in him values like modesty, truthfulness, courage, and fearlessness. She encouraged his oratory skills and vigilance. She arranged for excellent teachers and mentors to guide him. Her constant support and vision helped shape Shivaji into a just and brave leader. She motivated him to work for the welfare of the people and the establishment of Swaraj. Her role was instrumental in shaping Shivaji’s character and mission.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the significance of the royal seal (Rajmudra) of Shivaji Maharaj in relation to his vision of Swaraj.
questions.answer: The royal seal of Shivaji Maharaj carries a Sanskrit inscription that reflects his vision and values. It states that the seal will grow in splendour like the new moon, symbolising the gradual and steady growth of Swaraj. The seal also denotes the welfare of the people as the ultimate goal of his rule. It shows his gratitude towards his father, Shahajiraje, and his confidence in the success of Swaraj. The seal represents his commitment to justice, prosperity, and global respect. It was used on official documents to assert his authority. Thus, the Rajmudra is not just a symbol but a statement of his political philosophy.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Swaraj
questions.answer: Swaraj means self-rule or independence, especially the establishment of a sovereign kingdom free from foreign domination.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Jagir
questions.answer: Jagir refers to the right to enjoy the revenue of a region in exchange for service, rather than receiving a fixed salary.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: How did Shivaji Maharaj use the geographical features of Maval to his advantage in founding Swaraj?
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj used the hilly and valley terrain of Maval to conduct guerrilla warfare, which was difficult for large enemy armies to counter. The inaccessibility of the region helped him hide, regroup, and launch surprise attacks. He built trust with the local Mavala people, who became loyal soldiers and informers. The terrain allowed him to control entry and exit points, making it hard for enemies to invade. These advantages helped him lay a strong foundation for Swaraj despite limited resources.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the main outcomes of Shivaji Maharaj's conquest of Javali?
questions.answer: The conquest of Javali gave Shivaji Maharaj control over a strategic region and a huge amount of wealth. It increased his military and political strength significantly. He established his administrative control by placing loyal officers and built the Pratapgad fort to secure the region. The victory brought him into contact with the Siddi, Portuguese, and British powers on the coast. This prompted him to realise the need for a strong navy to protect his interests and challenge foreign powers.

questions.text: What was the significance of the fort of Jinji?

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the outcome of the raid on Lal Mahal.
questions.answer: In the raid, Shaistakhan lost his fingers and suffered great humiliation. He left Pune and shifted his camp to Aurangabad, which also caused him to incur Aurangzeb's displeasure.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the main terms of the Treaty of Purandar?
questions.answer: Under the treaty, Maharaj gave 23 forts and territories yielding four lakh hons to the Mughals. He also assured the Mughals of help against the Adilshahi.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why did Shivaji Maharaj perform two coronation ceremonies?
questions.answer: There were two traditions of religious ceremonies in India, Vedic and Tantric. Maharaj honoured both traditions and performed two ceremonies to satisfy both.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the importance of the coronation of Shivaji Maharaj?
questions.answer: It was a revolutionary event in Medieval Indian history. It established the Maratha Swaraj as a sovereign, independent state and gave it general recognition.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Conflict with the Mughals was inevitable for Shivaji Maharaj.
questions.answer: The Swaraj was expanding, and the Mughals posed a great threat to its existence. To ensure the survival and growth of Swaraj, it was necessary to confront the Mughal power.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Shivaji Maharaj decided to escape from Agra.
questions.answer: Aurangzeb did not treat Maharaj with due honour at his court and placed him under house arrest. To protect the Swaraj and himself, Maharaj devised a plan to escape.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Shivaji Maharaj undertook the campaign of the South.
questions.answer: Maharaj wanted to expand the Swaraj and create a base in the South. He also wanted to secure alliances, such as with Qutubshah, to strengthen the Maratha position.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Write a note on the Surat Campaign.
questions.answer: Surat was a rich Mughal trade centre. Maharaj marched on it to recover losses from Mughal ravages. Inayat Khan could not resist. Maharaj obtained wealth without harming common people. It was a stunning blow to Aurangzeb's prestige.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the preparations for the coronation of Shivaji Maharaj.
questions.answer: A grand throne was made with thirty-two 'mann' of gold and eight bejewelled pillars. Special gold and copper coins were minted. A dictionary of Sanskrit terms was prepared. Scholars were invited and donated wealth generously.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Swaraj'.
questions.answer: Swaraj refers to the independent and sovereign state established by Shivaji Maharaj, free from the control of foreign powers like the Mughals and Adilshahi.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Rajyabhisheka'.
questions.answer: Rajyabhisheka is the formal coronation ceremony of a king, marking his official ascension to the throne and the beginning of his sovereign rule.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the strategy of Shivaji Maharaj after returning from Agra.
questions.answer: Maharaj did not want direct conflict immediately but aimed to recapture lost forts. He sent well-equipped armies to capture forts and simultaneously attacked Mughal territories in the Deccan to keep the Mughals unstable and occupied.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the significance of the Rajya-vyavahara-kosha.
questions.answer: It was a dictionary prepared to provide Sanskrit alternatives for Persian words used in administration. It helped in promoting the use of indigenous language in royal correspondence and official work, strengthening the identity of Swaraj.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: How did Shivaji Maharaj encourage peasants to cultivate land?

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the importance of the intelligence department?

questions.subject: History & Civics

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the policy of Shivaji Maharaj regarding agriculture.
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj paid attention to the welfare of farmers and entrusted the land revenue system to Annaji Datto. He warned officers not to collect more than the fixed revenue and granted remissions in case of crop loss due to drought or excessive rains.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the two types of cavalrymen in the Maratha army?
questions.answer: The two types were Shiledars and Bargirs. The Shiledar had his own horse and weapons, while the Bargir was provided with a horse and weapons by the State.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why were forts important in the medieval age?
questions.answer: Possession of a fort made it possible to keep an eye on the surrounding area. In case of foreign invasion, it provided protection to the people and served as a storehouse for foodgrains and war materials.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the significance of the village economy?
questions.answer: Agriculture was the backbone of the rural economy. Many occupations developed to supplement agriculture, and artisans produced goods for local needs, making the village a self-sufficient unit.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Shivaji Maharaj charged heavy duty on salt imported from Portuguese territory. Give reason.
questions.answer: The import of salt from Portuguese territory was affecting the local salt industry in Konkan. By charging heavy duty, the imported salt became expensive, which decreased its import and encouraged the sale of local salt.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Shivaji Maharaj did not give jagirs to his ministers. Give reason.
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj wanted to ensure that the administration remained efficient and that ministers remained accountable to him. By paying handsome salaries instead of jagirs, he prevented the ministers from becoming independent or powerful enough to challenge the authority of the Swaraj.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Shivaji Maharaj is called a watchful administrator. Give reason.
questions.answer: He was not just a conqueror but a ruler who cared for the welfare of his subjects. He established an efficient administration, protected industries, supported agriculture, and maintained a strong intelligence network to ensure the safety and prosperity of his people.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Write a note on the Ashtapradhan Mandal.
questions.answer: The Ashtapradhan Mandal was a council of eight ministers appointed by Shivaji Maharaj at the time of his coronation. The administration was divided into eight departments, each headed by a minister. These ministers were selected based on merit and were directly answerable to Maharaj. They were paid salaries rather than land grants. This system ensured efficient management of the Swaraj's affairs and helped in maintaining order and welfare across the kingdom.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the importance of the Navy in the Swaraj.
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj realized that the one who controls the sea is powerful. He faced threats from the Portuguese, the Siddi, and the British on the west coast. To protect the coast and curb their activities, he raised a strong navy. He built about 400 ships of various kinds, including battle ships like the gurab, galbat, and pal. He established shipyards in places like Kalyan, Bhivandi, and Malvan. This foresight allowed him to protect the Swaraj from maritime threats and assert control over the coastal regions.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Baluta'.
questions.answer: Baluta refers to the definite share of agricultural produce that farmers gave to the village artisans in exchange for their services and goods.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Swaraj'.
questions.answer: Swaraj refers to the self-rule or independent kingdom established by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, characterized by a disciplined administration and welfare of the subjects.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the military organization of Shivaji Maharaj.
questions.answer: The army was divided into two main divisions: infantry and cavalry. The infantry was led by the Sarnobat, with officers like Havaldar and Jumledar. The cavalry consisted of Shiledars (who owned their horses) and Bargirs (who were provided horses by the state). The cavalry was also led by a Sarnobat. This organized structure allowed for effective protection of the kingdom and successful military campaigns.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the importance of forts in the foundation of Swaraj.
questions.answer: Forts were the backbone of the Swaraj. They allowed for surveillance of surrounding areas and provided refuge to people during invasions. Maharaj built about 300 forts, including hill forts and sea forts like Sindhudurga. Each fort was managed by a Killedar, Sabnis, and Karkhanis. The Ajnyapatra rightly states that the kingdom was created through the strength of these forts.

questions.subject: History & Civics

questions.answer: Maharaj's organisational skill was unparalleled. He inspired people to work for Swaraj and drew brave, loyal associates around him who were willing to risk their lives for the cause.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the grave dangers faced by Shivaji Maharaj?
questions.answer: Maharaj faced many grave dangers including the meeting with Afzalkhan, the siege of Panhala, the attack on Shaistakhan, and his daring escape from Agra.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: How did Maharaj show his concern for the ryot during military campaigns?
questions.answer: He strictly prohibited soldiers from robbing farmers of their crops, fodder, or vegetables. He warned officers that harassing the subjects would cause them to migrate and starve.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the revolutionary aspects of Maharaj in the field of religion?
questions.answer: He respected all religions equally, established family bonds with people of other faiths, and brought back into Swadharma those who had converted to other religions.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Shivaji Maharaj is called a pioneer of a new era.
questions.answer: Maharaj established an independent and sovereign Swaraj while fighting against powerful enemies. He created a new administrative system and focused on the welfare of all subjects, marking the beginning of a new era.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Maharaj built sea forts like Sindhudurg.
questions.answer: Maharaj built sea forts to counter foreign invasions that came from the sea. This shows his foresight in preparing for threats from naval powers.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Maharaj was a sculptor who created a new society.
questions.answer: He was not just a warrior but a visionary who established an ethical and cultured society. He focused on minor details like waste management and tree protection to ensure the well-being of his people.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the greatness of Shivaji Maharaj as an ideal ruler.
questions.answer: 1. He founded an independent and sovereign Swaraj. 2. He was a master of many arts and languages. 3. He possessed qualities like leadership, foresight, and political diplomacy. 4. He treated all religions with equal respect. 5. He cared deeply for the ryot and protected them from harm. 6. He maintained strict discipline in his army. 7. He aimed for the welfare of all, turning Swaraj into Surajya.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the importance of Shivaji Maharaj in the national movement.
questions.answer: 1. Maharaj was a great source of inspiration for the national movement. 2. Mahatma Phule described his greatness in powadas. 3. Lokmanya Tilak used Shivajayanti to create national awakening. 4. Lala Lajpatrai wrote a book about his greatness. 5. Poets like Subramanyam Bharati and Rabindranath Tagore praised his efforts. 6. Jawaharlal Nehru considered him a national hero who belonged to the whole of India.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define Swaraj.
questions.answer: Swaraj refers to an independent and sovereign kingdom established by Shivaji Maharaj that did not accept the dominance of any other power.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define Surajya.
questions.answer: Surajya is a kingdom that focuses on the welfare of all its subjects, ensuring justice, equality, and protection for everyone.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the policy of Shivaji Maharaj regarding his army.
questions.answer: Maharaj maintained strict discipline in the army. He ensured soldiers were paid in cash on time. He honored soldiers for bravery and took care of the families of those who died in battle. He also prohibited soldiers from harming the ryot or their crops during campaigns.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the importance of the letter written by Maharaj to his officers in 1674 CE.
questions.answer: The letter shows how minutely Maharaj thought about army discipline. He strictly ordered officers to prevent soldiers from robbing farmers of their grains, fodder, or vegetables. He warned that such actions would cause the subjects to migrate and starve, which would be a failure of the administration.

questions.text: Why did Sambhaji Maharaj decide to teach a lesson to the Portuguese?
questions.answer: The Portuguese of Goa joined hands with Aurangzeb and sent troops against Sambhaji Maharaj. They also laid siege to the Maratha fort of Fonda. To counter this alliance and protect Swaraj, Sambhaji Maharaj decided to attack the Portuguese.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: How did Maharani Yesubai show bravery and leadership after Sambhaji Maharaj’s death?
questions.answer: After Sambhaji Maharaj’s death, Maharani Yesubai refused to surrender to the Mughals. She made sure Rajaram Maharaj escaped from Raigad to Jinji and took important political decisions to protect Swaraj. She continued the administration with courage and wisdom.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the 'Safe deposit locker system' used by Maharani Tarabai?
questions.answer: When Mughals captured a fort after bribing the killedar, they stored wealth and grains there. Tarabai would later recapture the fort and seize the deposited wealth, which acted like a safe deposit. This weakened Mughal resources and strengthened the Maratha treasury.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why did Aurangzeb fail to defeat the Marathas despite his military power?
questions.answer: The Marathas used guerrilla tactics, knew the local terrain, and were highly motivated to protect Swaraj. Aurangzeb’s large army and artillery were ineffective against swift surprise attacks. Maratha sardars like Santaji and Dhanaji disrupted Mughal supply lines and morale.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why did Aurangzeb turn his attention towards the Adilshahi and Qutubshahi kingdoms?
questions.answer: Aurangzeb failed to make progress against the Marathas due to their strong resistance and guerrilla warfare. Frustrated, he decided to first conquer the Deccan kingdoms of Adilshahi and Qutubshahi to isolate the Marathas and gain resources before renewing his campaign against them.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why did the Marathas intensify their war against the Mughals after the death of Sambhaji Maharaj?
questions.answer: The Marathas were inspired by Sambhaji Maharaj’s brave sacrifice and refusal to compromise their self-respect. His death fueled their determination to protect Swaraj and avenge his martyrdom, leading to a more intense and widespread resistance.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why was the fort of Jinji difficult for the Mughals to capture?
questions.answer: The fort of Jinji was naturally strong and located on a rocky hill, making it hard to besiege. The Maratha soldiers defended it bravely, and the Mughals lacked familiarity with the terrain. Additionally, Maratha sardars like Dhanaji Jadhav harassed Mughal forces outside the fort.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the role of Maharani Tarabai in the Maratha War of Independence after the death of Rajaram Maharaj.
questions.answer: After Rajaram Maharaj’s death, Maharani Tarabai took leadership of the Maratha resistance despite being a woman in a male-dominated era. She managed the administration singlehandedly, motivated the sardars, and continued the war using guerrilla tactics. She expanded the war into Malwa, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh, keeping the Mughals occupied on multiple fronts. Her 'Safe deposit locker system' weakened Mughal finances. She never surrendered and kept the spirit of Swaraj alive. Her leadership preserved Maratha independence during a critical phase. Historians like Khafikhan praised her intelligence and courage. She proved to be a worthy successor to the legacy of Shivaji and Sambhaji.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain how the Maratha War of Independence ended and what happened after Aurangzeb’s death.
questions.answer: The Maratha War of Independence lasted 27 years and ended with the death of Aurangzeb in 1707 CE at Ahmednagar. Despite years of effort, Aurangzeb could not defeat the Marathas due to their resilience and guerrilla warfare. After his death, the Mughal empire weakened due to succession wars. The Marathas, under leaders like Shahu Maharaj, began to expand their influence. They gradually regained control of lost territories and even started influencing politics in Delhi. The Marathas filled the political vacuum left by the declining Mughals. Thus, the war ended not with a treaty, but with the triumph of Maratha perseverance.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Swaraj
questions.answer: Swaraj means self-rule or independence; in the Maratha context, it referred to their independent kingdom free from Mughal control.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Guerrilla technique
questions.answer: Guerrilla technique is a strategy of warfare involving surprise attacks, ambushes, and quick retreats, used by weaker forces to counter a stronger enemy.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain how Sambhaji Maharaj’s education and training prepared him for leadership.
questions.answer: Sambhaji Maharaj received excellent education in civil administration and military campaigns from a young age. He began participating in state affairs and army command at the age of fourteen. He studied Sanskrit and many other languages, and read ancient texts on polity. He wrote the book 'Budhbhushanam' based on his studies. This training helped him govern wisely and lead bravely in battles against the Mughals and Portuguese.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the significance of the Maratha War of Independence in Indian history.
questions.answer: The Maratha War of Independence was a prolonged struggle to protect Swaraj from Mughal domination. It showcased the Marathas’ courage, unity, and strategic brilliance despite being weaker in resources. The war exhausted the Mughal empire and contributed to its decline. After Aurangzeb’s death, the Marathas emerged as a dominant power in India. This period laid the foundation for Maratha supremacy in the 18th century.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the significance of the sanads obtained by Balaji Vishwanath in 1719.
questions.answer: The sanads gave the Marathas the legal right to collect one-fourth (Chauthai) and one-tenth (Sardeshmukhi) of the revenue from the Mughal territory in the Deccan. This strengthened the financial position of the Maratha Empire.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why did the Delhi Court need the help of the Marathas?
questions.answer: The Mughal power was weakened by internal competition, court tussles, and threats from Irani and Afghani invaders, as well as local rulers like the Jats and Rajputs, making them dependent on Maratha support.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the role of Chimajiappa in the expansion of Maratha power?
questions.answer: Chimajiappa led the campaign to Malwa and successfully conquered Thane and the Vasai fort from the Portuguese, forcing them to surrender despite their powerful artillery.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: How did Shahu Maharaj's time in Mughal camps help him?
questions.answer: Living in Mughal camps allowed Shahu Maharaj to observe Mughal politics closely, understand the strengths and weaknesses of the empire, and become acquainted with influential people in the Mughal Court.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Two separate Maratha kingdoms were formed.
questions.answer: Maharani Tarabai did not accept Shahu Maharaj's claim to the throne and proclaimed her son Shivaji II as Chhatrapati at Panhala, leading to the establishment of an independent Maratha kingdom at Kolhapur alongside the one at Satara.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Delhi needed the help of the Marathas.
questions.answer: The Mughal Empire was facing severe threats from foreign invaders like the Iranis and Afghanis, and internal instability caused by local rulers and court conflicts, necessitating Maratha military assistance.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Bajirao marched on Delhi in 1737.
questions.answer: Bajirao demanded the office of the Subhedar of Malwa from the Mughal Emperor. When the Emperor declined this demand, Bajirao marched on Delhi to assert Maratha power and pressure the Emperor.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Write a note on the achievements of Bajirao I.
questions.answer: Bajirao I was a great General who expanded the Maratha Empire significantly over 20 years. He established Maratha supremacy in the North, including Malwa and Bundelkhand. He defeated the Nizam at Palkhed and Bhopal and successfully conquered Vasai and Thane from the Portuguese. His leadership elevated the Maratha power to a formidable status in India.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the circumstances that led to the rise of the Maratha power in the 18th century.
questions.answer: After Aurangzeb's death, the Mughal Empire became weak due to internal succession struggles and court bickering. The Marathas, under the leadership of Shahu Maharaj and his capable Peshwas like Balaji Vishwanath and Bajirao I, adopted a policy of protecting the Mughal power while expanding their own influence. By securing revenue rights like Chauthai and Sardeshmukhi and defeating regional rivals, the Marathas extended their power across almost the whole of India.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define Chauthai.
questions.answer: Chauthai was the right granted to the Marathas to collect one-fourth part of the revenue from the Mughal territory in the Deccan.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define Sardeshmukhi.
questions.answer: Sardeshmukhi was the right granted to the Marathas to collect one-tenth part of the revenue from the Mughal territory in the Deccan.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the significance of the Battle of Vasai.
questions.answer: The Battle of Vasai was a major conflict between the Marathas and the Portuguese. Chimajiappa led the Maratha forces and laid a siege to the strong Vasai fort. Despite the Portuguese having powerful artillery, the Marathas showed great perseverance. The victory resulted in the surrender of the Portuguese and brought Vasai and large parts of the Konkan coast under Maratha control.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the policy of the Marathas towards the Mughal Empire.
questions.answer: The Marathas shifted their policy from direct conflict to a strategic alliance. They realized that the Mughal power was declining and faced threats from foreign invaders. By protecting the Mughal throne, the Marathas gained legitimacy and the opportunity to expand their own empire. This allowed them to secure administrative rights and establish dominance over vast territories in North and Central India.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.chapter: Marathas as Guardians of the Nation
questions.text: Describe the contribution of Peshwa Madhavrao to the judiciary.
questions.answer: Peshwa Madhavrao reformed the judiciary to ensure better justice for common people. He appointed capable judges like Ramshastri Prabhune to oversee the legal processes.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.chapter: Marathas as Guardians of the Nation
questions.text: What were the after-effects of the Battle of Panipat on Maharashtra?
questions.answer: The battle resulted in the death of a whole generation of young men in Maharashtra. Many brave Sardars lost their lives, causing a severe setback to Maratha prestige.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.chapter: Marathas as Guardians of the Nation
questions.text: How did the Marathas revive their power in the North after Panipat?
questions.answer: Madhavrao dispatched capable leaders like Mahadji Shinde and Tukoji Holkar to the North. They defeated the Jats, Rohillas, and Rajputs, and restored Emperor Shah Alam to the throne.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.chapter: Marathas as Guardians of the Nation
questions.text: What was the significance of the treaty of 1752?
questions.answer: The treaty was signed between the Mughals and Marathas for mutual protection. The Marathas agreed to protect the Mughal power from enemies in exchange for Chauthai rights.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.chapter: Marathas as Guardians of the Nation
questions.text: Why was the conflict between the Marathas and Abdali inevitable?
questions.answer: Abdali wanted to bring the region up to the Punjab under Afghan control. Since the Marathas were committed to protecting the Mughal Empire and the Punjab, a clash became inevitable.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.chapter: Marathas as Guardians of the Nation
questions.text: Why did the Marathas fail to get support from Northern rulers?
questions.answer: Northern rulers viewed the Marathas as competitors rather than protectors. They did not understand the Maratha vision of a unified India and preferred to remain neutral.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.chapter: Marathas as Guardians of the Nation
questions.text: Why is the death of Peshwa Madhavrao considered an irreparable loss?
questions.answer: He was an honest, hard-working, and determined administrator. His focus on public welfare and military reforms had stabilized the state, and his death left a void in leadership.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.chapter: Marathas as Guardians of the Nation
questions.text: Write a note on the broad vision of the Marathas.
questions.answer: The Marathas were the first to realize that India was one country. They believed that all native rulers should support the king regardless of religion. Sadashivraobhau communicated this viewpoint to Northern rulers, emphasizing that they were all sons of the soil and Abdali was a foreign enemy.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.chapter: Marathas as Guardians of the Nation
questions.text: Describe the role of Tipu Sultan in the history of Mysore.
questions.answer: Tipu Sultan was a skilled warrior, scholar, and poet. He increased the strength of his kingdom and established contacts with the French to challenge British supremacy. He fought bravely against the British until his death in 1799, remaining a persistent threat to their expansion.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.chapter: Marathas as Guardians of the Nation
questions.text: Define Chauthai.
questions.answer: Chauthai was a tax or tribute collected by the Marathas, usually amounting to one-fourth of the revenue, in exchange for providing protection to a territory.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.chapter: Marathas as Guardians of the Nation
questions.text: Define Rohillas.
questions.answer: Rohillas were Pathans who had migrated from Afghanistan and settled in the region to the north-west of Ayodhya, known as Rohilkhand.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.chapter: Marathas as Guardians of the Nation
questions.text: Explain the importance of the Battle of Panipat (1761).
questions.answer: The Third Battle of Panipat was a major conflict between the Marathas and Ahmadshah Abdali. It resulted in a massive loss of life for the Marathas and a temporary decline in their power. However, it also proved that only the Marathas had the strength to control the anarchy in the North.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.chapter: Marathas as Guardians of the Nation
questions.text: Explain the administrative reforms of Peshwa Madhavrao.
questions.answer: Madhavrao focused on public welfare by digging wells and improving water supply in Pune. He reformed the judiciary for better justice, established artillery and ammunition factories, and set up a mint to produce coins.

questions.text: What happened to the Maratha power after the death of Mahadji Shinde and Nana Phadnavis?
questions.answer: After their deaths, the Maratha power began to wane.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Who were the pillars of the Maratha power in its last phase?
questions.answer: The Holkars of Indore, Bhosales of Nagpur, Shindes of Gwalior, and Gaikwads of Vadodara were the pillars of the Maratha power.

questions.text: What major change occurred in Indian history after 1818 CE?
questions.answer: The medieval period of Indian history came to an end and the Modern period began.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the administrative qualities of Ahilyabai Holkar.
questions.answer: Ahilyabai was a capable and astute administrator. She made new laws for agricultural cess and revenue collection, promoted trade and industry, and personally looked into judicial matters to dispense justice.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the role of the Bhosales of Nagpur in the expansion of Maratha power?
questions.answer: Raghuji Bhosale was the bravest and most capable among them. He brought the areas surrounding Tirucherapalli and Arcot in the South, as well as Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha, under Maratha dominance.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: How did the Gaikwads establish their power in Gujarat?
questions.answer: Khanderao Dabhade and his son Trimbakrao laid the foundation of Maratha power in Gujarat. After Khanderao's death, his wife Umabai routed the Mughal Sardar of Ahmadabad, and later the Gaikwads made Vadodara their seat of power.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the consequences of the internal strife among Maratha Sardars?
questions.answer: Internal strife weakened the Maratha power significantly. It prevented them from uniting against common enemies, and during the reign of Bajirao II, it led to a decline in Maratha influence in both the North and South.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Mahadji Shinde is considered a brave General and astute statesman.
questions.answer: Mahadji is considered so because he re-established Maratha supremacy in North India after the defeat at Panipat. He modernised his army, defeated the British, and controlled the politics of Delhi by putting the Emperor under Maratha control.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: The Maratha Sardars were successful in establishing influence in both North and South India.
questions.answer: They were successful due to their individual valour, leadership qualities, and capability. They acted as pillars of the Maratha power and worked systematically to expand and defend the Maratha territories.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: The British managed to gain control over a large part of India after 1818 CE.
questions.answer: The British gained control because the Maratha power had waned due to internal strife and lack of strong leadership. The defeat of the Marathas in the battle of Ashti marked the end of their dominance, allowing the British to replace them.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Write a summary of the role played by the Maratha Sardar families in the expansion of the Maratha Empire.
questions.answer: The Maratha Sardar families were instrumental in the expansion of the Maratha Empire. The Holkars of Indore, Shindes of Gwalior, Bhosales of Nagpur, and Gaikwads of Vadodara were the key pillars. They expanded the territory in the North and South, modernised their armies, and established administrative systems. Their valour and leadership maintained Maratha supremacy for decades. However, internal feuds and the lack of unity eventually led to the decline of their power, allowing the British to take control.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the significance of the Battle of Panipat and the subsequent efforts of Mahadji Shinde to restore Maratha prestige.
questions.answer: The defeat at Panipat was a major setback that weakened Maratha prestige in North India. Mahadji Shinde realised that traditional guerrilla tactics were insufficient for the plains of the North. He modernised his army with the help of French expert de Boigne. He defeated the British, suppressed local rebels like the Rohillas and Jats, and reinstated the Emperor of Delhi. By becoming the 'Vakil-i-Mutlak', he brought the Emperor under Maratha control, effectively restoring the prestige and supremacy of the Marathas in the North.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Vakil-i-Mutlak'.
questions.answer: Vakil-i-Mutlak was a title conferred upon Mahadji Shinde by the Emperor of Delhi, which granted him the authority of both civil and military rights over the Empire.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Maratha Ditch'.
questions.answer: The Maratha Ditch was a defensive ditch dug by the British around the city of Kolkata to protect themselves from potential Maratha attacks.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the role of Nana Phadnavis in maintaining the Maratha State.
questions.answer: Nana Phadnavis was a famous administrator and statesman who set right the affairs of the Maratha State after the death of Peshwa Madhavrao. While Mahadji Shinde was busy in the North, Nana managed the affairs of the South. He was supported by Sardars like the Patwardhans, Haripant Phadke, and the Rastes. His efforts ensured that Maratha supremacy was established and maintained in the South during a period of potential disarray.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the importance of the naval power of the Marathas.
questions.answer: The navy, originally raised by Shivaji Maharaj, was significantly strengthened by Kanhoji Angre and his son Tulaji. This strong naval force was crucial for defending the long coastline of the Maratha State. It effectively contained the naval powers of the Portuguese, the British, and the Siddhis, ensuring that the Maratha State remained secure from maritime threats.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the importance of Dasara for the Marathas?
questions.answer: Dasara was considered an auspicious occasion to start new things and launch military campaigns.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the village system of 'balutedars'.
questions.answer: There were twelve balutedars in a village, including the blacksmith, carpenter, potter, and goldsmith. They performed essential services for the village people and were paid in kind, such as foodgrains or objects.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the common means of transport and communication?
questions.answer: Transport was carried out by roads, through ghats, and across river bridges. Goods were transported on the backs of bullocks, while small boats were used in rivers. Messengers and camel riders carried letters.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the features of the wada culture?
questions.answer: Wadas were built using baked or unbaked bricks, wooden columns, and dressed stones. They were decorated with paintings, wooden sculptures, and mirrors, often featuring one or two storeys in cities.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Mention the popular outdoor games of the period.
questions.answer: Popular outdoor games included Hututu, kho-kho, and atyapatya. Wrestling and martial arts like lathi, dandpatta, and bothati were also very popular.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: The villages were considered self-sufficient.
questions.answer: Villages produced most of their daily needs like grains and vegetables locally. Only salt had to be imported from outside, making them largely independent for their basic requirements.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Women's life was full of hardships.
questions.answer: Women's education was neglected and their world was confined to the house. Customs like child marriage, polygamy, and sati imposed harsh restrictions on their freedom and way of life.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Stone ghats were built on rivers.
questions.answer: Stone ghats were built to provide easy access to water and to prevent damage to the river banks due to strong water currents. They also added beauty to the construction with their wide steps.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Write a note on the social conditions of the people in the Maratha period.
questions.answer: 1. Agriculture was the main occupation. 2. Villages were self-sufficient. 3. Joint family system was prevalent. 4. People followed various customs and traditions. 5. Child marriage was common. 6. People believed in astrology, omens, and dreams. 7. Lack of scientific attitude led to reliance on navas instead of medicine.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the art and architecture during the Maratheshahi period.
questions.answer: 1. Architecture included wadas and temples. 2. Temples were built in Hemadpanti style. 3. Stone ghats were a characteristic feature. 4. Peshwas built water supply systems like pipes and dams. 5. Paintings adorned walls of wadas and temples. 6. Themes included mythological stories and Dashavatara. 7. Metal idols were commissioned for temples.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Balutedars'.
questions.answer: Balutedars were the twelve categories of village artisans and workers, such as blacksmiths and potters, who provided essential services to the village community and were paid in kind.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Hemadpanti style'.
questions.answer: Hemadpanti is a distinct style of temple architecture prevalent during the Yadav and Maratha periods, characterized by specific stone construction techniques and intricate sculpture.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the religious policy of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj followed a liberal religious policy. He believed that everyone should follow their own religion and should not impose it on others. The government provided grants to temples, mosques, and madarasas, and people of different faiths participated in each other's festivals.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the importance of the 'Ghat' construction in Maratheshahi.
questions.answer: Ghats were stone constructions on river banks, characteristic of the period. They featured a flight of steps with wide steps at regular intervals for beauty. Strong bastions were built at intervals to prevent damage from water currents, serving both functional and aesthetic purposes.
