questions.answer: नैसर्गिक वाढ

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येची घनता काढण्यासाठी लोकसंख्या भागण्यात येते _______ द्वारे.
questions.answer: क्षेत्रफळ

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करणाऱ्या घटकांमध्ये शेती कोणत्या प्रकारचा घटक आहे?
questions.answer: आर्थिक

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करणाऱ्या घटकांमध्ये वंश कोणत्या प्रकारचा घटक आहे?
questions.answer: सामाजिक

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करणाऱ्या घटकांमध्ये राजकीय धोरण कोणत्या प्रकारचा घटक आहे?
questions.answer: राजकीय

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येची घनता काय म्हणते?
questions.answer: लोकसंख्येची घनता हे एका क्षेत्रफळातील लोकसंख्या आहे.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करणाऱ्या प्रमुख भौगोलिक घटकांना सांगा.
questions.answer: स्थान, प्राकृतिक रचना, हवामान, मृदा, खनिज संफ्तती लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करणाऱ्या प्रमुख भौगोलिक घटक आहेत.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करणाऱ्या प्रमुख आर्थिक घटकांना सांगा.
questions.answer: शेती, कारखानदारी, नागरीकरण, वाहतूक, बाजारपेठ लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करणाऱ्या प्रमुख आर्थिक घटक आहेत.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करणाऱ्या प्रमुख सामाजिक घटकांना सांगा.
questions.answer: वंश, धर्म, भाषा, रूढी व परंपरा लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करणाऱ्या प्रमुख सामाजिक घटक आहेत.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करणाऱ्या प्रमुख राजकीय घटकांना सांगा.
questions.answer: युद्ध, राजकीय अस्थिरता, राजकीय धोरण लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करणाऱ्या प्रमुख राजकीय घटक आहेत.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करणाऱ्या घटकांचे नावे लिहा व त्यांचे दोन-दोन उदाहरण द्या.
questions.answer: लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करणाऱ्या घटक भौगोलिक, आर्थिक, सामाजिक, राजकीय आहेत. भौगोलिक घटकांचे उदाहरण: स्थान, हवामान. आर्थिक घटकांचे उदाहरण: शेती, कारखानदारी.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येची घनता काढण्याचा सूत्र लिहा व त्याचे घटक सांगा.
questions.answer: लोकसंख्येची घनता = लोकसंख्या / क्षेत्रफळ. याचे घटक लोकसंख्या व क्षेत्रफळ आहेत.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लिंग गुणोत्तर काय म्हणते व ते कसे काढले जाते?
questions.answer: लिंग गुणोत्तर हे स्त्रियांची एकूण संख्या ते पुरुषांची एकूण संख्या यांचे गुणोत्तर आहे. ते स्त्रियांची संख्या / पुरुषांची संख्या * 1000 म्हणून काढले जाते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: स्थलांतर काय म्हणते व त्याचे दोन प्रकार सांगा.
questions.answer: स्थलांतर म्हणजे व्यक्ती किंवा समूहाने एका ठिकाणाहून दुसऱ्या ठिकाणी जाणे. त्याचे दोन प्रकार: अल्पकालिक व दीर्घकालिक स्थलांतर.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येची घनता जास्त असलेल्या प्रदेशात संसाधनांची उपलब्धता कमी होते का?
questions.answer: लोकसंख्येची घनता जास्त असलेल्या प्रदेशात अधिक लोक एका सीमित क्षेत्रफळात राहतात, त्यामुळे उपलब्ध संसाधनांची मागणी वाढते. यामुळे संसाधनांची प्रति व्यक्ति उपलब्धता कमी होते. उदाहरणार्थ, पाण्य, शेतीची जमीन, रोजगारासारखे संसाधन सीमित असल्याने त्यांची प्रति व्यक्ति उपलब्धता घटते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येचा वितरण फक्त भौगोलिक घटकांवर अवलंबून असतो का?
questions.answer: नाही, लोकसंख्येचा वितरण फक्त भौगोलिक घटकांवर अवलंबून असत नाही. त्याआडा आर्थिक, सामाजिक, राजकीय घटकांचे देखील लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम होतो. उदाहरणार्थ, उद्योगांची उपलब्धता (आर्थिक) व शासकीय धोरणे (राजकीय) लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करती.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लिंग गुणोत्तर हे लोकसंख्येची गुणवत्ता व वितरणावर कसा परिणाम देतो?
questions.answer: लिंग गुणोत्तर हे लोकसंख्येची सामाजिक संतुलन व गुणवत्ता दर्शवतो. लिंग गुणोत्तर जास्त असलेला प्रदेश स्त्री सशक्तिकरण, शिक्षण व आरोग्य क्षेत्रात प्रगती दर्शवतो. लिंग गुणोत्तर कमी असलेला प्रदेश लैंगिक असमानता, स्त्रियांची शिक्षण व रोजगारात अडचणी दर्शवतो, ज्यामुळे सामाजिक व आर्थिक विकास अडथळे येतो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करणाऱ्या घटकांचे विस्तृत स्पष्टीकरण द्या व त्यांचे उदाहरण द्या.
questions.answer: लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम करणाऱ्या घटक चार प्रकारचे आहेत: भौगोलिक, आर्थिक, सामाजिक, राजकीय. भौगोलिक घटकांसाठी स्थान, हवामान, मृदा, खनिज संफ्तती उदाहरणे आहेत. आर्थिक घटकांसाठी शेती, कारखानदारी, वाहतूक, बाजारपेठ उदाहरणे आहेत. सामाजिक घटकांसाठी वंश, धर्म, भाषा, रूढी व परंपरा उदाहरणे आहेत. राजकीय घटकांसाठी युद्ध, राजकीय अस्थिरता, राजकीय धोरण उदाहरणे आहेत. ये घटक एकत्र लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम देऊन त्याच वितरणाला आकार देते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येची घनता व लोकसंख्येची गुणवत्ता यांचे अर्थ स्पष्ट करा व त्यांचे संबंध सांगा.
questions.answer: लोकसंख्येची घनता हे एका क्षेत्रफळातील लोकसंख्या आहे, ज्यामुळे क्षेत्रातील संसाधनांची मागणी समजते. लोकसंख्येची गुणवत्ता हे साक्षरता, आरोग्य, लिंग गुणोत्तर, बयो गट व कार्यक्षम लोकसंख्या यासारखे घटकांमध्ये मापली जाते. घनता जास्त असल्यास संसाधनावर ताण पडतो, पण गुणवत्ता जास्त असल्यास मानवी विकास व आर्थिक प्रगती होतो. उदाहरणार्थ, केरळमध्ये घनता मध्यम असल्यापणे गुणवत्ता जास्त असल्याने मानवी विकास निर्देशांक जास्त आहे. त्यामुळे घनता व गुणवत्तेचा संतुलन विकासासाठी आवश्यक आहे.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येची घनता परिभाषित करा.
questions.answer: लोकसंख्येची घनता हे एका वर्ग किलोमीटर क्षेत्रफळातील लोकसंख्या आहे.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लिंग गुणोत्तर परिभाषित करा.
questions.answer: लिंग गुणोत्तर हे स्त्रियांची एकूण संख्या ते पुरुषांची एकूण संख्या यांचे गुणोत्तर आहे, जी सामान्यतः 1000 पुरुषांवर स्त्रियांची संख्या दर्शवते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: भौगोलिक घटक व आर्थिक घटक यांचे लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम यांचे फरक सांगा.
questions.answer: भौगोलिक घटकांसाठी स्थान, हवामान, मृदा, खनिज संफ्तती यांचे लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर प्राकृतिक पायाभूत परिणाम होते, जसे की पर्वतीय भागात लोकसंख्या कमी. आर्थिक घटकांसाठी शेती, उद्योग, वाहतूक यांचे लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर आजीविका व रोजगार आधारित परिणाम होते, जसे की उद्योग नगरींमध्ये लोकसंख्या वाढते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: सामाजिक घटक व राजकीय घटक यांचे लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम यांचे फरक सांगा.
questions.answer: सामाजिक घटकांसाठी वंश, धर्म, भाषा, रूढी व परंपरा यांचे लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर सांस्कृतिक व सामाजिक स्वीकार्यता आधारित परिणाम होते, जसे की विशिष्ट समुदाये एकत्र राहतात. राजकीय घटकांसाठी युद्ध, राजकीय अस्थिरता, राजकीय धोरण यांचे लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर शासकीय निर्णय व सुरक्षा आधारित परिणाम होते, जसे की युद्धामुळे पलायन होतो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: चिह्नित आकृती/आकडेबारी/नकाशा/टेबल काढा व तिचे चिह्ने लिहा.
questions.text: लोकसंख्येची घनता दर्शविणारा एक सरल बार ग्राफ काढा, जिथे X अक्षावर जिल्हे (पालघर, मुंबई, पुणे, नागपूर) व Y अक्षावर घनता (प्रति चौकिमी) दाखवा. तिचे चिह्ने लिहा.
questions.answer: X अक्ष: जिल्हे (पालघर, मुंबई, पुणे, नागपूर), Y अक्ष: लोकसंख्येची घनता (प्रति चौकिमी), बारचे उंची: पालघर-1200, मुंबई-20000, पुणे-600, नागपूर-300

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: चिह्नित आकृती/आकडेबारी/नकाशा/टेबल काढा व तिचे चिह्ने लिहा.
questions.text: लिंग गुणोत्तर दर्शविणारा एक सरल पाई चार्ट काढा, जिथे दोन भाग: स्त्री (48%) व पुरुष (52%) दाखवा. तिचे चिह्ने लिहा.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येचा वितरण फक्त आर्थिक घटकांवर अवलंबून असतो का? स्पष्टीकरण द्या.
questions.answer: नाही, लोकसंख्येचा वितरण फक्त आर्थिक घटकांवर अवलंबून असत नाही. भौगोलिक घटकांसाठी हवामान व मृदा लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम देतात, जसे की उष्ण हवामानातील मैदानात लोकसंख्या जास्त. सामाजिक घटकांसाठी धर्म व भाषा लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम देतात, जसे की विशिष्ट धार्मिक समुदाये एकत्र राहतात. राजकीय घटकांसाठी शासकीय धोरणे लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम देतात, जसे की विकासात्मक योजनांमुळे नवीन नगरींची स्थापना होतो. त्यामुळे सर्व च चारों प्रकारचे घटक लोकसंख्येच्या वितरणावर परिणाम देतात.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोकसंख्येची घनता जास्त असल्याने सामाजिक समस्यांना कसं वाढतो? स्पष्टीकरण द्या.
questions.answer: लोकसंख्येची घनता जास्त असल्याने एका सीमित क्षेत्रफळात अधिक लोक राहतात, त्यामुळे पाण्याची, शेतीची जमीन व रोजगारासारखे संसाधनांची कमी होते. यामुळे बेरोजगारी, अयोजित बस्ती व स्वास्थ्यसेवांची अयोग्यता वाढते. अतिरिक्त लोकसंख्या शैक्षणिक संस्थांवर देखील बोझ डालते, ज्यामुळे शाळांची कमी व शिक्षणाची गुणवत्ता घटते. यामुळे सामाजिक असंतुलन व असुरक्षा वाढतो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोह-पोलाद उद्योगासाठी आवश्यक कच्चा माल व ऊर्जा साधने _______ प्रदेशात उपलब्ध होतात.
questions.answer: जमशेदपूर नजीकच्या

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: उद्योगांचे स्वरूपानुसार वर्गीकरणात अवजड उद्योगांचा उदाहरण _______ आहे.
questions.answer: लोखंडी सळई तयार करणे

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: कृषीवर आधारित उद्योगांचे उदाहरण _______ आहे.
questions.answer: फळप्रक्रिया उद्योग

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: औद्योगिक विकासामुळे देशाच्या _______ वाढतो.
questions.answer: राष्ट्रीय उत्पन्नात

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: महाराष्ट्र राज्य ओद्योगिक विकास महामंडळ (MIDC) चे स्थापना _______ रोजी केली गेली.
questions.answer: ऑगस्ट १९६२

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: लोह-पोलाद उद्योगासाठी कच्चा माल वाहून नेतं किफायतशीर असतो.
questions.answer: चूक

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: औद्योगिक विकासामुळे देशातील नागरिकांचे रोजगार मिळतो.
questions.answer: बरोबर

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: माहिती तंत्रज्ञान उद्योगातील कामकाज मुख्यतः हाताळली जाते.
questions.answer: चूक

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची एका वाक्यात उत्तरे लिहा.
questions.text: उद्योगांचे सामाजिक दायित्व हे प्रत्येक उद्योगधंद्यासाठी अनिवार्य नाही.
questions.answer: चूक

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: खालील बायें कॉलमचे उद्योग आणि दायें कॉलमचे त्यांचे प्रकार जोडा.
questions.answer: लोह-पोलाद उद्योग – अवजड उद्योग, फळप्रक्रिया उद्योग – कृषीवर आधारित उद्योग, सूती वस्त्र तयार करणे – लघुउद्योग, माहिती तंत्रज्ञान उद्योग – सेवा उद्योग

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: जमशेदपूर लोह-पोलाद उद्योगाचे स्थानिकीकरण झाल्यACHE मुख्य कारण कोणता आहे?
options: कच्चा माल व ऊर्जा साधनेचे स्थानिक उपलब्धता
questions.answer: कच्चा माल व ऊर्जा साधनेचे स्थानिक उपलब्धता

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: खालीलपैकी कोणती उद्योगांचे वर्गीकरण कृषीवर आधारित उद्योग असते?
questions.answer: साखर उद्योग

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: औद्योगिक विकासामुळे देशातील दरडोई उत्पन्न कसे प्रभावित होतो?
questions.answer: वाढतो

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: महाराष्ट्र राज्य ओद्योगिक विकास महामंडळ (MIDC) चा मुख्य उद्देश कोणता आहे?
options: औद्योगिक क्षेत्रांची निर्मिती व रोजगार पुरवणे
questions.answer: औद्योगिक क्षेत्रांची निर्मिती व रोजगार पुरवणे

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोह-पोलाद उद्योगासाठी आवश्यक प्रमुख कच्चा माल कोणता आहे?
questions.answer: लोह अयस्क

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: कृषीवर आधारित उद्योगांचे एक प्रकार सांगा.
questions.answer: दुग्धव्यवसाय

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: माहिती तंत्रज्ञान उद्योगातील प्रमुख साधन कोणता आहे?
questions.answer: संगणक

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: उद्योगांचे सामाजिक दायित्व अंतर्गत केलेली कृती कोणती सांगी?
questions.answer: पर्यावरण संतुलन

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: भारतातील औद्योगिक विकासासाठी विशेष क्षेत्रे कोणती सांगी?
questions.answer: विशेष औद्योगिक क्षेत्र

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: उद्योगांचे स्वरूपानुसार वर्गीकरण कसे केला जातो?
questions.answer: उद्योगांचे स्वरूपानुसार त्यांना लघुउद्योग, मध्यम उद्योग आणि अवजड उद्योगमध्ये वर्गीकृत केला जातो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: कृषीवर आधारित उद्योगांचे उदाहरण दोन सांगा.
questions.answer: कृषीवर आधारित उद्योगांचे उदाहरण दुग्धव्यवसाय व फळप्रक्रिया उद्योग आहेत.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: औद्योगिक विकासामुळे देशाच्या आर्थिक विकासावर कोणता प्रभाव होतो?
questions.answer: औद्योगिक विकासामुळे देशाच्या राष्ट्रीय उत्पन्नात वाढ होते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: माहिती तंत्रज्ञान उद्योगाचा महत्त्व कोणता आहे?
questions.answer: माहिती तंत्रज्ञान उद्योग आजच्या युगातील एक महत्त्वपूर्ण अभियांत्रिकी शाखा आहे.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: उद्योगांचे सामाजिक दायित्व अंतर्गत कोणती कृती केली जाते?
questions.answer: उद्योगांचे सामाजिक दायित्व अंतर्गत पर्यावरण संरक्षण व societaly upayogi कार्य केले जाते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: जमशेदपूर लोह-पोलाद उद्योगाचे स्थानिकीकरण झाल्यACHE कारणे सांगा.
questions.answer: जमशेदपूर लोह-पोलाद उद्योगाचे स्थानिकीकरण झाल्यACHE मुख्य कारण कच्चा माल (लोह अयस्क) व ऊर्जा साधने (कोयला) चे स्थानिक उपलब्धता आहे. कच्चा माल अवजड असल्याने तो उद्योगांच्या जवळच उपलब्ध होणे आवश्यक आहे, ज्यामुळे वाहतूक खर्च कमी होतो. त्यामुळे कच्चा माल असलेल्या प्रदेशातच उद्योग स्थापित करणे फायद्याचे होते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: कृषीवर आधारित उद्योगांचे वैशिष्ट्ये सांगा.
questions.answer: कृषीवर आधारित उद्योग कृषी उत्पादनावर आधारित असतात, जसे की दुग्धव्यवसाय, फळप्रक्रिया, अन्नप्रक्रिया. यात कृषी क्षेत्रातून उत्पादित होणाऱ्या उत्पादनांवर प्रक्रिया केली जाते. यांमध्ये उत्पादनाची विविधता दिसते व ते सर्वत्र स्थापित झालेत.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: औद्योगिक विकासामुळे पर्यावरणावर होणारे परिणाम काय आहेत?
questions.answer: औद्योगिक विकासामुळे हवा, पाणी, ध्वनी व जमीन यांचे प्रदूषण होतो. उद्योगांमुळे अपायकारक अवशिष्ट पदार्थ व प्रदूषके बाहेर पडतात, ज्यामुळे पारिस्थितिकीय संतुलन बिगडतो. त्यामुळे प्रदूषण नियंत्रणाची आवश्यकता पडते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: महाराष्ट्र राज्य ओद्योगिक विकास महामंडळ (MIDC) चे फायदे सांगा.
questions.answer: MIDC चे फायदे आहेत: औद्योगिक क्षेत्रांची निर्मिती, युवकांना रोजगार मिळवणे, दरडोई उत्पन्न वाढवणे, प्रत्येक जिल्ह्यात औद्योगिक वाढण्यास मदत करणे, आणि उद्योगांना बीज, पाणी, कर यांमध्ये विशेष सुविधा पुरवणे.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लोह-पोलाद उद्योगासाठी कच्चा माल वाहून नेतं किफायतशीर नसतो का?
questions.answer: लोह-पोलाद उद्योगासाठी वापरण्यात येणारा कच्चा माल (लोह अयस्क) अवजड असतो, त्यामुळे तो वाहून नेतं किफायतशीर नसते. वाहतूक खर्च वाढतो, ज्यामुळे उत्पादनाचा खर्च वाढतो. त्यामुळे कच्चा माल असलेल्या प्रदेशातच उद्योग स्थापित करणे फायद्याचे होते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: औद्योगिक विकासामुळे देशातील नागरिकांचे राहणीमान उंचावते का?
questions.answer: औद्योगिक विकासामुळे उद्योगांमध्ये रोजगार मिळतो, ज्यामुळे नागरिकांचे आय वाढतो. त्यामुळे ते अधिक वस्तू व सेवांची खरेदी करू शकतात, ज्यामुळे त्यांचे राहणीमान उंचावते. साथै, राष्ट्रीय उत्पन्नात वाढ होण्यामुळे शासन देखील अधिक सुविधा पुरवू शकतो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: माहिती तंत्रज्ञान उद्योगातील कामकाज मुख्यतः संगणकादूबारे चालते का?
questions.answer: माहिती तंत्रज्ञान उद्योगातील कामकाज मुख्यतः संगणकादूबारे चालते, कारण यात तांत्रिक माहिती शोधणे, मिळवणे, विश्लेषण करणे, संग्रहित करणे व आलेखांच्या स्वरूपात त्यापासून पक्का माल तयार करणे जसे कामे केली जातात. यासाठी विशिष्ट संगणक प्रणाली आवश्यक आहे.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लघुउद्योग
questions.answer: लघुउद्योग हे त्यांचे भांडबल, श्रमसंख्या व गुंतवणूक सीमित असलेले उद्योग असतात, जसे की बेकरी, गुऱ्हाळ इत्यादी.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: कृषीवर आधारित उद्योग
questions.answer: कृषीवर आधारित उद्योग हे कृषी क्षेत्रातून उत्पादित होणाऱ्या उत्पादनांवर प्रक्रिया करणाऱ्या उद्योग असतात, जसे की दुग्धव्यवसाय, फळप्रक्रिया, अन्नप्रक्रिया इत्यादी.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: मध्यम उद्योग - अवजड उद्योग
questions.answer: मध्यम उद्योग आणि अवजड उद्योग यांतील फरक: 1. मध्यम उद्योगात भांडबल व श्रमसंख्या लघुउद्योगापेक्षा जास्त परंतु अवजड उद्योगापेक्षा कमी असते. 2. मध्यम उद्योगात गुंतवणूक सीमित असते, परंतु अवजड उद्योगात मोठी गुंतवणूक होते. 3. मध्यम उद्योगात उत्पादनाची क्षमता सीमित असते, अवजड उद्योगात मोठी उत्पादन क्षमता असते. 4. मध्यम उद्योगात साधारण तंत्रज्ञान वापरला जातो, अवजड उद्योगात उन्नत तंत्रज्ञान वापरला जातो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: कृषीवर आधारित उद्योग - अवजड उद्योग
questions.answer: कृषीवर आधारित उद्योग आणि अवजड उद्योग यांतील फरक: 1. कृषीवर आधारित उद्योग कृषी उत्पादनावर आधारित असतात, अवजड उद्योगात तो आवश्यक नाही. 2. कृषीवर आधारित उद्योगात उत्पादनाची विविधता दिसते, अवजड उद्योगात एकरूप उत्पादन होतो. 3. कृषीवर आधारित उद्योग सर्वत्र स्थापित झालेत, अवजड उद्योग विशिष्ट प्रदेशात स्थापित होतात. 4. कृषीवर आधारित उद्योगात लघु आकारचे उद्योग अधिक असते, अवजड उद्योगात मोठे उद्योग असते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: उद्योगांचे सामाजिक दायित्व अंतर्गत केलेली कृतींचा चित्र काढा व लेबल लिहा.
questions.answer: पर्यावरण संरक्षण, जलसंरक्षण, पेडे लागवणे, शाळा व आरोग्य केंद्रांची सहायता, रोजगार पुरवणे

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: जमशेदपूर लोह-पोलाद उद्योगाचे स्थानिकीकरण दर्शविणारा नकाशा काढा व लेबल लिहा.
questions.answer: जमशेदपूर, लोह अयस्क खदान, कोयला खदान, रेल्वे मार्ग, बंदरगाह

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: उद्योगांचे सामाजिक दायित्व स्पष्ट करा व त्यांचे महत्त्व सांगा.
questions.answer: उद्योगांचे सामाजिक दायित्व म्हणजे उद्योजक व उद्योगसमूहांचे समाजाप्रति जबाबदारीचे आचरण. यात पर्यावरण संरक्षण, नैसर्गिक संसाधांचे संधारण, पर्यावरण व्यवस्थापन योजना, आरोग्यविषयक सुविधा पुरवणे, गावातील विकास, निराधार व्यक्तींसाठी केंद्रे चालवणे, शिक्षा व कौशल्य विकासासाठी मदत करणे जसे कामे शमील आहेत. यामुळे उद्योगांचे उत्पादन परत पारिस्थितिकीय संतुलन बिगडत नाही. साथै, समाजातील विश्वास व सहयोग वाढतो, ज्यामुळे उद्योगांचे दीर्घकालीन विकास होतो. उद्योगांचे सामाजिक दायित्व पाळण्यामुळे शासनाकडून कर सवलत मिळतात व ब्रांड प्रतिष्ठा वाढते. त्यामुळे उद्योग नफा कमवून देखील समाजोपयोगी कार्य करू शकतात.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: महाराष्ट्र राज्य ओद्योगिक विकास महामंडळ (MIDC) चे स्थापना, उद्देश व फायदे सांगा.
questions.answer: महाराष्ट्र राज्य ओद्योगिक विकास महामंडळ (MIDC) चे स्थापना ऑगस्ट १९६२ रोजी केली गेली. त्याचा मुख्य उद्देश राज्यातील औद्योगिक क्षेत्रांची निर्मिती करणे, युवकांना रोजगार मिळवणे, दरडोई उत्पन्न वाढवणे आणि प्रत्येक जिल्ह्यात औद्योगिक वाढण्यास मदत करणे आहे. MIDC चे फायदे आहेत: औद्योगिक क्षेत्रे विकसित केली जातात, ज्या मध्ये उद्योगांना बीज, पाणी, कर यांमध्ये विशेष सुविधा पुरवली जाते. यामुळे उद्योग स्थापित करणे सोयले होते, उत्पादन वाढतो, रोजगार संधी मिळतात व राज्यातील आर्थिक विकास होतो. MIDC ने विविध उद्योगांना आधार पुरवले जसे की तंत्रज्ञान, वाहतूक, रसायन इत्यादी, ज्यामुळे महाराष्ट्रातील औद्योगिक विकासात महत्वपूर्ण योगदान झाला.

questions.answer: बरोबर

questions.answer: नकाशावरील एकक

questions.answer: लघुप्रमाण नकाशा देश, खंड, जग इत्यादी जसे विस्तृत भूभागासाठी वापरले जाते.

questions.text: १ सेमी > ५० किमी असे शब्दप्रमाणाचा अंकप्रमाण काय आहे?

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: नकाशाप्रमाण बदलले नसले तरीही शब्दप्रमाण व अंकप्रमाण बदलताहेत का? कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: नकाशाप्रमाण बदलले नसले तरीही शब्दप्रमाण व अंकप्रमाण बदलत नाहीत, कारण त्यांचा मूल्य नकाशाप्रमाणानुसार निर्धारित असतो. फक्त नकाशेचा आकार बदलले असल तर त्यामुळे नकाशावरील अंतर बदलते, त्यामुळे जमिनीवरील अंतर बदलून जातो, परंतु प्रमाणाचं गुणोत्तर समान राहतो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: जमिनीवरील दोन ठिकाणांचे अंतर ६० किमी आहे. नकाशावर त्यांचा अंतर ३ सेमी दर्शवले असल तर नकाशाप्रमाण काय आहे? शब्दप्रमाण व अंकप्रमाण द्या.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लघुप्रमाण व बृहत्प्रमाण नकाशे कोणतीन वापरली जातात? दोन-दोन उदाहरण द्या.
questions.answer: लघुप्रमाण नकाशा जगाचा नकाशा, देशाचा नकाशा वापरले जातात. बृहत्प्रमाण नकाशा शाळेचा नकाशा, गावाचा नकाशा वापरले जातात.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: नकाशे तयार करताना प्रमाण लिहावे लागते का? कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: होय, प्रमाण लिहावे लागते, कारण नकाशा फक्त चित्र नाही, त्यामुळे जमिनीवरील अंतर काय दर्शवतो हे जाणून घ्यायच्यासाठी प्रमाण आवश्यक आहे. प्रमाण न लिहिल्यास नकाशा अपूर्ण व भ्रमकारक ठरतो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची उत्तरे कारण देत्या ३-४ वाक्यात लिहा.
questions.text: नकाशाप्रमाण १:५,००,००० असे असल तर नकाशा लघुप्रमाण किंवा बृहत्प्रमाण? कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: नकाशा लघुप्रमाण आहे, कारण १:५,००,००० अंकप्रमाणात नकाशावरील एक सेमी जमिनीवरील ५ किमी दर्शवतो, ज्यामुळे विस्तृत भूभाग कमी जागेने दर्शवला जातो, ज्यामुळे ते लघुप्रमाण मानले जाते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची उत्तरे कारण देत्या ३-४ वाक्यात लिहा.
questions.text: शब्दप्रमाणात १ सेमी > १० किमी असे असल तर अंकप्रमाण काय होईल? प्रक्रिया सांगा.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची उत्तरे कारण देत्या ३-४ वाक्यात लिहा.
questions.text: नकाशे लहान करण्यासाठी रेषाप्रमाण वापरणे फायदेमंद आहे का? कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: होय, कारण नकाशेचा आकार बदलले नसले तरीही रेषाप्रमाण वैध राहतो, ज्यामुळे नकाशा लहान किंवा मोठा केल्यावर प्रमाण बदलण्याची गरज नाही, व रेषा स्वयंचलितपणे जमिनीवरील अंतर दर्शते remain.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: नकाशाप्रमाणाचे तीन प्रकार सांगा व त्यांचे उदाहरण द्या. त्यामुळे नकाशे वाचता यामुळे काय फायदा होतो?
questions.answer: नकाशाप्रमाणाचे तीन प्रकार: (१) शब्दप्रमाण - जyasathi परिमाणदर्शक शब्द वापरले जातात, उदा. १ सेमी > १० किमी. (२) अंकप्रमाण - फक्त अंक वापरले जातात, उदा. १:१०,००,०००. (३) रेषाप्रमाण - रेषाप्रमाणपट्टी वापरली जाते, ज्यामुळे नकाशेचा आकार बदलले नसले तरीही प्रमाण वैध राहते. नकाशे वाचता यामुळे फायदा होतो की जमिनीवरील अंतर सापडतो, रस्ता, नदी, पर्वत इत्यादीची ओळख होऊ शकतो, प्रवासाची योजना बनवली जाऊ शकते, व भौगोलिक माहिती स्पष्टपणे समजली जाऊ शकते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लघुप्रमाण व बृहत्प्रमाण नकाशांचे फरक सांगा. त्यांचे वापर कोणतीन क्षेत्रात केली जातात? उदाहरण द्या.
questions.answer: लघुप्रमाण नकाश्यात नकाशावरील एक सेमी जमिनीवरील अधिक दूरी दर्शवतो, त्यामुळे विस्तृत भूभाग कम जागेने दर्शवला जातो. उदा. १:५०,००,०००. बृहत्प्रमाण नकाश्यात नकाशावरील एक सेमी जमिनीवरील कम दूरी दर्शवतो, त्यामुळे संकीर्ण भाग जास्त तपशीलाने दर्शवला जातो. उदा. १:५,०००. लघुप्रमाण नकाशा देश, खंड, जग, राज्याचा रस्ता नकाशा वापरले जातात. बृहत्प्रमाण नकाशा शाळेचा नकाशा, गावाचा नकाशा, शेताचा आराखडा, इमारतची योजना वापरले जातात.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: शब्दप्रमाण
questions.answer: शब्दप्रमाण हे नकाशाप्रमाणाचा एक प्रकार आहे, जyasathi परिमाणदर्शक शब्द वापरले जातात जसे की १ सेमी > १० किमी.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लघुप्रमाण नकाशा
questions.answer: लघुप्रमाण नकाशा हे नकाशा आहे जyasathi नकाशावरील एक सेमी जमिनीवरील अधिक दूरी दर्शवतो, त्यामुळे विस्तृत भूभाग कम जागेने दर्शवला जातो, उदा. १:५०,००,०००.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: शब्दप्रमाण व अंकप्रमाण
questions.answer: शब्दप्रमाणात परिमाणदर्शक शब्द वापरले जातात (उदा. १ सेमी > १० किमी), अंकप्रमाणात फक्त अंक वापरले जातात (उदा. १:१०,००,०००). शब्दप्रमाण वाचण्यास सोपा असेल, अंकप्रमाणात गणिताने रूपांतर करायचे लागतात.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: लघुप्रमाण नकाशा व बृहत्प्रमाण नकाशा
questions.answer: लघुप्रमाण नकाश्यात जास्त भूभाग कमी जागेने दर्शवला जातो (उदा. १:५०,००,०००), बृहत्प्रमाण नकाश्यात कम भूभाग जास्त तपशीलाने दर्शवला जातो (उदा. १:५,०००). लघुप्रमाण नकाशा देश, खंड वापरले जातात, बृहत्प्रमाण नकाशा शाळा, गाव वापरले जातात.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील आकृती काढा व लेबल लिहा.
questions.text: रेषाप्रमाणपट्टी काढा व त्यावर नकाशावरील एकक व जमिनीवरील एकक लेबल लिहा.
questions.answer: नकाशावरील एकक (सेमी), जमिनीवरील एकक (किमी/मी)

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील आकृती काढा व लेबल लिहा.
questions.text: नकाशाप्रमाण दर्शविणाऱ्या आकृती काढा (उदा. १ सेमी > १० किमी) व त्यावर शब्दप्रमाण लिहा.
questions.answer: शब्दप्रमाण (१ सेमी > १० किमी)

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: नकाशाप्रमाण बदलले नसले तरीही रेषाप्रमाण बदलत नाही का? स्पष्ट करा.
questions.answer: नकाशाप्रमाण बदलले नसले तरीही रेषाप्रमाण बदलत नाही, कारण रेषाप्रमाण नकाशावर काढली जatele रेषा नकाशेचा आकार बदलले नसले तरीही वैध राहते. रेषा नकाशावरील एका लंबी दर्शवते, ज्यामुळे नकाशा लहान किंवा मोठा केल्यावर त्याची लंबीही समानुपाताने बदलते, परंतु नकाशावरील एका लंबीची जमिनीवरील अंतर दर्शवती capacitie समान राहते. त्यामुळे प्रमाण बदलण्याची गरज नाही.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: नकाशे तयार करताना जमिनीवरील अंतर माहित असणे आवश्यक आहे का? कारण सांगा.
questions.answer: होय, जमिनीवरील अंतर माहित असणे आवश्यक आहे, कारण नकाशाप्रमाण हे नकाशातील अंतर व जमिनीवरील प्रत्यक्ष अंतर यांचा गुणोत्तर असतो. जामिनीवरील अंतर माहित नसेल तर नकाशाप्रमाण काढता येईल नाही. प्रमाण काढून नकाशे तयार केल्यावर फक्त नकाशावरील अंतर मोजून जमिनीवरील अंतर काढता येईल, ज्यामुळे भौगोलिक अभ्यास, प्रवास योजना, शेताचं नकाशा, इ.स.साठी नकाशा उपयुक्त ठरतो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेटच्या प्रक्रियेचा पहा पायरी _______ आहे.
questions.answer: योजना

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेटत माहिती संकलन करण्यासाठी वापरलेली तंत्रज्ञानाची पद्धती _______ आहेत.
questions.answer: साक्षात्कार, प्रश्नावली, अवलोकन

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट अहवालातील 'आभार' विभागात आभार मानले जाणारे _______ समाविष्ट केले जातात.
questions.answer: शिक्षक, मार्गदर्शक, सहाय्यक

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशा तयार करण्यासाठी वापरलेला साधन _______ आहे.
questions.answer: मानचित्र

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशावर दर्शविण्याऱ्या महत्त्वाच्या ठिकाणांचे चिन्हे _______ म्हणतात.
questions.answer: संकेत

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील कथनांचा बरोबर चूक असे सांगा.
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट अहवालात प्रस्तावना भागात भेटीचा उद्देश व महत्त्व लिहावा.
questions.answer: बरोबर

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील कथनांचा बरोबर चूक असे सांगा.
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशा तयार करण्यासाठी फक्त हस्तलिखित पद्धत वापरली जाते.
questions.answer: चूक

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील कथनांचा बरोबर चूक असे सांगा.
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट अहवालात संदर्भसूची भागात वापरलेले साधने व स्त्रोत लिहावे.
questions.answer: बरोबर

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील कथनांचा बरोबर चूक असे सांगा.
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशावर दिशा सूचक नकाशा नक्की दाखवली जाते.
questions.answer: चूक

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: खालील क्षेत्रभेट अहवालाच्या भागांना त्यांच्या सामग्रीशी जोडा.
pairs: भेटीच्या कार्यालयातील कर्मचारींची संख्या व ओळख
भेटीमध्ये आढळली अडचणी व त्यांचे उपाय
भेटीसाठी मदत करणाऱ्यांचे नाव व आभार
questions.answer: प्रस्तावना – भेटीचा उद्देश, स्थान, काल, कार्यालयातील कार्यरत कर्मचारी – भेटीच्या कार्यालयातील कर्मचारींची संख्या व ओळख, येणाऱ्या समस्या/उपाययोजना – भेटीमध्ये आढळली अडचणी व त्यांचे उपाय, आभार – भेटीसाठी मदत करणाऱ्यांचे नाव व आभार

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशा तयार करण्यासाठी वापरलेला मानक अपूर्णांक कोणता आहे?

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट अहवालातील 'संदर्भसूची' भागात कोणती माहिती द्यावी?
questions.answer: उपयोग केलेली पुस्तके, वेबसाइट, दस्तऐवज

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशावर दर्शविण्याऱ्या संकेतांचा वापर कोणती पद्धतीने केला जातो?
questions.answer: रंगे व आकारे

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट अहवालातील 'आभार' विभागाचा मुख्य उद्देश कोणता आहे?
questions.answer: भेटीसाठी मदत करणाऱ्यांचे आभार मानणे

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील पर्यायांमधील विसंगत शोधा व कारण सांगा.
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट अहवालाचे भाग: प्रस्तावना, कार्यालयातील कार्यरत कर्मचारी, कार्यालयाचे कार्य, नकाशा तयार करणे
questions.answer: नकाशा तयार करणे - हे क्षेत्रभेट अहवालाचे भाग नाहीत, तर तयार करण्याचा पद्धती आहे.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील पर्यायांमधील विसंगत शोधा व कारण सांगा.
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशावर वापरलेली संकेत पद्धती: रंगे, आकारे, प्रतीके, शब्दे
questions.answer: शब्दे - क्षेत्रभेट नकाशे प्रायः शब्दे वापरत नाहीत, तर रंगे, आकारे, प्रतीके वापरले जातात.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट अहवालातील 'आभार' विभागात कोणते शब्द वापरला जातो?
questions.answer: धन्यवाद

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशा तयार करण्यासाठी वापरलेली साधनाची एक शब्दे नाव?
questions.answer: मानचित्र

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशावर दर्शविण्याऱ्या महत्त्वाच्या ठिकाणांचे चिन्हे कोणते नाव देण्यात यात?
questions.answer: संकेत

questions.subject: Geography

questions.answer: उपयोग केलेली पुस्तके, वेबसाइट, दस्तऐवजांची यादी.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट अहवालातील प्रस्तावना व आभार भागांचे महत्त्व सांगा.
questions.answer: प्रस्तावना भागात भेटीचा उद्देश, स्थान, वेळ, व सहभागींची माहिती दिली जाते, ज्यामुळे वाचकाला संदर्भ मिळतो. आभार भागात भेटीसाठी मदत करणाऱ्यांचे नाव व आभार मानले जाते, ज्यामुळे त्यांचे योगदान मान्यता मिळतो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशा तयार करण्यासाठी वापरलेली साधने व त्यांचे वापर सांगा.
questions.answer: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशा तयार करण्यासाठी मानचित्र, रंगे, आकारे, प्रतीके वापरले जातात. मानचित्रावर भेटीच्या स्थानाची ओळख केली जाते, त्यानंतर रंगे व आकारे वापरून विविध ठिकाणे दर्शवितात, प्रतीके वापरून विशिष्ट सुविधा दर्शवितात.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट अहवालातील 'संदर्भसूची' भागाचे उद्देश व सामग्री सांगा.
questions.answer: संदर्भसूची भागात क्षेत्रभेट करण्यापूर्वी व दरम्यान वापरलेली पुस्तके, वेबसाइट, दस्तऐवजांची यादी दिली जाते. हे वाचकांना माहितीचे स्त्रोत ओळखणे व अहवालाची विश्वासार्हता वाढविण्यास मदत करते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट प्रक्रिया चालू करण्यापूर्वी योजना तयार करण्याचे आवश्यकते सांगा.
questions.answer: योजना तयार करण्यामुळे क्षेत्रभेटचा उद्देश स्पष्ट होतो, आवश्यक साधने व माहिती संकलनाची पद्धती ठरवली जाते, व वेळ व संसाधनांचे योग्य नियोजन होतो, ज्यामुळे क्षेत्रभेट सुगमतापूर्ण व प्रभावी होतो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची उत्तर द्या. कारण सांगा.
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट अहवालात प्रस्तावना भाग लिहायचे का?
questions.answer: प्रस्तावना भाग लिहायचे आहे कारण त्यात भेटीचा उद्देश, स्थान, वेळ, व सहभागींची माहिती दिली जाते. हे वाचकाला क्षेत्रभेटाच्या पृष्ठभूमीची ओळख करतो व अहवालाच्या शेवtetसाठी संदर्भ तयार करते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची उत्तर द्या. कारण सांगा.
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशावर संकेत वापरायचे का?
questions.answer: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशावर संकेत वापरायचे आहे कारण ते विविध ठिकाणे, सुविधा, व भौगोलिक वैशिष्ट्ये सोप्या व स्पष्टपणे दर्शवितात. संकेत वापरण्यामुळे नकाशा वाचणे सोपे होतो व माहिती तुलनेत अचूकपणे समजली जाते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.instruction: खालील प्रश्नांची उत्तर द्या. कारण सांगा.
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट अहवालातील 'आभार' विभाग लिहायचे का?
questions.answer: आभार विभाग लिहायचे आहे कारण भेटीसाठी मदत करणाऱ्यांचे, जसे की शिक्षक, मार्गदर्शक, व सहाय्यक, त्यांचे योगदान मान्यता मिळवण्यासाठी. हे त्यांचे प्रयत्न सराहनीय ठेवतो व सामाजिक कृतज्ञता दर्शवतो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट अहवाल तयार करण्याची संपूर्ण प्रक्रिया सांगा. योजना तयार करणे, माहिती संकलन, नकाशा तयार करणे, अहवाल लिहणे, व आभार देणे यांचा समावेश करा.
questions.answer: क्षेत्रभेट अहवाल तयार करण्याची प्रक्रिया खालील पायरींच्या पालनाने केली जाते: १) योजना तयार करणे: क्षेत्रभेटचा उद्देश, स्थान, वेळ, व सहभागींची ओळख केली जाते. आवश्यक प्रश्नावली व साधने तयार केली जातात. २) माहिती संकलन: भेटीच्या दिवस साक्षात्कार, अवलोकन, व प्रश्नावलीद्वारा माहिती जमा केली जाते. नकाशे, चित्रे, व छायाचित्रे देखील वापरले जातात. ३) नकाशा तयार करणे: माहितीच्या आधारावर मानचित्र तयार केला जातो, जिथे रंगे, आकारे, व प्रतीके वापरून विविध ठिकाणे व सुविधा दर्शवितात. ४) अहवाल लिहणे: प्रस्तावना, कार्यालयातील कार्यरत कर्मचारी, कार्यालयाचे कार्य, येणाऱ्या समस्या/उपाययोजना, आभार, व संदर्भसूची यांचे भाग लिहिल्याने अहवाल तयार केला जातो. ५) आभार देणे: भेटीसाठी मदत करणाऱ्यांचे नाव लिहून त्यांचे आभार मानला जातो. हे सर्व पायरे पूर्ण झाल्यानंतर क्षेत्रभेट अहवाल तयार होतो.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशा तयार करण्यामध्ये वापरलेली संकेत पद्धती व त्यांचे महत्त्व सांगा. विविध प्रकारचे संकेत, त्यांचे वापर, व नकाशा वाचण्यात त्यांची भूमिका सांगा.
questions.answer: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशा तयार करण्यामध्ये संकेत पद्धती खूप महत्त्वाची आहे. संकेत म्हणजे रंगे, आकारे, प्रतीके, व प्रतीकात्मक चिन्हे जे विविध ठिकाणे, सुविधा, व भौगोलिक वैशिष्ट्ये दर्शवितात. उदाहरणार्थ: हिरवा रंग वन क्षेत्र दर्शवितो, नीला रंग पाणी दर्शवितो, भाकरी आकार पर्वत दर्शवितो, त्रिकोण आकार पावसाचे संकेत दर्शवितो, घराचा प्रतीक निवासी क्षेत्र दर्शवितो, शाळेचा प्रतीक शैक्षिक क्षेत्र दर्शवितो. हे संकेत नकाशा वाचणे सोपे बनवितात कारण ते भाषा स्वतंत्र हवे व तात्काळिक ओळख करतात. संकेत वापरण्यामुळे नकाशावर अतिरिक्त लिहित न घेऊन देखील माहिती स्पष्टपणे संप्रेषित होतो. हे विद्यार्थ्यांना भौगोलिक माहिती समजणे व तुलना करणे सोपे बनवितात.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट
questions.answer: क्षेत्रभेट म्हणजे काही विशिष्ट स्थानावर जाणे व त्यातील भौगोलिक, सामाजिक, आर्थिक व पर्यावरणीय aspects चा अवलोकन, माहिती संकलन, व विश्लेषण करणे.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट अहवाल
questions.answer: क्षेत्रभेट अहवाल म्हणजे क्षेत्रभेट प्रक्रियेचा दस्तऐवजीकरण जिथे योजना, माहिती संकलन, अवलोकन, नकाशा तयार करणे, व आभार देणे यांचा समावेश केला जातो, ज्यामुळे भेटीच्या अनुभवाची संरचित पेशकश केली जाते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट अहवालातील प्रस्तावना व आभार
questions.answer: प्रस्तावना भागात भेटीचा उद्देश, स्थान, वेळ, व सहभागींची माहिती दिली जाते, ज्यामुळे वाचकाला संदर्भ मिळतो. आभार भागात भेटीसाठी मदत करणाऱ्यांचे नाव व आभार मानले जाते, ज्यामुळे त्यांचे योगदान मान्यता मिळतो. प्रस्तावना अहवालाची सुरुवात करते, आभार अहवालाचा शेवट होते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशा व सामान्य नकाशा
questions.answer: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशा विशिष्ट भेटीच्या स्थानावर आधारित असतो व त्यात फक्त भेटीसंबंधी माहिती दर्शविती जाते, जसे की भेटीच्या ठिकाणे, सुविधा, व समस्या. सामान्य नकाशा विस्तृत प्रदेशाचा प्रतिनिधित्व करते व त्यात सर्वसाधारण भौगोलिक वैशिष्ट्ये, जसे की नद्या, पर्वत, जिल्हे, दर्शवितात. क्षेत्रभेट नकाशा प्रायः लहान प्रमाणाचा असतो (जसे की 1:10000), ज्यामुळे तपशीलवार माहिती मिळते, जबकि सामान्य नकाशा मोठा प्रमाणाचा असतो (जसे की 1:100000) व सर्वसाधारण माहिती देते.

questions.answer: भेटीच्या स्थानाची ओळख, विविध ठिकाणे (शाळा, कार्यालय, पाणी स्रोत), दिशा सूचक (उत्तर, दक्षिण, पूर्व, पश्चिम), संकेत पद्धती (हिरवा रंग - वन, नीला रंग - पाणी, भाकरी आकार - पर्वत, घराचा प्रतीक - निवासी क्षेत्र)

questions.answer: प्रस्तावना, कार्यालयातील कार्यरत कर्मचारी, कार्यालयाचे कार्य, येणाऱ्या समस्या/उपाययोजना, आभार, संदर्भसूची

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट प्रक्रिया चालू करण्यापूर्वी योजना तयार करणे कोणतींती आवश्यक आहे? त्याचे फायदे सांगा.
questions.answer: क्षेत्रभेट प्रक्रिया चालू करण्यापूर्वी योजना तयार करणे आवश्यक आहे कारण त्यात भेटीचा उद्देश स्पष्ट होतो, आवश्यक साधने व माहिती संकलनाची पद्धती ठरवली जाते, व वेळ व संसाधनांचे योग्य नियोजन होतो. यामुळे क्षेत्रभेट सुगमतापूर्ण व प्रभावी होतो, अनावश्यक खर्च व वेळाची बर्बादी टाळली जाते, व माहिती संकलनाची अचूकता वाढते. योजना न झाल्यास क्षेत्रभेट असंगठित होऊ शकतो व आवश्यक माहिती चूकू शकते.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.text: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशावर संकेत पद्धती वापरण्याचे फायदे सांगा. त्यामुळे नकाशा वाचणे कसे सोपे होतो?
questions.answer: क्षेत्रभेट नकाशावर संकेत पद्धती वापरण्याचे फायदे हे की ते भाषा स्वतंत्र हवे, तात्काळिक ओळख करतात, व अतिरिक्त लिहित न घेऊन देखील माहिती स्पष्टपणे संप्रेषित होतात. संकेत वापरण्यामुळे नकाशा वाचणे सोपे होतो कारण रंगे, आकारे, व प्रतीके वापरून विविध ठिकाणे, सुविधा, व भौगोलिक वैशिष्ट्ये सोप्या पद्धतीने दर्शवितात. हे विद्यार्थ्यांना नकाशा त्वरितपणे समजणे व तुलना करणे सोपे बनवितात, ज्यामुळे शिकण्याचा प्रक्रिया प्रभावी होतो.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: How are photographs useful as a source of modern Indian history?
questions.answer: Photographs provide visual proof of historical events, people, clothing, and structures. They help us see what people looked like and how places appeared in the past. Compared to paintings, they are considered more reliable and authentic.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What are audio-visual sources? Give two examples from the chapter.
questions.answer: Audio-visual sources combine sound and visuals to record history. Examples include films of the Dandi Yatra and recordings of speeches by leaders like Rabindranath Tagore singing the national anthem.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why is it important to preserve historical sources like films and recordings?
questions.answer: Preserving films and recordings ensures that future generations can access authentic records of historical events. It helps maintain the rich tradition and variety of modern Indian history. Without preservation, valuable sources may be lost forever.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why are photographs considered more reliable than paintings for studying modern Indian history?
questions.answer: Photographs are considered more reliable because they capture actual scenes as they exist, without artistic interpretation. Paintings may reflect the artist’s imagination or bias, while photographs provide objective visual evidence. This makes photographs better for accurate historical study.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why are Powadas considered important sources for studying the freedom movement?
questions.answer: Powadas are important because they were composed during the freedom movement and reflect the emotions and struggles of the time. They motivated people and spread awareness about revolutionary acts. Being oral traditions, they preserve the spirit of resistance in a memorable form.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why are films considered a unique discovery of modern technology in the study of history?
questions.answer: Films are unique because they record both moving images and sound, allowing us to see and hear historical events as they happened. This audio-visual format provides a more immersive and realistic understanding than written or oral sources alone. They preserve gestures, expressions, and context that other sources may miss.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the different types of sources used to study modern Indian history with examples.
questions.answer: Modern Indian history is studied using written, oral, material, and audio-visual sources. Written sources include newspapers, books, and official records. Oral sources are Powadas, inspirational songs, and recorded speeches. Material sources consist of photographs, films, and objects like tools or clothing. Audio-visual sources such as films of the Dandi Yatra and recordings of leaders’ speeches provide both sight and sound. These sources together give a rich, varied, and authentic picture of India’s recent past.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain how technology has improved the preservation and study of historical sources in the modern period.
questions.answer: In the modern period, technology such as photography, recording, and filmmaking has greatly improved how we preserve and study history. Photographs capture real images of people and events, making history more visual and authentic. Recordings save voices and speeches, allowing us to hear leaders’ words exactly as spoken. Films combine visuals and audio to show events in motion, giving a lifelike experience of the past. These tools help store information accurately and share it widely. Unlike older periods that relied on manuscripts or paintings, modern technology ensures that history is recorded with greater accuracy and can be passed on to future generations.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Oral sources
questions.answer: Oral sources are spoken traditions, such as songs, stories, and speeches, passed down through generations by word of mouth and used to study history.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Audio-visual sources
questions.answer: Audio-visual sources are historical records that combine both sound and visual elements, such as films and video recordings, used to study past events.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: How did the discovery of photography change the way we study modern Indian history?
questions.answer: The discovery of photography allowed historians to capture real-life images of people, events, and places, providing visual proof of the past. Unlike paintings, which could be imaginary or biased, photographs showed actual appearances and surroundings. This made historical study more accurate and objective. Photographs helped document the freedom movement, showing processions, leaders, and public reactions. Over time, they became a vital source for understanding social and political changes in modern India.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why are films considered important sources for studying events like the Dandi Yatra?
questions.answer: Films are important because they record events in motion, allowing viewers to see how people moved, dressed, and behaved during historical moments. The film of the Dandi Yatra shows Gandhi and followers walking, giving a real sense of the event’s scale and spirit. It captures facial expressions, crowd reactions, and the route taken, which written descriptions might miss. Films also preserve the atmosphere and emotions of the time. As audio-visual sources, they make history more engaging and authentic for learners and researchers.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the impact of the Renaissance on European society.
questions.answer: The Renaissance led to a revival of Greek and Roman art, literature, and philosophy. It promoted humanism, encouraging people to value human potential and achievements. This shift in outlook reduced the dominance of religious dogma and encouraged scientific inquiry and individual expression.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why did European countries seek new trade routes to Asia in the 15th century?
questions.answer: European countries sought new trade routes to Asia because the Ottoman Turks captured Constantinople in 1453, blocking the traditional overland routes. This made trade difficult and expensive, prompting explorers to find sea routes to access Asian spices, silk, and wealth directly.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: How did the Battle of Plassey contribute to the foundation of British rule in India?
questions.answer: The Battle of Plassey in 1757 resulted in the defeat of Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah due to the betrayal of Mir Jafar. This victory allowed the British East India Company to install Mir Jafar as a puppet Nawab and gain control over Bengal’s resources, laying the foundation for British political dominance in India.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the main causes of the American War of Independence?
questions.answer: The American colonies revolted against British rule due to oppressive taxes and restrictions imposed by the English Parliament without colonial representation. The colonies resented laws like the Stamp Act and Tea Act, which they viewed as violations of their rights. This led to organized resistance and eventually war for independence.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why is the period of Renaissance also known as the 'Age of Discovery'?
questions.answer: The Renaissance period is also known as the 'Age of Discovery' because it was marked by significant geographical explorations. During this time, European sailors like Vasco-da-Gama and Christopher Columbus discovered new sea routes and lands, leading to increased global contact, trade, and the exchange of ideas, which complemented the intellectual and cultural revival of the era.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why did the Industrial Revolution begin in England?
questions.answer: The Industrial Revolution began in England due to several factors: availability of capital from trade, abundant natural resources like coal and iron, a stable political environment, a strong navy protecting trade, and a large workforce from rural migration. Additionally, England had a culture of innovation and scientific thinking that encouraged technological inventions.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why did Siraj-ud-Daulah oppose the British East India Company?
questions.answer: Siraj-ud-Daulah opposed the British East India Company because they misused the trade concessions granted by the Mughal Emperor, fortified Calcutta without his permission, and interfered in Bengal’s internal affairs. He viewed these actions as a threat to his sovereignty and an insult to his authority as Nawab.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the course and consequences of the French Revolution.
questions.answer: The French Revolution began in 1789 when the common people, burdened by heavy taxes and food shortages, rose against the absolute monarchy and feudal privileges. The storming of the Bastille symbolized the start of the revolution. The National Assembly abolished feudalism and declared the Rights of Man and of the Citizen. King Louis XVI was executed, and a republic was established. The revolution spread ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity across Europe. It ended the monarchy temporarily, led to the rise of Napoleon, and inspired future democratic movements worldwide. The revolution also weakened the power of the Church and aristocracy, paving the way for modern secular and democratic states.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain how the Industrial Revolution transformed society and economy in Europe.
questions.answer: The Industrial Revolution brought about a shift from hand production to machine-based manufacturing in factories. This led to mass production, lower costs, and increased availability of goods. Urbanization accelerated as people moved from rural areas to cities for factory work. New social classes emerged: the industrial bourgeoisie (factory owners) and the urban working class (laborers). While it boosted economic growth and technological progress, it also brought poor working conditions, child labor, and overcrowded cities. Innovations like the steam engine, railways, and steamers revolutionized transport and communication. The revolution laid the foundation for modern capitalism and transformed Europe into the 'Workshop of the World'.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Imperialism
questions.answer: Imperialism is a policy or practice by which a powerful country extends its control over weaker territories or countries, often through colonization, military force, or economic dominance, to exploit their resources and markets.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Capitalism
questions.answer: Capitalism is an economic system in which trade, industry, and the means of production are privately owned and operated for profit, with prices, production, and distribution determined by competition in a free market.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: How did geographical discoveries lead to the rise of trading companies in Europe?
questions.answer: Geographical discoveries opened new sea routes to Asia and Africa, enabling direct access to valuable goods like spices, silk, and precious metals. To manage the risks and costs of long-distance trade, merchants pooled their resources and formed joint-stock trading companies. These companies, such as the British and Dutch East India Companies, were granted monopolies and military support by their governments. They established trading posts and colonies, gradually expanding political control. This system allowed European nations to accumulate wealth and establish global trade networks.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the effects of the American War of Independence on Europe?
questions.answer: The American War of Independence inspired liberal and nationalist movements across Europe by proving that colonies could successfully overthrow imperial rule. It challenged the idea of divine right monarchy and strengthened Enlightenment ideals of liberty and self-governance. The French, who had supported the Americans, faced financial strain from the war, contributing to the outbreak of their own revolution. The loss of the American colonies prompted Britain to focus more on expanding its empire in India and Africa. Overall, the event marked a shift in global power and encouraged demands for democratic reforms in European societies.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the main features of the Permanent Settlement introduced by Lord Cornwallis in Bengal.
questions.answer: The Permanent Settlement fixed land revenue demand permanently on zamindars, made them proprietors of land, and ensured a stable income for the British. It was introduced in 1793 in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa. However, it led to exploitation of peasants as zamindars increased rents while revenue remained fixed.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the objectives of Lord Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance system?
questions.answer: The Subsidiary Alliance aimed to establish British paramountcy over Indian states by stationing British troops in their territories, requiring rulers to accept a British Resident, and prohibiting alliances with other powers without British consent. It allowed the British to expand control without direct annexation.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: How did the British land revenue policies lead to the exploitation of farmers?
questions.answer: The British fixed revenue in cash, which had to be paid even during crop failures, forcing farmers to sell produce at low prices, borrow from moneylenders at high interest, and eventually lose their land. Revenue systems like Ryotwari and Mahalwari also subjected farmers to frequent reassessments and harsh collection.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What changes were introduced in the Indian army after the Revolt of 1857?
questions.answer: After 1857, the proportion of British soldiers in the Indian army was increased, artillery was placed exclusively under British control, and recruitment was based on the 'divide and rule' policy, favouring certain castes and communities considered loyal to prevent unity among sepoys.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why did the British introduce the Permanent Settlement in Bengal?
questions.answer: The British introduced the Permanent Settlement to ensure a fixed and regular income from land revenue, reduce the need for frequent revenue assessments, and create a loyal class of zamindars who would support British rule in exchange for hereditary rights over land.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why did the commercialisation of agriculture under British rule harm Indian farmers?
questions.answer: The commercialisation of agriculture forced farmers to grow cash crops like cotton and indigo for export instead of food crops, making them dependent on market prices and vulnerable to fluctuations, while food security declined and famines increased due to reduced grain cultivation.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Why was the Regulating Act of 1773 considered a landmark in British administration in India?
questions.answer: The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first step by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India, establishing a centralized administration by appointing a Governor General of Bengal and creating a Supreme Court at Calcutta, thus beginning parliamentary control over Company rule.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the effects of British land revenue policies on rural life in India.
questions.answer: British land revenue systems such as Permanent Settlement, Ryotwari, and Mahalwari disrupted the traditional village economy. Revenue was demanded in cash, forcing farmers to grow cash crops and borrow money, leading to debt and land loss. Zamindars and moneylenders exploited peasants, while frequent famines worsened due to neglect of irrigation and food crops. The rural population faced increasing poverty, indebtedness, and loss of land ownership, weakening self-sufficient village communities.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain how British rule led to the decline of traditional industries in India.
questions.answer: British economic policies destroyed traditional Indian industries by imposing heavy tariffs on Indian goods entering Britain while allowing duty-free or low-tariff entry of British manufactured goods into India. Machine-made textiles from Britain flooded Indian markets, undercutting handloom weavers. Lack of state support, raw material shortages, and colonial trade policies led to the collapse of industries like textiles, metalwork, and shipbuilding, causing widespread unemployment among artisans and de-industrialisation of rural India.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Subsidiary Alliance
questions.answer: A system introduced by Lord Wellesley under which Indian rulers accepted British protection in exchange for disbanding their own armies, accepting a British Resident, and not forming alliances with other powers without British consent.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Commercialisation of Agriculture
questions.answer: The shift from growing food crops for domestic use to cultivating cash crops like cotton, indigo, and tea for sale in the market, often under British encouragement or pressure.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the role of the Civil Services in strengthening British rule in India.
questions.answer: The Civil Services were established to provide a loyal, efficient, and merit-based administrative machinery for British governance in India. Officers were recruited through competitive examinations in Britain, ensuring loyalty to the Crown. They held key positions in revenue collection, law and order, and policy implementation. The Indian Civil Service (ICS) became the 'steel frame' of British rule, enabling control over vast territories with minimal military presence. Over time, it facilitated uniform administration and the integration of princely states into the British Indian system.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the impact of the introduction of railways and telegraph on India during British rule.
questions.answer: The introduction of railways in 1853 and telegraph in the same year revolutionised transport and communication in India. Railways enabled faster movement of raw materials from interiors to ports and finished goods from ports to markets, boosting colonial trade and administrative control. They also facilitated troop movement during uprisings. The telegraph allowed instant communication between British officials across India and with London, improving coordination and response to emergencies. While these developments aided colonial exploitation, they also later helped nationalist movements by connecting people and spreading ideas.

questions.answer: The main aim of the Prarthana Samaj was to reform society based on principles like opposition to idol worship, monotheism, and opposition to rituals, stressing devotion and prayers.

questions.answer: Swami Vivekananda's message to the Indian youth was, "Arise, Awake and stop not till the goal is achieved."

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the purpose of the Singh Sabha established at Amritsar?
questions.answer: The Singh Sabha was established at Amritsar to achieve reforms in the Sikh religion, spread education among the Sikh community, and bring in modernization among them.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the contribution of Ramabai Ranade through the Seva Sadan Institute?
questions.answer: Through the Seva Sadan Institute, Ramabai Ranade started the Nursing course for women and demanded the right to vote for women.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the aim of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh?
questions.answer: The aim of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh was to set up a disciplinary and virtuous organization of Hindu youth.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Write a short note on the principles of Brahmo Samaj.
questions.answer: The Brahmo Samaj, established by Raja Rammohan Roy, was based on principles of monotheism, caste and class equality, protest against rituals, and following the way of prayers. He also opposed Sati practice, child marriage, and the Purdah system, while promoting widow remarriage and female education.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What efforts did Mahatma Phule take for the emancipation of women?
questions.answer: Mahatma Phule started the first school for girls in Pune in 1848 with the support of his wife Savitribai Phule. He also established the 'Bal Hatya Pratibandhak Gruha' in his own house and conducted a strike of barbers against the custom of shaving the heads of widows, all for the emancipation of women.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the social reforms advocated by Sir Sayyad Ahmad Khan?
questions.answer: Sir Sayyad Ahmad Khan started social reforms among the Muslim community. He established 'The Mohammedan Literary Society' and 'The Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College'. He advocated western science and technology, firmly believing that Muslims could make progress only by studying modern education and science.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the role of newspapers and magazines during the Rennaissance period in India?
questions.answer: During the Rennaissance period, new newspapers and magazines became a source of social reform and political awakening. They provided a platform for educated thinkers to create public awareness through writings, discuss social problems, and express thoughts on social reforms, inspiring people to gain independence.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: The modern educated Indians became aware of the backwardness of India.
questions.answer: The modern educated Indians became aware of the backwardness of India because they realized it was due to superstitions, casteism, old customs, the class system, and a lack of critical outlook. Exposure to Western thoughts and culture through English education made them understand the need to eradicate these flaws for the country's progress.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Mahatma Phule conducted a strike of barbers.
questions.answer: Mahatma Phule conducted a strike of barbers against the custom of shaving the heads of widows. This practice was a symbol of the miserable position of women in society and was part of his broader efforts to challenge unjust social customs and promote the emancipation of women.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: The 'Go Back to the Vedas' slogan was given by Arya Samaj.
questions.answer: The 'Go Back to the Vedas' slogan was given by Arya Samaj because Swami Dayanand Saraswati believed that the ancient Vedic religion was the true religion. He asserted that it had no place for casteism and promoted gender equality, thus advocating a return to these original Vedic principles.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the contributions of Maharshi Dhondo Karve to women's education and empowerment.
questions.answer: Maharshi Dhondo Karve made significant contributions to women's education and empowerment. He started the 'Anath Balikashram', an orphanage for girls, with the intention of providing education to all women and making them self-reliant. Through his relentless efforts, the first women's university was established in the 20th century, a landmark achievement that opened doors for higher education for women in India. His work aimed at ensuring women could stand on their own feet, challenging societal norms that restricted their access to education and independence.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the concept of 'Indian Rennaissance' and its impact on Indian society.
questions.answer: The 'Indian Rennaissance' refers to the intellectual awakening in contemporary Indian society during the 19th century. This era saw the spread of new thoughts, ideas, and philosophy, largely influenced by Western education and culture. Educated Indians became aware of the backwardness caused by superstitions, casteism, and old customs. This awakening led to significant changes in social, religious, economic, and cultural aspects of Indian society. Thinkers started social awareness campaigns through writings to eradicate flaws and create a new society based on humanity, equality, and fraternity. This period marked the beginning of various social and religious reform movements that aimed to modernize and uplift Indian society.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Monotheism' as understood by the Brahmo Samaj.
questions.answer: Monotheism, as understood by the Brahmo Samaj, refers to the belief in one God, rejecting the worship of multiple deities or idols. It was a core principle advocated by Raja Rammohan Roy, emphasizing a singular divine entity and opposing polytheism and idol worship prevalent in society.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Keshavapan' in the context of women's position in British India.
questions.answer: Keshavapan refers to the custom of shaving the heads of widows, a practice that symbolized their marginalized and miserable position in society during the British rule in India. It was one of the many unjust customs that social reformers like Mahatma Phule actively protested against.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the principles and work of the Prarthana Samaj.
questions.answer: The Prarthana Samaj was founded by members of the dissolved Paramhansa Sabha, with Dr. Atmaram Pandurang as its first President. Its core principles included opposition to idol worship, monotheism, and opposition to rituals, stressing instead on devotion and prayers. Prominent figures like Justice Ranade and Dr. R. G. Bhandarkar furthered its work. For social reform, the Prarthana Samaj established orphanages, institutions for women's education, night schools for workers, and societies for Dalits. Maharshi Vitthal Ramji Shinde, a member, started the 'Depressed Classes Mission' to address social problems, demonstrating the Samaj's commitment to practical social upliftment.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the role of Raja Rammohan Roy in the social and religious reforms in Bengal.
questions.answer: Raja Rammohan Roy was a pioneer of social and religious reforms in Bengal, establishing the Brahmo Samaj in 1828. He was a scholar of many languages and religions, which shaped his ideology of Advaita philosophy. His principles included monotheism, caste and class equality, and protest against rituals, advocating prayers as a way of devotion. He staunchly opposed the Sati practice, child marriage, and the Purdah system, while actively promoting widow remarriage and female education. He also founded the Hindu College in Kolkata and raised public awareness through his newspaper 'Samvad Kaumudi', making significant contributions to the Indian Rennaissance.

questions.text: What was the main purpose of the British building roads and railways in India?
questions.answer: The British built roads and railways for the convenience of administration and swift movement of the army, but these facilities also benefited Indians by increasing communication and contact.

questions.text: Who were considered extremist leaders in the Indian National Congress?
questions.answer: Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal were believed to be extremist leaders.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was observed as National Mourning Day during the Anti-Partition Movement?
questions.answer: The day of partition, October 16, was observed as National Mourning Day during the Anti-Partition Movement.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was Lokmanya Tilak's famous statement regarding Swaraj?
questions.answer: Lokmanya Tilak firmly stated that, "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it."

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the economic reasons for the growth of discontent among the Indian people?
questions.answer: The Indian wealth flowed towards England due to imperialist policies. Farmers were compelled to take cash crops, faced heavy land taxes, and continuous famines, which broke the backbone of Indian agriculture. Traditional industries declined, leading to unemployment, and capitalists exploited the worker class, while new taxes were imposed on the middle class, all contributing to widespread discontent.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: How did Lokmanya Tilak use national festivals for political awakening?
questions.answer: Lokmanya Tilak started organizing Shiv Jayanti and Ganesh Utsav with the objective that people should come together, exchange ideas, and get inspiration from national personalities. He believed that if people gathered for religious reasons, the government would not ban them, unlike political gatherings.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the main objectives of the Servants of India Society?
questions.answer: The main objectives of the Servants of India Society, founded by Gopal Krishna Gokhale, were to create love for the country, teach sacrifice of self-interest, destroy differences between religion and caste to create social harmony, and spread education.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the 'Responsive Cooperation' policy declared by Lokmanya Tilak?
questions.answer: Lokmanya Tilak declared that if the British government showed sympathy and a considerable attitude towards the demands of the Indians, then the Indian public would be ready to cooperate with the British. This policy was known as 'Responsive Cooperation'.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: The feeling of nationalism developed among the people due to British administration.
questions.answer: The British administration brought the nation under one roof with identical reforms and equality before law, which fostered a sense of unity. Additionally, the network of roads and railways, built for administrative convenience, facilitated contact and communication among people from different parts of India, further strengthening the feeling of nationalism.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: The British implemented the policy of "Divide and Rule" in India.
questions.answer: The British implemented the policy of "Divide and Rule" to cause a split in the national movement. They aimed to create a rift between Hindu-Muslim communities, believing that if these communities were divided, the freedom movement would be weakened. This strategy was evident in their decision to partition Bengal.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Everybody was disappointed due to the Montague Chelmsford Reform Act of 1919.
questions.answer: Everybody was disappointed due to the Montague Chelmsford Reform Act of 1919 because it did not give much exposure to the demand for Responsible Government of Indians. Less important departments were transferred to Indian ministers, while crucial departments like Finance, Home affairs, and Revenue remained under the control of the Governor, which was seen as insufficient progress towards self-governance.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the Anti-Partition Movement and its impact on the Indian National Congress.
questions.answer: The Anti-Partition Movement was a widespread public awakening against Lord Curzon's decision to partition Bengal in 1905, which was seen as a 'Divide and Rule' tactic. October 16, the day of partition, was observed as National Mourning Day across India, with protest meetings condemning the government's decision. 'Vande Mataram' became a popular slogan, and 'Raksha Bandhan' programs were held as a symbol of unity. Students boycotted government schools and colleges. Leaders like Surendranath Banerjee, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Rabindranath Tagore played significant roles. The movement's severity led the British to annul the partition in 1911. This movement significantly increased the extent of the Indian National Congress, transforming it into a national movement and strengthening the demand for Swaraj.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the differences between the Moderates and Extremists within the Indian National Congress.
questions.answer: The differences between the Moderates and Extremists became prominent in the Surat session of 1907. The Moderates, active from 1885-1905, were realistic, highly educated leaders like Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Ferozshah Mehta, and Surendranath Banerjee. They believed in peaceful and constitutional methods, hoping the British would grant justice to their demands. Their approach was slow but consistent, influenced by Western liberalism. In contrast, the Extremists, active from 1905-1920, like Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal, believed in severe struggle and extensive public agitation for freedom. They used methods like newspapers (e.g., Kesari, Maratha), national festivals, and national education to awaken political consciousness. While both groups aimed for the country's development, their working systems and ideologies regarding the pace and intensity of the movement differed significantly.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Swaraj' as pronounced by Dadabhai Nowrojee.
questions.answer: Dadabhai Nowrojee pronounced 'Swaraj' as the aim for India to achieve self-rule and a respectable position among developed countries, enabling it to save its people from poverty, hunger, and diseases.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Home Rule'.
questions.answer: 'Home Rule' means self-government, a movement that demanded the right of self-government in India, similar to movements against colonialism in other countries like Ireland.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the role of newspapers in the beginning of the freedom movement.
questions.answer: During this period, English and Vernacular newspapers and periodicals played a crucial role in political and social awakening. They served as a medium to criticize the government's policies and spread nationalist ideas. Newspapers like Darpan, Prabhakar, Hindu, Amrit Bazar Patrika, Kesari, and Mahratta openly criticized the British administration. Lokmanya Tilak, through 'Kesari' and 'Maratha', made severe criticisms of the British's suppressive policies, while 'Amrit Bazar Patrika' in Bengal became a mouthpiece for extremist ideology. These publications helped to inform, unite, and inspire the common people, fostering a sense of national identity and discontent against British rule.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the significance of the 'Four-point programme' accepted by the Indian National Congress in 1906.
questions.answer: In the 1906 session, under Dadabhai Nowrojee's presidency, the Indian National Congress unanimously accepted a 'Four-point programme' consisting of Swaraj, Swadeshi, National Education, and Boycott. 'Swaraj' was the ultimate goal of self-government. 'Swadeshi' aimed for self-sufficiency by bringing together capital, resources, and manpower within India, benefiting the country. 'Boycott' involved boycotting foreign goods as a first step, with the ultimate goal of boycotting foreign rule, thereby attacking the roots of British imperialism. 'National Education' aimed to create a generation concerned about its own language and tradition. This programme provided a clear direction and a more assertive approach to the freedom movement, unifying different factions under common goals.

questions.text: Why did Gandhiji support the Khilafat Movement?

questions.answer: The main objective of the Non-co-operation Movement was to make the British government collapse by Indians adopting complete non-co-operation.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the significance of 26th January 1930?
questions.answer: On 26th January 1930, people all over the country took a pledge for carrying out the freedom movement with non-violent means for the attainment of India's independence.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the demand of the young leaders like Pandit Nehru and Subhash Chandra Bose?
questions.answer: The young leaders like Pandit Nehru and Subhash Chandra Bose were demanding complete independence, also known as Poorna Swaraj.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the treatment of Indians in South Africa during Gandhiji's time there.
questions.answer: In South Africa, Indians were treated as criminals and subjected to constant humiliation. In 1906, the government made it compulsory for blacks to carry identity cards, restricting their freedom. Gandhiji launched Satyagraha to fight against this injustice and secure rights for the Indian community.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What was the 'Black Act' and why was it called so?
questions.answer: The 'Black Act' was the Rowlatt Act passed in 1919. It gave the government the right to arrest anyone without a warrant or imprison them without trial, and prohibited appeals against punishment. Indians called it the 'Black Act' due to its oppressive and unjust nature.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the constructive programmes undertaken by Gandhiji along with the Non-co-operation Movement?
questions.answer: Along with the Non-co-operation Movement, Gandhiji undertook constructive programmes such as the spread of Swadeshi, Hindu-Muslim unity, prohibition of alcohol, removal of untouchability, popularising the use of Khadi, and national education. These programmes aimed to make the national movement more comprehensive, especially in rural areas.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: What were the main proposals put forth in the Nehru Report?
questions.answer: The Nehru Report proposed establishing self-government in the colonies of India, implementing the Adult Franchise system, and the linguistic division of provinces. It was a response to the challenge that Indian leaders could not draft a unanimously accepted constitution.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Rabindranath Tagore gave away his 'Sir' title after the Jallianwala Baug massacre.
questions.answer: Rabindranath Tagore renounced his 'Sir' title as a protest against the brutal Jallianwala Baug massacre. He was deeply shocked and angered by the indiscriminate firing on unarmed civilians by General Dyer's forces. This act was a strong condemnation of the British government's oppressive policies and a solidarity gesture with the victims.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: The Indians boycotted the Simon Commission.
questions.answer: The Indians boycotted the Simon Commission because it did not include any Indian members. The commission was appointed to suggest reforms to the Montague-Chelmsford Act of 1919, but the exclusion of Indians from a body that would decide their political future was seen as a grave insult and an undermining of their aspirations for self-governance.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Give reason: Gandhiji suspended the Non-co-operation Movement.
questions.answer: Gandhiji suspended the Non-co-operation Movement due to the violent incident at Chauri Chaura in February 1922. A peaceful procession turned violent, leading to the burning of a police station and the death of 22 policemen. Gandhiji, a staunch believer in non-violence, was deeply hurt by this incident and felt that the movement was deviating from its core principle, hence he called it off.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the Jallianwala Baug Massacre and its impact.
questions.answer: The Jallianwala Baug Massacre occurred on April 13, 1919, in Amritsar. People had gathered peacefully at Jallianwala Baug to protest against the Rowlatt Act and the arrest of leaders. General Dyer, with armed forces, blocked the only exit and ordered his soldiers to fire on the unarmed crowd without warning. Approximately 400 people were killed, and many more were wounded. The impact was profound: it sparked widespread outrage across India, leading Rabindranath Tagore to renounce his knighthood and intensifying the demand for Swaraj. The British government appointed the Hunter Commission to investigate, but the incident deeply eroded Indian trust in British rule and became a turning point in the freedom struggle.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Describe the progress of the Non-co-operation Movement in India.
questions.answer: The Non-co-operation Movement, launched after the Nagpur session of the Indian National Congress in 1920, saw widespread participation. It involved boycotting government offices, courts, foreign goods, and government schools and colleges. Eminent lawyers like Motilal Nehru and Chittaranjan Das boycotted courts. National schools and colleges were established as alternatives. There was a boycott of elections and foreign clothes, leading to a decrease in imports. The visit of the Prince of Wales in 1921 was met with hartals. The movement spread from Assam planters to Bengal rail workers. However, it was suspended by Gandhiji in February 1922 after the violent Chauri Chaura incident, where a police station was set on fire.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Gandhian era'.
questions.answer: The 'Gandhian era' refers to the period in the Indian national movement from 1920 to 1947, during which Mahatma Gandhi's leadership, principles of Truth, Non-violence, and Satyagraha, and his mass movements significantly shaped India's struggle for independence.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Define 'Poorna Swaraj'.
questions.answer: 'Poorna Swaraj' means complete independence. It was the objective adopted by the Indian National Congress at the Lahore session in December 1929, signifying a shift from the demand for Dominion status to a full and unconditional freedom from British rule.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the philosophy of Satyagraha.
questions.answer: The philosophy of Satyagraha, introduced by Mahatma Gandhi, means 'insistence on truth'. Its main objective is to make an unjust person aware of truth and justice through patience and non-violent resistance, thereby bringing a transformation in their views. Gandhiji taught that a person following Satyagraha should never resort to violence or untruthful means. This novel technique aimed at moral persuasion rather than physical force, influencing movements globally, including those led by Martin Luther King and Nelson Mandela.

questions.subject: History & Civics
questions.text: Explain the significance of the Lahore session of the Indian National Congress in 1929.
questions.answer: The Lahore session of the Indian National Congress in December 1929, presided over by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, was historically significant because it formally adopted the resolution for 'Poorna Swaraj' or complete independence as the ultimate objective of the national movement. This marked a crucial shift from the earlier demand for Dominion status. On December 31, 1929, Pandit Nehru unfurled the tri-colour flag, and January 26, 1930, was declared as Independence Day, with people taking a pledge for a non-violent freedom struggle. This session infused a new spirit and direction into the independence movement.

questions.subject: History & Civics
